interaction.content: Thank you for being here today. When it’s time, we’ll go ahead and begin.
(Yes. Thank you.)
Hello, I’m the counselor. To start, could you tell me your age, gender, and what you’d like to talk about today?
Hello. I’m 26, male. Recently my mother hasn’t been in good health, and when I think about the future, I feel anxious.
Thank you for telling me. I see... Could you tell me a bit more about that?
At the end of last year, she had surgery once, and I was relieved that the treatment was completed safely. But recently it seems like there might be another area that isn’t good...
I see... That would make you worried, wouldn’t it. You mentioned another area recently—if you don’t mind sharing, what kind of issue might your mother be having with her health?

It seems there was a little blood mixed in with her stool... She already has hemorrhoids, so we don’t know yet, but because there’s also a possibility of colon cancer, it seems she needs a detailed examination...
I see. So she is actually having symptoms like that. That’s worrying... What kind of surgery did she have at the end of last year?

She had stones built up in her gallbladder, so it was surgery to remove that. My mother and I live in the same prefecture, but we live separately, and my father passed away a little while ago, so she lives alone, which makes me even more worried... And I don’t have any siblings besides me...
Mm-hmm. I see. That would make you even more worried...
Yes...
Mm-hmm. You said you live in the same prefecture as your mother—about how far apart do you live?
It’s about 15 minutes by car, so I can go see her right away.
Mm-hmm. I see. With your mother not feeling well and living alone right now, what feels like the biggest worry for you?
She’s close enough that I can go see her right away, but I worry when I think about what if she suddenly collapsed...

Mm-hmm, I see. Even if she’s nearby, when you think about something happening suddenly, it’s worrying... You said you’re living separately from your mother right now—what is your current family situation like?

I’m married and have a wife. So it’s pretty hard for me to go back to living at my parents’ home again... When I think about the future, like whether living together might be an option, I feel anxious.
Mm-hmm, I see. There are parts of it that must feel frustrating emotionally, too.
Yes...
For you, what kind of situation would you feel would be good from here on?
Of course, I think the most important thing is for my mother’s health to get better, but...
Yes, of course. When is your mother scheduled to have the detailed examination?
In early April.
I see. Until you know the results, it can leave you feeling kind of unsettled, can’t it.
Yes. I’m very anxious.
Mm-hmm. I think it’s completely understandable to feel that way. Until she has the examination, is she planning to be at home?
Do you mean my mother? Or me?
Your mother.
Yes. At the moment, she doesn’t have any symptoms other than the bloody stool, so she’s able to work as usual.
I see. So your mother is working, too. What kind of work does she do?
She mainly washes cars.
I see. About how many hours and how often does she work?
Five days a week, about seven hours a day.
I see. Does it feel like you’re especially worried when she’s not at work?
Yes. If there’s someone around, they might notice if something is wrong. And when I think that if it is cancer, she won’t be able to keep working, that makes me anxious again.

Mm-hmm, yes... Thinking about that would make you feel even more anxious, wouldn’t it. You’ve shared a lot with me so far, and I imagine you’re hoping your mother gets better, but through this consultation, what is it that you feel you’d like to talk through?
I’m not really sure myself, but it may be anxiety about what I should do if my mother has cancer.
Mm-hmm, so that’s how you’re feeling. When you think, “What if,” it’s completely understandable to feel full of anxiety.
Yes...
Mm-hmm. Are you talking with anyone about these concerns right now?
I have talked about it with my mother herself and with my wife.
I see. How are your mother and your wife taking it?
My mother seems like she intends to face her health properly. My wife has also said that if something happens, we’ll have to think about the three of us living together.
I see. So your wife is being understanding, too.
I feel bad that my wife is being so considerate...
I see... So for you, do you feel that ideally, you’d like to be able to respond right away if something happens to your mother, without making your wife worry or be overly considerate?
I think it’s impossible not to make her worry at all, but I think it would be while getting her cooperation. Family really is important, so I just want my mother to be safe somehow.

Mm-hmm, that’s how you feel. Hearing what you’ve shared so far, I can feel that you care about your mother very deeply. At the same time, I also get the sense that you’re carrying the feeling that you have to do something about this yourself. How does that sound to you?
Yes... There may be a part of me that’s taking it all on myself.

Mm-hmm, I see. I think that’s because you care so much about both your mother and your wife. For example, so that you can respond even if something happens to your mother, there are monitoring services offered by security companies and such, and I wondered if making use of that kind of support could be one option. What do you think?
I didn’t know there were services like that. I think I might consider it a little.
Mm-hmm. By using that kind of support, I think you may be able to create a little more time for yourself to feel calmer.
Thank you. Including that kind of thing, I think I’ll try talking with the people around me a bit more.
Yes. I’m rooting for you. How was it for you to talk today?
Thank you. I felt that maybe there is a part of me that’s been carrying it by myself, so I think I’ll try relying on the people around me a little more.
Mm-hmm. I think you are someone who truly cares very much about your family, so please take care of yourself, too.
I understand. Thank you.
If anything else comes up, please feel free to use this service again.
I understand. Thank you, and I hope to speak with you again if needed.
It’s still the season when mornings and evenings are chilly, so please take care of your health. With that, we’ll end the consultation here.
Yes. Thank you very much.
Thank you very much. (Thank you. I’d be grateful if you could let us know anything you noticed, including any suggestions for improvement.)
(Thank you. Would it be okay to write that in the evaluation?)
(Yes. Thank you.)
(I understand. Thank you very much.)
(Thank you very much. Take care.)

interaction.content: Hello. Thank you for working with me today. If possible, I’d appreciate it if you could play the role of a client with strong suicidal thoughts.
Hello. Understood. Thank you.
Thank you. Hello, I’m the counselor. Could you tell me your age, gender, and what you’d like to talk about?
30 years old, male, I want to die.
Something happened that was painful enough to make you feel like you want to die. Could you tell me a little about it?
My wife was having an affair.
That must have been very, very painful.
Yes.
Are you living separately right now?
We live together.
I see. When did you find out that she had been having an affair?
I found out a few days ago.
That must have been a real shock. You may feel like you want to die, but what other feelings are you having?
The biggest thing is that I trusted her, and she betrayed me.
Yes. The feeling of being betrayed is the biggest thing. I imagine that’s very painful. What has your partner said about it?
She doesn’t really seem remorseful. She’s even saying it’s my fault.
I see. She’s even saying that it’s your fault.
I can’t believe she would betray me and then say something like that too.
Yes. It’s hard to believe she would say something like that.
Yes.
What do you want to do from here?
I can’t find any value in living.
I see. It feels very painful to keep living right now.
Yes.
What kinds of things have you talked about with your partner?
We talked about her never contacting him again, and about rebuilding our relationship. I do think about trying again, but the way she seems remorseful still feels like an act.
You’re thinking of forgiving your partner and trying again.
Yes. But I don’t know if my wife feels that way.
I see. It feels like you still don’t know how your partner feels.
It’s like her words and actions don’t match... She says remorseful things, but nothing changes in her behavior.
She says remorseful things, but her behavior doesn’t change. That would leave you feeling unsettled.
That’s right.
Do the two of you have children?
We have two children.
I see. Is having children part of why you’re thinking of forgiving your partner?
Yes.
Is it that you feel you can’t trust her because your partner’s behavior isn’t changing? Is your partner a full-time homemaker?
It’s not so much that I can’t trust her, it’s more like, after betraying me, is that really all the remorse she can show? I wonder what kind of person she is. She works.
I see. Her remorseful attitude is only coming across a little bit.
Yes.
From your side, even in the current situation, you’re thinking of trying again.
Yes. But if my wife doesn’t change too, we can’t make it work.
Yes. It feels like your partner needs to change too, or you can’t keep going.
Yes.
How would you like your partner to become?
How I want her to become... More than that, I want to erase the memory of this affair.
You’re suffering so much that you want to erase the memory of the affair.
Yes. I keep thinking, why, how could this happen?
Yes. It’s very painful.
Was I the one who was wrong, like my wife says?
I don’t think that’s true. Whatever the circumstances, I think the person who has an affair is the one in the wrong.
That’s what I thought. Why doesn’t my wife feel remorse?
Yes... It’s hard to know why she isn’t feeling remorse.
What should I do?
I think it may be okay to take some time and think about what comes next. How does that sound?
Yes.
Are things going okay in your daily life with your children right now?
I’m not really sure what you mean by going okay, but it’s normal.
So you’re able to live normally. From here, please take your time thinking about what comes next.
I understand.
Thank you for sharing your story with me. Would it be okay to end here for today?
Yes. Thank you very much.
Thank you. We’ll end here.

Thank you, likewise.
(It’s time, so we’ll begin.) Hello, I’m the counselor. What would you like to talk about today?
My parents treat me terribly.
That sounds really hard. Could you tell me more specifically what they do?
I get yelled at even though I haven’t done anything.
It feels awful to be yelled at when you haven’t done anything, doesn’t it? By the way, could you tell me your age and gender?
16, male.
Thank you for telling me. If you’re 16, are you in your second year of high school?
Yes.
I see. When did this kind of thing start happening?
Since I became a second-year high school student.
So you’ve been going through this pain for more than half a year. Around the time you started your second year, was there anything you can think of that might have led to it?
I don’t know.
I see. When you can’t think of any reason, but suddenly start getting yelled at, it feels unfair, doesn’t it? Is it hard to reply right now? If it’s okay, please tell me what’s going on on your end.
I was waiting for you.
Oh, I see. I was waiting too, I’m sorry about that. Who do you live with?
Just normal people.
Do you have a father, mother, siblings—who is in your family?
My dad and my mom.
I see. Is it your father who yells at you even though you haven’t done anything? Or your mother?
My mom.
I see. When she yells at you, what kinds of things does your mother say?
She says all kinds of things.
It’s exhausting to have all kinds of things said to you. Does your father know about this?
I think he probably knows.
So your father knows... You think he probably knows. And how does your father respond to it?
He doesn’t get involved, so I don’t know.

I see. It seems like he probably knows, but he doesn’t really do anything. I think it must be very painful to carry this on your own. When you say you’re treated terribly, is there anything else besides being yelled at even when you haven’t done anything?
Like not being called for meals, I guess.

So that has happened too. Even while that was happening, you endured it alone. Even while that was happening, you endured it alone. I think these days must have been truly painful. Thank you for having the courage to come here and talk about it today. I think what you’re experiencing amounts to abuse. How do you feel about that?
Oh, I didn’t know that.

You haven’t done anything wrong. And yet, being blamed over and over is unfair. Also, not properly giving you meals is called neglect, and it’s something that absolutely must not be done. When you’re yelled at all the time, it can make you feel like you’re the one at fault, and that’s really sad. But you are absolutely not to blame.
It’s time, so I’ll excuse myself.
Understood. Thank you for your time. Thank you very much. I’d appreciate it if you could share your honest feedback. So, is it okay to end the role-play here?
Yes, thank you very much.
Then we’ll end here. Thank you very much.

interaction.content: Thank you for being here today. When it’s time, we’ll go ahead and begin.
Thank you.
Hello. I’m the counselor. To start, could you tell me your gender, age, and what you’d like to talk about?
Yes, I’m a man in my 40s. It’s about my high school daughter’s future path.
Thank you for sharing that. So you’d like to talk about your daughter’s future path. Could you tell me a bit more about that?

She’s a first-year student at a college-prep high school in Tokyo right now—she’ll be a second-year from April—but at this point she doesn’t really have anything she wants to do at all. She’s just vaguely thinking, maybe it would be better to go to university.
As her father, that’s something you end up thinking about, isn’t it. Have you talked with your daughter about this?
We talk about it sometimes. I think my daughter and I talk quite a lot, relatively speaking.

I often hear that as children get older, they stop talking as much, so it sounds like you have a lovely relationship. So, your daughter also doesn’t have anything in particular she wants to do right now, and it’s kind of like, maybe she’ll go to university?

Somehow, both she and I feel like it might not be right to just go to some random university—one she can probably get into. I feel like I want to give her some other kind of advice... It seems like she herself doesn’t have something she really wants to do, like, “This is it!”
I see. So you’re looking for better options for your daughter. What are her friends around her like?
I’ve never really asked what her friends’ situations are like.
I see. You mentioned that at this point she’s thinking maybe it would be better to go to university. Have you thought about other options?

Because it’s a college-prep school, the school talks as if getting into a university with a high entrance score is everything, so she’s fed up with it. But people around her are just naturally aiming for that and kind of going along with the flow. I think what should really matter is that she has something she wants to do, values that are important to her, and then we think about the means to get there. So I don’t want to steer her in the direction of just going to university for the time being.
I see. It’s wonderful that, as her father, you care about what she wants to do and the values that matter to her.
Of course, if it’s appropriate as a choice that connects to what she wants to study or her future dream, that’s different.
You want your daughter to find what she wants to do and the values that matter to her. By the way, do you have values that are important to you?
Me?

Yes. At your daughter’s age, I imagine it can be quite difficult to find those things. So I think if you talk to her about examples from different people, it may help her get a clearer picture. And I thought the people closest to her would be her family, so I asked.
So you mean values in terms of thinking about the future—what I would do myself, that kind of thing?
Yes. What do you think?

Looking back on my own experiences, I’d say if I have even a little interest in something, I try it. You don’t know whether it suits you or not until you do it, and if there’s a possibility there, you try it first and think about it after. Something like that.

Thank you for sharing that. So you’ve approached things with action first. Have you ever talked to your daughter about that? If she’s in a place where she hasn’t found what she wants to do yet, I think it could be good advice...

I haven’t talked to her about that kind of thing yet. In the flow of talking about taking action first. So, if hypothetically my daughter said she wanted to work instead of going to university, how should I advise her? Right now she’s putting a lot of effort into her part-time job, and she’s highly motivated about working and earning money.

I see. She’s finding enjoyment in working. From what you said earlier, you want your daughter to find what she wants to do. But do you feel some resistance to the option of not going on to university?
It’s a difficult point, but it’s not zero.
That makes sense. Since she’s attending a college-prep school, if she doesn’t go to university, that would feel like something that gives you pause.
Both my daughter and I have that conflict.

I see. So that’s how it is. She can work part-time even if she goes to university, and she can also study while working. There are many different options now, aren’t there. I feel that continuing to think it through together a bit more could be one approach, but is there a deadline by which you want to decide?
There isn’t any particular deadline for when we have to decide.
Even so, as a parent, you worry about your daughter’s future, don’t you.
Yes, that’s true.

The things someone wants to do and the values that matter to them are developed by actually coming into contact with many different things. Just as you found them through taking action. Your daughter is in a relatively narrow set of values, where going on to university from a college-prep school is the norm, so it might be good to help her encounter different values. What do you think?
You mentioned helping her encounter different values, but specifically, what would that look like?

I think putting herself in places outside of school is a good way. In that sense, a part-time job is good too. Other than that, you could introduce books you recommend, or have her meet people you respect, and so on.
I see. Introducing books might be good.

Yes! Please do try that. I was very moved by how seriously you’re thinking about your daughter’s future. I hope you and your daughter continue to get along well and look for a path that will make her happy.
Thank you. This was helpful for me as well.
Thank you for today. I’m sorry, it looks like we’re out of time... I apologize that I wasn’t able to wrap things up properly. If it’s all right with you, we’ll end here.
Yes, thank you for today. It’s OK to end here.

interaction.content: Thank you for meeting with me today.
Thank you.
When it’s time, I’ll reach out to you again.
Yes, thank you.
Hello, I’m the counselor.
Hello.
What would you like to talk about today?
I’m struggling with getting the urge to spend money as a way to relieve stress.
I see. That must be troubling.
Yes.
When does that tend to happen?

It happens a lot when I’m tired, I guess. I don’t know if you’d call it a positive feeling, but it tends to happen when I’m looking for something fun. It’s not just for myself either; sometimes I try to boost my self-esteem by spending money on my family or my partner.
Mm-hmm. When you’re tired and you can’t lift your mood on your own, you look for something enjoyable.
That’s right.
So it’s not only for yourself… When your family is happy, it raises your self-esteem. And for that, you spend money… and that’s what you’re struggling with, is that right?

That’s right. Rather than because they’re happy, I feel like I get a sense of satisfaction from the fact that I’m buying things for them. I think I need to save money, but sometimes I end up giving in to the impulse.
I see. Thank you for telling me.
Yes.
By the way, about how much is it? It’s not to the point where it causes trouble in your daily life, is it?
It doesn’t cause trouble in my daily life, but it slows down the pace at which I’m saving for things I want to do in the future.
I see. So it means you’re not able to invest in your future.
That’s right.
That must feel painful.
Yes, I can get a temporary sense of satisfaction, but afterward I start feeling guilty for spending the money.
What do you think would be good for you?
Well, I’d like to either change the way I relieve stress in the first place, or be able to not give in to the impulse.
I see. If your stress is relieved, it seems like you may not have to give in to it.
That’s right.
Earlier, you told me that when you’re busy, you feel stressed… What kinds of times are especially busy for you?
Probably when I’m at work. I feel like the urge is strongest after work.
I see. Is that every day? Or is it after work on days when you especially feel busy?
I’d say it’s pretty much every time.
Mm-hmm. When you finish work, you get tired, don’t you.
It’s physical work too, so my body gets really exhausted.
At times like that, wanting to find something enjoyable… I think that’s natural. It shows how hard you’re working every day, giving it your all.
Thank you.
Do you think there’s anything that might make your family happy without spending money?

Well... I can’t really think of much. They’re not the kind of people who usually say thank you, and if I do something special, they make fun of me a little, so I can’t really think of things that would make them happy. Maybe there’s a part of me that wants to be acknowledged or praised, even if I have to spend money.
I see. You’ve noticed that feeling in yourself.

Yes. I don’t have confidence that other people will acknowledge me, and I was aware that I do things like treat younger coworkers, using money to show my own value. So I wondered if this might be the same.
Mm-hmm. Wanting to be acknowledged… that may be something everyone has.
I wonder if that’s true.
In that situation, what would you think about shifting your perspective a little and trying to find things you enjoy for yourself?
If I could find them, I think that would be wonderful.
Yes. Rather than what other people think… I feel it might be better to focus on what feels enjoyable to you. What do you think?
I think that would be better.
Mm-hmm. Yes, that makes sense. By the way, earlier you said there’s something you want to do in the future. Is that something you’re looking forward to?
I’m really looking forward to it.
I see. Do you think spending your time on that could help lift your mood?
It can lift my mood, but the fatigue from that seems like it would make my desire to buy things come up again.
That can happen too, then.
That’s right. I think it would be nice if there were something I could enjoy now, rather than in the future.

For the thing you want to do in the future, what about making a schedule for yourself, deciding roughly how many years from now, working backward and writing down what you can do now, and clearing each step one by one… Could that become something enjoyable?
I can’t really imagine it. My image is that it becomes fun when I reach the goal.
I meant it in the sense that a big goal is like a board game, something that lies beyond small steps. I’m sorry I didn’t explain it well.
I understand that image, but even if there’s a sense of accomplishment from getting one step closer, I don’t know whether it would be fun. I’m sorry too.
No, no, I’m sorry.
I think I’ll try looking again for things I can enjoy.
I’d like to think together with you about what you enjoy, so I hope you’ll come back for another consultation.
Yes, I’ll come again. Thank you.
We’ll end here for today. Thank you for letting me listen to something important to you.
Thank you as well.
Take care.
Take care.
(Thank you for the role-play.)
Thank you.
Then we’ll end here. I’d appreciate it if you could share any points for reflection. Thank you.

interaction.content: (Good evening. I look forward to speaking with you.)
(Good evening. Likewise, thank you.)
Good evening, I’m the counselor. Thank you for coming to talk with me. To start, please let me know your age, gender, and what you’d like to discuss.
I’m a man in my 40s. My company went bankrupt, and I’m looking for work, but I just can’t seem to find the next job.
I see. Thank you for telling me. You came to talk with me while you’re in a very difficult situation.
That’s right.
Yes, I see. By the way, when did you start looking for your next job?
It’s been half a year.
I see. So you’ve been doing your best, looking for work for six months.
I just can’t find anything. I’m anxious.
Yes, I see. With something beyond your control like your company going bankrupt, not being able to find your next job would make you feel very anxious.
Yes, that’s right.
You’ve been feeling very anxious every day, and that’s what brought you here today. What has your family been saying?
They tell me to hurry up and find a job, and they also say it can’t be helped that I haven’t found one yet.

Yes, I see. They’re trying to be there for how you feel, and at the same time they’re expressing their anxiety about life going forward. Hearing those kinds of words can feel relieving, but it can also make you feel pressured.
Yes. They say all kinds of things.
Yes, so you and your family also have a relationship where you can share your feelings naturally. If you don’t mind, could you tell me about your current family situation?
It’s just me and my wife. Also, she’s in her last month of pregnancy.
I see. Thank you for telling me.
Yes.
So your precious child is expected to be born soon. And because you’ll be welcoming your child, you want to find your next job.
Whether the baby is here or not, we don’t have any savings, so we can’t live.
Yes, that’s how you’re feeling.
Yes. Of course I don’t want my child to go without, but if we can’t make a living, then there’s nothing to even talk about.
I see. So first of all, you feel that day-to-day living is what matters.
Yes, that’s right.
I think it’s very natural to feel that what matters first is getting through each day right in front of you.
Yes, that’s right.
Yes, I see. By the way, when the company went bankrupt, what did you think?
It was a shock, after all.
Yes, of course. I imagine you were very surprised, and it must have made you anxious too.
Yes.
Having to suddenly look for your next job must have left you feeling at a loss.
I was at a loss, and at the time, I feel like I couldn’t think about the future at all.
I see. You were just overwhelmed with anxiety. If the company you worked for ended up like that, I think that’s completely understandable.
They told us so suddenly, and I never imagined it would go under, so I was shocked.
Yes, I see. Being told all of a sudden, you were forced to respond before you could even sort out your feelings. That must have been painful.
Well, yes.
You suddenly had to look for your next job, but for yourself, what kind of direction are you hoping things will move in from here?
To get into my next job quickly.
Yes, that’s what you’re thinking. In this consultation, I’d like to think through your next employment together with you. How does that sound?
Yes. Please.
Thank you. You said you’re looking for various jobs right now. What are you focusing on as you search?
The conditions would be having weekends off and finishing at 5 p.m., I guess.
I see. What makes those conditions important to you?
I got married, so I need to look after my family.
Yes, that’s how you feel. You want to take care of your family too. I can sense your kindness. When it comes to finding new employment from here, what do you feel is difficult?
I want to get a job in construction, which is what I’ve been doing, but surprisingly, it’s hard to get hired, and that’s difficult.
I see. So it’s an industry where changing jobs is difficult. What have your former coworkers or seniors been saying about that?

I haven’t really talked much with people from before. I had the impression that there were a lot of openings in construction, but even when there are openings, it’s hard to get hired, and that’s painful.
I see. In that kind of situation, I think it’s natural to feel worn out.
Yes.
What do you think might help you in getting your next job decided?
By help, do you mean like my family helping me?
I asked because I wondered if there might be some kind of hint for getting a new job, but do you feel like there might be help from your family?
For now, I’m probably thinking there isn’t any help from my family, and that it depends on me. I don’t really know about hints. I guess I’m looking on job sites and going to interviews.
I see. Thank you for telling me. You’re doing your best every day toward finding employment.
Yes.
We’ve talked up to this point, but it’s now time to end today’s consultation. We’re still in the middle of the conversation, but how was it for you to talk about this?
Well, it doesn’t fundamentally solve anything, but I felt like maybe we could continue from here next time.
I see. If you’d like, I’d be glad to hear more from you next time.
Yes, thank you very much.
Thank you for sharing your story with me today.
Thank you very much.
I want to support you, so if you’d like, I hope you’ll continue to tell me more next time. With that, I’ll end today’s consultation.
Yes, thank you very much.
(Thank you for your time. Thank you.)
(Thank you for your time. Likewise, thank you.)

interaction.content: Good evening. I’m a counselor. To start, please let me know your age, gender, and what you’d like to talk about.
Yes. I’m a 40-year-old woman. My son has stopped going to school, and my husband and I have ended up arguing about it, so I’m really at a loss.

Thank you for sharing that with me. You must be worried about your son. And you’re having conflicts with your husband. I imagine that’s very painful. Are you arguing with your husband about how to respond to your son?
Yes. Just the fact that he’s not going to school is hard enough...
I’m sorry. Please go on.
Yes. That’s right.
Even just having a child who isn’t going to school must be really hard, and when there are differences between husband and wife about how to respond, it becomes even more painful, doesn’t it.
Yes. I just don’t know what to do anymore...

When things are hard, you want your husband to be someone who understands and supports you, so if that isn’t the case, it’s completely understandable that you wouldn’t know what to do. What kinds of things are you specifically arguing about?
I say that if he doesn’t want to go to school, we don’t have to force him to go, but my husband says we should be stricter.
That means your views are completely opposite. How long have you been discussing how to respond to your son?
Since about a month ago.

So you’ve been at a standstill for a whole month now. That sounds like going around in circles. It must be exhausting. From your perspective, you feel it would be better not to force him to go, but does your husband show no understanding of that at all?
Yes... He doesn’t.
I see. Your husband isn’t wavering in his view. How is your son spending his time now? If you tried to make him go, does it seem like he might be able to?
It’s summer vacation now, so he’s at home. Even if we try to make him go, he says he doesn’t want to, so we haven’t forced him.

With recent approaches to school refusal, it’s often said that it’s better not to force a child to go, isn’t it. Of course, it depends on the case... Do you have any idea what might have caused your son’s difficulty with school? I think it’s important to look closely at that and respond in a way that fits.
Yes.
I meant to say school refusal, not difficulty with school. I’m sorry. So you do have some idea. Would you be willing to tell me?
As for what might be behind it, I’m not really sure... But since around the time he stopped going to school, I’ve felt like his appetite has gone down.
It’s worrying that his appetite has gone down. It’s said that if someone can eat and sleep well, they can gradually recover, but he doesn’t have much appetite. How is his sleep?
Yes. It’s a little irregular.

It sounds like it’s become a little irregular. But if it’s not that he can’t eat at all, and his sleep has only become somewhat irregular, then I also think your approach—really accepting your son as he is and gently watching over him—may be appropriate.
Yes.
Are you able to communicate well with your son?
Yes. I think we are.
How about your husband? I mean communication between your husband and your son.
My husband comes home late, so on weekdays he doesn’t talk with our child much. Even on his days off, he often goes out for golf and things like that.

Then since you are the one who is watching your son closely, communicating well with him, and understanding his current state, I think your feeling that forcing him isn’t good is probably the right response.
Yes. But my husband says we should make him go in a strict way, and that’s what leads to fights.

I do think your husband cares deeply about your son, too, but since he isn’t home very much and it seems they don’t communicate that much, he may not really understand your son’s current state. Do you think it might be possible to somehow help your husband understand how your son is doing now, become more flexible in his thinking, and move toward meeting you halfway?
What should I do...?

Well, first, I think it’s important that neither of you gets emotional. Then, I think the next step is to calmly tell him about the situation with your son as you understand it. And I think it may help to give examples of recent ways people respond to school refusal, so he can understand that forcing him isn’t good. What do you think?
My husband is strict, so he gets angry quickly, and when it turns into an argument, he just leaves. I hope he’ll understand, but...

That does sound like it would be difficult to have a calm discussion. But for your son’s sake, do you think you might be able to find ways to communicate with your husband so that he can somehow understand?
How can I get him to understand?

Yes... I’m also thinking about how we might help your husband understand, but it seems difficult to put together a good idea within today’s time. Our time is up for today, but I’d like to keep thinking together with you about what to do about this issue. If you’d like, please come again. We can continue from here.
Yes. I understand. Thank you for today.

You are someone who can be a good source of understanding for your son and support him. I’m rooting for you. Thank you for sharing with me today. I’m sorry that our time is up, but we’ll end here for today.

interaction.content: Hello. I’m Hanamaru, a counselor. If you don’t mind, could you tell me your age and gender for this consultation?
Hello. I’m 34, male.
Could you tell me what you’d like to talk about today?
There’s something I want to do, but I just can’t seem to get motivated.
So there’s something you want to do. If you don’t mind, could you tell me what that is?
I’m thinking about leaving my company job and becoming independent.
That’s amazing. I think it’s truly wonderful that you have that kind of aspiration. When did you first start feeling that you wanted to become independent?
Since I was about 20.
So you’ve had that feeling for quite a long time. Is there anything specific that you think is making it hard for your motivation to come up?
Hmm, I’ve been planning my goals, but...
So you’ve been thinking through various things in concrete terms. What exactly is it that you want to do? If you don’t mind, could you tell me?
I want to become a professional mental trainer.
That’s wonderful. You want to become a professional mental trainer. Have you not taken any concrete action yet?
No, I started studying and things like that last year.
It’s great that you’ve really been taking action. I think leaving a company job takes a lot of courage, and you really do have a clear dream.
Yes.
Once you become a professional mental trainer, how would you like to work?
I’d like to start working locally first, and eventually work around the world.
Amazing. You already have a vision. What made you want to become a professional mental trainer?
Because I’ve often been involved in things like sports.
So you’ve often been involved in sports. You have a vision, and you have a reason for wanting to do it, so what do you think is causing your motivation not to rise?
Even when I think, “I’m going to do it,” there are times when I end up slacking off.
I see. I understand. I have similar tendencies myself. But I think it’s really great that you’ve already started taking action. Have you been moving forward with your studies little by little?
Yes. I’m making progress little by little.
I think it’s wonderful that you’re moving forward toward your goal, even if it’s little by little. Specifically, when are you thinking you’d like to become a professional mental trainer?
Within two years at the earliest. Within six years at the latest.

Since you’re 34 now, that means you’d like to become a professional mental trainer by age 40 at the latest. You’re still young, MTKH, and I think it’s okay to keep moving toward your goal little by little. I think it would be painful to force yourself when you don’t feel up to it, so maybe it’s okay to do it when you feel like you want to.
That’s true. Getting impatient or cramming too much in isn’t always good, is it?
Yes. I think it’s amazing that, even though you’re still young, you have something you really want to do and you’re moving toward your goal, even little by little, MTKH.
Thank you.
Do you feel like you’ll be able to achieve your goal?
I’ll try to work hard while keeping a good balance.
Yes. Let’s take it slowly, bit by bit. I think it’s wonderful that you’ve already taken action and are moving forward toward your goal, MTKH. How was it talking today?
It made me feel again that I want to work hard toward my goal. Thank you very much.
I’m glad to hear that. We still have a little time left. Is there anything you feel you haven’t talked about enough?
No. I’m okay.
All right. I’m rooting for you to achieve your goal, MTKH. Thank you for talking with me today.
Thank you as well.
Well then, we’ll end the consultation here. Thank you for your time today.
Thank you for your time.

interaction.content: (Good morning. I look forward to working with you again today. This is our fourth matching session. Thank you, as always, for your insightful comments.)

(Good morning. I look forward to working with you. On my end, the other person doesn’t show up until the consultation is over… but I’m guessing on my own that you might be the person I worked with the other day (laugh)) (Do you have any preferences for the client?)
(As before, I’d like to work with a younger female high school student, if possible.)
(Understood. Then I look forward to working with you when the scheduled time comes.)
Good morning. I’m the counselor. To start, if it’s okay, could you tell me your age, gender, and what you’d like to talk about?
Hello. I’m 16, female, and I’m worried about my future path.
I see. So you’re struggling with that.
Yes.
More specifically, what part of your future path are you worried about?
People around me are encouraging me to continue my education, but I also wonder if it might be better to get a job.
I see. That would be something to worry about. You mentioned that you think it might be better to get a job—what makes you feel that way?
Continuing school costs money, and I’m not confident about being able to manage day-to-day living.
I see. So you’re worried about financial issues. That would make you anxious.
Yes. I’m the oldest daughter, but I still have two younger siblings, so I’m wondering what I should do.
I see. You have siblings, and that’s part of what you’re worried about.
That’s part of it, yes.
You’re a kind older sister who thinks about your siblings. What other things are you thinking about?
I don’t know if it’s kindness… it’s more like we’re just barely getting by.
I see. You said you’re just barely getting by—what is the situation like, specifically?
My family is a single-parent household, and my mother works too, but I also work quite a bit at a part-time job, and that’s how we’re just managing to live.
I see. Thank you for telling me. So that’s the kind of situation you’re living with day to day.
Yes.
Are you managing to balance studying and your part-time job?
I think I am. I do like studying, so while I’m at school, I’m fairly focused on my studies.
I see. That’s good to hear. I feel a little relieved. What kinds of subjects do you like studying?
I think I mostly like science and math subjects. But I also like books, so I enjoy modern Japanese and things like that too.
I see. You’re interested in various things and enjoying your studies. That’s wonderful.
Thank you.
Do you have a dream for the future, or any idea of the kind of person you’d like to become?

In the future, I’d like to get some kind of qualification and be able to work with it. I haven’t clearly decided what qualification yet, but I feel like if I have one, I’ll be okay no matter what happens.

I see, that makes sense. Having a qualification can be a real strength. I think that’s a very reasonable way to think about it. If you chose to continue your education, have you thought about any schools you’d want to go to?
I haven’t decided clearly yet.
I see. How does your mother feel about your future path?
My mother is also encouraging me to continue school. She said that an expensive private school might be difficult, but that she would do her best as much as possible.
I see. When you heard that, how did you feel?
I’m happy about how my mother feels. I’m grateful because she’s always working hard for us. But I’m worried about what she means by working even harder than she already is.
So that’s how you felt. You’re a kind person who really cares about your mother.
I don’t know whether I’m kind or not, but thank you.

No, truly. From what you’ve shared, you’re struggling with your future path because of financial concerns. I think there are various options, like scholarships or studying while working. What do you think about those?
I’ve heard that there are systems like scholarships. I hadn’t really thought much about studying while working.
I see. Have you talked with a teacher at school about this?

My younger siblings will be continuing their education too, so living expenses will go up even more. So it’s not just about me—our family is going to need more money. I talked a little with my teacher during a meeting.
I see. What did your teacher say?
My teacher said that since my grades are good, I should aim higher.
I see. How did you feel when you heard that?
I’m happy that my teacher thinks that way. But then I start thinking about all kinds of things, like how much money I’d need if I continued school, and how we would manage from here on.
I see. That would make you worried. I think if you make it visible—specifically, how much it would cost if you continued school—it may become clearer. What do you think?

Yes… I’ve never actually calculated how much it would cost. I still don’t know whether I’d choose university or vocational school, or what kind of place I’d want to go to, and I also haven’t really asked properly how much I could earn if I got a job.
So that’s how you’re thinking. I’m glad. If you try making different simulations, I think things may become more concrete. What do you think?
I’ll try talking properly with my mother. I don’t really know how to do a simulation? but I’ll look into it. By the way, does making it visible mean looking at the amounts and thinking about them?

Yes. When you’re just thinking about it in your head, it can be hard to see clearly, but if you actually write out the amounts and things like that, I think it can help you organize it. What do you think?
It’s like study methods, then. I can picture it now.
I’m glad to hear that. Please value your own feelings, and whatever direction you choose, continue the studies you enjoy and work toward getting a qualification.
Thank you. I’ll try talking it over with them.
Thank you for coming here today. Please let me hear from you again.
Yes, thank you very much. (That is all from the client.)
(Thank you very much. As always, I learned a great deal.)

interaction.content: (I’m standing by. Thank you for being here today.) (We’ll begin at the scheduled time.)
(Hello. Yes, once it’s time, thank you in advance!)
Hello, I’m the counselor. To start, could you tell me your age, gender, and what you’d like to talk about?
I’m 20, female, and I’m scared of nighttime…
I see. Thank you for telling me. Was there a reason or something that triggered you feeling scared?
Yes…
Please tell me whatever you feel comfortable sharing. It’s okay to share only what you can.

About two weeks ago, I was heading toward the station after work, and even though there weren’t many people around, I had this feeling that a man was following me the whole time. I thought maybe it was just my imagination, but even after I got off the train, he kept following me. I got scared and went into a convenience store, and he came in too, so I ran home. But when I looked through the curtains, he was wandering around for about 30 minutes…
That must have been really frightening… Are you safe now?
I’m okay. But ever since then, I’ve been scared all the time. Like after work, or at night… Just because someone is a man, I tense up.
That makes sense. Having something frightening happen like that would make you feel worried.
Yes… It was only once, so I wonder if it’s not really stalking or anything… But I’m scared at night.
I see, so it was just that one time. And the main thing you want to work through is being especially scared at night.
Yes… I think maybe I’m worrying too much, but…
I see. Still, first of all, I’m glad you came here to talk with me today, and that you’re safe.
Thank you…
No, not at all. By the way, you said you might be worrying too much. What makes you feel that way?
Because it only happened once… I wonder if normal people wouldn’t worry this much. Even at work, when I’m serving customers, I keep thinking, maybe it’s this person…
I see, that’s how you’ve been feeling. But I think it was a very frightening experience for you, so it’s completely natural to feel anxious.
Yes…
By the way, are you currently working a part-time job in customer service?
Yes, I work at a hostess club. So the customers are almost all men.
I see. I imagine it must have been painful to work while feeling scared of men. How has that been for you?
Yes… it has…
Yes, so I’m glad you talked about it. Today, let’s think through together what you’re anxious about and what might help you live with a sense of safety.
Thank you. I want to think about that.
Yes, I’d like to help if I can. By the way, what is your life like right now? For example, during the day when you’re not working, whether you live alone, and so on.
During the day when I’m not working, I go to university and things like that. I live alone.
I see. Other than nighttime and men, are there any other times or situations where you feel scared?
Those two feel the strongest right now.
I understand. Living alone while carrying those feelings must have been very anxiety-provoking. Was there a reason you chose to work at a hostess club?
I was scouted, and the hourly pay is good.
I see. Since that happened, have you talked to anyone about it, or are there things you’ve been careful about?
I haven’t really talked to anyone. Things I’m careful about… I end up checking the locks over and over every day. And that’s not just at night. Even when I’m asleep, if I wake up, I go check again.
I see. Then even at home, it must be hard to really relax…
Home is the scariest place…
I see. Is that because being alone feels frightening?
Yes. Since I live alone…
That makes sense. For you, is the biggest thing that you want to be able to relax and feel safe at home? Or are you thinking you’d rather find ways not to be at home? What do you feel you want?
I want to be able to feel safe at home… When I’m alone, the scene from that night keeps replaying in my head, and I dream about being chased… It’s exhausting.
Of course, that would be exhausting. You mentioned school and work, and with all this anxiety too, have you been able to sleep?
I haven’t really been able to sleep, and when I remember it, my heart starts pounding, and then I can’t sleep even more… I go check the locks over and over.
I see. First, let’s think about ways for you to be able to sleep more peacefully. It would be difficult if it starts affecting your health too.
Yes…
After hearing what you’ve shared so far, I also feel that the first thing is to find ways for you to feel safe at home.
Yes… thank you.

You mentioned that you might be worrying too much, but on the other hand, I think it’s good that you noticed, “I might be being followed.” Because you went into the convenience store and hurried home, and even if it was a misunderstanding, you were able to come here and talk today.
That may be true.

The fact that you felt anxious is real, so first, would it be possible to talk to your workplace? I’ve heard that some places offer transportation depending on the club. There may be something your workplace can do. Even if it was a misunderstanding, just having other people who are aware and looking out for you might change things a little. What do you think?
Yes… I’ve been hesitating because things haven’t been going that well with the club, but it might be okay to tell them what actually happened.

I see. I suggested it because I hadn’t asked about your relationship with the club, but if it seems possible to talk to them, it might be good to try. Also, if you talk to the police, they may come patrol around your home at night. This is personal, but I’ve asked them myself before and they came. You could just casually talk to them, tell them the days of the week or times when you feel scared, and ask them to come check the area. That might help you feel a little more at ease.
I see. I thought the police wouldn’t do anything unless something had already happened. Thank you.

If you’re going to continue working at the hostess club, it might also be good to talk with them about your hours. We’re out of time for today, but next time I’d like to talk more specifically about your concerns around work and concrete steps you can take after your shifts, so please feel free to come talk anytime.
Okay. Thank you.
I’ll make a note of what we discussed today, so please don’t worry. If there are any developments, please let me know. Thank you for today.
Thank you very much.
(I’m sorry we went over time. This was my first case like this, so I learned a lot. Thank you very much.)
(Thank you as well! I learned a lot. Let’s end here!)

interaction.content: (Good evening. Thank you for being here today. We’ll begin when it’s time.)
(Good evening. Thank you as well. I appreciate your time.)
Thank you for coming to talk with me today. To start, could you tell me your age, gender, and what you’d like to talk about today?
I’m a 20-year-old woman. Being alive is painful.
I see. That sounds painful. When do you find yourself feeling that way?
I feel it especially when I watch news programs.
Mm-hmm. So it’s when you watch news programs. What kinds of news make you feel that pain?
Murder cases, or reports about celebrities dying by suicide.
I see. I think it’s only natural to feel distressed when you see reports like that.
Yes, it makes me want to die too.
It gets so painful that you want to die. That must be really hard. Since when have you been feeling that way when you see news reports?

Recently, I guess. I’ve had feelings of wanting to die for a long time, but lately there’s been so much news about all kinds of things, right? When I see that kind of thing, I start wanting to die too.

Mm-hmm. There really has been a lot of news lately. When you have more chances to see reports like that, it can make things feel even more painful. So you’ve had feelings of wanting to die for quite some time.
Yes, that’s right.
Thank you for sharing that with me. What kinds of times have you felt like you wanted to die?
I wonder if there’s any point in living from here on, or I don’t really have anything I want to do, and it’s like I don’t have any hope.
Mm-hmm. You’ve been wondering whether there’s any meaning in being alive. It’s really hard to end up thinking that way. Was there something that happened that made you start feeling that way?
I don’t really know what triggered it, but somehow I don’t have anything I want to do, and being alive isn’t interesting, and I think maybe it would be better to die.
I see. How long have you been feeling this way?
I’ve been pretty much like this since around high school.
I see. So you’ve been struggling with this since high school. I imagine it must have been painful for a long time. Have you ever told anyone about these feelings?
No, I haven’t. It’s like I’ve just vaguely been thinking about it by myself the whole time.
I see. Even if it’s been vague, I’m concerned that it must have been really hard to keep thinking about it all alone for so long.
I’ve gotten tired of thinking about it, so I’ve started to feel like maybe that’s enough.

Mm-hmm. Thinking about it for so long is truly exhausting. I think it’s natural to feel that way. From what you’ve shared with me so far, I get the sense that you’ve been living while thinking about the meaning of continuing to live, because you don’t have things you want to do or a sense of hope.
I can’t find any meaning in living, so I want to die.

Mm-hmm. You’ve been continuing to think about the meaning of living, haven’t you. You must be very exhausted. At the same time, to me it feels like you’re looking closely at your own future and really thinking about it. That may be exactly why you came to talk today.
I can’t see any future at all. I have absolutely no hope.
It’s truly painful to feel like you can’t see the future and have no hope. For example, what kind of future might let you begin to see some hope?
Maybe a future where I’m doing what I want to do and living with energy.
That sounds good. A future where you’re doing what you want to do and living with energy sounds really wonderful.
Right now, I don’t feel like I could live that way at all, though...
It’s hard to find what you want to do, isn’t it. You spend each day thinking about so much—are there things that make you feel relieved, or things you feel are enjoyable?
Hmm. I guess I feel relieved when I’m listening to music.
Mm-hmm. You like music. Listening to music you like can feel comforting. When do you usually listen to music?
When I have free time, I might spend most of it listening to music.
So when you have free time, you spend most of it listening to music. Having something you like that lets you lose track of time like that is really wonderful.
It’s just that I don’t have anything else to do...

You feel like you don’t have anything else to do. From hearing what you’ve shared today, I got the sense that you’ve been exhausted from continuing to think about the meaning of being alive because you can’t see a future or hope ahead. But even within that, you do have music as a way to feel even a little bit relieved. I think you likely have various ways of thinking about hope for the future. If you’re willing, I’d be glad if we could think together again about what kinds of hope might be possible.
Yes, please.
I’m sorry we went over time. Thank you for letting me hear your story.
Thank you very much.
We’ll end here, then. (Thank you for your time. I’m sorry we went over. Thank you very much.)
(Thank you as well. I learned a great deal.)
(We’ll end here, then.)

That sounds troubling. Do you also feel that it would be better to have that image first?
Yes. I want to marry someone I can always feel, “I’m glad I married this person.”
It would be wonderful to always feel that way. So for you, having an image of your ideal man first feels like it would help you marry someone you can feel glad you married.
Yes. I think it’s important to understand my own wishes myself.
I think you’re absolutely right. By the way, what led you to want to marry someone you can always feel, “I’m glad I married this person,” about?
My father and mother didn’t get along very well. I do want to get married, but my father was harsh toward my mother, so I don’t want to marry someone like him.
I see. That makes the question of what kind of person you end up with all the more important for you, doesn’t it?
Yes.
You mentioned that it’s hard to picture your ideal man. I interpreted that as meaning that, for you, “ideal” means you’re not sure what you want in a partner. Is that right?
Yes... I don’t know where to start thinking from. For example, even if I say “kind,” there are many different kinds of kindness...
That’s true. So you’re not sure where to start in thinking about what kind of person would make you feel, “I’m glad I married this person,” at any time.
That’s right. I’m sorry it’s such a vague concern...
Not at all. It’s a concern that comes from wanting to choose a partner seriously, so I think it’s a meaningful concern. Today, I’d like for us to think through that together.
Yes, thank you. I appreciate it.

Thank you as well. In order to have a wonderful married life with your partner, what kinds of things would you want to value? For example, someone with whom you can both express gratitude to each other—anything that comes to mind is fine.

Let’s see, I’d like someone who can accept the things we’re each not good at and gently support each other. Seeing my father criticize my mother for what she couldn’t do made me feel that this is important.
That really is very important. Given your experience with your father, this value may be an important point for you that you can’t compromise on.
Yes, somehow I feel like I may be too caught up in my father... but I’m starting to get a bit of an image.
I see. By the way, when you think, “Maybe I’m caught up in my father,” how does that make you feel?
I feel like I’m losing sight of some important element. I feel like I want to look at it from a broader perspective, not just in contrast to my father.

Yes, that may be an important realization. Rather than comparing things with your father, how would it feel to set your father aside for now, as you said, and try thinking from a broader perspective from here?
Yes, how should I do that?

After setting your father aside for the moment, when you think about having a wonderful married life with your partner, what kinds of things would you want to value? If your thoughts seem like they might change from what you said earlier after trying to set that aside, please tell me.
Thank you. Hmm, I think I’m someone who tends to be considerate of others. So I think if the other person isn’t someone who does that too, I’d get tired.
Yes. What kind of consideration do you mean?

I pay attention to how they’re feeling physically or emotionally that day, and I’m careful about whether what I say might make the other person uncomfortable, as well as my words and the other person’s background. I don’t really bad-mouth people much to begin with, though.

I see. You’re a very sensitive and kind person. It does make sense that if the other person were completely indifferent and not considerate at all, you might feel like you’re the only one getting worn out.
Yes.
Have you had experiences before where you dated someone who was less considerate than you, and it ended up exhausting you?
Yes, one person I dated was like that, and even breaking up was difficult.
I see. So for you, a relationship where you can both be considerate of each other is one part of your ideal.
Yes. I realized that I’ve always thought it would be nice to be with someone who helps me feel relieved when I’m anxious.
That’s an important element in building a relationship where you can support each other. If anything else comes to mind, please let me know.
Let’s see, from having you listen to me, what’s kind of coming up is...
Yes.

Someone who encourages me in a bright and positive way, and if they’re going to do that, I think I’d respect them more if they also actually had something they were working on positively themselves. Also, I’d like someone who doesn’t have two sides. I’m really not good with people who have a hidden side.
Yes, I see. What does someone with a hidden side mean to you?

Someone who is smiling and friendly on the surface, but behind the scenes casually disses others, or... when I see someone saying bad things about other people, it scares me. But I also have times when I want to complain, or rather talk about my feelings, and I think it might be hard if everything is answered with positivity. Oh, I really do have a strong feeling of wanting someone to listen to me. I think it would be good if they really understood my feelings.

People who only show a nice face in some situations but then speak badly about others behind their backs can feel scary to be around... It may be important to you that when you open up about your own feelings, the person really listens to your feelings and thoughts and understands you.

Yes, I also think that if they’re too kind to everyone, I might get jealous, so I’d want them to get along with people around them in a way that feels reassuring to me. I’d be happy if they were kind to me.
That’s actually quite important, isn’t it. Whether someone can be considerate in a way that reassures their partner, rather than making them anxious, is an important point of judgment for you.
That’s true. I realized that I’m asking for quite a lot of consideration from the other person. I hope they wouldn’t feel I’m too much...

I think that’s probably because you yourself are also that considerate toward the other person. For a man who, like you, values properly caring about the other person, I don’t think he would see it as too much. I didn’t feel it was too much at all. I felt that if you could be with someone who sees that as an important shared value, you would be very happy.
Thank you. I’m really happy to hear you say that...! Yes, maybe I should look for someone like that. Values really are important.

Yes. It may be good to look for someone who empathizes with you when you share your wish to be with someone who can value these things. I’ve summarized the values you want to consider important in choosing a partner. How does it feel after talking through them? 1. Someone who values mutual consideration. 2. Someone who helps you feel relieved when you’re anxious. 3. Someone who encourages you in a bright and positive way → if they also actually have something they’re working on positively, you can respect each other. 4. Someone who doesn’t have two sides. 5. Someone with whom you can listen to each other and understand each other’s feelings. 6. Someone who can value making an effort to help each other feel secure.

Wow, that’s amazing!!! Thank you so much for summarizing it so carefully!! I feel like I’d like to read it over many times and keep expanding the image even more! Yes, I’ll try talking about my values. Maybe someone I can naturally have that kind of conversation with would be good.

That sounds good! If your image expands or changes again, please let me know. If you start marriage-hunting based on these important points and run into any stumbling blocks or struggles, let’s look again together at your values and things like that. So please feel free to come talk anytime. I’m truly rooting for you in choosing a partner.
Thank you so much. From such a vague place, talking with you helped me see so many things, so I’d like to consult with you again.

Thank you as well for gathering the courage to come here today! I’m very glad to hear you say that. Please come back anytime. Thank you very much for your valuable time today and for participating as the client role. Since our time is up, would it be all right to end here?
Thank you very much. (You asked so many wonderful questions, and I truly learned a lot. It’s okay to end here. Thank you!)
Thank you for your kind words... You’ve done really well today. I apologize for the trouble, but I would be grateful if you could provide feedback. With that, I’ll take my leave.

interaction.content: Hello. I’m a counselor. Thank you for coming in to talk with me today. To start, could you tell me your age, gender, and what you’d like to discuss?
Hello. I’m a woman in my 30s, and what I want to talk about is some mom friends in my neighborhood.
Thank you for sharing that. Please tell me more about your mom friends.
In my neighborhood, there are seven mom friends, including me. Three of them have ended up getting along really badly, and the whole atmosphere is just awful right now...
I see. So you’ve been feeling uncomfortable. What was it that led to those three becoming so strained with each other?

Yes, it’s awkward... Those three all have children who are the same age. It’s a combination of a rambunctious boy, a very outspoken girl, and an extremely serious girl. So it seems like there were quite a lot of problems between the kids. From what I hear, it’s like the rambunctious boy and the outspoken girl would go after the serious girl. And then the serious girl’s mom seems to have snapped.
I see. So the trouble between the children affected the relationships between the moms. Do you know specifically what happened among those three?
That’s right. If it were just the three of them fighting, that would be one thing... I’ve heard the details. I heard about it from everyone.
So it wasn’t just an ordinary fight?

Hmm. How should I put it... it feels like everyone reached their limit. The serious child’s mom is pretty sensitive. And she can’t feel satisfied unless she says everything she wants to say, so even if it’s a small fight between the kids, she apparently always tells the other two moms about it. Like, “Please teach your children properly!” The two moms who are told this are pretty easygoing, so no matter what she said, they didn’t really try to improve anything, and the kids apparently kept fighting over the same kinds of things. That went on for three years, and it seems like they were all irritated with each other, and finally the moms started ignoring each other even when they passed on the street...

It sounds like there’s a big difference in values. When a group becomes tense like that, it can feel very uncomfortable. Going forward, how would you like things to be between the mom friends? Also, if you don’t mind, could you tell me what you’d like me to call you?

Their values are just too different. It would be good if they could accept that about each other, but the sensitive mom can’t do that... because she’s always right... Hmm... To be honest, I don’t want to get dragged into it, I guess... Please call me “Shi-mama.”

Shi-mama, then. Thank you. I think the feeling of not wanting to get dragged into it is very natural when it comes to protecting yourself and your important family. So your concern is about how to respond so that you don’t get pulled into the conflict between your mom friends—is that right?
I see. Yes, that’s true. I’ve been listening to all kinds of things too, and I’ve gotten really tired.
Listening to all of that can be tiring, can’t it? I think it shows that you’ve been listening very sincerely to the other moms.

I wonder... Sorry, I didn’t really understand what I wanted to do. Yes, I think I may want to be conscious of not getting dragged in. Thank you. I’ve been hearing from both sides, and I ended up not knowing what I should do...

What about the other mom friends who aren’t in the conflict? Are your relationships with them the same as before? Sorry, our messages came at the same time. Since you’re able to hear from both sides, Shi-mama, it sounds like both moms rely on you.

No, no, it’s okay. The other mom friends—three of them, not including me—aren’t really on either side either. We often talk with those three like, “What should we do about those three...?” But with that sensitive mom, I feel like she’s kind of fixated on me, and I think the people around us feel that too. I think it’s probably because I don’t deny her opinions. I just listen, basically. So it feels like she has decided on her own that I’m on her side.

I see. When you say “fixated,” does that mean you feel like you’d like to put some distance between yourself and that sensitive mom? Are you thinking that, like the other two moms, you don’t want to take either side?

Hmm... I was closest with that sensitive mom. She’s just very serious, and she isn’t a bad person at her core. She’s simply someone who loves her child very, very much. So I guess she ends up being equally strict with other people’s children too. And also, maybe the way she communicates is wrong... But people around her often call her “dangerous” or “not okay”... and I feel like I want to distance myself... but somehow, I can’t quite take that step... Because I know her good side too, I feel like I can’t just cut it off so cleanly.
I can really feel how kind you are, Shi-mama. Since she was the person you were closest with, do you think you might be able to share your own thoughts with that sensitive mom?

Because we were the closest, I feel sad that things have become like this. Hmm... I have gently told her things like, “There are people with all kinds of ways of thinking,” and, “Just because you think something is right doesn’t mean the other person feels the same way. Even if it really is justice.” But she said, “But, you know, my child was hurt, right? Those kids’ way of speaking is awful, and their personalities are harsh, so my child is always the only victim. Even if there are different ways of thinking, I don’t think it’s okay to hurt someone!! That’s why I’ve decided to stop forgiving them!”

Yes. I see. When you shared your thoughts with her, she told you she had “decided to stop forgiving them.” Listening to what you’ve shared so far, two options came to mind. Would it be okay if I talk about them?

That’s right. She’s the kind of person who often says, “But,” or “But, you know!” so the people around her also feel like they don’t want to talk anymore. She cuts off my opinions too, lol. Thank you. Please go ahead.

Thank you. I’ll summarize them, so please give me a moment. Sorry for the wait. The first option is to continue listening without denying her, as you have been. The benefit is that you can keep relating to someone you were close to and still have feelings for, in the way you are now. The downside is that it will continue to place a burden on your own feelings, Shi-mama. The second option is to clearly tell her something like, “I understand that you can’t forgive them, but it’s painful for me to keep listening to this topic, so I’d like you to stop.” If she doesn’t stop, it may be okay to put some distance between you. The benefit is that the burden on your feelings may become lighter. The downside is that you may end up falling out with the sensitive mom.

I see...! That’s amazing. It’s easy to understand. So it’s about thinking through the pros and cons. I do feel like... the first suggestion you gave me fits best for now. It’s possible that the downside may become bigger over time and become a burden, so when that happens, I think I can consider the second option you told me about!

I see! That sounds wonderful. When you have a next plan—if this doesn’t work, then I’ll do this—I think it can help you stay calm too. I support the decision you’ve made, Shi-mama!! I hope your kindness and the care you feel for the mom you were close with reach her.
Thank you（；＿；）She has helped me before too, so I feel like I want to calmly think again about what I should do now! Thank you for sharing so many thoughts with me!

Thank you as well for sharing such an important situation with me. I’ll be rooting for you, Shi-mama, and hoping that things ahead become even better for you!! I’ll end the consultation here, if that’s alright with you.
Yes! I’ll keep trying! If something comes up again, please listen...! Thank you for today ⭐︎ It’s okay to end here!
Yes, if anything happens, please feel free to come here anytime. Thank you for today.

interaction.content: Good evening. Thank you for being here today.
Good evening. Thank you for meeting with me.
Thank you. I’ll let you know when it’s time, so please wait just a little while.
Understood.
Good evening. I’m the counselor. Thank you for coming to talk with me today. To start, could you tell me your age and gender?
Good evening. I’m 25, female.
Thank you. What would you like to talk about today?
How should I put it... maybe because of COVID, I just can’t feel motivated to do various things.
I see... COVID really doesn’t seem like it’s settling down, does it. For example, what kinds of things are you finding it hard to feel motivated about?
That’s right. I don’t know when it’ll settle down, and I feel anxious too... Mainly work, I guess. And also things around the house, like housework, feel a little more bothersome than before.
I see, so it feels like that with both work and housework...

Yes. People around me are all trying so hard and doing what they’re supposed to, but I’m the only one like this, and I start thinking maybe I’m no good, and then I fall into self-disgust and my mood drops again. It’s a vicious cycle, isn’t it.
I see... It feels to you like the people around you are doing their best...
Yes.

It makes sense that if you compare yourself to others and feel like you’re the only one who can’t do things, you would feel that way. Specifically, what kinds of things do you feel you haven’t been able to do?
(I’m sorry, it seems the connection wasn’t working well, and I just received the message now.)
(Oh, I see. I’m sorry about that.)

(No, I’m sorry too.) That’s right. It’s not exactly that I’m not able to do things, but even though the amount of work hasn’t changed, I feel more tired than before. Like my mood has been low all the time.
I see, so you feel more tired than before. And you also feel like your mood has been low.
Yes. I guess it feels like there’s nothing to look forward to.
I see... When you’re tired, it really is hard to feel motivated, and it can feel like you don’t have that sense of purpose or excitement.
That’s true. Before COVID, even if I felt down or tired, I think I recovered a little faster... I can’t see my friends, and we can’t go out drinking, so maybe stress is building up.

That makes sense. Before, you were able to release stress by going out for drinks with friends and things like that. By the way, at the moment, are you not able to see or talk with your friends at all?
Yes. I liked going out with friends and going drinking with people from work. Also, my hobby was things like karaoke, so now it feels hard to go. I have talked a little remotely.
So there are times when you can talk remotely. But not being able to meet in person or sing your heart out at karaoke to let off steam is hard, isn’t it.
Yes. Exactly! I end up thinking it’s just not the same as seeing people in person.
That’s true. By the way, how are you distracting yourself or taking your mind off things now?
I haven’t found any hobbies I can do at home, so I’m just kind of getting through it. Oh, but I do listen to music.
I see, so there’s music you like.
Yes. There’s an artist I like, and before, I used to go to their concerts too.
I see... Concerts are difficult now too, aren’t they.
Yes... There aren’t any big events, so maybe the reason is that I can’t feel like, “I’ll work hard and look forward to that!”
That may be it. Up until now, you were able to work hard by having something to aim for, but now it’s hard to see any prospects, so it feels like you can’t really get fired up about anything.
Yes. I think that’s probably the reason.
I see, that’s how it feels to you. Would it be okay if I summarized what we’ve talked about so far?
Yes, please.
All right, I’ll try to summarize, so please give me a moment.
Okay.

Because of COVID, perhaps, you haven’t been able to engage with various things with motivation. You don’t know when it will settle down, and you also feel anxious. People around you look like they’re doing their best, and that makes your mood drop as you wonder whether you’re no good. Until now, you used to relieve stress by seeing friends, going out drinking, and doing karaoke. And you were able to work hard while looking forward to going to events for an artist you like, but you can’t do that either now. Does that sound right?
Yes. That’s right.
Thank you.
What should I do...?
Until you’re able to go to events again, it would be good if you could find something that helps you feel a little more energized.
That’s true. Do you have any recommendations for ways to spend time at home? lol

Let’s see... For example, if you’re feeling tired, it might be good to try something that engages your senses. For instance, enjoying scents, or music is of course good too. And moving your body a little might also be effective.

I hadn’t thought of scents! If I put on music I like and stretch, that does seem like it would help me relax. Even if there aren’t any events, if I do it every night before bed, it might be a nice change of pace.
Mm-hmm, yes, that sounds good. While you’re doing that, if you focus on it as much as you can, even for a short time, you may be able to step away from those anxious feelings.
That’s true... There are so many kinds of scents, and it sounds fun to find one I like.

Yes, I think so. Please try out different things. And once COVID settles down, I think you’ll be able to work hard at various things again while looking forward to events. How was it talking here today?

Thank you. I really hope it settles down soon. Until then, I’ll try to keep going while looking for ways to refresh myself. I felt like you understood my anxious feelings. I feel like maybe I can try to enjoy my time at home too, and I think I feel a little more positive.
I’m glad if your feelings have become even a little more positive.
Yes, thank you very much.
Let’s both do our best until things settle down. Well then, would it be all right to end today’s consultation here?
Yes, and please take care of yourself too. It’s okay to end.
Thank you for your kind words. Then we’ll end here.
Thank you very much. Goodbye.
(Thank you for your time. Goodbye.)
