interaction.content: (Thank you for being here today. We’ll begin when it’s time.)
(Thank you. Understood.)
Hello, I’m the counselor. Thank you for coming in to talk. To start, could you tell me your age, gender, and what you’d like to discuss?
Hello. Thank you. I’m 25, male. My girlfriend, who I’m currently dating, keeps doing things that trouble me, and I don’t know what I should do.
I see, that’s what you’ve been struggling with. Could you tell me specifically what kinds of things she does that trouble you?

Yes. For example, she’s stood me up on dates over and over, or she says she’s going to die and sends me a photo of a cut wrist, and when I call her it turns out to be a lie and it was an image from the internet. She does a lot of things that make me worry.
I see. In that kind of situation, it must feel like you’re being pulled around by her, and that would be really troubling… How have you been responding to her about this?
I got angry. I told her it makes me worry, and it’s a burden, so I want her to stop.
That makes sense. I think it’s natural to feel that way. How does your girlfriend respond to that?
At the time she seemed sorry, but in the end she does it again.
I see. That would make it hard to know what to do. When did your girlfriend start doing these kinds of things?
A few weeks after we started dating, the troubling behaviors started coming out little by little.
I see. So it was around the time when a sense of trust was gradually starting to develop, perhaps. Could you tell me how you feel about your girlfriend right now?
Well, I do like her and I want to keep dating her as things are, but if it seems like this won’t get better, I think breaking up might be okay too.
So that’s how it feels. You still have feelings for her and want to continue the relationship. But if this situation continues, you also feel you may want to break up. Is that right?
Yes, that’s right.
How long has this situation been going on, and does it feel like it’s getting worse and worse?
It’s been going on for about eight months. It is getting worse.

That has become quite a long period of time. I can imagine that right now, you’re in a very difficult situation. During that time, has your girlfriend ever talked to you about any worries, problems, or things she wanted to discuss?
There have been various things. She’s said there’s no point in living, and that she hates her job.
I see. When she says there’s no point in living, does it seem like there’s any specific reason for that?

We talked about a lot of things, but I couldn’t really understand it. She said things like, because she isn’t beautiful, because she isn’t needed, because her boss hates her. But she also says there isn’t really any basis, or particular reason, for it.
I see. It sounds like your girlfriend herself is putting herself down. It may be that she has gone through hardships in her upbringing.
That may be true. Her parents divorced, and it seems she was raised by her mother alone.
I see. Given your girlfriend’s situation, I get the sense that if things stay as they are, it may become too much for you, being by her side, to take in all on your own. How does that feel to you?
Yes. That’s why I think I’m also considering breaking up.

It sounds like you’re in a place of a lot of uncertainty. And if things stay this way, it seems your feelings about breaking up may become stronger. So, let me summarize a little here. In response to your girlfriend’s worsening troubling behaviors, you still have feelings for her, but over a long period of time you’ve become exhausted and unsure how to handle it or what to do. Does that sound right so far?
That’s exactly right.
And if things continue like this, it’s very hard on you as well, and you’re beginning to consider breaking up.
Yes.
And that’s what brought you here to talk with us. You’re feeling that you’d like to make those unsettled feelings clearer. How does that sound?
Yes. I mean, rather than wanting to make things clear, I want to know how to get her to stop the troubling behaviors.
I see. So it’s about wanting to stop the behavior. In that case,
Yes.

Considering her upbringing, it seems likely that your girlfriend is carrying some things, but has she ever gone anywhere to talk with someone about her mental or emotional state? I wondered if it might be good for her to have a place like that.
I don’t think so. I’ve never heard her mention counseling or anything like that. That does make sense.

I see. Then, taking this as an opportunity, if it’s not too difficult, suggesting counseling, a consultation center, or a mental health clinic—somewhere she can talk and get support—may be one option. What do you think?
I think that’s good. I’ll suggest it to her.
I see. I’m glad to hear that. Given how your girlfriend seems right now, I felt it would be very difficult for you to carry this all on your own.
Thank you.
Not at all. If you still care about your girlfriend and want to support her, then all the more, I think it may be good to get help from a third party.
Yes. I was struggling to somehow deal with it by myself. Relying on someone is important too.

Yes. Even though she is someone important to you, there are limits to carrying this alone for as long as eight months. I felt it might be good if you could tell her that because she is important to you, you want to help her. We’re almost out of time, but were you able to talk about what you wanted to?
Yes. I’ll try talking to her. Thank you.
I’m rooting for you and your girlfriend to build a better relationship. If anything else comes up that you’re struggling with or would like to talk about, please feel free to come here anytime.
Yes. Thank you very much.
Thank you as well. (Thank you for today. Is it alright if we end here?)
(Thank you as well. Yes. That’s fine.)
(Then we’ll end here. Sorry to trouble you, but please leave a rating.)

interaction.content: Good evening. Thank you for being here today. When it’s time, I’ll go ahead and begin from here.
Good evening. Thank you for having me.
Good evening. I’m the counselor. Thank you for coming in for a consultation today. To start, could you tell me your age, gender, and what you’d like to talk about today?

Thank you. I’m a man in my 40s. I’d like to talk about my relationship with my supervisor at work. There’s a supervisor who is strict only with me... He isn’t like that with the other employees. I guess you could say he treats me differently...
Thank you. I see. That sounds really difficult. So he acts differently toward the other employees.
Yes, that’s right. He’s strict only with me. His attitude toward the other employees is kind, especially toward the women.
How can such unfairness be okay? He’s especially kind toward the women... What kind of work are you doing now?

Yes, I do feel it’s unfair. I think he probably just doesn’t like me. I do office work, mainly using the computer and answering phones. My current department is understaffed, and that supervisor pushes an uneven amount of work onto only me.
Thank you. I see. Was there anything that might have triggered him to dislike you?

On top of that, when I can’t get the work done, he nitpicks and says things like, “Do it properly,” or “What are you doing?” His attitude is really bad. Something that might have made him dislike me...? Hmm, I wonder what it could be.
He’s doing such awful things so openly. That must be really painful.
Yes, that’s right. I feel like it’s probably because there was a time when I pushed back against that supervisor a little...
Pushed back... Could it be that you were simply expressing your own opinion?

Yes, that’s right. It’s not like I said anything bad about him. We just had a slight difference in thinking, and I only shared my opinion about that. Also, I think the biggest reason is that our personalities just don’t match.

I see. Personality... Even while enduring such a harsh and cold attitude from your supervisor, you’ve been doing your best at work. I imagine it must be truly difficult. In today’s consultation, what would be most helpful for us to talk about?

Thank you. I do think I’ve been trying my best, but... if anything, maybe the reason is that I’m the gloomy type who doesn’t really go along with the mood. The other employees respond to that supervisor in a more upbeat way, so maybe that’s why he likes them. From that supervisor’s point of view, I think I seem hard to approach and like I’m being defiant. Yes... I’d like him to treat me equally with the other employees, and to be able to work peacefully. That would be the ideal.
That’s how you’ve been feeling. How are your relationships with the other employees?
Well, if anything, I guess I feel a bit out of place... I do feel a sense of isolation somehow.
I see. Being on your own like that must make you feel quite anxious. So is there no one around you that you can talk to about this?
There are a few employees I get along with... But it’s a large organization, so it does feel hard to fit in. As for the supervisor, I can’t really talk to anyone about that.
I see. So you do have some coworkers you get along with. How about your family?
Even if I say we get along, it’s not like we have a very close relationship. I live away from my family. I live alone... and I’m single.
I see. Thank you for telling me. So you’ve been worrying about this on your own until now. I imagine it must have been very painful.
Yes, there isn’t really anyone I can talk to... so I’ve been kind of brooding over it.
That must have been really hard. You can talk about anything here, so please feel free to share without holding back.
Yes, thank you.
You’ve been carrying stress from work. How has your physical health been?

Well, yes, my supervisor is cold toward me, but maybe the issue is also that there’s distance between me and the other employees. As for my health, there are times when I can’t sleep. I can’t get up in the morning. Also, my stomach and intestines get upset, and I have headaches and stiff shoulders too. I guess it might be stress after all.
I see. That’s concerning.
My doctor has prescribed me medication, and I take it sometimes.
I see. So you’re taking medication as well. First of all, I hope your body can recover.
Yes, thank you. Even if I take the medicine, it may only help a little, though.
You mentioned that there aren’t many people around you whom you can talk to. What do you think would be good to do from here?
I’m starting to feel that maybe my current job just isn’t suited to me after all... So I’ve begun to think that it might be okay to start considering another job soon.
That’s how you’re feeling. You’re beginning to think about finding an environment that suits you better.
Maybe I’ve been trying too hard to force myself to stay there for a long time. Yes, I’ve started thinking that I probably need to reevaluate my environment.
Mm-hmm, mm-hmm, yes. I imagine you’ve been working really hard on your own for quite some time.

Do you think so? Hearing you say that makes me feel kind of relieved. I’ve devoted myself to this company for 20 years. I’ve never changed jobs or anything like that. But I do think maybe it’s time to change my environment.

You’ve endured it for that long. I think that’s truly admirable. Listening to what you’ve shared so far, I think your supervisor’s behavior clearly may be power harassment. It seems like a malicious pattern of targeting an individual. It is absolutely not acceptable.
Yes, he treats the other employees kindly and not harshly, but only me. I feel, even myself, that he’s taking advantage of my vulnerability. I’m definitely being targeted.
If you decide to continue in your current job, I recommend consulting with a labor union or a similar organization.
I did consider that, at least... but I’m anxious that if I consult someone, he’ll find out that I did.
I see. You’re worried that it will get out. However, you are an important person. I think a firm response is necessary in order to protect yourself.

But through today’s consultation, I’m starting to think that maybe I don’t have to keep putting up with it after all. Yes, if I ruin my health, then it’s all for nothing. I’m starting to feel that I want to think in the direction of not just enduring it, but asserting myself or changing my environment.
Thank you. I’m also glad to hear that your thoughts have become more forward-looking. We’ve talked through quite a bit up to now. How are you feeling?
Thank you as well. Somehow I feel like I can become more positive. I’d also like to consult with you again afterward.
I believe you will surely be able to get through the painful things ahead. I’ll be here supporting you as well.
That makes me very happy. Thank you so much.
Our time is up. Thank you very much for coming to talk with me today. Please come back anytime. I’ll be here.
Thank you very much. I look forward to talking with you again.
Thank you for today. I learned a lot. Thank you for your time. We’ll end here for today.
Thank you as well. Thank you for your time.

interaction.content: (Good evening. Thank you for meeting with me today.)
(Good evening. Thank you.)
Good evening. Thank you for coming in to talk with me today. To start, could you tell me your gender, age, and what you’d like to discuss?
Good evening, thank you. I’m a woman in my 40s, and what I want to talk about is that I’m having trouble finding a job.
Thank you. So you’re having trouble finding a job. How long has it been since you’ve been looking?

At the end of March this year, the part-time workplace I’d been at suspended operations, and it had been a pretty heavy environment, so for my next job I thought, I want an environment where I can do what I want to do! Maybe my hopes got too high, but since April I’ve considered about 20 companies, had interviews, and tried working a little, but it wasn’t what I imagined. Right now I’m doing contract work and registered with temp agencies, and somehow managing to secure the minimum income I need.

Your previous part-time job was really heavy, then... I see. It’s hard when you’re looking for an easier place to work, but it still doesn’t match your ideal. You’re somehow managing to secure income and so on, but would it be right to say that you want to work as a full-time employee in an environment that feels comfortable to work in?

I’m kind of thinking I may be done with working in organizations. I want to build my skills and raise my hourly wage, but the reality isn’t like that... I’m not thinking about full-time employment for now, and while my child is still little, for about two more years, I think 4 to 5 hours on-site is enough. I don’t really want to work 8-hour days...
You’re feeling that reality just doesn’t go that smoothly. Yes. When you think about your child too, working 8 hours is quite a lot.

Where I was until last year, I worked about 70 hours a month and was able to earn just under the dependent income limit, so I started thinking I want at least that level, or to raise my hourly wage more and earn enough to be outside the dependent category. It may sound like a privileged kind of problem, but... I’ve been feeling more and more strongly that I want to make better use of myself and create that kind of environment. But I know I’d probably come to hate working within the fixed 8-hour full-time framework. Sorry, this is just complaining...
I get the sense that you’re thinking both for your family and for yourself. So, over these next two years, are you hoping to build your skills and raise your hourly wage even a little?
Yes. Like, I’d like to increase the amount of work I can do from home, too. This is just me complaining, but I kind of want you to hear it.
It certainly sounds exhausting to manage childcare and the household while also working a full 8 hours. What happened?
The other day, there was a company where I thought, this is it! They offered an hourly wage I hadn’t seen before, so I thought I could build my skills, had an interview, and got hired, but...
Yes.

The first job they gave me wasn’t work to be doing at that hourly wage. I’m a nurse, but they told me it would be as a housekeeper. I just couldn’t accept it, and in the end I turned it down... I feel like I ended up being someone with too much pride who’s hard to work with, like I was being looked down on, and I just can’t stop feeling unsettled and irritated. What do you think?

I see. Yes, being told it’s as a housekeeper does seem like it would become a completely different kind of job. I felt that it would move further and further away from the kind of work you had in mind. So that irritation comes up for you. Does that mean you worked at that workplace for a little while and then left?

Right... I do want to keep living as a nurse, but if I only do on-site work, it won’t connect to where I want to be 20 or 30 years from now, so I’m searching right now. I turned down the first housekeeping job they requested, and I’ve been getting some one-off nursery school nurse work a few times a month, and I started that this month. Since it’s contract work, I’m treated as self-employed. So I’m working that alongside temp work.
You said you’re searching—do you mean work as a nurse that isn’t on-site work? I see. So even though it’s one-off work, you started this month.

Yes. I think it could be something else, too. I don’t know, I want to change the negative image people have of nurses. The ideals I’m holding up have gotten too big, and I’m getting tired from the gap between that and my current reality.
Is it a little difficult to reply right now?
I’m okay. Did you ask me something? Sorry!
I’m relieved to hear back from you. I’ll send it again.
Yes, sorry.
Earlier you said you’re searching, but as a nurse, going forward, do you mean you want to do something other than on-site work?
Yes, that’s right. For now, having on-site work be about half of what I do feels just right.

Thank you. So you feel that, for now, the amount of on-site work you have is about right. Other than on-site work, is there anything in particular you’d like to do? I mean, if it were something outside on-site work.

Yes. I considered four companies in the education field too and was hired by two of them, but the hourly wage wouldn’t really go up, and I could picture myself feeling frustrated a few years down the line, so I stopped. It feels like, within the organizations and jobs that exist now, there really isn’t much that matches my ideal...
I see. It’s hard to find something that matches your ideal, isn’t it... How is the atmosphere at your current workplace, and how easy is it to work there?

Yes, exactly. Somehow, the things I could do in my 20s, thinking I was just training and throwing myself into it, now have become things I can’t do, won’t do, don’t want to do. For now, I like the nursery school because it’s soothing. As for the company itself, it feels like they have nurses work as housekeepers, so I’m taking a step back and just watching for now.
I see... I wonder if feeling that way is also influenced by how easy the workplace is to work in, the atmosphere, and so on... I understand. So you’re taking a wait-and-see approach.

If housekeepers, care workers, and nurses were all treated at the same hourly wage, and there were a culture of interprofessional collaboration where each person’s strengths were used, I could accept that, but it doesn’t seem to be that way. It was pretty shocking not to be treated as a nurse... This feeling of not being able to get past my pride... am I being naive?

I see. There are parts that feel especially unacceptable to you. Is it being treated as a housekeeper, I wonder... Since you’re a nurse, I can understand that not being treated as a nurse would feel upsetting.
Yes, I wasn’t needed as a nurse, and the instruction was basically to just go make meals. I couldn’t help thinking, does it really have to be me?!

Yes. So the situation is that nurse-like work isn’t being assigned to you... Even so, the fact that you feel soothed by the children at the nursery school, and that you’ve been able to create a source that helps you keep going, makes me feel that you are still facing forward. How does that feel to you?

But apparently they introduce me to the places I visit as a nurse. A nurse coming to make meals just feels off somehow. If I were the client, I’d feel like, is this nurse working as a housekeeper because she couldn’t work as a nurse? The nursery school is something I’m hopeful about, and I do think I’ll keep trying there. It’s about time, isn’t it. I’m sorry today was just me complaining the whole time.
Yes, I imagine there’s anxiety about how people around you might see it, too. It is about time. How was it for you to talk up to this point?
Yes, this was the first time I tried venting like this... I don’t exactly feel refreshed, but thank you for listening.
Thank you. I imagine there are still parts you didn’t get to say. Please do come talk again.
Yes, thank you. (Thank you.)
(Thank you. I’d appreciate it if you could also leave an evaluation.)

interaction.content: (Hello, thank you for being here today.)
(Hello. Thank you.)
Hello, I’m the counselor. Please tell me your age, gender, and what you’d like to talk about.
16 female I don’t want to go to school
I see. That sounds really hard. What kinds of things make you feel like you don’t want to go?
It’s a hassle
I see. What grade are you in?
First year of high school
Thank you for answering. Even though it feels like a hassle, are you going to school right now?
Yes
I see. I imagine you’re doing your best to go. When did you start feeling like it was a hassle?
Right after I started school
I see. So you’ve been feeling that way since around April. Could you tell me what was going on around that time?
Nothing in particular
I see. When you say you started feeling right away after entering school that it was a hassle, was it something like it wasn’t a school you wanted to go to? How do you feel about it?
I didn’t really care what school it was
I see. Who are you living with in your family right now?
My parents
So it’s you and your parents, the three of you. How do you usually spend time with your family?
Normal
I see. Do you communicate with your parents?
I think it’s normal. I don’t talk much with my dad
I see. How do you feel about not talking much with your dad?
I don’t really think anything of it
I see. Have you talked to your parents or friends or anyone about not wanting to go to school?
No
I see. Do you feel like there isn’t anyone around you who you can talk to?
Yes
I see. It feels like you may have been carrying this on your own for a long time. What is it that makes it hard to talk to someone about it?
I don’t click with everyone when we talk
I see. When you don’t click in conversation, you may have felt lonely. What do you think?
It’s not exactly lonely, more like tiring. A hassle
I see. When it’s tiring, it can start to feel like a hassle too. Do you feel like you don’t want to go to school because you don’t click with people there?
Yes
Spending all that time not clicking with people may be really exhausting. I think you’re still doing your best to go, but how do you feel about it?
I don’t know. Everyone goes

I see. There may be things you don’t understand yourself either. Since your feelings of not wanting to go are strong enough that you came here to talk, I feel that must be painful. What do you think is the biggest reason it feels like such a hassle?
It’s a hassle to match what my friends talk about. Clothes and makeup and stuff. I don’t care
I see. So you’re not interested in clothes or makeup. What kinds of conversations with everyone would make you want to go to school?
I don’t know. I don’t know what kind of things would be fun to talk about
I see. Are you unsure how to communicate with others?
I don’t know. I’ve never really been able to make close friends. How can I?
I see. What would a close friend be like for you?
A friend I can say whatever I’m thinking to, someone I don’t get tired being with, someone I feel happy with
I see. You want a close friend. Do you feel like you can’t make one from here on?
I couldn’t before, so I don’t know what to do to make one
How have you felt up until now about not being able to make close friends?
Lonely. Maybe I’m weird. Even when I talk with everyone, it’s not fun
So that’s how you’ve been feeling. You’ve been carrying loneliness all this time. I think it’s natural not to feel happy when conversations with friends don’t click.
Everyone else looks like they’re having fun talking, but I’m the only one forcing it. It’s always like that
I see. Being there may feel really exhausting. Even in that kind of situation, you keep going to school. I feel that you’re mentally independent. How do you feel about that?
I wonder if I’m independent... I don’t know. I just go to school because I have to.

That’s how you feel. The fact that you go to school feels very grown-up to me. I don’t think you’re weird even if you don’t click with people. You’ve shared a lot with me so far. How do you feel after talking up to this point?
Thank you for listening to me.
Thank you for sharing so much with me. I think there may have been things you weren’t able to talk about too. Please let me hear from you again. I’d like to end here for today.
Thank you very much.
(Thank you for your time. I’d appreciate your advice. I’ll send the closing message.)
(Thank you very much. Yes, please.)

interaction.content: Hello. I’m a counselor. Thank you for coming in for a consultation. To start, could you tell me your gender and age range, and what I should call you?
Yes, thank you. I’m a 27-year-old woman, and my name is Rena. Thank you.
Rena, then. It’s nice to meet you. What would you like to talk about today?
Yes, three years ago I married for love, to a young employee who worked at the same company as me.
I see. And what happened after that?
In the first year after we got married, I became pregnant and left the company.
Yes.
After that I was busy with childcare, but my husband is busy with work and often comes home late at night, and he works on weekends too.
I see... (Since you’re on your phone, it’s better if I wait a little longer, right?)
Recently, my husband and I don’t talk much anymore, and I’ve been feeling kind of depressed, so I asked to speak with a counselor. Thank you.
I see. You’re not used to childcare yet, and your husband isn’t able to help... That must be really exhausting.
That’s right.
When there isn’t much conversation, it can feel like you don’t get a chance to refresh yourself, too. When you say you’ve been feeling kind of depressed, what kinds of things have you been feeling?
It’s my first time raising a child, so I’m anxious, and on top of that my husband comes home late, so instead of feeling happy, it feels like every day is filled with anxiety.

I see, yes... It’s your first time raising a child, after all... You’d want to talk with your husband about all kinds of things, wouldn’t you... Do you have any friends or family nearby you can talk to about childcare?
We live in an apartment building, so I don’t have friends around, and going outside has started to feel like too much trouble.
I see... So it’s an environment where it’s hard to get a change of pace?
Yes,
That sounds painful... Has it been like that ever since your child was born?
Yes, I don’t really see many young people either, so I’m inside the apartment most of the time.
I see... You live in an area where there aren’t many younger people. You said your husband is busy with work, but since your child was born, how has he been with the child?
Maybe the younger people are out at work during the day?
I see.
When the baby was born, he would come home from work early, but lately he’s so busy he barely even has days off.
He’s that busy... Then it sounds like it’s hard to find time to talk things over about different things.
It feels like we don’t have time to slowly separate— I mean, to talk.
(Yes.) I see, you want him to be the first person you can talk to about fun things, and to listen to what you’re struggling with, right? (I meant “listen.”)
Yes, if we could do that, I think I’d feel a little better.
That makes sense... Raising a child on your own is really hard. You’ve been working so hard. Rena, how do you feel about your husband right now?
I do understand that he’s working really hard for the family, without even having time to rest, but...
Mm-hmm. Is it that you’d like him to make a little more time to talk with you?

Even on his days off, he says he has work and leaves the house, but... I start feeling strange, like, “Is it really work?” Sometimes I know I’m overthinking it, and that makes me feel even more anxious.

I see... He’s so busy that he hardly has any days off, so when he goes out on a day off, you start having doubts, like, “Is it really work?” And because the time you have to talk has decreased, it makes you even more anxious.
I know I’m overthinking it, but...
Mm-hmm. Since you’re often at home with just your child, once you start thinking, it may be easy to end up overthinking things.
That’s right.
Have you ever tried telling your husband that you’re raising the child mostly on your own, and that sometimes it gets exhausting and you end up overthinking all kinds of things?
I have sometimes, but my husband says he doesn’t know what to do, and I think being caught between work and me makes it hard for him too, so right now we don’t really talk much.
I see, that’s how it is. Because you’re thinking of your husband, it feels like you can’t talk to him about it... That’s painful... You said your husband is busy with work, but how does he seem?
It seems like he wants to rest, but can’t. I just hope he doesn’t hurt his health. Sometimes I think I’d like to go back to my parents’ home for a little while and rest too.
I see. That would make you worry about your husband’s health too... That sounds like a good idea to me, but would it be difficult? By that, I mean the idea of going back to your parents’ home.
It’s about an hour by car.
In that case, how would it be to go back to your parents’ home? I imagine your parents would be happy too.
I should let them see their grandchild once in a while.
Mm-hmm.
But because of COVID right now, maybe it would be hard to go to my parents’ home. If I passed it on to the elderly, that would be terrible. Am I overthinking again?
I see... It’s understandable that you’d worry about that... So even though they live nearby, you’re feeling that it’s hard to have them watch your child and things like that.
Lately it’s been like this, and I’m always overthinking things.

It may be because you’re tired in many ways. You’re doing your best to raise your child on your own, and I do think it would be good if you had a chance to let your own body rest a little. Would a babysitter or temporary childcare not be possible? Or is it that COVID still worries you?
I’ve been looking, but because of COVID, I haven’t been able to find anything easily.
I see. So you’ve been looking already. When you can’t find anything, that kind of thing can make you feel more pressured too. By the way, what do your parents think about all of this?

My parents have said they want to come check on me, but because of COVID, it feels like they can’t really move around much. Just having you listen to how I feel now, and feeling a little understood, has made me feel better. I think I can keep going a little.
I see. I’m glad your feelings have eased even a little. I’m sorry, but our consultation time is almost up. Were you able to talk about what you wanted to talk about?
If I’m struggling again, please listen to me. Thank you for today. Gassho.

Yes, I’m glad to hear that. You’re raising your child on your own, and I think there will be times when you get tired. I hope you can find an opportunity to rest yourself. I really do think you’re working very hard. I also hope that maybe by taking a COVID test or something like that and reducing your anxiety, it might become possible for someone to help watch your child. Please think about that too. Thank you very much for today.
I understand. Thank you very much. Gassho.

interaction.content: (Hello. Thank you for being here today. We’ll begin at 10 o’clock. Thank you.)
Thank you.
Hello. I’m the counselor. Thank you for coming in for a consultation today. To start, could you tell me your age, gender, and what you’d like to talk about?
Hello. I’m 40, male. What I want to talk about is that I’m unsure whether or not to quit my company.
Thank you for answering. I’d like to ask a bit more in detail—what has been going on with your current company?
I have to move because my child is going on to school, but from where we’ll be, I won’t be able to commute to my current workplace.
I see. In that kind of situation, I imagine you must be feeling very distressed. When was it decided that your child would be going on to that school?
It was decided on January 5th.
I see. Thank you for answering. So over this past week, you’ve been struggling while carrying these painful feelings. How did you feel when your child’s school plans were decided?
I was happy that my child got in. They got into the school they wanted.

Mm-hmm. Because you care so much about your child, I think it’s natural that you’re struggling over your current company and your child’s schooling. Have you talked about this with your partner or anyone else?
I got divorced five years ago, so I don’t have a partner. I haven’t talked to anyone about it.

Mm-hmm, I see. So while it was very happy news that your child got into the school they wanted, from April it will be difficult for you to commute to your current company. Because you’ve been balancing parenting and work on your own, I imagine this must have left you feeling very confused. How does that sound to you?
Yes. I want to do what I can for my child.
Mm-hmm, of course. I think that feeling comes from having raised your child on your own while balancing work for the past five years. Have you talked with your child about life from April onward?
We have talked. My child said they’ll probably be busy with club activities and won’t be able to manage everyday things on their own, so they want me to live with them.

I see. Thank you for answering. Your child chose the school they wanted because they really want to work hard at their club activities, and they were accepted. So all the more, they’re talking with you from a place of trust between parent and child, wanting you to support them. I think that’s truly wonderful. I imagine that’s why you’re struggling with the work situation, but does that mean you haven’t consulted anyone at the company yet?
I talked to my direct section manager.
Mm-hmm, I see. How was it when you talked to your section manager?
The section manager was overwhelmed with his own things, and he told me, ‘I guess you’ll just have to decide for yourself.’

Thank you for answering. Even though you worked up the courage to talk about your current situation, your supervisor responded that way, and I imagine that left you feeling really at a loss. How did you feel?
I’m unsure what I should do. If I quit, there’s my child’s tuition and our living expenses to think about.

Mm-hmm, of course. You’ve raised your precious child on your own all this time, and now that they’ve been accepted into the school they wanted, I think it’s very natural to want to let them move forward in the way they hope. And of course, you also have to think about living expenses and tuition. Some time has passed since you spoke with your supervisor—have you thought about anything regarding what to do from here?
I have.
Mm-hmm, I see. Would you be able to talk about whatever you’ve been thinking during that time, starting with whatever feels okay to share?
I can.
Thank you. What kinds of things have you been thinking about?

Changing jobs to a workplace near my child’s school. Transferring within my current company to a branch near my child’s school. Having my child live in a boarding arrangement. Those are the three things I’ve thought of.

Thank you for answering. Because you’re thinking seriously about your child, you’ve been considering different possibilities, and I feel you are a very sincere parent. Are you thinking of narrowing it down to these three options?
For now, these are the options I can think of, and I’d like it if there were some better option.
Mm-hmm, I see. When there are a lot of options, it can feel confusing, and I imagine you may feel rushed. At this point, which option do you feel might be the best for you?
Well, yes. I think it would be good if I could transfer within my current company.
I see. Thank you for answering. Since your child’s life is involved too, a transfer within your current company would be the best option. Is there anything you can tell the company about that?
Even when I talk to the section manager, he won’t really take it up and says I probably can’t do something so self-centered, so I’m not sure what to do.

Mm-hmm, I see. Being told something like that would leave you feeling at a loss. I feel that this is by no means something self-centered. Situations are always changing. In that situation, is there anyone other than the section manager you could talk to? For example, a coworker you’re close with, or a former supervisor, if there’s someone like that…
I’d like to talk to the branch manager, who is above him, but if I go over the section manager’s head and talk to him, I’ll be told, ‘Why didn’t you tell me first?’
Mm-hmm, I see. That would make you feel rushed and unsettled. Does that mean you’ve had that kind of experience before, after talking to the branch manager about something?
I have.

I see. That must have been painful for you. By the way, I imagine there are procedures for your child’s enrollment as well. How much time do you have before you need to make a final decision? Or, since it involves a transfer, do you need to decide right away?
I’m thinking I’d like to decide on housing by March and be ready to live there.

I see. Since it’s March, there is still a little time, but if the situation is that you need to decide very soon, I imagine you feel rushed. To change the current situation, realistically, I think you may need to take some action. For example, asking the section manager to set aside time to sit down with you and hear you out again, or, though it may take a bit of courage, talking to the branch manager for the sake of your child’s wishes could be one option. How does that sound?
Yes. I’ll try telling the section manager that I want to consult the branch manager about this. Thank you.

Mm-hmm, yes. I think it may take a bit of courage, but I mentioned it because taking a small step for the sake of your child having a wonderful life may be a good thing to try. I’m sorry to interrupt while we’re still talking, but our consultation time is almost coming to an end. How has it been for you to talk up to this point?
I was unsure what to do, but for now I’ve found a way to start taking action and move forward. Thank you very much.

Thank you. I think this consultation came from how carefully you’ve thought about your child’s life, after living together with your child all this time. I think you still have a little time. Please take care of your own health as well while thinking about your child. I was able to hear something very important from you today. Thank you. I’d like to end the consultation here.
Thank you very much.
(Thank you. You did well today.)

interaction.content: Hello. I'm a mental trainer. Today's topic is mental training for romantic relationships.
Hello. Actually, one month before the wedding, he broke off our engagement, saying he couldn't marry me after all.
Thank you for reaching out. Oh... I see. With it being one month before the wedding, that must be really painful.
Yes. My mind just went completely blank...
Mm-hmm, mm-hmm. That must have been such a shock. I think it's completely understandable that your mind went blank. Could you tell me a bit more about the situation?
Yes. When I asked him the reason, he said it was my “appearance.” I do think I gained weight over these four years.
I see.
So I went on a diet for two weeks. And then I told him I wanted to see him and talk, and we met just once.
You really worked hard on the diet too. Mm-hmm. What were you able to talk about?
I thought maybe if he saw me after I lost weight, his feelings might change.
Mm-hmm. I see.
But he said his feelings wouldn't change...
I see. You worked hard on the diet, and you wanted his feelings to change.
But it didn't work.
I see. That must have been really painful.
Maybe he never really loved me...
Mm-hmm. It's understandable that you would feel that way.
What does it even mean that he can't marry me because of my appearance? After we were together for four years.
Really. That doesn't feel acceptable, does it? Four years, too!
Yes.
That makes it even more shocking. How do you feel you would like things to go from here?
He says, in his own way, he had been encouraging me to diet during that time. I don't know. I'm so frustrated that I want to show him, but I'm not emotionally there yet.
I see. Yes, of course. It would be hard to just switch your feelings right away.
Yes. For now, my parents are saying we should go to court.
I see. Is that something you want as well?
I do think we should go to court. There's also the issue of the wedding costs. But I don't know if that will make me feel any clearer...
Mm-hmm, mm-hmm. I see. So, you want to clarify what happened through the court case,
Yes.
and if that could help you feel clearer, that would be good—is that how it feels?
Hmm... Even if we go to court, I can only get about two million yen in compensation. It's frustrating...
I see. Is that right. So you feel frustrated that the compensation would only be about two million yen. Earlier, you mentioned wanting to show him,
Honestly, it feels like I should get around ten million yen, doesn't it?
That's how deeply frustrated and hurt you feel.
I want to show him, but I don't know what I should do.
I see. So, showing him is what you're wanting right now.
The money and the time won't come back.
That's true.
It's so frustrating...
Mm-hmm. Have you been talking to anyone about these feelings?
Yes. To my friends.
I see. After talking with them, has there been any change in how you feel?
Maybe it got a little easier.
I see. It sounds like you have all kinds of feelings built up inside right now, and letting them out helps you feel a little clearer—is that right?
But I keep thinking, why did something like this happen to me?
Mm-hmm. Truly... I think it's natural to feel that way.
My friends listen to me and they're kind, but what happened doesn't change.
That's true. Remembering it can make you feel frustrated all over again.
Yes.
You may not be able to feel this right away yet, but I think that you getting back on your feet and becoming happy would be the best way to show him.
Yes.
What do you think?
That might be true.
I think it's only natural that you can't easily switch your feelings right away right now.
Yes.
I think there will be times when it feels painful,
Yes.
but please let those feelings out, whether it's with your friends or through this support service.
Thank you very much.
We'll end here for today. Thank you very much.

interaction.content: (Thank you for being here today. We’ll begin when it’s time.)
(Thank you very much for today.)
Hello! I’m the counselor. Thank you for coming today. To start, could you tell me your age, gender, and what you’d like to talk about?
I’m 35, female. Lately I’ve been tired and I can’t get motivated to do anything... Maybe I have depression...
I see. Thank you for telling me. You feel that it might be depression, is that right? That sounds really painful... When have you been feeling this way?
Yes. I guess since around the beginning of this year...
(I’m sorry. I meant, “Since when...” Thank you.)
(It’s okay! I just answered based on the flow!)
Thank you for telling me. I see. Feeling that way for about five months must be really exhausting.
Until last year things were going well, but suddenly I lost motivation for everything, and every day I just kind of stare off into space.

I see... So that’s what it’s been like... If anything comes to mind, could you tell me whether something happened around the time this year began? (I meant “around the time this year began.” I’m sorry for all the typos.)
(It’s okay, let’s keep going.)
(Yes, thank you!)

If I had to say what changed, maybe just that the members at work changed a lot. Last year was actually busier, but... I was planning to work hard at both my job and raising my child, but suddenly I just couldn’t get motivated...

I see. There was a change at work. Changes like that can sometimes be harder than just being busy. And with raising a child as well, I imagine you’ve been working very hard through a lot. You mentioned not feeling motivated—how about your daily life? If there are specific things, like your body not moving, could you tell me about them?

Thank you. It was hard, but I used to think it was enjoyable. Now I can’t think that anymore... It’s not that I feel physically unwell, but no matter how much I sleep I’m still sleepy, and even when I’m working I find myself spacing out.

I see. Thank you for sharing that. I imagine you may feel worried, like, “Am I okay?” I’m glad to hear you’re not feeling physically unwell. But when you feel sleepy and space out even at work, it makes you wonder what to do, doesn’t it... I think it’s precisely because you’re working so hard every day. If it’s okay, could you tell me how you would like your current situation to change?

I wonder... I’ve been getting irritated with my child more often, I can’t get motivated at work, and I just feel kind of unsettled. I want to be positive and do my best like before. But even when I think I should try hard, for some reason my body won’t move, and in the end I just sit there spacing out, and that keeps repeating, and then I get depressed.

You feel that there have been more moments when you get irritated with your child... I think it’s understandable that things would become that way. And even while carrying that unsettled feeling, you want to keep trying in a positive way. Yes. I see. I can feel that even though every day is hard, you are truly trying your best.
Thank you. I kept thinking maybe someday, somehow, I’d be able to switch gears, but five months have already passed this year.

I see... You’ve done so well carrying this for five whole months! You said you end up feeling depressed—aside from your body not moving, if there’s anything else you notice yourself feeling, could you tell me? It could be emotions you feel, like emptiness, loneliness, frustration, feeling like no one understands... anything like that is okay.
Thank you. Ah—there are times when I feel lonely for some reason.
Yes, I see. Thank you for telling me. For example, when do you feel lonely?

Since I’ve been working from home more, I don’t see people much, so I feel lonely, I guess. And also, I’m simply tired. I barely move because I’m at home, but I’m tired... I’m anxious that if things go on like this, my motivation and physical strength will keep declining.

I see. Working from home means there’s no commute, but on the other hand, I think it can often feel lonely. Even while feeling tired, you’ve been managing each day so well. It makes sense that you would feel anxious. Today, even while carrying that anxiety, you came here to talk because you want to change the situation. Please let me think through with you how the situation might be changed.
Thank you. I’m glad. How can I improve things?

Thank you. Let me organize things for a moment. Right now, you often find yourself spacing out and not feeling motivated. But you would like to be able to move with a more positive mindset—is that right?
Yes, that’s right.

Thank you. This is just my personal impression, but in talking with you, I feel that you are a very sincere and hardworking person. And originally, you seem to be a positive person. But right now, there have been changes at work and other things, and your fatigue has built up, leaving you in a state where motivation isn’t coming...
Yes, that’s about right. I don’t know whether I’m sincere or not, but I did think I was a positive person. I’m kind of shocked that I’m feeling this depressed.

I see. Thank you for sharing that. It’s shocking to think, “I never thought this would happen to me,” isn’t it... This is my thought, but first of all, I’d really like you to praise yourself a lot for having come this far with both parenting and work. How does that sound?
Thank you. Praise myself... Is it really okay to praise myself?

Yes!! You really are doing so well. Parenting alone is very hard, and on top of that you’re working hard at your job too... not everyone can do that. If you’re willing, I’d like you to first acknowledge and praise yourself as you are right now. And if possible, I wonder if it might also be good to consult with or talk to someone close to you. Over these past five months, have you talked to anyone about this?
Thank you. Somehow, I haven’t really been praised by people much, and I didn’t think I was working that hard, so I’m happy to hear that.
I’m happy to hear you say that, too.
Come to think of it, I haven’t talked to anyone about it.
I see. You’ve really been doing your best on your own. Is there a reason you didn’t talk to anyone?
I thought if I said I had no motivation, my husband or people at work might get mad at me... We both work, and my husband helps with housework and childcare too, so I feel bad.

I see. Your husband is usually cooperative, then. I’m glad he seems like a kind person. And the way you care about him and feel bad shows that you’re a kind person too. If your husband is kind like that, I feel like he might be able to hear your honest feelings now. What do you think? Do you feel that talking to your husband might make you feel a little lighter? Or would someone else be better?? (I’m sorry for asking several questions in a row. Please go ahead.)

I’m not really kind, but... Still, I feel like we could share that things are hard day to day. Rather than saying I have no motivation, I think I could talk about how we’re both working hard at work and parenting.

That’s how it feels to you. I’m glad you feel you may be able to talk with him. Just having someone listen to your feelings can sometimes make things a little easier. It seemed like you feel the cause this time may be the changes at work... If it’s okay, do you think you could talk with someone at your workplace about making improvements?

Yes, talking here today, and having you say that I’m doing my best with both work and parenting, made me think that’s something the two of us can share too. As for work, rather than consulting with someone, I’m thinking maybe I’ll increase how often I go into the office a little.
I’m glad to hear that. You really are doing so well every day. Please give yourself a big gold star.
Earlier, when you said working from home can make it easier to feel lonely, I thought, yeah, that might be true...
I see, that’s what you’re thinking. You talked it through yourself and gained that insight... That’s really wonderful.
Thank you. I thought working from home was only good things, since pickups are easier and there’s no commute, but maybe there are some things that surprisingly aren’t like that.

That’s true. After all, in-person communication has good aspects too, like being able to share enjoyable things. How does it feel? Do you think increasing how often you go into the office and talking with your husband are things you can actually do?
Yes! I feel like I’m getting a little more motivated. For now, I want to talk with my husband and try going to the office a little more often.
I’m glad to hear that! Since you’re originally a positive person, I think your own actions will surely help things move toward improvement.
Yes, you’re right! I feel like I can get back to the person I was a little while ago. Thank you.

I’m happy that I can feel your positive energy coming through your words. We’re getting close to the end of our time. Thank you for talking with me today. I truly want to support you, with how hard you’re trying. If anything comes up again, please feel free to come talk anytime.
Yes, I think I’ll try a little more. If anything comes up again, I’ll reach out!
Yes! I’m sure you can get through this. Please come back anytime. I’m rooting for you!! Thank you for coming today. I’ll end here for today.
(Thank you for today. I learned a lot.)
(Thank you as well. You did well today. I’m very sorry for all the typos. Thank you for your valuable time.) (We will end now.)

interaction.content: Thank you for your time. It’s 1:00 now—is this still okay?
Yes, I’m the counselor. Thank you, I look forward to working with you.
Thank you!
Could you tell me your age and gender? Sorry, I’m having a bit of trouble sending messages.
(No worries!)
I meant I’m having trouble.
I’m a 25-year-old man.
Thank you. What would you like to talk about today?
The dog we had at my parents’ house passed away...
The dog you had passed away. That’s sad.
Yes. I’m really sad.
You’re feeling very sad. Around when did they pass away?
About a week ago. I’ve calmed down a little, but I keep remembering and getting sad.
I’m sorry for asking you various things when you’re feeling so sad. Please only answer what you feel able to.
Thank you for being considerate. It’s okay!
It was about a week ago... That’s very recent. Are you feeling okay physically? I mean, were you feeling okay?
Yes, I’m physically okay. I’m getting through things normally. But I keep remembering a lot, and I get sad, and then I don’t feel like doing anything, so I thought I’d try talking to someone for now!
It must feel like losing a family member you always lived with. That’s really painful.
Yes, I feel drained, and when I think about how long this feeling will last, I get anxious.
What kind of dog was the dog you had?
He was a Shiba Inu, and he was like a comforting presence for everyone in the family every day!
I don’t know if my own experience will be helpful, but even after they pass away, they stay by your side. I see, he was like a comforting presence.
Thank you. I hadn’t thought of it that way.
Would it be okay if I asked what caused his passing? Only if you don’t mind.
The cause was old age. It wasn’t an illness or anything, and while it’s sad, I think it was a good way to go!
I see. You feel it was a good way to go. I think your dog was happy, too.
Thank you. It would really be nice if that were true!
Dogs’ lifespans are shorter than humans’, so even if we think we’re prepared for that when we get them, it’s still painful when that time actually comes.
When I think about it, he was in our home for about 15 years, so I really never imagined he would actually pass away. I tried not to think about it, so it felt like, this time has finally come, haha.
I see... You always loved him like family, and maybe your dog is looking back on those happy days. When you live together for so long, you don’t even think about them passing away, do you?
I hope so!
From your messages, Neya, I can tell that you’re a very deeply caring person.
Thank you! Talking like this makes me feel like I need to start properly accepting that he has passed away.
It’s completely understandable that your feelings would be weighing you down, but seeing your thoughts shift in that way makes me feel that you’re strong, Neya.
It’s already been a week since he passed, so I’d like to try to think even a little more positively.
I hope the dog who passed away is happily watching you do that.
Yes!
Still, I don’t think it’s a bad thing at all to remember your dog and feel sad. I’m sure you’ll think about him from time to time going forward.
That’s true. I hope I can remember him as a good memory!
I hope you can continue enjoying a happy life, for your dog’s sake as well.
Yes, that’s true! Thank you!
Is that all right for today’s consultation?
Yes. That’s okay!
Thank you.

Thank you for your hard work! This was the setup for the person seeking support. A 25-year-old man whose family dog at his parents’ house passed away one week ago. He just wanted to talk to someone for now. It would also be good if the conversation could help him feel more positive. That was the setup. Since it’s his first time using SNS counseling, rather than speaking up a lot himself, he wants the counselor to expand the conversation. For example, he wanted words that could help him feel more positive, like, “It would be nice if you can cherish the happy memories you shared together.”
Please feel free to reach out again if anything comes up. Yes, thank you. You’re right, I should have expanded the conversation more.

I think I wanted more questions. Since this is training, we’re both being conscious of it, but I somehow felt like I was the one expanding the conversation! Since the setup was that I wanted someone to listen, rather than asking about the reason he died, I wanted you to draw out fun memories, or say something like, it would be good if I can live positively from here on while holding onto him as a good memory. That’s the kind of words I wanted! Playing the counselor role is hard, isn’t it 😅
Yes, I learned a lot. The screen cut off partway through, and it was hard to read the whole text. Is there some way to operate it?
You can see the history in the role-play evaluation section!
I understand, thank you. I’ll take a look right away. I’ll end here, if that’s all right.
Yes! I’ll put in an evaluation again! Let’s both keep at it! It’s okay to end here! Thank you very much!
Yes, thank you very much.

interaction.content: Hello.
Thank you for seeing me.
Thank you for coming to talk today. To start, could you tell me your age, gender, and what you’d like to discuss?
Male, 30 years old. Work isn’t going well.
I see. In what way does it feel like it isn’t going well?
Well, rather than saying it isn’t going well, it might be more like I just can’t get motivated.
I see. Was there something that made you feel like you couldn’t get motivated?
That’s what I’m not really sure about...
When did you start feeling this way?
It feels like all my energy has kind of drained out. I do think I want to get motivated and try hard again, but since the start of this year I just haven’t been able to get into it.
I see. From last year into this year, has anything changed in your work situation?
Well, the end of the year is a busy season, so it’s hectic, and then from the beginning of the year it becomes the slow season and work suddenly drops off, so I do think that might be part of it.
I see.

Every year during this period, I’ve still worked on various things, thought about what’s ahead, and stayed active in a positive way, but somehow I just don’t have the energy. I thought maybe if I talked to someone once, something might change.
I see. That sounds really hard. Since losing motivation, has it been affecting your work?
I’m self-employed, so the more I don’t do, the more I lose out, so I think it will affect things eventually.
I see. Even though you’re in this state of not feeling motivated, there hasn’t been any especially major impact on your work?

That’s right. The situation is the same as every year, but what’s different is my own feelings, I guess...? Even when I try to do something, I put it off, and in the end February has already passed, so there were times I thought maybe it’s time to quit.
I see. Do the busy seasons and slow seasons happen several times a year?
Yes. By the way, I’ll be entering a busy season soon, so things will get somewhat busier. I’m sure that’ll make me motivated again, but I got worried about how much I slacked off this time.
I see. Including the end of the year, during busy seasons, it sounds like you may be pushing yourself extremely hard, don’t you think?
Busy seasons are always like that. I also strongly feel that it’s fun! And the difference in energy compared to the slow season is huge...
I think it’s wonderful that you can feel it’s fun when you’re busy. How have you usually spent the slow seasons up to now?

That’s because it’s work I love! I’d prepare various things, do sales activities, bring in customers, things like that! I wonder what everyone does when they lose motivation. A lot of my friends are full-time employees, so our situations are completely different and they don’t really understand.
It’s wonderful that you’re doing work you love. I think everyone probably has their own way of coping when they lose motivation.
Thank you! That’s true. What kinds of ways of coping are there?
Are you still doing preparation, sales activities, and customer outreach now?
It’s like I put them off and do them once in a while.
I see. How many years have you been in your current work?
This is my fifth year. This is the first time I’ve slacked off like this. I’m really worried about what’s going to happen from here.
I see. Feelings and states you’ve never experienced before can make you anxious, can’t they?
Yes, really. I turned 30 this year, so I’ve started thinking more about myself going forward, and now I’m thinking maybe that’s part of the reason too.
Mm-hmm, that makes sense. Since this is your fifth year, I imagine you’ve gotten quite used to the flow of your current work, haven’t you?
Yes, I think so.
That makes sense. Maybe because you’ve gained a certain amount of room in the flow of your work, this might be a time when you’re thinking about your current age and various things.
The more I think about all kinds of things, the more tired I get! I really think that’s true!
I think it’s wonderful that you’ve noticed that.

Do you think so? It’s true, I can also see it as having gained some room. Though embarrassingly, realistically speaking, I don’t have that much room... But mentally, I’ve gotten used to it and I know the flow, so in a way I feel settled. It might be something like that.

Mm-hmm, yes. For example, while continuing your current sales activities and customer outreach to the extent that it doesn’t cause problems, it might also be okay to use this as time to think about what comes next.
Yes, maybe I was thinking too much about all kinds of things. Thank you for the suggestion.
You may be able to make some new discoveries too. I’m glad. If even a little of your anxiety has been eased, I’m happy.
New discoveries are also something I’d kind of forgotten in my fifth year. Maybe I’d forgotten my original mindset. Yes, I’m glad I was able to talk.
That makes sense. I’m glad if this could be a chance for you to remember your original mindset.
Thank you for listening to me!
Thank you as well for taking the time. When you feel anxious, please feel free to come talk again.
Yes, I’ll do that!
Then, we’ll end today’s counseling here. Is that okay?
That’s okay. Thank you very much!
Yes, thank you. Well then, take care.
(Thank you for playing the counselor role. I appreciate it 😊)
Thank you as well, and thank you for playing the client role. Is it okay to end the role-play?
Yes, that’s okay. Thank you for your work!
Thank you for your work.

interaction.content: (Thank you for being here today. When it’s time, I’d like to begin.)
(Thank you as well. I appreciate it.)
Hello. I’m the counselor. Thank you for coming today. To start, could you tell me your age range, gender, and the name you’d like me to call you by? A nickname is perfectly fine.
Hello. I’m in my 20s, female, and my name is Yuri.
Thank you. Yuri, what would you like to talk about today?
Actually, I’ve come down with an illness, and I’m feeling anxious about a lot of things, and it’s painful.
I see. That must be worrying. About the illness—what kind of illness is it? Only if you’re comfortable sharing.

I don’t really want to go into too much detail… I’m sorry. It’s not a life-threatening illness, but I’ll have to keep going to the hospital for a while, and it seems like I’ll need various tests from here on, so I’m anxious. Also, I’ll be starting job hunting next year, so I’m worried the illness might affect that…
I understand. Of course, that’s completely fine. Thank you. I see—yes, that would make you anxious. Is it clear how long treatment might take, or what kind of treatment it will be?

I’m sorry. Thank you. Fortunately, my doctor is a good person, and they explained a lot to me in detail. First, it seems like they’ll do a definitive test to confirm whether it really is that illness. If it’s confirmed, I’ll have to continue taking medication for at least six months, and even after the medication ends, I’ll apparently need to have tests once every six months for a while to check that it hasn’t come back.

I see… Thinking about that test, and then the medication treatment afterward, it must feel very worrying and painful not knowing what will happen. When you think about the illness, what kinds of thoughts come to mind for you?
Yes… well, I guess things like, “Will it really get better?” and “What if it comes back?” and “What if I can’t get a job because of the illness?” come to mind.
Yes, of course… I can imagine how anxious you must feel. When did you find out about the illness?
I found out really recently. About a week ago, the hospital told me there was a possibility I might have it.
I see… You must have been so shocked at the time. Have you told anyone?
Yes, I felt like, “I can’t believe this is happening to me.” I’ve told my family.
I see. It must feel hard to believe… How did your family seem?
Yes, my family seemed surprised too. But my mother especially has been supporting me, like coming with me to listen to what the doctor says.
That’s good to hear. I imagine that must feel very reassuring for you, more than anything.
Yes. If I didn’t have my family’s support, I might have been much more depressed.

I’m glad. Even so, the illness is something happening to you, so even if your anxiety is soothed by your family, I don’t think it disappears. Right now, do you feel that you’d like that anxiety to feel even a little lighter?
Yes. That’s right. I’m just full of anxiety, so I think it would be good if it could feel lighter.
I’d like us to think through this together, so that your feelings can lift even a little. How does that sound?
Thank you. Please.
Could I organize things a little? Yuri, about a week ago, at the hospital, you were told that there might be a possibility of an illness, and you were shocked,
Yes.

You have to undergo tests to confirm the illness, and after that, if it is the illness, medication treatment will begin, and even afterward you’ll need to continue having tests to check for recurrence. Yuri, you have job hunting coming up next year, and you’re worried it might affect that. Also, you’re full of anxiety about whether it will really get better, whether it might come back, and so on—is that right? I said end-of-life preparations, but I meant job hunting, I’m sorry.
Yes. That’s about right.
Yuri, are you feeling physically okay right now?
Fortunately, it was found early, so I don’t have any noticeable symptoms at the moment. Thank you for worrying about me.
I was a little concerned. Thank you for telling me. I think anxiety may be something that grows when there are things we don’t know for certain. Yuri, what do you think?
Yes, that’s true. I think a big part of my anxiety is because I don’t know what will happen.

Because it’s something you can’t see or grasp, I think it may often swell up larger than reality. Your anxiety right now is completely understandable, but first, at this point, whether it really is that illness is not yet definite—is that right?
Yes. That’s true, there are still parts that aren’t clear, but the doctor said it probably is. It seems like the test is more just to be sure.

I see, that makes sense. Since you were told you might have the illness, I imagine all kinds of feelings have been crossing over each other this past week. Even within that, were there times when you were able to take your mind off it a little?
Yes. The times I could take my mind off it were… well, when my family encouraged me, and when I was doing things I like, I guess.
I see… By the way, may I ask what kinds of things you like?
Reading, listening to music, and also, I have an idol I like, so watching live concert videos.
Ah, I see. That sounds lovely. Just hearing about all of those makes it feel enjoyable. When you were absorbed in the things you like, did the illness come to mind?
When I was absorbed in them, I feel like I was able to forget about the illness a little.

That must be good time for you. I’ll put this in a very practical way, but I feel that being driven by anxiety you can’t really grasp can lead to more negativity than necessary. Yuri, how does that feel to you?
Hmm, that may be true.

I think your anxiety is completely understandable. Rather than fearing it more than necessary, you learn what is certain and respond to what is certain. And for the rest, you do things for yourself that raise your own immunity… That’s the kind of image I have of what might be good. Yuri, how does that feel to you?
Yes. I think if I knew for sure that it would get better, my anxiety would go away. But I end up thinking that maybe you can’t know that for sure…

I see. Yes, that’s true. Whether it will definitely get better may not be something anyone can guarantee. But I think what will certainly happen is that you’ll receive the best treatment aimed toward that. First, I wonder if you could trust that, and take good care of yourself with care and kindness… How does that sound?
Yes. For now, I want to listen carefully to what the doctor says and properly go through treatment. Like you said, I also want to take care of myself.

Yes. When I imagine you taking good care of yourself, Yuri, it makes me feel very glad. Also, one more thing, about the image of the illness… Rather than being crushed by a vague, large black cloud, what would it be like to imagine it just a little smaller, make it about the same size as yourself, and try holding hands with it… something like that?
An image, you mean?

I probably like her. She doesn’t talk to me at all, and she never seems energetic, but when I see bright, cheerful families, I wonder what makes such a difference.

Yes, right now you feel that your home is different from that kind of bright, cheerful family. You’ve been holding all kinds of feelings by yourself for a long time. I wonder if you like your mother and want her to feel better, and you want to talk with her a lot... Is that how it feels?
I think that’s probably true.
That makes sense... Have you talked with your grandmother or grandfather about your mother? Have you talked with your grandfather, grandmother, or relatives about your mother?
I met my grandma when I was little, but I think she lives far away. I haven’t seen her in a long time.
I see... Thank you for coming to talk in such a difficult situation, and for sharing your feelings with me. Would it be okay if I summarized the situation a little?
Yes.

When you ask people the meaning of being alive, no one can answer; school and home aren’t fun at all. At home, since your father left, you haven’t had much conversation with your mother. But you yourself really love your mother, and you want her to feel better and talk with you about all kinds of things. Is that the situation?

You’re the counselor who told me that everyone doesn’t know the meaning of being alive. I’d never talked about it with anyone before, so as for loving her... I wouldn’t go that far. I want her to talk to me like she used to.

I see... You asked a question you’d never asked anyone before... Thank you. I see... You asked a question you’d never asked anyone before... Thank you. The consultation is limited to one hour, so if it’s okay, may I make the meaning of living my homework?
Yes. I don’t have many, but maybe I’ll try talking to my friends too. I was happy that you listened to me.

Yes, maybe some good ideas might come up. I’ll do the one thing I can do for you right now. In human life, there is never only one path. There are thousands, tens of thousands. Yes, if you try talking about it, a different way of thinking might come up too. (Sorry, are my messages going through?)
(They’re going through!)
(Got it, sob.)
Thank you. I’ll try living a little longer.

Thank you too, for sharing your important feelings with me. Today’s consultation ends here; is that okay? I’ll work hard on your homework too, so if anything comes up again, please do come talk with me.
Yes, thank you.
(Thank you. I’m really sorry for the trouble with the system not working well.)
(Good work playing the counselor role!) (It’s totally okay!)
(Thank you for the role-play.)
(Thank you too 😊, I look forward to working with you again!)
