interaction.content: Good evening. Thank you for being here today.
Thank you as well.
Thank you. We’ll get started when it’s time, so please wait just a moment.
Yes, I understand.
Then let’s begin. Good evening. I’m the counselor. Thank you for coming in for a consultation today. To start, could you tell me your age and gender?
Yes. I’m 48 years old, and I’m a woman.
Thank you. So, what would you like to talk about today?
I’m struggling with something related to work.
It’s about work, then. Could you tell me specifically what’s been going on?
Yes. I started working as a temp in an office job in January, but I’ve started worrying about money and wondering if I should look for a full-time permanent position.
I see. With temp work, is it that your working hours are limited, or something like that?

Rather than that, the amount I actually take home each month is less than I expected, and there’s no bonus. I know it’s a bit late to realize this, but I’ve started panicking that I can’t go on like this...
I see. Yes, that makes sense. That would make you feel anxious.
Yes, exactly.
Was there a particular reason you started working as a temp?
Because of the pandemic too, I was looking for a full-time office job, but nothing was getting decided, and when I reluctantly registered with a temp agency, I finally got this job.
I see. So even before getting your current job, you went through quite a lot.
I know that at my age, getting a full-time office job from here on is difficult.
That’s how you’re feeling. But at the same time, of course you’d like to have stable work.
Yes. So even though it’s temp work, I did finally get in, and part of me wants to do my best, but I wonder if I should look again for a full-time position, even outside of office work...
Yes, yes. That’s a difficult place to be, isn’t it... Are you thinking that if it’s a full-time permanent position, it doesn’t necessarily have to be office work?
Yes. I’ve never done work outside of office work, so I do feel anxious... I think sales might be good too, but I’m not good at driving.

I see. I think the work itself often depends a lot on getting used to it and gaining experience, so I don’t think you need to feel too anxious about that! You’re also considering sales, then. There are also inside sales roles where you don’t have to drive, so looking in that direction could be one option.
This is the first time I’ve heard the term inside sales. That sounds good. What kind of work is it, for example?
Let’s see, maybe it’s easiest to describe it as work like a sales assistant. So I think you could definitely make good use of the office work experience you’ve had so far!
I worked in sales administration at a trading company for a long time, so I’m good at that kind of work! But when I search for sales administration jobs, it’s tough.
Oh, I see! In that case, I think it would probably be a great fit for you. I see, had you already been searching for that?
I’ve never searched under inside sales, so I wonder how it would be? Office work and sales give different impressions, so if I search under inside sales, maybe I’ll find something new?

I think sales administration and inside sales have some things in common, but with inside sales, my impression is that you may have more business discussions by phone and spend more time directly interacting with customers. Yes, I think it would be good to try searching for “inside sales” once. It also fits the way things are done nowadays, so I think there’s definitely demand!
I see! That sounds good. I might actually be good at business discussions over the phone!
Is that right! Even in our exchange now, I get the impression that you’re very quick and efficient, so I’m sure you’d be good at it! (laughs)
People often tell me I’m quick and efficient, or really brisk and lively. (laughs) But with places like Hello Work, there are a lot of companies that don’t seem great...
I see... Have you used anything besides Hello Work?
I’m wondering how I should search. I was registered with a Recruit agent before.
I see. How was Recruit?
At that time, I was searching for office jobs, so nothing worked out at all.
I see... I get the impression there are a lot of applicants for office jobs.
Do you know any agency companies you’d recommend? I’m sorry for asking something like this... Someone told me before that office jobs are like musical chairs.

No, no, it’s okay! I’m sorry to go back a little, but earlier you mentioned that with Hello Work, there were a lot of companies that didn’t seem great. What kinds of things were you dissatisfied with? Musical chairs—yes, I can see how it would feel that way, but luck and timing are also a big part of it!
With Hello Work, even listings for full-time permanent positions didn’t have bonuses and things like that. That said, it may have been because I was looking for office jobs.
I see. In that case, would you say that salary is the priority for you? Yes, with office jobs, I do think it’s true that it can be difficult to find something that works in terms of pay.
Yes, that’s exactly it. I’m single, so I feel like I have to earn my own living.

I see. You’re looking ahead carefully and taking action for your own future, and I think that’s really wonderful. In terms of your living situation, do you feel it would be difficult to continue with your current job?

No, no, I’m just panicking. I really wonder if I’ll be okay from here on. If things stay as they are, I’ll just keep eating away at my savings. And my current job is a bit too hard for me. There are a lot of small details to remember, and it’s painful...
I see... It’s true, when you see your savings going down, it makes you panic. And yes, having to learn all those little details from scratch is hard...
I’m already an older lady, so it feels like, “No way, I can’t do this~” (laughs)

No, no! With your brisk and lively energy, I don’t think you need to worry about that! (laughs) That said, there is the idea of work-life balance, so it’s possible to change jobs and become a full-time employee, only to find that the work is so demanding you have no private life... So I think it would be good to really picture the kind of lifestyle you want for yourself.
I see. That’s true. I’d been avoiding sales because I had this image of being crushed by quotas. My health matters too, doesn’t it?

Yes, exactly. Health is your greatest asset. Even if you have savings, if your body can’t move, you can’t use them, right! For example, five years from now, ten years from now... how would you like to be spending your time?
I want to be doing work I can think is fun♪ with lots of energy, and I want to earn a lot of money!

Mm-hmm, that’s wonderful! That’s the best lifestyle. (laughs) Then, first of all, it might be good to look for work that you can genuinely feel is fun! For example, there are lots of people who turn something connected to their hobbies into work.
I don’t have any hobbies... But I like talking to people, so maybe I’ll try looking around for inside sales jobs first.

Liking talking with people is a truly wonderful thing! It’s an excellent skill! Yes, there are many different industries within inside sales, so it might be good to look at it by industry as well. This has gone a little off from recommending an agent, but from everything you’ve told me, you seem very positive and considerate of others, so I really hope you can find work that involves connecting with people.
Thank you! I feel like I want to search for inside sales across different industries and do my best!
Please do! I’m cheering you on! I also felt like I should do my best so I don’t lose to your bright, energetic spirit! (laughs)
Not at all. Thank you so much for encouraging me. I was happy that you stayed with me through such a real-life concern. ♡
No, no, thank you as well! Well then, would it be all right to end today’s consultation here?
Yes, thank you very much!
(Then we’ll pause here for now.) (Thank you for your hard work. I learned a great deal today. Thank you.)
(Thank you as well. I learned a lot too! Thank you for your hard work!)
(If we work together again, I look forward to it! ☺ Well then, would it be all right to end the role-play?)
Same here, I look forward to it then. (^^) It’s OK to end!
Thank you! Well then, goodbye.

interaction.content: (Good evening, thank you for meeting with me today.)
Thank you for meeting with me.
Good evening, I’m the counselor. Could you tell me your age, gender, and what you’d like to talk about?
Good evening. I’m a man in my late 40s. It’s about struggling with things like poor physical health.
I see. That must be hard. Since when have you been feeling unwell?
It’s been since I was young, really. I’ve gone from hospital to hospital up to now, but it hasn’t gotten better at all... It feels like going to the hospital doesn’t really solve anything...
I see. I imagine you’ve been going through a lot for a long time.
I think it’s probably something mental or emotional.
I see. That sounds really exhausting. You mentioned it’s been since you were young—what kinds of symptoms do you have?
Well, when I feel stressed or have trouble with relationships, it gets even worse. I get headaches, stiff shoulders, and my stomach feels off. When it’s bad, I end up staying in bed.
I see. That may be putting quite a burden on you emotionally. Have you talked with anyone about this?

I’ve had tests done at hospitals many times, but there’s never anything particularly abnormal. They do give me medicine and things, but when I talk to the doctor, they just prescribe medication and that’s it. So I don’t really get much consultation.
I see. Not knowing the cause may be making you feel anxious or impatient. How is your physical condition right now?

Right now I’m somehow managing to go to work. But maybe because it’s the end of the fiscal year and I’m busy, I’m not feeling very well. When my physical condition is bad, my mental state also goes down.
I see. So you are going to work. Are you able to sleep and things like that?
With sleep, I wake up in the middle of the night, or I wake up early in the morning. I’m somehow managing to go to work, but when I get home I’m completely exhausted...
I see. When you can’t sleep well, I imagine it affects both your physical condition and your mood. You’re working every day while things feel really hard.
Yes, when it’s hard, it’s really hard. And I end up disliking myself for being like that.

I see. In that kind of situation, I think it’s natural to feel that way. Earlier, you shared that your symptoms come out when you have trouble with relationships—what kinds of things are difficult for you?

I’ve thought for a while that maybe I’m HSP. When I looked into it, most of it seemed to fit me. I get nervous in front of people, communication is difficult, and I have friction with people in various ways. I think I have a very sensitive personality. It may be one of those developmental disorders you hear about a lot lately.
That’s how you’ve been feeling. At the moment, do you have any family members living with you?
Right now I live alone. I was divorced about 10 years ago.
I see. So you’re living on your own. At your current workplace, with communication or getting nervous in front of people and so on, what feels the hardest for you?

Well, there are bosses I don’t like, and I sometimes experience harassment too. I feel nervous in meetings or when dealing with customers. The main thing is that I get tired easily in places where there are people.
I see. If you’re experiencing harassment, I imagine you might feel tense or shrink back. You may not be able to function as you normally would. How do you feel about it?

Yes, in situations that feel like harassment, I do shrink back. Also, I tend to be overly considerate of people. When I’m around people, I feel like I’m the type who gets more tense and tired more easily than others. I may be the kind of person who watches people’s expressions and is overly careful and hesitant around them. So maybe that’s why I get tired and it tends to show up in my body...

That’s how you feel. If you’re overly considerate of others, it may leave you exhausted. And if you’re experiencing harassment, I imagine that makes it even harder. You mentioned that it’s busy because it’s the end of the fiscal year—have you always felt this way around this time of year?

Yes. At the end of the fiscal year there’s a lot of work, and a lot of contact and dealings with different people, so it’s a mentally and physically hard time. When I’m busy and I’m not feeling well physically, I tend to get even more down... And there are even more situations where I have to be considerate, so it feels like it becomes more and more of a vicious cycle.

I see. I think you’re doing your best every day while things are really hard. Being considerate of others and worrying about their reactions may be because you’re working so earnestly. Since your work involves interacting with many different people, I feel that may also be one of your strengths. How does that feel to you?

Yes, when I really think about it, I can see that there’s a part of me that’s trying so hard to do my job well somehow, and to be liked by people. Talking about it like this, I’m starting to feel like maybe I’m trying too hard. Because I take things too seriously and try too hard, I get tired easily and I’m too considerate of others. I guess it makes me exceed my capacity.

That’s how you see it. You may be someone with a strong sense of responsibility. I think it’s also natural that when you’re not feeling well physically, you become even more concerned about the people around you. Would it be possible to vent to someone, or do something to change your mood?

Maybe I do tend to feel an excessive sense of responsibility... Well, I don’t have many friends to begin with, so there aren’t really people of the same gender I can vent to... But there is someone I’m dating now, and I feel like I could talk to that person about anything.

I see. It might be good to try talking with them. I feel that you’re someone who really faces yourself. It’s good that you have someone you can talk to. Since you feel you get tired easily, it may also be good to think about ways you can refresh yourself.

I do talk to them a fair amount normally, but I’m thinking maybe I should vent more openly. I see—maybe because I’m HSP and have a sensitive side, I do face my inner self. Yes, having someone to talk to is one thing, but I also like listening to music and watching movies by myself. I thought it would be good to include some time to refresh myself once in a while.

I see. Since you’re someone who works very hard, you may have often had to face yourself too. The parts of yourself that you see as sensitive feel to me like strengths, so I think you can learn to relate to them in a good way. How do you feel after talking through this so far?

Yes, I often focused only on the parts of myself I don’t like, so I feel like I can start seeing my sensitive side and things like that as strengths, and not deny myself so much. I feel like my thoughts have somehow been sorted out. I’m starting to feel like I want to take better care of myself. Thank you for today.

That’s how you feel. You came here to talk because you tend to worry about others, push yourself too hard, and your physical condition hasn’t been good, but it seems you’ve been able to view yourself more positively, so I’d like to end the consultation here.
Yes, as you said, I feel like I’ll be able to see things more positively. I’d like to talk with you again sometime.
Thank you for coming to talk with me today. If you’re having trouble with anything again, I hope you’ll come talk with me. Thank you very much.
I look forward to talking with you again. Thank you very much.
(We went a little over time. Thank you for giving me your valuable time.) (I would appreciate your advice. I’ll end here.)
Thank you as well. Thank you for your hard work.

interaction.content: Hello. I’m the counselor. Thank you for coming in today. To start, if you’re comfortable, could you tell me your gender, age, and what you’d like to talk about?
I’m 34, female, and I’m struggling with relationships with other moms at my child’s daycare.
Thank you for sharing that. You mentioned you’re struggling with relationships with other moms at the daycare. Could you tell me a bit more about that?
Recently, we moved to a larger daycare, and I’m feeling confused because the relationships among the moms in the same class are really close-knit.
I see. That sounds like it’s been really difficult. You said the relationships among the moms are close-knit—what is that like?

Everyone is in a group LINE chat, so I joined too, but almost every night they’re sharing something or other about the kids. I’ve always been bad at socializing, and I’m having trouble because I don’t know how to respond.
I see. That would be troubling.
It’s just tiring somehow.
Yes, I can understand that. It would be tiring. Since you’ve only just changed daycares, it must feel unsettling. Does it seem like you absolutely have to be in that group?
I’m not sure, but when I look at the number of people in it, everyone is there.
I see. Then if you didn’t join, it would feel like people might think something of it, wouldn’t it.
Yes. Even though I’m not good at it, I want my child to get along with everyone, so I’m somehow managing to take part.

Yes, that makes sense. The fact that you’re trying to do it even if it’s hard, because you’re thinking of your child, really shows how much you care about your child. In those exchanges, does it feel like everyone replies?
Sometimes I reply by copying what someone else said. That’s all I can manage.
I see. That must take a lot of mental energy.
Yes. Also, my pickup time overlaps with one of the main moms,
Yes.
and maybe because I don’t talk much, she seems concerned and talks to me a lot, and she sends me individual LINE messages too, so it feels kind of heavy.
I see. That sounds painful. I imagine it must be very tiring. Are there any other parents you’re close with?
Not at the moment, and I don’t know if I’ll be able to become close with anyone.
I see. It seems to me that you really take in what the other person is feeling, and that may be why you get tired. How does that sound to you?
I’m not good at dealing with people, so maybe I’m overreacting.
You may be getting tired because you’re a very sensitive person. How is your child spending time at the daycare?
They’ve gotten pretty used to it and seem to be enjoying it, so I feel relieved.
I see. That’s good to hear. I think your child is able to enjoy going to daycare because of the effort you’ve been making.
Do you think so? I’m envious of my child for fitting in so well.
Yes. So, going forward, how would you like to handle your relationships with the other moms?
Actually, I’ve been invited to something like a picnic at the park on a day off. I don’t want to go, but I don’t know if I should, or how I should act. I guess it would be better to go, wouldn’t it?
I see. That’s a difficult decision.
I think I should get along with them for my child’s sake. But I don’t know what “getting along well” means.
I see. I think you’re really trying hard to respond to your child’s feelings.
My child is looking forward to going to the park too. I guess I should go, right?
Your child is looking forward to it, then. But I think it’s quite difficult to get along well with everyone. Do you feel that you don’t want to go?
If possible…
I see. But when you think about your child, you feel that it would be better to go.
I think… maybe I have no choice but to go.
I’d like us to think together about how you can relate to them from here. How would that be?
Yes, thank you. Please.
For example, I’m wondering if you might gradually communicate a little of how you feel to the other person. How does that sound?
How should I say it? I’m sorry, I can’t really think of the words.

Right. For example, with the group LINE, you could tell them something like, “I’m not very good at replying right away, so my replies may be slow.” Or, “I’m not very good at talking a lot, so would it be okay if I take my time talking?” How does that sound?
Yes… I don’t know if I’ll be able to say it, but would everyone understand if I did? It makes me a little nervous.

I think it takes a lot of courage, but if things stay as they are, you’ll have to keep feeling worn out. So I thought it might help if the others could understand even a little. How does that feel to you?
Yes. Thank you. A lot of them will probably go on to the same elementary school too, so it would be better if they understood me, wouldn’t it.
Yes. As you continue these relationships, if more people come to understand you, I think the hard feelings you’re carrying may ease a little.
Yes. I’m really nervous, but I’ll try talking to them. I’m thinking maybe I could tell them when we’re at the park.
Yes. I know it takes courage, but please try. I’m sincerely rooting for you.
Thank you. I’ll give it a try.
Yes, please do. We’re getting close to the end of our time. Is there anything else you feel you haven’t talked about enough?
I’m okay. I hope I can somehow manage it well without pushing myself too hard.
Yes. Please don’t push yourself too hard; I think it’s best to go at your own pace.
Yes. Thank you.
Well, we’re just about out of time, so would it be all right if we end here?
Yes.
Thank you. If there’s anything else you’d like to talk about, please feel free to come anytime. I’ll be here. Thank you for coming in today. We’ll end the consultation here.
Thank you very much. (I learned a lot. Thank you very much.)
(Thank you for today. I learned a lot. Would it be all right to end the role-play?)
(Yes. Good work.)

interaction.content: Hello. Thank you for working with me today. If possible, could you play the role of a client who has suicidal thoughts?
Hello, thank you. Suicidal thoughts... this is my first time, but I’ll try. I’ll probably be thinking a lot as I respond, so my replies may tend to be slow. Would that be okay?
I’m sorry, thank you. That’s completely fine. Thank you.
Thank you!
We’ll begin when it’s time.
Okay.
Hello, I’m the counselor. Thank you for coming in to talk today. To start, could you tell me your age, gender, and what you’d like to discuss?
Hello. I’m 43, female. I lost my husband in an accident three months ago, and it’s been painful.
Thank you for telling me. I see... that’s very painful... Thank you for coming to talk, even in the midst of that.
Yes. We were very close, and he was suddenly gone, and my heart just can’t keep up.
Yes, if a husband you were so close to suddenly disappeared from your life, I think it’s completely understandable...
Yes... I just want to go to where he is... Every day, I don’t understand the point of being alive.
That’s how you’re feeling...
Yes.
The feeling of being in so much pain and suffering that you don’t understand the meaning of living... I can really feel how painful that is...
Yes.
You said that every day you don’t understand the meaning of living. How are you feeling as you spend your days right now? If it’s painful to talk about, you don’t have to force yourself, okay...
It feels like I’m just getting by day to day, doing the bare minimum. Time is just passing by, but the sadness doesn’t change, so I keep thinking that I want to disappear from this world.
Sorry, our messages crossed. I see... that’s what you’ve been thinking...
Yes. I’m so sad I can’t stand it.
I imagine it may be all you can do just to get through the minimum of what needs to be done... Feelings of sadness don’t heal easily, do they...
Yes.
When your husband was still here, what were your days like? (Only what you feel comfortable sharing is okay.)

On weekdays, we’d eat together at home and watch TV, and on weekends we’d go cycling or do active things. We both liked drinking, so we’d go out for drinks and talk about all kinds of things and laugh a lot. That’s the kind of couple we were.
I see. I can really feel that you shared the things you enjoyed, were very close, and spent your time together happily.
Yes, it was so much fun. We don’t have children, so suddenly being alone is painful. Will this sadness ever go away...?
When you think back on the days you spent together, suddenly being alone must feel painful and exhausting... You’re wanting this sadness to go away...
Yes. It’s too painful, and I want to get out of this sadness. I think he would want me to be smiling. But even though I know that, it’s just too painful, and I don’t know what to do.

Even though you know your husband would want you to be smiling, it’s still natural to feel so sad that you don’t know what to do... But I thought that feeling that way may be because you loved your husband that deeply.
Yes, I loved him so much.

Yes, I could really feel that as I listened to you. For now, rather than trying to force yourself to smile, I wonder if you could talk here about your feelings for your husband and face them little by little... How does that sound?

Yes. Thank you. As I talked, I realized that my husband probably would want me to be smiling, and I thought it would be nice if I could become a little more positive, little by little, so that he won’t be sad.

I see. I think the fact that you came here to talk may also mean you’re getting ready to face this little by little. The sadness of losing someone precious may not heal easily, but I hope we can continue thinking together about how you can live alongside those feelings. When you feel pain or sadness, I hope you’ll come here to talk again.
Yes, thank you. Those words mean a lot to me. Talking today made me feel a little lighter. When I feel sad again, I’ll come and talk with you.
Not at all. I’m glad you feel even a little lighter. Please don’t carry this alone—come here when you need to.
Yes, thank you.
Well then, would it be all right to end today’s consultation here?
Yes, that’s okay. Thank you very much! I’m not sure if I was able to be the kind of client you were hoping for, but if there’s another opportunity, I’d be happy to work with you again.
This was very helpful for my learning! Thank you. I’d appreciate it if you could leave an evaluation as well.
Yes, of course. Thank you for today 🙏
Likewise, if there’s another opportunity, I’d be happy to work with you again. Thank you very much. I’ll send the closing message now.

interaction.content: Good morning. Thank you for being here today. We’ll get started when it’s time.
Good morning. Thank you as well for today.
Hello, I’m the counselor. Thank you for coming in for a consultation today. Please feel free to talk about anything here, and know this is a safe place.
Thank you.
To start, could you tell me your age, gender, and what you’d like to talk about?
I’m a woman in my 30s, and I came because of trouble with neighbors. Thank you.
Thank you for telling me. You’re having trouble with neighbors, then. Could you tell me a bit more about that?

Yes. I have two boys, ages 3 and 5, and they’re always running around inside the house or jumping down from the sofa. So, even though it’s the floor below us, I don’t know which apartment it is, but we’ve gotten complaints. I try to tell the children not to run as much as possible, and…

So you’ve been getting complaints from someone downstairs. Even though they’re not your children, that would be difficult. Since children are coming over to play, is this about relationships with other moms?
No, that’s not it. They’re my children.
I’m sorry, I misunderstood. So this is a neighborhood issue with someone on the floor below. You warn your children, but they just don’t really stop?

That’s right. For a moment after I tell them, they get quiet, but before I know it they’re thumping around again. It seems like the person downstairs finds the sounds of our daily life noisy too, and we get complaints regularly through the building manager.
I see. Having to scold them is exhausting, and you’re also having to be mindful of the person downstairs. I can imagine how difficult this must be.
Yes. That’s exactly it.
Is it also difficult not knowing who the complaints are coming from?

Yes. I’ve asked the building manager, but they won’t tell me who it is. So I don’t know if the complaint is from the person directly below us or from next door, and I end up feeling on edge every day.
Not knowing who the complaint is coming from makes you have to be careful about all sorts of things, and you’re feeling on edge. That sounds really painful.
That’s right.
If you knew who it was, you might be able to go say hello, or respond in some way, but since you don’t know who it is, you can’t do anything about it, and that leaves you stuck.
That’s exactly it. I want to apologize directly, but not knowing who it is… that part is really wearing me down… It’s hard.
Yes, of course. It’s wearing you down. You’ve been doing your best every day under such difficult circumstances. By the way, when did this start?
I think it was right around a year ago.
For about a year now—that must have been really hard every day. Have you talked with your partner about it?
Yes. I talked to my husband too. So since the floor is hardwood, we immediately covered it with cushion-type flooring, but it seems like it didn’t have much effect…
I see. You thought it through together and tried what you could do. And when even that doesn’t have much effect, it can feel like you’re at a loss.
That’s right.
You said you feel on edge every day. What else have you been feeling?
I feel sorry, and maybe because I don’t have any emotional room, I get irritated with the children too. The people I feel sorry toward are the neighbors.

You feel sorry toward the neighbors, and toward your children, you’re losing your emotional room and ending up irritated. It sounds like you’re in a situation where you feel that cornered. You’ve really done well to make it this far.
Thank you. Lately we’ve also started considering moving.

When you lose your emotional room and end up irritated with your children, it may feel like you’re in a negative cycle. You’re considering moving, then. Since that came up, how have you been feeling? I’m sorry for asking one question after another.

It’s okay. Yes, that’s right. I want my children to grow up freely and comfortably, so every day I feel self-disgust toward myself for getting irritated. We’re considering moving, but where we live now, the children have a lot of friends and I have a lot of friends too, so it feels hard to make that decision.
Yes. When you want them to grow up freely and comfortably, getting angry makes you feel self-disgust and leaves you with that unsettled feeling.
That’s right. I keep thinking, why do I get so irritated… and I hate that about myself too, and it feels really hard.

I see. If you move, your environment changes a lot, and your friendships would change too, so it’s hard to take that step. It’s an important decision, so I think it’s only natural to feel unsure. You’re a very kind-hearted person, aren’t you. You’re considerate of your neighbors, and you want the children you love to grow up freely and comfortably.
Thank you.

At the same time, when things don’t go the way you hope and you lose your emotional room, I think it’s natural that it becomes painful and exhausting. If there are any other feelings of anxiety or concerns you have, please tell me anything at all.

Yes. Hearing you say that makes me feel a little relieved. My older child is also starting elementary school soon, and he’s looking forward to going with his friends, so if we move, I have to think about school too… It’s a headache.

Your older child, the 5-year-old, is in the final year of kindergarten? He’ll be an elementary school student soon. It’s exciting to see them grow. And in the middle of that, having to think about school too adds even more to your mind and gives you a headache. Are you sleeping and getting rest each day?

That’s right. He’s in his final year, and next is elementary school. Both my child and I will be starting a new life, so if possible, I want to keep living somewhere where we know a lot of people, but… I haven’t really been able to sleep at night.

Yes. With elementary school, there are things to look forward to, but there’s also anxiety about a new environment, so I imagine it would feel more reassuring to have people you know around. You haven’t really been able to sleep. I’m very concerned.

That’s right… My child is shy around people too, so if possible, I want elementary school to be the same place as his friends… Thank you. Only when the children are at kindergarten is there no noise, so I can feel a little relieved, but…

I see. Considering your child’s tendencies too, the current environment feels reassuring. I’m glad there’s at least some time during the day when you can feel a little relieved. That time is the only time when your worries ease a bit.

That’s right… When I think about both my children and myself, I really don’t want to move, but… living while constantly being careful not to make noise is hard too… Yes… only while the children are at kindergarten is there a time when I can feel a little…

You want to put your own family’s life first, but as you go about daily life, issues with neighbors come up too. Because it’s not a problem you can easily separate yourself from, even if you wanted to, I think it becomes painful and exhausting.
Yes. That’s exactly right.
When it comes to the neighborhood issues and moving, are you able to talk things through properly with your husband?
Yes. We do talk about that.
I feel a little reassured that you have a trusted partner close to you.
Thank you. It’s too much to carry alone…
That said, your husband isn’t home all the time, so I think you’re the one who feels the greatest burden in the current situation.
Yes. That’s true.
I hope that while continuing to talk with your husband, you’ll also feel free to come here and talk anytime.
Thank you.
How was it for you to talk through things up to this point today?
Well… I had so much self-disgust from feeling irritated and on edge, but having you listen helped me organize things a little.

The irritation and feeling on edge—I think both are really hard feelings to carry alone. In the midst of that, for a whole year, you’ve thought carefully about what you could do and put it into action. I think you’ve been working very hard.
Yes.

You’ve been being so careful with your neighbors, and then getting irritated with your children… Thank you for finding the courage to come here and talk today. You have a reassuring partner, and you also have this place where you can talk about anything.
Yes. That’s reassuring.
I hope the situation improves even a little, and that your heart starts to feel lighter too.
Thank you. I feel much lighter now.
Please let out those hard feelings as much as you need to. If things get hard—or of course, even before they get hard—please come and talk with us again anytime.
Yes. I’ll come again.
Then, would it be all right if I send the closing message here for today?
That’s fine. Thank you very much.
I’ll be here if you’d like to talk again. Thank you for today.

interaction.content: (Hello. Thank you for making time today. We will start at 3:30 p.m. I look forward to speaking with you.)
(Thank you. I look forward to speaking with you.)
Hello. I’m the counselor. Thank you for coming to talk with me. To start, could you tell me your age, gender, and what you’d like to talk about?
16, male. I’m struggling with orthostatic dysregulation.
Thank you for telling me. So it’s orthostatic dysregulation. What specific symptoms are you struggling with?
I can’t wake up in the morning and I feel unwell in the morning.
(Yes, I’m listening.) I’m sorry. It’s hard not being able to wake up in the morning, isn’t it. Are there any other symptoms you’re struggling with?
That’s about it for symptoms.
I see. How did you find out that you have orthostatic dysregulation?
I was diagnosed at the hospital.
When were you diagnosed?
Since around the upper grades of elementary school.
I see. So you’ve been struggling with those symptoms for several years. Are you going to school?
Sort of.
What is the situation like?
I don’t really understand what you mean.
I’m sorry. When you say “sort of,” do you mean you go while taking days off here and there? Or is it more like you go every day, but arrive late?
Every day, but I’m late.
So even though you’re late, you’re going every day. With having orthostatic dysregulation, what are you struggling with the most right now?
Not being able to wake up in the morning.

It’s really difficult when you can’t wake up in the morning, isn’t it. Are you struggling with being late to school because you can’t wake up in the morning? Or are there other things you’re struggling with?
Being late, yes.
Yes, that makes sense. Is there anything else?
It’s hard to talk about.
I see. You don’t have to force yourself to talk about it. Have you ever talked with your family or people around you about what you’re struggling with?
Yes.
How was it when you tried talking with them?
Nothing changed.
I see. So you feel that even after talking about it, nothing changed. It’s painful when a situation that doesn’t change keeps going. Who did you talk to about it?
Do I have to keep suffering forever?

Of course not. I’d like us to think together about how you can get to a place where you don’t have to suffer like this. You mentioned that you were diagnosed at the hospital—what has your doctor said?
I don’t remember what we talked about in that much detail.
I see. You said it’s been since elementary school—have you been going to the hospital regularly?
Yes.
From elementary school until now, does it feel like your symptoms haven’t changed? Did your doctor talk with you about ways to improve them?
They haven’t changed. They just prescribed medicine.

I see. To summarize what you’ve shared so far, you’ve been struggling with orthostatic dysregulation for several years, since the upper grades of elementary school, and at the hospital they only prescribe medication, while your symptoms have stayed the same. Even when you’ve talked to people around you, nothing has changed, and this painful situation has continued.
Yes.
You said you’re struggling with not being able to wake up in the morning and being late to school. How does being late make you feel?
It hurts.
Yes, yes, it’s painful. Is it painful because you fall behind in class, or because you have less time to spend with friends, or because your body feels so exhausted—or what is it like?
Everything.
Everything... You really have been struggling with this for a long time... In the afternoon, does your body feel okay?
No.
Is it painful in the afternoon too?
No.
So the afternoons are okay. Do you talk with your friends about this?
Yes.
What do your friends say?
Nothing in particular.
I see. So it’s more like they just listen when you talk. What kind of situation do you think would make it so you could feel a little less distressed than you do now?
I don’t know.
Yes, it’s difficult, isn’t it. What kind of things do you talk about with your family?
I don’t know how to answer that.
That was a hard question to understand, wasn’t it. Does it feel like your family is thinking together with you about what to do regarding what you’re struggling with?
I can’t really say either way. They’re busy.
Your family is busy. Do you not have much time to talk with them in daily life?
Yes.
I see... It’s painful to carry what you’re struggling with all by yourself...
Am I going to stay in pain forever from here on out?
I don’t think that’s true. I believe there must be ways to reduce the pain you’re feeling.
I’m tired of hearing nice-sounding words.

It makes sense that you’d be fed up with hearing nothing but nice-sounding words all this time. Our consultation time today is almost over, but if you’re willing, I’d like to continue thinking together with you through this consultation service about ways for you not to have to suffer so much. How would that feel to you?
I’m okay now. Goodbye.

I see. I believe there is no one who has to keep suffering forever. I believe there must be a way for you not to have to suffer so much. It may sound like just nice words, but if you ever feel like you do want to talk again, please feel free to reach out anytime. Thank you for coming to talk with me today.
(Thank you for your work. Please proceed with ending it as it is.)
(Thank you. I’ll send the closing message.)

interaction.content: Hello. Thank you for seeing me today.
Hello. Thank you as well. When it’s time, we’ll go ahead and begin.
Yes.
Hello. Thank you for coming in for a consultation today. First, could you tell me your age and gender?
Hello. I’m a woman in my 40s.
Thank you. Then, could you tell me what you’d like to talk about today?
I’m currently working part-time, but I’m not sure whether I should quit...
I see, that’s what you’re thinking right now.
Yes.
What kind of work are you doing now?
I work as an operator for a cosmetics mail-order company.
I see. Is your work busy?
Yes, it gets busy when ads go out.
I see. So there are times when it gets busy.
Yes, that’s right.
Could you tell me just a little more about why you’ve started wanting to leave your current job?
Yes. I mainly take order calls, but sometimes complaint calls get mixed in, and when I take those calls, it really wears me down mentally.
I see. Handling complaints is painful, isn’t it.
Yes. It really is.
Do you get complaint calls about once a day?
Yes, we do. I seem to be especially likely to get them, and I often end up taking complaint calls.
I see. It’s exhausting to deal with complaints, isn’t it.
Yes. It gets me down.
I can imagine.
Yes.
Is handling complaints the main reason you want to leave your current job?
Yes, dealing with complaint calls. There are people who are fine even when they take complaint calls, but I get really down, and even after I go home I keep dragging it with me, and it’s exhausting.
That sounds really painful. I think dealing with complaints is very hard, but there are people who are okay with it?
Yes, there are.
There may be some people who are okay with handling complaints, but still, I think dealing with complaints is really quite painful.
Yes... I’ve seen coworkers crying when I go to the bathroom.
I see. So handling complaints really is very harsh.
Yes...
Have you already thought about around when you might quit?
I haven’t thought specifically yet about when I would quit, but my mind is constantly wavering.
I see. How is your physical condition right now? Are you doing okay?
When I think about going to work, I can’t sleep at night, and when I notice it, my breathing has become shallow, so I consciously take deep breaths.
I see. That sounds really painful.
Yes, it is.
But you notice that your breathing has become shallow and try to take deep breaths, so you’re trying to cope with it yourself.
Rather than coping, I guess it feels like my body reacts and I take deep breaths because it gets hard to breathe.
I see. But not being able to sleep at night is really hard, isn’t it.
It’s painful.
On your days off, are you able to relax or let your body rest?
Yes, I do things to change my mood, and it’s fun only while I’m doing them. But when I remember it, I get this heavy, gloomy feeling.
I see. So you remember it sometimes. That shows how painful handling complaints is for you.
Yes. Even when I talk to friends about it, they say I’m “worrying too much,” and that hurts me even more, so I can’t tell them.
That sounds painful. For you, it’s that distressing, so being told you’re “worrying too much” must feel really sad.
That’s right. I end up thinking, is it my fault for worrying too much?
I don’t think it’s your fault. I think handling complaints is just that painful.
Hearing you say that makes me feel saved.
No, I really do think handling complaints is very hard.
On the phone, you can’t see the other person, so I think it’s easier for customers to say things. They throw really harsh words at me.
That is painful. Because they can’t see the other person, they probably feel like saying more and more.

Yes, I think so. It seems like they’re just venting their anger. Depending on the content, I can’t handle it myself, so I transfer it to my supervisor, but by that time, apparently the customer has let off steam and speaks calmly.
I see. That’s painful. I’m sorry I couldn’t resolve anything, but we’re almost out of time. Is there anything you feel you haven’t had a chance to say?
No, thank you for listening to me. I’m okay.
Thank you. How was it for you to talk about it?
Yes, I was able to let a little of it out, so I feel better.
I’m glad to hear that. Then we’ll end here for today. Thank you very much.
Yes, thank you very much.

interaction.content: Good morning. Thank you for being here today.
Thank you.
When it’s time, we’ll go ahead and begin. Hello, I’m the counselor. Thank you for meeting with me today. If you don’t mind, could you first let me know your age and gender?
Thank you. I’m 23 years old, male.
Thank you. What would you like to talk about today?
I can’t seem to feel motivated at work.
I see… About when did you start feeling that way?
Around three months ago, roughly.
I see… three months… It must feel heavy even getting up in the morning…
That’s right.
Yes… that sounds really hard… Is there anything you can think of that may have triggered it?
Honestly, I can’t really remember…
I see… That must make it even harder, not knowing what to do. You mentioned that you don’t feel motivated at work. How are things after work or on your days off?
After work it’s not that different, but on my days off I don’t especially feel it.

So you’re able to rest properly on your days off, then. I’m a little relieved to hear that. So for today’s consultation, would it be okay to say that you’d like to think about how you might be able to feel motivated? If that’s not quite right, please feel free to say so.
That’s fine.
Then I’d like to think through it together with you. Would it be okay if I ask a few more questions about the situation?
That’s fine.
Thank you. When did you start your current job?
A little over about two years ago.
I see. How did you feel about the job at the beginning?
Well, there were a lot of things I had to do, so it was hard, but it felt worthwhile.
I see… Do you still feel that sense of purpose now?
Honestly, not so much now…
I see… Is it that the difficulty of having too much to do is outweighing that sense of purpose?
No, it’s the opposite. I’ve started having less to do, and I don’t feel that it’s worthwhile.
Oh, is that right! …When you say you’ve started having less to do, could you tell me a bit more about why that is?
At first it was kind of like training, and I had to study a lot of different things, but now that’s gone, so there’s less for me to do…
I see. So there are fewer chances to learn new things like during training, and now it’s just the actual work, so you’re not feeling a sense of purpose… is that the kind of situation?
That’s about right.
I see… Not feeling a sense of purpose can make it feel like you’re losing the energy to go to work too… How are your relationships at the workplace?
My relationships are good.
I see. Have you talked to anyone about this?
I haven’t talked to anyone about it.
I see… You’ve been carrying this on your own, and that must have been painful. Is there a reason you haven’t talked to anyone at work about it?
I don’t really want to tell people at work, “I can’t feel motivated.”
Yes… Why is that?

I don’t think I’d get a very good response even if I talked to them, and since we work at the same workplace, I don’t think it would feel very good for them to have someone come to them saying, “I can’t feel motivated.”

That’s how you see it, then. You’re being considerate of the people around you. I think the fact that you’re struggling with “not feeling motivated” means that you want to feel motivated, that you want to do more. So I don’t think it would be a bad thing to talk to a supervisor or senior colleague in terms of, “I want to work with more of a sense of purpose.” What do you think?
I see… Now that you put it that way, that might actually be a little better.
Yes. Listening to you, I feel that you’re very sincere, and that you really want to work hard at learning and at your job. I get the sense that you’re a very positive person.
Positive, you think…?

Yes, that’s how it felt to me. You said that when training was hard, it actually felt more worthwhile, and the fact that you’re struggling because you don’t feel that sense of purpose makes me feel that you want to do more, that you want your work to feel fulfilling. I also got the sense that you may feel guilty about not feeling a sense of purpose yourself. How does that sound?
That may be true.

Yes. I feel that because you’re very considerate of the people around you, and because you have that sense of guilt, the feeling of “I can’t feel motivated” is standing out more than your original positive attitude. When we’re working, there are inevitably times when our motivation goes down. On the other hand, I think there will definitely also be times when your motivation rises again, even more than before. I think your feeling of wanting to have more of a sense of purpose, wanting to do your work with more motivation, is a very good thing. So perhaps you could start by talking with a senior colleague or supervisor about those feelings. What do you think?
Yes. I’ll try talking to someone a little.
Yes, please do. We’ve come to the end of our time, but you can continue this conversation with another counselor as well. If you’d like, please come back to talk more about it.
Thank you.
Thank you for coming in to talk with us today. Thank you. (I’m sorry about the end there. Thank you for your time.) (We’ll end here. Thank you.)

interaction.content: Hello, I’m the counselor. To start, could you tell me your age and gender?
Hello. I’m 38, female.
Thank you. What would you like to talk about today?
Yes. I’ve been struggling with how to relate to the mother of one of my daughter’s classmates.
I see. Would it be okay if I asked you to tell me more? You can start wherever feels easiest to talk about.

Yes. I’ve known her for about four years now, but if I say anything that’s even a little different from her own way of thinking—like, a different opinion?—she gets very upset and starts denying what I’m saying.
Yes, that must be hard to keep up with... And it doesn’t feel good to be dismissed. So you’ve known her for four years.

She lives in a different district from me, but this is something I heard from someone else—if someone in her own district says or does something she doesn’t like, or doesn’t behave in a way she thinks is appropriate, she’ll send them a long email protesting it at around 2 in the morning. So, she doesn’t really have a very good reputation with the people around her...
Oh my... the person on the receiving end would be worn out by that. Yes, that wouldn’t be seen in a good light...

When the person told someone in the same district about that, it spread all at once among the mothers in the area, and it seems like people say quite a lot about her behind her back. So it seems like she doesn’t really have many people she can rely on, and she contacts me often.
I see. So everyone is feeling similar things about her. I imagine that because you’re kind, you’ve become someone she relies on.
So the people around me who are worried about me tell me I should keep my distance. Maybe I just don’t know how to get away...
The people around you are worried about you too, then.
Yes. They do look out for me. At school events and things, I end up being next to her the whole time.
It sounds like there are a lot of kind people around you as well. That makes sense, since your children are classmates. Do you feel like you want to get away from her?

Honestly, I want to cut off the relationship, but when I think about her personality and how she usually acts and speaks, and also because of the children, I think what feels best right now is that I want to keep some distance.

Yes, so right now you’re feeling like it would be good if you could keep some distance. At the moment, how do you respond when she invites you to things? Since your children are involved too, it’s hard to completely cut off the relationship, isn’t it.

Yes... If I turn down her invitations too often, I don’t know what she might say, so at this point I accept once every few times. In that sense, during the pandemic, when everyone was staying home, it was a relief. Even when they move on to junior high school, it’ll still be the local public school, so the relationship will probably continue for a while yet.
Yes, that makes sense. It would be hard if you upset her too. The timing with COVID was helpful in that way. I see, so it seems like the involvement will continue for a while.
Actually, there were about two times before when she got upset during our LINE exchanges and blocked me.
I see! She even blocks you... That must be emotionally exhausting.
So when she gets really angry, she stops taking in my opinions at all... At that time, she didn’t unblock me for about a week, so it was complicated. Honestly, it’s really mentally tiring...

Yes, I can understand that. Being pushed around like that, of course you would feel tired. Because you’re a kind person who thinks about your child and also takes in the feelings of the people around you who are worried about you, I think that makes it even more emotionally draining.
I wonder if I’m really kind... Sometimes I think maybe I’m just scared of her and unreliable... Like, if I cut off the relationship, will it affect my child? Things like that.
That’s not true. Anyone would feel nervous about upsetting someone like her. And yes, the impact on your child is especially worrying.

I appreciate you saying that. A friend of mine was criticized by her before, and since then she even says things about my friend that aren’t true. At that time, I was really angry. So when I said something to defend my friend—because she was saying things that weren’t facts—she completely blew up at me. She said, “Aren’t you on my side?”
So something like that happened. That’s far too unreasonable, and it’s awful toward your friend. She probably has a rather childish way of thinking.

Rather than childish, I get the impression that she doesn’t really trust people very much. Also, she’s not good at expressing herself. It’s like she’s saying, “Read the room for me!” She even says bad things about my friend’s daughter. Even though she hasn’t done anything.

I see. Thank you for telling me. It’s impressive—you’ve really observed her carefully. That’s the only way she knows how to express herself, then. You mentioned that currently, when she invites you and things like that, you accept once every few times, but...
I think she’s an awkward person.
So the question is how to relate to her going forward, perhaps? Because she has a kind person like you by her side, she’s probably leaning on you. I’m sorry, I sent that twice.
I gathered a lot of information about how to deal with this type of person, but most of the answers were things like it’s better not to get involved, or to keep a good distance.
You took action by gathering information and so on. That’s wonderful. You do want to keep some distance...
At the moment, I don’t contact her from my side, and I’m trying to keep distance in my own way, but she keeps wanting things from me...
I see. You want to keep your distance, but that makes it difficult.
I’ve seen those weak parts of her too, and I also have this thought that maybe she isn’t a bad person at heart. That’s why it’s hard. It’s just that her way of living is awkward...
I see. So you’re also seeing her clearly beyond just the bad parts. Those are parts that people around her don’t know about.

That’s right. Parts that people around her can’t see... parts you wouldn’t know unless you were involved with her. I’m the type who likes to take care of people, so cutting someone off just doesn’t really feel right to me. That’s why I’ve been worrying about this for a long time.

I see. You’ve been struggling with this for a long time, so it must have been painful. Thank you for coming to talk with me despite that. We’re almost at the end of our time, but how was today for you?

Oh, it’s already time. I understand. This time, by having you listen to me here, I wanted to check in with my true feelings. I still don’t have an answer about what I should actually do, but having you listen has made me feel a little lighter. Thank you.

I’m glad to hear that. Thank you for today. You’re a kind person, so please don’t carry this alone—feel free to come back anytime to talk or consult again. We can also continue the consultation from here, so please tell me anything you’d like.
Yes. Thank you.

Thank you for today. I hope you’re able to spend your time feeling even a little more at ease. (Thank you for your hard work. Thank you for responding on short notice today. I’d be grateful if you could leave feedback in the comments. Thank you.)

Yes. I can’t let my children see me looking troubled. (Thank you as well, and good work today. This situation is something I personally experienced three years ago. In reality, I had known her for five years. Thank you for today. Please end the role-play.)
(Thank you for sharing your valuable real-life experience. I’ll reflect on it and learn from it.)

interaction.content: (Good evening. Thank you for making time today. We’ll begin when it’s time. I appreciate your cooperation.)
Thank you as well for your time. I appreciate it.
Good evening. I’m the counselor. Thank you for coming to talk with me. To start, could you tell me your age, gender, and what you’d like to discuss?
Good evening, I’m a 33-year-old housewife. I’ve been feeling down, and I can’t seem to feel positive.
I see. It’s hard when you can’t feel positive, isn’t it? What has been going on?
Part of it is that I haven’t been feeling well since giving birth, but I guess I can’t think of my child as cute... I’m wondering if maybe I’m kind of depressed.
Mm-hmm, I see. After giving birth, your body is going through a lot, and caring for a newborn is really hard. Are you able to sleep at all?
Well, I’m not really getting much sleep, or rather, my child wakes up many times during the night, so it’s hard.

You haven’t been sleeping much, then. When you’re woken up many times at night, you end up sleep-deprived, and that must be really hard on your body, too... In that kind of situation, I think it’s very understandable that your mood would sink. When did you start feeling like you couldn’t be positive?
Since I gave birth and came back home.
I see. Is there anyone who helps you with housework or childcare?
No, there’s no one. My husband is busy with work, so I’m always alone, and I don’t have any friends nearby...
I see... Not having anyone to rely on must feel really lonely. How old is your baby now?
Yes, everything is new to me, and things like giving the baby a bath are hard, and anyway, I just end up feeling so distressed. My child is exactly one month old.
Mm-hmm, when everything is new, there are so many things you don’t know, and it can make you anxious.
Yes. It seems like everyone thinks their child is cute, but I can’t feel that way...
At one month old, there is still a lot of crying at night, and it’s a difficult time with so many things you’re not used to.
That’s right. I’m not used to it, and I’m anxious.

When you’re handling unfamiliar childcare on your own, and your body is also in a difficult state, I think it can be natural to feel that way. How do you feel about not being able to think of your child as cute?
Well... it feels like I’m looking at things objectively, and I wonder, will I be able to think they’re cute from now on? Right now I’m close to emotionless...
I see. When you don’t have any emotional space, sometimes feelings just don’t come up. Is there anyone you can talk to about your current situation?
There isn’t anyone I can talk to. There aren’t people around me who have children.
I see. You’ve been carrying these painful feelings on your own. You mentioned your husband is busy, but on his days off and so on, how is he involved with housework and childcare?

It seems like he doesn’t understand how hard it is with a child... Even when the baby wakes up in the middle of the night, he sleeps next to us. My husband doesn’t do housework. He can’t cook either...
I see... That would leave you feeling unsettled, wouldn’t it... You’d want him to wake up with you. I see. So you’ve been doing your best with both housework and childcare on your own.
I thought I could manage it, but I didn’t think I would end up feeling this way.
Mm-hmm, it’s confusing when you notice changes in your own feelings, isn’t it? Especially after giving birth, hormones can have an effect, and I think emotions can shift more easily.
I wonder if that’s true. I was thinking I’d start working again soon, but feeling like this, I can’t get motivated to do anything... I’m at a loss.
Is there anything about how you’d like to relate to your child, if you could, like, “I’d like to be involved with them in this kind of way”?
Right now I don’t have any image of how I’ll relate to my child. It’s just hard right now...

Mm-hmm, of course. Right now you’re carrying so much on your own and things are really difficult, so I think it’s completely understandable that you can’t picture it. When you want to start working soon but the days continue where you can’t feel positive, it seems like that would make you feel impatient too...
I can’t see what’s ahead... I don’t know what would make my feelings clear up, or what would make things feel enjoyable.
That makes sense. When you can’t see what’s ahead, it can make you anxious too. What are you hoping would change about your current situation?
I want these feelings to become more positive, and I want to be able to go out freely.
Mm-hmm, I see. One month after giving birth, it’s hard to go out much, and you want a change of pace too, don’t you?
Yes. I want to go out. But I’m scared to go outside with my child.
Going out with a one-month-old baby brings up all kinds of worries, doesn’t it? What kinds of things feel scary to you?
I’ve never used a stroller, and I worry about what I’d do if the baby suddenly cried, and where I can go with a child.
I see. You don’t know whether your baby will like the stroller, and you don’t know when they might start crying, so it makes sense that you’d feel anxious.
Yes.
For example, do you have information about a city-run child-rearing support center or local parenting support events?
There’s a city hall near my house.
I see. If you talk with someone at city hall, they may be able to tell you about places that are easy to go to with your baby. How does that sound?
Yes, that’s true. I don’t have any information about child-rearing, so I thought maybe I’ll try going with the stroller.

Mm-hmm, if you go, I think you may be able to get various kinds of information. I know using a stroller for the first time may feel worrying, but crying is a baby’s job, so I don’t think you need to worry too much about it.
I see. Somehow, I feel a little relieved. Now that I have a reason to go out, I think I’ll try going.

I’m glad to hear that. With no one to rely on, I think you’ve really done your best on your own through this difficult postpartum period. You came in with the concern that you couldn’t feel positive, but the fact that you now feel like trying to use the stroller and go to city hall seems to me like your feelings have become at least a little more positive. It’s about time for us to finish, but is there anything else you’d like to talk about before we end?
No, I’m okay. Having you listen to feelings I couldn’t tell anyone else has made me feel lighter. Thank you.

I hope that going out with your baby will help you feel even a little refreshed and become an enjoyable time. If you feel down again or feel like you want to talk, please come back anytime. Thank you for coming to talk with me today.
Thank you too.
(Thank you for your time today. I appreciate you giving me this valuable time. Would it be all right if I send the closing message?)
Yes.

interaction.content: (Thank you for being here today. We’ll begin at one o’clock.)
(Yes, thank you.) (Thank you.)
Hello. I’m the counselor. If you don’t mind, could you start by telling me your age and gender?
I’m 22, male.
Thank you. And for this session, what would you like me to call you?
Please call me Yu.
Thank you again. What brings you here today?
I’m self-conscious about not being good at communication and having shallow relationships with people.
I see. That must be weighing on you.
Yes.
Would it be okay if I asked a little more about that? Yu, when did you start feeling concerned about communication?
I think I started thinking about it seriously around when I was 20.
I see. Is there anything you can think of that may have triggered it?
I’ve thought about it, but it wasn’t really a trigger exactly... it was more like I gradually started realizing what kinds of things I’m not good at.

I see. So something that had kind of been bothering you for a while became something you started to notice around age 20—that because you weren’t able to communicate well, your relationships weren’t really deepening... is that right?
Yes. I’d always thought I wasn’t good at it, but because of things like having few friends, I started to realize that I’m really bad at it.
I see... Yu, how do you feel about that situation yourself?
I know it’s not like having a lot of friends is automatically good, but it still bothers me.
I see. It’s true that people with a lot of friends can look like they have really fulfilling lives.
That’s right.
I really understand that feeling. There’s even that song, like, “Can I make 100 friends?”
Yes. I only really spend time with people I’m very close to, but there are people who can hang out or go drinking with others who are more like acquaintances, and I feel envious of that.
I see. So even if the number is small, you do have people you can talk to about anything.
Yes. But everyone moved to different places for work, so they’re not nearby now.
I see. That must make it feel even lonelier. Yu, specifically, what would you like to do from here?
I want to make new friends.
I see. Are you working now?
Yes.
Would it be okay to ask what kind of work you do?
It’s hotel-related.
I see. Is there anyone at your company who seems like you might get along with them, or someone you’d like to become friends with?
Not right now. During work it’s basically individual tasks, so there are almost no chances to talk.
I see.
Yes.
With people from work, it might be difficult, because if you talk about private things, you may worry that other people could find out. Yu, do you have any hobbies?
I have various hobbies.
That’s wonderful. Are you participating in any circles or groups related to your hobbies?
I did when I was a student, but now I’m in such a rural area that even if I look, there aren’t any groups like that nearby.
I see. This is one approach I use—would it be okay if I suggested it?
Yes.
Thank you. Since we’re in the middle of the pandemic, online could be okay too, but would it be possible to first try joining some kind of new community?
It’s possible, but I feel a little scared too.
That makes sense. Getting involved with something new and with new people can feel a little scary.
Yes.

Yes, I understand. Actually, in our daily lives, there are ways in which we’re “playing roles,” and when getting involved with something new or new people, there’s a communication method where you consciously create a bit of a “new character” for yourself.
I see.
Yes. This is something I’ve actually tried myself, but I’m not very good at smiling, so I tried something like playing the role of “someone whose smile suits them.”
I see. So maybe I could try playing someone who isn’t bad at talking?

Yes. For example, if you think, “I’m going to become someone whose smile suits them,” you can end up thinking too seriously, like, “I have to become a kind person,” or trying to change even how you feel, which makes it difficult. But if you approach it like “playing pretend,” it can actually go surprisingly well.
So it’s important not to take it too heavily, too.

Yes. Also, “someone who’s good at talking” is a little vague, so first, if you change your clothes or the way you use your voice a little, and approach it from something like “playing a sociable person,” your feelings may naturally follow along.
I see, yes.
Yes. To do that, people who already know you might be surprised, so it may be easier to try joining a new community while “pretending to be a sociable person.”
I think I could try that.

I’m glad. However, if it stays as “pretending” forever, it can get tiring, so once you start becoming closer with people, little by little, you might reveal, “Actually, I’m not very good at relationships,” and I think that may help you build relationships that are both broad and deep.
I see. That way, it doesn’t seem like I’d have to keep staying on edge so much, so it feels like less of a hurdle.
Was that helpful?
Yes, I think I’m able to think about making friends a little more casually now.
If anything else comes up, please feel free to come back anytime. Would it be all right to end today’s consultation here?
Yes, that’s fine. Thank you.
Thank you for talking with me today. (Thank you. Would it be okay to end the role-play?)
(Thank you as well. It’s okay to end.)
(I learned a great deal. Thank you.)

interaction.content: (Good evening. Thank you for being here today. We’ll begin when it’s time.)
(Thank you.)
Hello. I’m the counselor. Thank you for coming today. To start, could you tell me your age, gender, and what you’d like to talk about?
12, girl, I don’t want to go to school.
Thank you for telling me. Are you in junior high school now?
I’m a first-year junior high student.
I see. About when did you start feeling like you didn’t want to go to school?
Since the day I started.
I see. So you became a junior high school student this spring, and since then you’ve been feeling like you don’t want to go to school.
Yes. I don’t want to go tomorrow either.
Yeah, it’s that hard for you... Was there something that triggered it?
Well, yeah. I can’t make any close friends, and I can’t get into any groups.
I see. That would make it hard to go to school.
Yes.
By the way, how was it when you were in elementary school?
Elementary school was fun because I was in the same class as a friend I was close with.
I see. Did you and that friend end up being separated?
Yeah.
I see. When that happens, it can feel hard to make friends from scratch.
Yeah. I might never make close friends anymore.
I see, I see... That’s how you’re feeling right now.
Yeah. I’m not good at starting conversations myself.
I see. It takes a lot of courage to talk to someone you’ve never talked to before.
And the groups are already formed, so I might be a bother.
That’s how you’re feeling right now. What kinds of things make you think you’d be a bother?
If I joined partway through, I wonder if it would mess up the group’s relationships.
Mm-hmm, that’s how you’re feeling right now.
Yeah. I don’t know what I should do.
Since the environment has changed, it might not just be you—everyone may be confused or anxious too, and they may still be in the middle of making new friendships.
I wonder if that’s true. I can hear them sounding like they’re having fun, but I pretend I don’t hear it.
I see, I see. Do you feel like you’d like to have fun together with them?
I do think it would be nice if I could join in.

I see. It takes a lot of courage to join a circle, but if somewhere inside you feel like you’d like to enjoy things together, one option might be to watch for a good time and try talking to them. I really don’t think you would be a bother.
I wonder. I don’t know when, or what I should say.
Yeah, you said you’re not good at starting conversations yourself. It can be hard to figure out how to start talking to someone...
Yeah...
Since it’s a new class right now and you probably don’t know everyone yet, I wonder if starting with a self-introduction could be one way. What do you think?
A self-introduction?
For example, “My name is ___, but what should I call you?” or something like that.
Oh, I see. I wonder if I can do that.
If that seems difficult, it might be good to start by just saying hello first.
I might be able to say hello.
Even just saying “Good morning” might become a chance to start talking.
Yeah. I’ll try my best.
Mm-hmm. If you think, “I have to say something!” it might feel exhausting, so starting with “Good morning” might be a good first step.
Yeah. I wonder if they’ll answer.
Yeah, anxious feelings come up too, don’t they.
Yeah, it’s a little scary, but I don’t want to be alone forever either.
I see, I see. I can tell that you do want to have fun together with them. At first, talking to someone can be scary, and it takes courage.
Yeah. But I’ll try.
Try it once, and please tell me how it went. Then we can come up with another plan together.
Okay. Thank you. If it doesn’t work, I’ll come talk again.
We won’t know whether it doesn’t work until you try, so for now, I’d like you to practice greeting them with a smile. Please come talk anytime, just like today.
Okay. Thank you very much. First, I’ll do my best to try talking to them.
Mm-hmm, try it at your own pace. Thank you as well. I’ll be here if you’d like to come again.
Yes. Thank you for today.
(Thank you for the role-play. I learned a lot from it. We’ll end here.)
(Thank you as well. Good work today.)
