interaction.content: (Good morning. Thank you for being here today. We’ll begin when it’s time.)
Thank you.
Good morning. I’m the counselor. To start, could you tell me your age and gender?
I’m 14, female.
Thank you. You’re 14, so would that make you a second-year junior high school student?
Yes.
Thank you. What brings you here today?
Yes, living feels exhausting, so I came here.
I see. That must feel really painful. Could you tell me about those exhausted feelings?
I feel like maybe I’m not needed.
You’ve been feeling that way. I’d like to understand more about how you feel, so would it be okay if I asked you a few questions?
Yes.
When do you feel like, “I’m not needed…”?
Every day.
You feel that way every day. That’s really hard.
Yes.
For example, is it in your school life, or at home? What kinds of times do you feel it most strongly?
School, I guess, if I had to choose.
You feel it often in your school life. Are things going okay with your friends?
Yeah, they’re okay, I guess.
I see. In your school life, what kinds of situations make you feel like you’re not needed...?
It’s all the time, but I’m scared people will say bad things about me.
It’s painful when people say bad things about you. Has something like that happened before?
Rather than before, I feel like they’re still saying things about me now.

You feel that way even now. That would make you anxious. What makes you feel like they’re still saying things about you? If there are things your friends do, like certain behaviors that make you feel that way, could you tell me?
Yes, they look over at me and laugh, or whisper to each other. And before, they said bad things about me loud enough for me to hear.
So that’s happened… It makes sense that you would feel hurt. Has the whispering and saying bad things been going on for a while?
Since I became a second-year junior high student, I guess.
I see. You’ve been doing your best through this for a long time. Were things going okay with those friends when you were in your first year of junior high?
I do have friends normally. The ones saying bad things are boys.
I see. I’m sorry for misunderstanding. Are those boys your classmates?
Yes.
Was there some kind of trigger or reason?
I don’t know what started it… But I heard them saying bad things about my face, and it made me feel really awful.
Not knowing what started it, you’ve endured this all this time… It must have been really exhausting.
Yes…
Is it okay if I summarize what we’ve talked about so far?
Yes.

Some boys in your class have been saying bad things about you, and some of it was about your appearance, and they even said it on purpose so you could hear. That has made you feel really hurt. And because of that, you’ve been feeling like you’re not needed, and it’s become really hard.
Yes, that’s right.
Is there anyone who knows how hard this has been for you?
I don’t think so.
I see. I wonder if you’ve been trying hard not to let your friends notice.
Do I really have to try harder?
When I said “trying hard,” I meant that you had been hiding your painful feelings in front of your friends. When you say “try hard,” what do you think that means?
There are a lot of cute girls around me, and they have boyfriends and seem like they’re having fun. But I have a mean-looking face and I’m gloomy, so I wonder if I can’t be like that.
You think of “trying hard” as making an effort to become cute.
I don’t think I can become cute, so I don’t know. I’m not good at studying or sports either. I don’t have anything.
That’s how you feel. When you think that way, it makes you feel really hurt, doesn’t it.
Yes, that’s right. I think the girls around me are amazing.
What kinds of things make you think they’re amazing? I’d like to hear.
They’re cute, and they have boyfriends and seem like they’re having fun. They’re good at studying and athletic too. They have a lot of friends, and I think that’s nice.
So there are girls around you who seem able to do everything. I got the sense that you might also admire them in some way. How does that sound?
I think that’s true.
Yes. They look like they’re really shining, don’t they.
Yes.
Among appearance, looks, sports, and studying, is there anything you most want to improve?
It would be nice if I could do all of them, but I think it’s probably impossible for me.
You feel like it might be impossible. It takes courage, doesn’t it.
Yes...
But in talking with you, I’ve also sensed a feeling of “I want to change.” How does that sound?
Well, yes. But I can’t change my appearance, so I guess there’s nothing I can do about that.
You feel that you can’t change your appearance. But you also want to change. That’s difficult, isn’t it. It’s almost been an hour now—how was it for you to talk today?
It was the first time I was able to talk about my worries, so that was good.
Thank you for sharing something that was hard to talk about. Even just letting out painful feelings can help you sort through how you feel, so please come here to talk again.
Yes, I understand.
Let’s talk again. I’ll be here waiting.
Yes.

(Thank you for today. If there was anything you wanted me to hear more about, or if you have thoughts on how it would have been better to proceed, I’d appreciate it if you could write that in your feedback. Thank you.)
Thank you for your time. Thank you very much.

I can’t start conversations myself. Right now, people talk to me, and then I talk with them.

Really just a few. I don’t even remember what we talked about. I’m so nervous that my head feels foggy.

I hate myself for getting this nervous.

I like reading books.
Books! I love reading too. What genre of books do you like?

Yes. I have a really strong anxiety about whether I’ll be able to manage.

Thank you.
We’ll end here.
Yes. Thank you very much.

Going back to what you were saying, when you say what you’re saying doesn’t get through to the other person, do you mean it feels like 100% of what you want to say isn’t being conveyed? Or is it more that they misunderstand what you say...?
There’s no misunderstanding. It gets across to them 100%. It’s just that sometimes the other person isn’t listening and isn’t paying attention. And then I always get blamed for it.
I see. Even though you’re telling them what you need to tell them, they aren’t listening, and then later they blame you, saying things like, “I didn’t hear that”... That does feel kind of unfair.
It’s so unfair that I get sick of it.
Yes, it’s completely understandable that you’d get sick of it. When you talk with them, is it mainly about work-related matters?
It’s mostly about work.
I see. By the way, who are you usually talking with—supervisors, subordinates, or someone else?
Mainly my supervisors.
Talking to a supervisor already takes a lot of care as it is, so if that happens, it would really wear you down... What kind of people have your supervisors tended to be?
Yes. I do have to be careful. And when things turn out like this, it wears me out emotionally.
It wears you out emotionally and makes you fed up, doesn’t it.
At this point, I think I’m the one who’s no good.

You’re struggling so much that it makes you feel that way, aren’t you. I’m sorry, this is repeating my earlier question, but what kind of type have your supervisors tended to be? Moody, or always seeming busy, things like that...
They’re always busy.

I see, always busy... It can be hard to even find the right timing to talk to them, can’t it. By the way, aside from your supervisors, how is your communication with, for example, friends or family? Do you ever feel like what you’re saying isn’t getting through?
I communicate normally with them. It gets through.

I see. Then, to organize things a little, would it be fair to say that at work, even though you tell your always-busy supervisor what you need to tell them, they aren’t listening, so it doesn’t get through, and then they blame you later—and that’s painful, and you want to do something about it?
Yes, that’s right.
Thank you. By the way, when you usually talk to them, what kind of way do you start the conversation?
What kind of way? Could you give me an example of what you mean?

That was hard to picture, wasn’t it? I’m sorry. For example, before getting into the conversation, whether you add a small step like saying, “Do you have a moment?” and what the beginning of the conversation is usually like...
I see. That’s what you mean. I always ask, “Do you have a moment?”

Right, of course—you’re being very considerate about that. Even so, if they don’t listen, it does feel awful. As advice to help keep you from being blamed even a little afterward, this is something I’ve done in the past too: if possible, after telling them verbally, leave a note or email, so that you have a “log” showing that “I told the other person”...
Yes. I haven’t done that before.

Telling someone verbally is easy, and since it’s face-to-face, there’s also the good part that you can feel you’ve clearly told them. But with someone who’s busy, this method can also be effective. It’s like protecting yourself so they can’t say, “I didn’t hear that”...
I see.
Depending on the work environment, it may be difficult to leave a log in a way other than verbally... but if it’s possible, I’d like you to try it.
Yes, that’s true. I’ve quit my job now, but I’ll try it at my next job.
I’m sincerely rooting for you, Nakai, and I hope your concerns about communicating with your supervisors ease even a little, and that you’ll be able to continue working with more stability.
Thank you.
I hope you find a good next workplace. But don’t rush! Since we’ve reached the time, we’ll end here. Thank you!
Thank you.

interaction.content: (Good evening, thank you for meeting with me today.)
Thank you.
Good evening, I’m the counselor. Thank you for coming to talk with me. To start, could you tell me your age and gender?
I’m 14, female.
Thank you. What would you like to talk about today?
I’m struggling with something about my friends.
I see. You only have to share what you feel comfortable with, but could you tell me what kind of thing you’re struggling with?
Even when I’m with my friends, it’s not fun...
I see, I see. Was there something that triggered that?

Hmm... there wasn’t really a trigger, but when I’m with them, they talk behind people’s backs or gossip... There are three of us who are close, but I often get left out too, and it’s just not fun somehow.
I see. When you can’t have enjoyable conversations even though you’re together, it can start to feel painful to be with them, can’t it. When that happens, how does it make you feel?
I think, we don’t really fit, I want to go home.
That makes sense. I understand why you’d feel like going home.
Yes... I don’t have the same sense of humor as everyone else either.
I see. When your ways of thinking are different, it’s not fun being together, and it can get tiring, can’t it. Have you been friends with them for a long time?
About a year.
I see. When did you start feeling like you didn’t really fit with them?
Recently. Sometimes it feels like the two of them are in their own world...
I see. It must feel kind of lonely, like you’re being left all by yourself. When they get into their own world, how does that make you feel?
I think it’s boring. I also wonder why they go into their own world when I’m right there.
I see. That must feel really unpleasant.
Rather than unpleasant, it feels uncomfortable to watch.

That makes sense. Even though you’re right there in front of them, when they go into their own world, it can feel like your presence is being ignored, and that would feel really uncomfortable. When they get into their own world, Chapi, what do you usually do?
I used to watch them or follow along with them, but I got tired of that too... But since I’ve been with them for a year, it feels like it takes courage to leave now, and I don’t know what to do.

That must have been painful. You’ve been together for a long time, and you have lots of fun memories too, so suddenly stepping away takes courage, doesn’t it. Until you came here to talk, you had been carrying this in your heart alone, not knowing what to do, and I imagine it was very painful. You’ve done really well holding on by yourself.
Thank you... Do you think there will come a day when I can have fun with friends too?
You want to be able to enjoy spending time with friends like before, don’t you. Let’s think through what you can do together.
Yes, please.
Chapi, what would need to happen in your current friendships for you to enjoy spending time with them?
Hmm... I want a relationship where we can laugh together. Because it’s fun when we’re laughing.
That’s true. When you’re having fun conversations and laughing together, it really does feel enjoyable, doesn’t it.
Yes...
In your current friendships, does it seem difficult to get excited together about fun topics?
Hmm, it seems difficult... in my current group.
You’re feeling that it would be difficult in your current group. Are you able to talk enjoyably in other groups?
If possible, I want to go to another group.
I see. So you’re thinking you’d like to leave your current group and join another group. Is there anything that feels like a problem when you think about changing groups?
I don’t have the courage to abandon my current group. I’m also worried about what other people will think.

I see. In your heart, Chapi, you already want to leave and have fun conversations with friends in another group, but because you don’t have the courage to abandon the group of friends you’ve been with for a long time, and because you’re worried about how people around you will see it, you’re in a situation where you can’t take that step forward.
Yes.
If you keep staying in your current group, what do you think will happen from here on, Chapi?
It’ll be boring.

That makes sense. Being with friends whose sense of humor no longer matches yours, and who go into their own world, would make you feel uncomfortable, and even being with them would become boring, wouldn’t it.
Yes.
Whatever choice you make, it won’t be wrong. Whichever group you choose to be in, each has its pros and cons, so it’s hard to decide right away, isn’t it.
I just want courage.

It sounds like, inside you, Chapi, you already have your answer. That’s wonderful. I imagine it took a lot of courage to come here and talk, too. Because of the choice you’ve made, I believe your life from here on will surely become the fun life you hope for. Chapi’s life belongs to Chapi. Let’s live this one life as fully and enjoyably as possible. Chapi, you are not alone. I’m rooting for you. Please come here anytime and talk with us. (Thank you for today. I learned a great deal.) (We’ll end the role-play here.)

interaction.content: (Good morning. Thank you for being here today. When it’s time, I’ll begin from here.)
Thank you.
Hello, I’m the counselor. Thank you for coming to talk with me today. To start, could you tell me your age and gender, and what you’d like to talk about today?
Will what I talk about here be told to my mom?
No, it’s okay. I won’t tell your mother about the questions or what we talk about here.
It’s about romance—is that okay?
Yes, that’s okay. You can share only what you feel comfortable sharing, but could you tell me about it?

I have a boyfriend, but things were kind of awkward from the start, and even though we know we like each other, we have way too little to talk about and it’s awkward. And he’s in 7th grade and I’m in 6th grade, so we can’t see each other much anymore, and I’m wondering if it’s okay for us to keep dating...
I see. I imagine it may have taken courage to come and talk about this, so thank you for coming in today.
Everyone around me is all lovey-dovey, so I can’t talk to them about it.
Yes, I see. In that kind of situation, it really can be hard to talk things over with people. Since when have you and your boyfriend been dating?
7 months.
So, if it’s been 7 months, is it okay to understand that you started dating when you were both still in elementary school?
Yes.
Thank you for telling me. At the beginning, you said the relationship was awkward from the start. What kinds of things feel awkward to you?
There’s just way too little to talk about. Do you have any topics or something?

I see. So it gets awkward because there’s just not enough to talk about. When there isn’t anything to talk about, even being together can feel kind of restless and uncomfortable, and it gets awkward, doesn’t it? It sounds like you’re wanting to reduce that kind of time, even just a little. I can tell that you care about your boyfriend, and that you’re trying to make the time the two of you spend together at least a little more fun.
That’s exactly it,, Thank you 🥰
That’s a cute emoji. I can really tell how much you like your boyfriend. What kinds of things did you talk about when you first started dating?
That’s the thing, we didn’t really talk much. It’s just been awkward the whole time 😢

So even back then, you didn’t really have much to talk about. That must have been really hard. When you’ve been with someone you really like for 7 months, but you always feel unsettled, I think it’s completely understandable to wonder, “Is it okay for us to be dating?”
What should I do?

Right. You want to do something about it, don’t you. Then, would it be okay if we use today’s time to think together about what kinds of things you could talk about, so you can have an enjoyable time with your boyfriend?
Yes.

Thank you. Earlier, when you told me what you wanted to talk about, you said, “We can’t see each other much anymore.” Is there something that made it harder to meet, like your boyfriend joining a club activity or something?
Until now we could see each other at school, but now it’s different.

Yes, so that kind of change in the situation is the reason. If you can’t see each other at school anymore, then the time you can see each other really would decrease. So, right now, how are you creating chances to talk with your boyfriend?
That’s the thing, there aren’t any,,
I see. Because there aren’t any chances to talk, that’s why you’ve been feeling like, “Is it okay for us to be dating?” ...I see. That must feel really hard and lonely right now.
That’s right.
You’re really struggling with this right now, but what are you hoping for most?
It would be good if we could talk, but,,

Yes, of course. It would be nice if there were an environment where you could talk. If that were possible, I think your feelings might feel a little lighter too. Given the situation, since when have you not been able to talk?
Spring break was the last time.
I see. You’ve done well holding on through that loneliness. During spring break, were you able to meet somewhere and talk?
Not really...
So you were able to meet, but you weren’t really able to talk much—is that right?
Yes.
I see. Even though you finally got to see him, not being able to talk must have felt really disappointing. When you usually meet your boyfriend, how do you feel?
It’s like, how should I talk to him, what should I do?

I see. It sounds like you feel a little nervous. When you’re in front of someone you really like, it’s true that those kinds of feelings can come up. But I’m wondering if those thoughts are running around in your head so much that you can’t really think about anything else. How does that sound?
That’s right. What should I do?

Right. You want to be able to talk about something. If you’d like, it’s okay to just imagine it. If you were able to talk with your boyfriend, what kinds of things would you want to talk about? This is just between us, so please feel free to write anything you’d like to try talking about. I’m sorry, I may have asked something a little difficult. I’m very sorry to have to stop in the middle of our conversation, but our time is up.
Yes.

I feel that you are a kind person who truly wants to treasure your time with your boyfriend. I think bringing up even one topic with him takes a lot of courage, but because you came here for counseling, I also think you have the courage to get through this situation. It’s possible to continue today’s session as well.
Yes.
I’ll always be here, hoping that what you’re struggling with now moves in a good direction. If you’d like, please feel free to come in for a session again anytime.
Thank you very much.
I’m sorry we couldn’t resolve it today. But I’ll always be here waiting. With that, we’ll end for today. Thank you very much.
(Thank you very much, and thank you for your time.)
(Thank you very much.)

interaction.content: (Good evening. I’ll be playing the counselor role. Thank you for being here today. We’ll begin when it’s time.)
(Good evening. Thank you.)
Good evening. I’m the counselor. Thank you for coming to talk with me. To start, could you tell me your age, gender, and what you’d like to talk about today?
I’m a 27-year-old man, and ever since I got infected with COVID, it’s been really hard.
I see. You’ve been carrying that painful feeling for a long time.
Yes.
Could you tell me a bit more about what happened? You can start wherever it feels easiest to talk about.
I got infected with COVID. My health hasn’t really gone back to normal.
Mm-hmm. It’s really hard when your health doesn’t recover easily. Are you able to eat and sleep properly right now?

I have symptoms like loss of taste and smell, brain fog, numbness in my legs, shortness of breath, chest pain, and problems with reproductive organ function. I can eat, but my lungs hurt, so I can’t sleep properly. Am I going to be like this for the rest of my life?
I see... you’ve been going through so much suffering... I think it’s only natural to feel anxious about what lies ahead. By the way, how many days ago was the infection?
It was about two years ago now, and I think I’ve been infected several times.
I see. So for about two years now, your health hasn’t really returned, and you’ve had various pains and functional problems?
Yes.
I see.
The infection I had before getting vaccinated was the worst.
Mm-hmm. What was it like then?

The symptoms I explained above came out really strongly. I had a pretty high fever too, and even sleeping was hard. Breathing was painful, and when I lay down, it felt like water was filling up in my lungs and I might not be able to breathe.
I see... I can really hear how hard it was for you, both when you got infected before the vaccine and throughout the two years since then. By the way, what is troubling you the most right now?
Am I just going to stay like this? That’s what makes me the most anxious.
I can really feel how anxious you are. Since I’m not a doctor, I can’t speak to medical matters, but I hope I can be of some help in easing that anxiety, even a little.
Yes.
By the way, are you going to a hospital?
No, I’m not. I hear there’s no treatment for aftereffects.
I see. That must feel really difficult.
Yes.
Earlier, you talked about the aftereffects. What kinds of feelings have you been living with over these past two years?
There were a few times when I thought maybe this was it.
Mm-hmm. There were times when you felt close to breaking down.
No, I thought that if I fell asleep, I might not wake up again. When there weren’t vaccines yet, I thought I might just die like this.
I see. You’ve been feeling that much pain and fear.
The news was reporting the number of deaths every day, and my symptoms were severe, so living alone, if it became hard to breathe and I couldn’t even speak, I thought I’d probably just die like that.

Mm-hmm. You were fighting COVID and the fear of death in a situation where you had to somehow manage on your own. I don’t think getting through something like that is something just anyone can do. How did you get through that situation and make it to today?
It’s not like I wanted to die. I just thought maybe I might die, and I’m only here today because I was able to stay alive.
Mm-hmm. That’s how you see it. By the way, has it affected your work?
Breathing is a little hard and I have brain fog, but I’m managing somehow.

You’ve been doing your best in that situation. I imagine you’re dealing with various aftereffects and feeling pain and anxiety. Are you able to have time for hobbies or relaxation—time when you can forget about those aftereffects for a while?
I don’t know, not really. It’s painful, so I don’t really feel like doing much of anything. I’m also scared of getting COVID again.

I see. You’ve been going through that much suffering. Thank you for sharing all of this with me. I can’t lightly say that I understand what it’s been like for you to keep fighting these aftereffects for two whole years while still dealing with so many of them, but I can really sense it from what you’ve told me. Even now, when things are already hard, I imagine your anxiety becomes very strong when you think about the future. Because it’s so painful and you don’t feel like doing much of anything, I really hope you’ll make a point of taking time to rest your body. For example, listening to music you like, smelling scents you like, enjoying conversations with friends—please try to value the small things in daily life.
Yes.

I can’t say for certain whether that will directly help the aftereffects, but I can say it will definitely support your mental health. I hope you’ll try starting with whatever feels easiest for you. How does that feel to you?
Well, maybe that’s true. But I’m scared of COVID. I think I could try things that don’t seem likely to make me get reinfected with COVID.

Mm-hmm. You suffered that much because of COVID, so I think it’s natural to feel that way. Yes. Please try doing what you can, within a range that doesn’t feel like too much. We’ll be ending the consultation shortly, but do you have any questions before we finish?
No, nothing in particular. Thank you very much.
Understood. Then we’ll end here. Thank you for sharing such important things with me today.
Thank you very much.
It must have taken energy just to talk about this, so please rest well after this. Take care. (Thank you for the role-play. I appreciate it.)
(Thank you very much.)
(I’d appreciate it if you could leave an evaluation when you have a chance. Thank you. We’ll end here. Thank you very much.)

interaction.content: Hello, I’m a counselor. To start, could you please tell me your age, gender, and what you’d like to talk about?
Thank you. I’m a woman in my 40s, and I’m struggling with my husband’s verbal abuse.
He says abusive things to you, then. That must feel really unpleasant and hurtful. Could you tell me a bit more specifically about what’s been happening?

Yes, that’s right. We’ve been married for over 10 years, but no matter how much I talk to him, he won’t take it seriously, and I’m tired of having to process all the hurt feelings. Looking at it over the long term, things have improved little by little, so I do acknowledge that, but once he starts saying abusive things, it doesn’t settle down easily, and I’m unsure whether I can keep going with this marriage as it is.
I see. So you’ve been trying to face things with your husband for more than 10 years. I imagine that must have taken a lot of patience, and it must have been very difficult.
Thank you. I’ve been unsure for a long time, and I’m not trying to come up with a perfect answer yet, but it’s been getting hard to carry it all alone, so I wanted to talk to someone.
I see. Thank you for sharing that with me. Even if things are improving little by little, no one feels good being verbally abused. Have you been carrying this on your own all this time?
Thank you. I’ve talked to my parents and friends, but only to the extent that I won’t make them worry too much. Like, “I feel better after talking, so I think I can keep trying again...”

I see... Even though you’re the one who’s hurting the most, you’ve been talking to people while still being considerate of those around you. I’m glad you came here today. Please do let me hear what’s been going on.
I’m really glad you said that 😭 Thank you, I appreciate it 🙏
Not at all. By the way, you mentioned that you’ve talked things through with him. What kinds of things have you talked about with your husband?

Well... I’ve studied a lot myself, and I try to communicate using I-messages. I say things like, “When you say it that way, I feel sad, so I’d be happy if you could say it this way.” But most of the time he says, “I don’t care if you’re sad. If you don’t like it, get out.”

You’ve really been making efforts and studying ways to improve things. I can feel that you’re a very proactive person. And yet, when it gets dismissed with one phrase like “get out,” it must leave you feeling empty... What kinds of things lead your husband to say things like that?

Thank you. I also think there may be things I’ve unknowingly assumed are common sense... so I reflect on myself, but basically it doesn’t turn into a back-and-forth where he says something like, “I’ll be careful about this too”... I just get rejected one-sidedly. Well... first, he hates it when anyone comments on his way of doing things, and he’s also a perfectionist, so he’ll say my ability to do housework is zero. Also, we’re financially strained, so he complains about things I buy, and we have two children, but he only points out their bad points.
I see. So at the moment, your husband is working, and you’re a full-time homemaker—is that right?
Yes, that’s right. I think that setup probably makes it easier for him to say abusive things to me, so I’m preparing to start working too.
I see. You really are someone who takes action. With children as well, I imagine making that decision must not have been easy.
You understand that? I’m glad. The truth is, I wanted to be a full-time homemaker so I could focus on raising the children, so it was a very big decision...

Yes, that makes sense. Even though it’s hard, because you care so much about your children, you want to be there to watch over these precious days. At the same time, you’re also taking action by looking for work for the sake of your relationship with your husband, and I feel that you’re really doing your best.

That’s exactly it. I want to watch over these moments that only happen now, while having enough time and emotional space. So I’m thinking of doing work that I can do online. Thank you. Money is the thing we tend to fight about the most, so I’m wondering if things might ease if I gain some earning power myself. And if I can reach a level where I can support myself, then I’d also have the option of leaving.

I see. That’s a very realistic perspective, and it sounds like you may be able to start seeing a brighter future. It seems like you might be able to balance work and home life—how does that feel to you?
Really? Hearing you say that gives me courage. The work is in psychological support, so I feel like it may also help with my children’s growth. I feel like I can manage both.

Yes, and hearing that you feel you can balance both makes me feel reassured too. I get the sense that your schedule will be important going forward, so I hope you can leave yourself some room and not push yourself too hard. Also, you’re considering work in psychological support, then. Is that where you studied things like “I-messages”?

Thank you. Yes, managing my schedule so I don’t overdo it is important. Yes, I knew about I-messages from before I started studying, but through studying for psychological support work, I’ve gained all kinds of other useful knowledge, and it’s been helpful in my relationship with my husband too. Also, before I start working, would it be okay if I talked to you about some things I’m anxious about?
I see. That knowledge is something you gained because you’ve been working so hard. Of course.

Thank you. There have been hardships along the way, but I feel happy that I was able to start studying. Thank you. I feel like I’ve found a realistic solution, and I think I’ve been able to take action, but...
Yes, I’m listening.

It seems like it will still take some time before I’m actually working and have financial independence, and the abusive words I’m hit with during that time are really painful. In my heart, I always strongly think, “I want to leave right now.”
Yes, of course. That must be very painful. You said you want to leave—would physically separating from him not be an option? For example, even temporarily.

Yes... It’s frustrating, and I wonder why I ever got married. But I was able to have my beloved children, and there have been enjoyable times and memories too, in their own way, so I feel like blaming myself would just be painful too... My parents’ home is far away. And my children’s lives are based in this area now, so I don’t want to pull them away from that. I thought about getting help from the local government and going to a shelter, but I was told, “Only if you’re prepared never to return to this area again.” If we separated while staying in this area, I expect my husband would harass me relentlessly. He has an incredible attachment.

Yes, I think it’s natural to feel frustrated or want to leave when someone says abusive things to you. At the same time, there are things you feel grateful for too. It sounds like the biggest of those is your children. I see. Thank you for explaining so specifically.
Yes... now that you say it, the children are the biggest thing I feel grateful for.

You’ve considered various options, and realistically, physically separating is difficult at this point. In that case, would it be fair to say that the biggest thing that would stabilize your daily life would be for your husband’s verbal abuse to improve?

Yes, I’ve also secretly gone for a free consultation at a law office. Right now, I think the best strategy is for me to gain financial strength. Of course, if I learn about other options, I’d like to consider them too. Yes... it’s the verbal abuse and things related to money.
When you say money, do you mean income? If it’s hard to talk about, you don’t have to say it, okay? Please feel free to tell me only what you’re comfortable with.
His obsession with money is intense, and I just can’t keep up with it. He cuts living expenses down so severely.
I see, that’s what you mean.
Thank you. I’m okay 😊 I’m glad you’re listening.

You’re already busy every day with raising children, and if the cutting back on living expenses is that severe, it must be exhausting. Are the parts where your husband says abusive things often related to money? Also, when is he most likely to say those things? For example, during busy periods at work, or when he’s sleepy—does anything come to mind?

Yes, that’s right. Even if I tried to buy something just to save myself a little trouble, he’d say it was wasteful. For a long time he said the children could only have snacks that cost under 100 yen, and recently there are fewer things under 100 yen, so they could hardly even get ordinary snacks that children their age would normally be able to have bought for them, and I felt so sorry for them. But after talking about that, it has improved quite a lot. A lot of it is related to money. He says, “I’m the one earning it, so I can do what I want with it,” and he also says things about housework and childrearing. He’s most likely to become verbally abusive when... my husband tends to see things negatively, and if I push back against that even a little, he argues back with incredible force, like he’s determined not to lose no matter what, and it’s full of abusive language. He’s also in a bad mood when work is busy or when he’s sleepy, but basically once some kind of switch gets flipped, he doesn’t stop easily. I never know whether something happened to him, or whether there’s a reason related to us, and even if I ask, he won’t say. Maybe he doesn’t know himself.

I imagine there has been a very long period of hardship, but I’m glad that at least the issue with your children’s snacks has improved. What do you think got through to your husband and helped that improve? For example, if he cares about appearances, maybe something like “they can’t buy the same things as their friends” made him allow it. Thank you for talking with me. We’re getting close to the end of our time, and from what I’ve heard so far, I feel that your efforts and your calm perspective are truly admirable.

Thank you. Maybe the long, drawn-out persuasion does work each time. I usually persuade him all through the night for 6 to 8 hours, and then my request gets accepted. Even while facing all kinds of strange counterarguments, if I keep talking without running away, he says, “I’ll allow it up to about this much.” Maybe it’s like payment for the hardship, so to speak (wry smile). Thank you. I felt that you were truly empathizing with me, and it helped me a lot.

I get the sense that your husband may have difficulty with feeling denied or criticized. Psychologically speaking, sometimes when you start with “acceptance,” it can be easier for the other person to take in what you’re saying. For example, if you begin with words like, “So that’s how you were thinking,” or words of appreciation such as “That must have been hard,” or “Thank you for everything,” he may be a little more able to accept the conversation. That said, I also think that once you realistically begin working, a fairly large portion of the emotional burden may be reduced, so the goal is in sight.

Yes, I thought I was accepting him, but I’ll try to be a little more conscious of it and make sure I include it properly. I haven’t always checked each time whether it’s actually getting through to him!
I imagine there may still be times when things feel that painful, so when that happens, please do come here and let us hear what’s going on.
Thank you! I feel that the fact that I’m moving in that direction is also reducing my emotional burden right now. Thank you. I’d really appreciate your help again.
I’ll keep a record of what we discussed today, so that we can respond quickly next time as well.
That helps. I’ll ask to continue from where we left off next time.

You are someone who cares deeply about your children, so please don’t push yourself too hard. We would be glad to support you as well. And with your approach to your husband, please try checking whether it’s getting through to him. Thank you for today.
Understood!! I’m grateful that you listened so carefully and stayed with me so kindly. Thank you very much.
(I’m sorry, we’ve gone over time. Thank you for today. I learned a lot.)
(Thank you as well for continuing even though we went over time!! It’s okay to end here! I’ll send the evaluation too.)
(Thank you. I appreciate it.)

interaction.content: Hello. Thank you for meeting with me today. I’d like to avoid overlapping consultation topics, so if it’s okay, could you tell me your nickname?
Hello. Thank you. I’m Yuu.
Got it. Thank you, I look forward to talking with you.
Same here. We’ll start when it’s time.
Okay.
Hello. I’m the counselor. Thank you for coming in to talk with me today. To start, could you tell me your age, gender, and what you’d like to discuss?
I’m 30, female. I don’t want to go to work.
I see. You can start wherever it feels easiest to talk, but could you tell me what led you to start feeling that way?

My boss has a bad personality, and I’ve only been working there for two months, but I’m scared of my boss, so I get intimidated no matter what I do and I can’t focus on anything. Every morning feels depressing.

I see... I think it’s completely understandable that you’d feel depressed in that situation. You said your boss has a bad personality and scares you—what kinds of things make you feel that way? (Only as much as you feel comfortable sharing is okay.)

They yell right away over even the smallest mistake, use abusive language, and after work they invite me out drinking and I can’t say no. The abusive comments are really awful, like they attack who I am as a person.
I see... That sounds really painful... By the way, do you work with that boss every day?
Yes, every day. They’re almost always in a bad mood, irritated from the morning, and I work all day while constantly watching their expression.

I see... Even with a boss like that around, you’ve been enduring it and doing your job. I think you’re doing really well. What is your work like? For example, is it team-based, or do you work individually, things like that...
It’s a team. Because I have coworkers, I can talk to everyone, so that’s how I’m managing to keep going.
I see. So you’ve also had support from your coworkers.

Yes. Everyone has gone through the same thing too. But it seems like the person they take it out on changes depending on the period—I heard that from my coworkers. Apparently, I’m the target right now.
I see. That’s just awful. When you talked to your coworkers about it, what did they say?

Everyone empathizes with me and says things like, “I get it,” and “That’s awful.” People who understand what sets my boss off teach me how to do things before I get snapped at. Also, we complain together, so that helps me let off some steam. But no matter how much my coworkers support me, I really hate being yelled at in front of people, and it’s just too painful.

Even though you’re able to get advice from your coworkers and let off some steam by complaining together, I think it’s completely understandable that being yelled at in front of people still feels awful and painful... If someone says abusive things that attack who you are as a person, that’s really hurtful...
Yes. I used to have more confidence, but lately I’ve lost it.
I see... That’s a really exhausting situation...
Yes.
Those kinds of abusive comments that attack your character would be considered power harassment, I think. What do you think?
I was just about to ask, “Isn’t this power harassment?” Yes, I definitely think it’s power harassment. What should I do?
So you had been thinking that yourself too. Right. What do you think might be best to do?
I’ve thought about quitting, but it was hard to find a job and I finally got hired, so I can’t quit right away, and I’ve been struggling with that.
So quitting has been one option you’ve considered. By the way, have you talked to anyone other than your coworkers about this?

Yes, my family and friends. Everyone says I should quit. Also, my coworkers and I have talked about whether I should consult the company president, who is in another prefecture. But since they’re in another prefecture, I’m scared the bullying might get even worse...
I see. You’ve been taking various steps to try to do something about it. If the president is in another prefecture, there may be things they can’t easily keep an eye on...
Yes.
At the workplace you’re going to now, is there anyone above that unpleasant boss?
No. So I think my boss can do whatever they want.
I see. So that’s how it is. By the way, when you talked to the president in another prefecture, what did you discuss?
I haven’t talked to them yet. I’ve only talked with my coworkers about whether maybe I should consult them.

I see what you mean. I misunderstood—sorry about that. Right, as things are now, I think it must be really painful and exhausting for you both mentally and physically, so even if the president is in another prefecture, consulting them once might be one option.
That’s true. I’d like to talk it over with my coworkers and decide whether to consult them.
Yes. There are also private consultation services, so if you’d like, please consider using those too. And of course, I’m also here to listen whenever you want to talk.
Okay, thank you.

I think you’re doing very well, managing your work every day while enduring that unpleasant boss. I’ll be quietly rooting for you as you talk things over with your coworkers and hopefully the situation changes even a little.
Thank you. I feel a bit relieved.
I’m very glad to hear that. Thank you as well for sharing something so important with me. I’ll end the consultation here, then.
Okay, thank you very much!
(Thank you for your hard work. Thank you.) (Then we’ll end the role-play here.)

interaction.content: (Hello, thank you for being here today. We’ll begin when it’s time.)
(Hello. Thank you as well.)
Hello, I’m the counselor. Could you tell me your age and gender?
Hello. I’m a 17-year-old boy, a third-year high school student.
Thank you. What brings you here today?

It’s about tennis, which I’ve been playing for a long time. In practice things go well, but when it’s a match, I get nervous and can’t play like myself at all. Even when I win, I sometimes feel miserable, and it’s been bothering me.
I see, so that’s what’s been happening. That would really weigh on you.
Yes. Even when I think about why it happens, I don’t know.
I see. It’s definitely frustrating when you can do something in practice but can’t do it when it really counts. Earlier, you said that even when you win, you feel miserable. Why do you think that is?

Well... shots I can hit with full confidence in practice become scary in a real match, and I can’t hit them. I end up playing timidly, just keeping the ball in play to win, so I think that’s why I feel miserable.
I see, so that’s what it was like.
It happens especially often in matches that are related to higher-level tournaments. I mean, matches that lead to higher-level tournaments.
I see. So the higher the level of the tournament, the more you feel like you can’t bring out your strength in the actual match.
When it’s an important tournament, I get nervous. If I lose, it feels like everything I’ve built up until now will disappear.
I see. If you can’t win, it feels like all the effort you’ve put in so far will come to nothing. I understand.
It’s painful because even I don’t know why I end up feeling that way.

When you play timidly in order to win in that moment, you also feel frustrated, and that’s really painful for you. I see. I can really tell that you’re facing tennis very sincerely. But because you’re working so hard at it, it’s painful and frustrating, isn’t it. It makes you not know what to do. Is this the first time you’ve been in this kind of situation?

Yes. I often panic in matches. As for whether I’m working hard enough... I think there are still areas where I could push myself a little more. Also, I have practice six days a week, and my parents drive me there and back, and the monthly fees are expensive, so when I lose, I also feel sorry toward my parents. Oh, sorry, this has been since I entered high school.
I see. So that’s how it’s been. It’s been the past year or two, then. You feel sorry to your parents if you don’t get results.
I think maybe it’s because after entering high school, my thinking became more adult-like.

That’s painful, and it’s something you’d worry about. I see. As you’ve been growing up, you’ve changed and become able to think about your parents too. Maybe you’ve started to think about things you didn’t think about before.
Until middle school, I was just enjoying it, but now matches are scary, and there was even a time when I threw up in the morning from nerves.
Is that so. That sounds really hard. It’s painful that it’s affecting your body, too. Do your parents say anything?
My parents don’t really say anything. People around me often say, “All that’s left is the mental side,” but...

I see. People around you recognize that you already have enough ability, and that all that’s left is the mental side. In a way, that’s wonderful. I think you’ve worked so hard and have that much ability for people around you to say that.
I also think that, technically, I’m not behind players from the strong schools. But when it becomes a match, I feel like I’m not myself anymore, and I can’t play the way I usually do.

I see. Even though you should have the ability, when it becomes a match, you end up feeling like you’re not yourself. I can definitely understand why you’d feel like you don’t know what to do. Have you ever tried thinking for yourself about why that might be?

Earlier I told you it feels like everything I’ve built up disappears, and I felt like you understood that. But there was a time when I wondered, why do I think that losing means everything I’ve built up disappears? And I couldn’t find an answer. What do you think?

Well... I really love watching sports and watch them often, but I’m not watching because I want to see the person who always wins. I feel like I’m watching more for the way they give it everything they have, and the way they don’t give up even in painful situations. So I don’t think what they’ve built up disappears. From that kind of presence, I feel like I can always see the effort that person has built up, and it moves me and gives me courage.
I feel like I understand that, but still, if I don’t win, I feel bad toward my parents, and I end up thinking that the version of me who loses is pathetic.

Yes, I think if you’re a kind person who cares about your parents, you would feel that way. But your parents don’t say anything, right? They’re probably watching you work hard and supporting you in their hearts. I get the sense that they trust you to get through this situation and are watching over you.
Is that how it is. Do you think something might change if I ask my parents?

I think it would be good to ask your parents. I don’t think your current situation is meaningless at all. If you keep playing sports, I feel like everyone runs into a wall like this at some point. And I think you get nervous precisely because you’re facing tennis seriously and sincerely. If you weren’t taking it seriously, you wouldn’t get nervous.

That’s true. I’ve thought many times that I should try to see it positively and do my best, but it doesn’t really go well. What should I do so I can go into matches with that kind of positive mindset?

I see. I’m not really in a position to say anything too grand, but I wonder if trying to think, “I’ll just play the way I do in practice,” might help you feel a little more at ease. Your ability is already recognized, after all.
Thank you. I’ll try it. I’m sorry to ask again, but for my last question, I want to know how to find the answer to why I end up thinking that everything I’ve built up will disappear.

Because sports are a world of winning and losing, it may be easy to fall into the way of thinking that if you lose, it was all pointless. But I have never once thought that the practice of Koshien baseball players who lost was meaningless. I’m sure many people are getting courage from seeing you work hard. Unfortunately, our time is up for today, but please feel free to come back for counseling anytime. I’ll always be here.
Thank you very much. (Thank you for today. I learned a lot. As for the evaluation, it’s difficult to do it right away, but I’ll do it sometime today.)
(Thank you as well.)

interaction.content: Thank you for being here today. We’ll begin when it’s time. I look forward to speaking with you.
Thank you as well. I look forward to it.
Good evening, I’m the counselor. To start, please tell me your age, gender, and what you’d like to talk about.
I’m 45, female. I’m tired of trying hard.
Thank you for reaching out. Could you tell me a bit more about that?
I got breast cancer. I was told there’s a high chance it can be cured if I have surgery, but I keep thinking, well, I’ve already lived this long.
Thank you for sharing that with me. I imagine things have been painful since you became ill. What is your situation like right now?
I’m doing fine. They said there’s a high chance it can be cured if they remove my breast with surgery... But having it removed is painful for me. I don’t know why.
I see. I’m glad to hear you’re feeling well. I feel it’s only natural that it would be painful to lose something that has always been there as a matter of course.
I want to just die like this.
That’s how you’re feeling. Have you talked with anyone about this?
My husband and my friends.
What did your family and friends say? If you don’t mind, could you tell me?
That I don’t want to have my breast removed.
Yes, of course.
Just imagining it makes me unable to stop crying.
Yes, I can feel that this is an extremely painful decision.
Yes.
What has your family said?
My husband went quiet. He said it’s a feeling men can’t understand. I haven’t told my child about this.
I see. Maybe your husband couldn’t find words because it was painful for him to see how much you’re suffering. How old is your child?
What feelings are behind not telling your child?
They’re in that rebellious phase and tend to stay shut in their room... And I can’t say that their mother doesn’t want treatment because she doesn’t want to have her breast removed.

I see. There are times like that, aren’t there. While you’re going through something so painful yourself, it must be really hard to face that as well. Why do you feel you can’t tell your child your true feelings?
Because if my child said the same thing, I wouldn’t allow it.
I see. What do you mean by “wouldn’t allow it”?
I would make life the priority.
That’s how you feel. Your family’s life is important to you. I can really feel how deeply you care about your family.
My child’s life is more important than anything. But I feel like I’ve already done everything I needed to in my life, and I wonder whether I really need to keep trying any more than this.
You feel that your child is more important than anything. When you say you feel you have to “keep trying” right now, what kinds of things come to mind?

I’ve raised my child mostly on my own up to now, and we’ve gotten to the point where they don’t need as much care anymore. They had just gotten accepted into a combined junior high, high school, and university program, and I was thinking I’d fulfilled at least the minimum of my responsibilities. Then this happened. I hear chemotherapy is painful too... This household can run even without me.
It’s understandable that you would feel anxious about the treatment ahead as well. I think you’ve carried responsibility for your family and worked so hard that you can say you’ve done all you could.
Yes, I thought from now on I could have some time for myself too.

Yes, I hope that for you too. Your family may also have feelings similar to yours. I wonder if the reason your husband couldn’t put it into words was that, just as much as your life is important to him, he also wanted to honor your feelings. How does that sound?
That might be true.
I think your child is old enough to understand what you’re saying. How would it be to try telling them how you feel, just once?
I don’t think my child would understand. Or rather, even I had never thought about what it means for a woman to have her breast removed until I got this illness.

Yes, there are things you can’t understand unless you’re in that situation. Even if they don’t understand the meaning of that itself, perhaps your painful feelings could still come across.
(I’m sorry. My mouse stopped working for a moment. Please excuse me.)
Yes, I suppose so. I’m scared, though.
Because you’ve cared so much about your family up to now, you’re worried about whether those feelings will come across, aren’t you.
I’m afraid they’ll think I’m a foolish mother. They’re in that rebellious phase, after all...
I think your child has seen you working hard for your family all this time. After talking today, how are you feeling now?
I was only thinking that I wanted them to understand how I feel. I need to think about my family’s feelings too. Thank you.
I think it’s natural to want your own feelings to be understood. I also wonder if wanting to be understood comes from feeling that they might be able to understand you.
Maybe I wanted motivation to go through treatment.

The fact that you were able to feel that yourself seems very significant to me. Thank you for speaking with me today. We’ve reached the end of our time, so we’ll end here, but if anything comes up, please feel free to come back anytime.
Yes. Thank you very much.

Thank you. I’ll end the consultation here.
(I apologize for the interruption earlier. Thank you.)

interaction.content: (Hello, thank you for meeting with me today.)
(Hello. Thank you as well for meeting with me today.)
(When it’s time, we’ll begin.) Hello, I’m the counselor. Thank you for coming in today. To start, please tell me your age, gender, and what you’d like to talk about.

Hello. I’m 28, female. Lately, I haven’t been doing well mentally or physically, and I haven’t really been able to go to work, so I’ve started having money problems too. I don’t have enough money, and I ended up borrowing a little, so I’m anxious about what’s going to happen from here.
Thank you for telling me. When your mental and physical health are poor, it can become really painful. Since when have you been unable to go to work?
Since about a month ago.
When you’re struggling with money, it makes you anxious, doesn’t it.
Yes, I don’t have money, and I’m not feeling well, and it’s really painful.
So you’ve been struggling for about a month. That sounds really hard. Was there some kind of trigger?
Well, yes. I started feeling like I didn’t want to go to work in the morning, and from there I got more and more depressed, and I feel like my physical condition has been getting worse.
When you start feeling depressed, it can really bring you down. If you don’t mind, may I ask about what made you start feeling like you didn’t want to go to work in the morning?

I end up feeling like I hate going to work in the morning. I especially don’t want to ride the train during rush hour. When I get on the train, I start feeling sick, and I couldn’t take it, so there was even a day when I took the day off work because of it. It’s not okay to take time off for something like this, is it... I feel like I’m a failure as a working adult.
Thank you for telling me. If you start feeling sick, it makes you not want to do it anymore, doesn’t it.
Yes, if I could just tolerate feeling sick during the commute, I could work. I like the work itself, and my relationships at the workplace were good too...
It’s painful when you end up blaming yourself. By the way, did the rush-hour commute suddenly start making you feel sick?
I think it’s only natural to blame myself when I’m like this.
You feel it’s only natural. That must be painful. Have you talked to anyone about it?

Recently, I changed jobs and started working hours that put me in the rush-hour commute. Before, the hours I worked were different every day, so after changing jobs, I gradually started feeling sick during the commute. I told my mother that I feel sick. My mother is exasperated, like, taking time off work over something like this?
I see. Even though you’ve come to like your job, that must feel frustrating. What parts of the rush-hour commute feel unpleasant to you?
Yes, it’s frustrating. There are so many people packed into the train, and I hate the smells and how close everyone is.
When you’re bothered by the smells and how close people are, it can really wear you out. Is there a difference between your commute time at your previous workplace and now?
Yes. Before, my start times were all over the place, so there’s a difference of about one to four hours.
I see. So your environment has become completely different from before. Have you always been uncomfortable with rush-hour times?
I don’t know. In the past, I didn’t ride the train during rush hour...
I see. Is there anything you’d like to change about your current commute time?

I’d like them to shift my working hours. I’ve already told my supervisor that I’d like my hours shifted. But I’m the only one asking for something like this, and it seems like it’s pretty difficult...
If you could avoid rush hour, that would help you feel more at ease. So you’ve talked with your supervisor about it.
Yes. But right now I’m off work because I’m not feeling well, and asking for something like this is impossible, isn’t it...
If shifting your commute time is difficult, that’s a real concern. How are you commuting now?
I’m still commuting by train. There’s no other way, so...
I see. That’s tough. You feel like making that request is impossible. What is it that makes you feel that way?
Right now, I keep calling in sick on the same day because I’m not feeling well, and I think I’m causing trouble for everyone, so I feel like it’s impossible.
When you think you’re causing trouble for others, it makes sense that you’d feel that way. How has your supervisor reacted?
My supervisor is a very kind person, so they tell me to take my time and rest. But when I’m absent, someone else has to do my work, so I think I’m causing trouble.
I see. Hearing that may give you a little room in your heart, but maybe you have a strong sense of responsibility and end up blaming yourself?
That might be true.
Do you think you could consider any ways to deal with the rush-hour commute besides shifting your work hours?
I don’t know. What should I do?
Not knowing is hard. I think there are options like moving closer to your workplace, but what do you think?

I live with my parents right now, and if I moved, I’d have to live on my own, so there’s the money issue too, and I can’t really think about that right now. I’m sorry I can’t live on my own even though I’m a working adult...
Right, you were also struggling with money. Do you think you could shift the rush-hour timing by going to work earlier?
Well, yes. If I’m feeling okay, I might be able to do that.
So when you’re feeling well, you might be able to go. Going in early sounds like it could also make fatigue build up. By the way, why do you blame yourself so much?
Yes. But I’m starting to feel like that’s the only option. I don’t know. Maybe it’s because my mother is a strict person.
We’re almost out of time for today, but I was thinking that maybe you could try challenging yourself with something that seems doable first. How was it, talking about this today?
Yes, I think I’ll try. Thank you for listening to me talk even though I’m such a useless person.
Please do try it once. I’m here to talk with you as many times as you need, so please come back anytime. Thank you for sharing something important with me today.
Thank you very much.
(Thank you for playing the role of the client today!)
(Thank you as well. Good work playing the counselor role.)
(Good work today. I’d appreciate your feedback again. Excuse me.)
(As for me, I’m fine ending the role-play here.)
(Understood.)

interaction.content: Good evening. Thank you for being here today. We’ll begin when it’s time.
Good evening. Thank you as well.
Good evening. I’m the counselor. Thank you for coming to talk with me today. To start, could you tell me your age, gender, and what you’d like to talk about?
Good evening. I’m 16, female, and it’s about my best friend.
I see. About your best friend—could you tell me what you’d like to talk about, as much as you feel comfortable sharing?
We’ve been best friends since middle school, but we went to different high schools, and lately I feel like she’s kind of drifting away from me...
Mm-hmm. I see. That would feel lonely... By the way, what year are you in high school now?
I’m a first-year.
So you’ve been at different high schools since April this year. What makes you feel like she’s drifting away?

Yes, we talked on the phone earlier, but it felt like she wasn’t really listening to me, like she was just giving half-hearted replies. Also, at her new school, she seems to have made new friends and is having fun.
I see. When it feels like someone isn’t really listening, it can feel empty, can’t it... And your best friend seems to be enjoying school too.
I wonder if she doesn’t need me anymore.
That’s how it feels... If you think maybe she doesn’t need you, that would feel really sad...
Yes. Am I not her best friend anymore?
You’re getting the feeling from your best friend that maybe you’re not best friends anymore. When you were in middle school, what was it like between you—how did you spend time together or interact?
Yes, on the phone, it feels like the conversation doesn’t flow the way it used to.
When the conversation doesn’t flow like before, it makes you anxious, doesn’t it...
In middle school, we’d get excited talking about shared interests, and we’d go shopping together.
I see. You said earlier that the conversation doesn’t flow—does that happen even when you talk about things you have in common?
Well, lately we haven’t been able to meet much, so we talk on the phone sometimes, but we don’t talk a lot, I guess. Earlier too, she somehow felt distant.
I see. When you say distant, what was that like?
It felt like she wasn’t really listening to what I was saying, like her mind was elsewhere. I wondered if maybe she doesn’t have fun with me anymore.
I see. That would make you feel lonely... How do you feel about your best friend being that way?
I wonder if she wants to stop being best friends with me—though saying “stop being best friends” might sound strange. That’s the feeling.
That’s what you’re thinking. It must feel painful to talk with your best friend while carrying those feelings...
Not painful exactly, but more like, I wonder what she really thinks.
Is it that you want to know how your best friend feels?
Yes, that’s right.
I see. Then, would it be okay if we take a moment to organize what you’ve shared?
Yes, please.
It may be a bit long, so please give me a moment.
Okay.

Lately, you feel that your best friend from middle school may be drifting away, partly because you now go to different high schools. Even when you talk on the phone, her replies feel half-hearted and her mind seems elsewhere, so you feel like maybe she doesn’t enjoy talking with you. In middle school, you used to have lively conversations about things you had in common, and you went shopping together. You feel like maybe she wants to stop being best friends. You want to know what your best friend thinks.
Yes, that’s right.
Is that about right? Thank you. So, based on what we’ve talked about so far, what would you like to talk about today?
I want to know how my best friend feels. What kind of person I am to her.
I understand. Today, let’s think through this together so we can understand what kind of person you are to your best friend.
Yes, please.
Thank you. What kind of relationship would you like to have with your best friend from here on?
I guess I want us to have that close feeling we used to have again. Of course, we’ll have fewer chances to meet, but...
I see. When you say you’ll have fewer chances to meet, what do you mean?
In middle school, we could spend time together every day, but in high school I think we’ll only meet about once a month. She also has a part-time job.
When you’re at different high schools, your schedules may not match up, right. How often are you meeting now?
It’s about once a month after all.
I see. What is it like when you meet?
Compared to before, I guess we talk about things happening in our new environments, each of us talking about our own stuff. When I listen to her, I feel a little lonely.
I see. When she talks about things you don’t know about, it can make you feel lonely or anxious, can’t it...
That’s exactly it. I feel a little like I’m being left out.
Mm-hmm. You end up feeling left out... You said you want to know how your best friend feels—how do you think you might be able to find out?
Hmm. Asking her directly somehow feels kind of weird.
I see. Asking directly takes courage too, doesn’t it.
Yes.
What about LINE or your phone?
LINE is... I had a misunderstanding with a friend on LINE before, and it caused trouble, so I think I’m scared of that.
I see. With social media, since it’s only text, misunderstandings can happen easily.
Yes, I think I’d be scared.

What about a letter? I know people don’t often have chances to write or receive letters these days, but if you write sincerely and from the heart, I think a letter can be a good way to communicate your feelings... What do you think?
Yeah... I haven’t really written one before, so I wonder if I can do it.
I’m sure you can. You can rewrite it as many times as you need. The next time you come to talk, if you’d like, would you like us to think about what to write in the letter together?
Yeah... We’re out of time now, aren’t we. I’ll try writing it, and if it’s difficult, I’ll come talk again.
Yes, I’ll be here. And if you decide a letter really feels impossible, you don’t have to force yourself to write one, okay? Let’s think of another way. How was it for you to talk today?
Yes. Thank you very much. I feel a little lighter. I think maybe it might be okay to write a letter to my best friend.

I’m glad your feelings feel even a little lighter. Yes, if you’d like, please try writing it. After talking with you today, I felt that you’re honest, that you care very much about your best friend, and that you have a warm heart. I think that will surely come through to your best friend too.
I hope it comes through. (Thank you very much.)
Yes. Thank you for today. We’ll end our conversation here.
(Yes. Thank you for your time.)

interaction.content: Thank you for being here today. When it’s time, we’ll go ahead and begin.
(Thank you. Do you have any requests or anything?)
(Nothing in particular. Thank you.)
(Got it.)
Thank you for coming today. To start, could you tell me your age, your name, and what nickname you’d like me to call you?
I’m Non, a 14-year-old girl.
Thank you. Non, are you in your second year of junior high? What would you like to talk about today?
Yes. I don’t want to go to school.
I see... That must feel really exhausting. When did you start feeling that way?
Since last week.
I see... I wonder what happened?
My best friend betrayed me.
That’s really painful... If you don’t mind, in what way?
She left me out and joined another group. I don’t want to live anymore.
You’ve been pushed to the point of feeling that way... That’s so painful. Is there anything you can think of that might have led to it?
Probably because a girl higher up in the social ranking invited her, so I think she threw me away.
I see... That’s awful. So, Non, are you alone now?
Yeah.
I see... That must feel lonely. At school now, is there anyone you talk to, even a little?
No. Nobody talks to me. I didn’t have many friends to begin with.
Mm, then it may be only natural that you don’t want to go to school... Have you told anyone else... like someone at home?
No. I can’t tell them.
I see... What do you do at lunchtime?
I’m alone. But it’s embarrassing, so I go to places like the bathroom or the outside stairs.
Hmm... I see... That’s painful. Is there anyone from first year of junior high, or from elementary school, that you could tell?
Since starting junior high, I was mostly with that girl, and I haven’t really kept in touch with my elementary school friends.
I see... So she’s been your friend since first year of junior high. If you could say something to her now, what would you want to say?
I’d want to say, “Why?” I think it’s awful. To betray me like that. But maybe it’s my fault? I’m plain, and boring, and ugly. Maybe I’m boring to be with.
That’s honestly what you’d want to say, isn’t it. Non, I don’t want you to think of yourself that way.
Thank you. But it’s true. I’m not smart, I’m short, I’m fat, and I don’t have anything good about me.
Even if someone is small or overweight in appearance, I don’t think that has anything to do with who they are inside. And I feel like it’s unfair to yourself... What do you think, Non?
I want to think that, but the world doesn’t see it that way. People who are pretty, cool, and smart are the ones who get accepted... So I think that’s why my best friend went over there too.
That’s how it feels to you right now, Non. But I think there are good things about you that only you have...
I don’t know.
Yes, you may not know right now, but I’m sure there are. I wonder, was that girl really a true friend to you?
I thought she was my best friend. It was fun being with her.
I see... But suddenly leaving out a friend you’ve been with for a year and a half... I find myself wondering whether that can really be called a true friend. What do you think?
That’s why I keep thinking, why?
Mm, of course you do... Non, what do you want things to be like with her? I also feel like she hasn’t shown much kindness... but I wonder how it is for you.
I think it would be nice if we could be together like before. But I guess I’ve kind of stopped being able to trust her...
Yes, I see. So you’re also feeling like you can’t trust her. Does it feel like she has no idea at all how you’re feeling right now?
I think she probably feels bad, but she’s already joined that group, so maybe she can’t go back now. And I think she cares more about herself than about me.
I see... Herself more than other people... That’s lonely. Non, do you feel like you want to talk to her?
Hmm, I do want to ask her why, but I’m too scared to ask.
I see... Do you think you could tell her how you feel through social media or something?
Would she read my LINE...? I’d hate it if she just ignored it...
Mm, that would make you feel anxious... If she did ignore it, do you think you could shift your feelings and think, okay, that’s enough?
Hmm, you’re right... If that happens, maybe I have to think, okay, that’s enough... Maybe that would help me move on... But still, being alone is painful...

Yes... Since this only happened last week, I think you’re surprised and shocked, Non. Right now, I imagine your mind is full of it, but I wonder if little by little, your thoughts might start turning in a different direction too... What do you think?

That’s right. I still don’t really know what I should do... But tests start tomorrow, and after they end it’s summer vacation... and I also feel like being all alone during summer vacation would be lonely... I keep thinking about all kinds of things.

Mm-hmm, when you think about so many things, it gets hard to know what to do. But from here on, you may not be alone like this forever. I think it might be good to turn your attention to new things, new people... What do you think? Attention to people.
Will I be able to make new friends...? I don’t have confidence.
Yes, even if you don’t have confidence, I think that’s okay. Non, I want you to value yourself, to deepen the things you like, broaden your perspective... May I ask you one thing?
Yes.
At the beginning, you used the words “I don’t want to live anymore”... After talking together, how are you feeling now?
It hurts so much that I want to die, but I can’t actually kill myself.

That’s how deeply painful it feels... Feelings change. So I hope that from here, even a little, things will feel lighter for you, Non. For now, how about trying to focus your mind on the tests right in front of you?
I don’t know if I can focus on the tests, but I do think I have to study.

I see. If you feel like you have to, then you might regret it if you don’t. For now, maybe you can pack the thoughts about that girl into a backpack and set it beside you... Then later, you can take your time thinking about it, and if at that point you feel, “Oh, I don’t need this anymore,” it may be baggage you can throw away... What do you think?
Yes. Maybe I’ll try thinking of it that way...
Do you think you can...? And Non, I hope you’ll take your time looking for the wonderful parts of yourself.
Yes, I understand.
Non, would it be all right to end today’s consultation here? After you try this, if there’s anything else you’d like to talk about, please come back anytime.
Yes, thank you very much.
Thank you as well for telling me about your painful feelings. Please also try looking for things you like about yourself. Well then, we’ll end here for today.
Yes, thank you very much.
Thank you. (I’m rooting for you.) (Thank you. As for the evaluation, I hope you’ll write it honestly, without holding back.)
(Thank you for your time! I learned a lot!)
(Thank you as well!)

interaction.content: Hello, thank you for working with me today. I’m a psychological counselor, and the theme is romance. I’d like to do a consultation about a relationship where someone has been hurt. Has this message reached you?
Likewise, thank you. Damage, right.
Yes, thank you. Rather than marriage-hunting, I’d like you to play the role of a client who is struggling with a romantic relationship.
Yes, understood.
Hello, I’m the counselor. What would you like to talk about today?
Lately, my boyfriend has been acting strange, and I’m anxious.
I see. That sounds worrying.
Yes.
Could you tell me in more detail what he’s been like?
Lately, he hasn’t been contacting me first.
That would make you feel even more worried and anxious, wouldn’t it?
That’s right.
If you’re comfortable, could you tell me your age and gender, and his age and gender?
I’m a 29-year-old woman. He’s 27.
Thank you for telling me. When and where did you meet?
We met at a group party three years ago and started dating.
I see. So you’ve been together for quite a long time. That makes it even harder when he stops contacting you, doesn’t it?
Yes...
When you say lately, how often did you used to keep in touch before?
He’s always been a really busy person, so I guess about once a week.
I see... Can you think of anything that might have triggered him to stop contacting you?
I can’t really think of anything in particular, but...
Mm-hmm.
Actually,
Yes, I’m listening.
There was a time when I found out he was cheating, so I’m suspicious.
I see... That must have been a shock.
I mean, it’s obvious, isn’t it?
When you start to suspect that, it can make you feel even more unsure about what to do. What happened that made you realize he was cheating?
It’s the same pattern as when he cheated before, so it’s easy to tell.
I see... What kind of pattern is it?
We have mutual friends,
Mm-hmm.
He told me he couldn’t because of work, but then I heard through that person that they saw him at a bar.
That happened? It would make you think, no way...
It’s easy to tell.
So he was with another woman at the bar.
It seems so.
When you heard that, did you say anything to him?
I asked him on LINE, but he’s playing dumb.
I see. That would feel unacceptable and make you angry.
I can’t forgive him.
Of course. I think it makes complete sense that you’d feel unable to forgive him. What kinds of conversations do you usually have with your boyfriend? Do you feel like he values you?
Now that I think about it,
Mm-hmm, mm-hmm. Please go on.
Most of the time it was about going out or hobbies, just fun conversations,
Mm-hmm.
Maybe we didn’t really have many deep conversations.
I see... So you feel like maybe the conversations were kind of superficial.
I actually wanted to talk about important things too.
I see. What kind of important things, for example?
All my friends have started getting married, and people often say to me, “You’re next,” and... somehow, at times like that, I don’t know what to say,
Mm-hmm, mm-hmm. You actually wanted to talk about things like marriage... Was there an atmosphere where it felt hard to bring it up?
I felt unsettled, so I thought about just telling him exactly that, but I haven’t been able to bring it up.

Let me summarize what you’ve shared so far. You always had fun conversations, but even though you’ve been together for three years, you’re wondering if maybe you haven’t really had deeper conversations. Would it be okay if I shared what I’ve felt from listening to you so far?
Yes.
I think you are someone who deserves to be treated with care. I’m going to press the end button now.
