interaction.content: Good morning. Thank you for coming in for a consultation today. What would you like to talk about today?
Yes, I work in the food service industry, and partly because of the COVID situation, we’ve had fewer customers and lower sales, so I’m feeling anxious about what lies ahead.
I see. Could you tell me more specifically what the situation is like?
Yes.
Also, if you don’t mind, could you tell me your age and gender?
Sales have dropped by half, and my salary has been cut by a quarter. I’m a 31-year-old man.
Thank you for telling me your age and gender. I see. A quarter! That must feel really worrying.
I think I’m truly grateful just to have a job, but I wonder how long this situation will continue.
Yes. When it comes to your anxiety about the future, what part feels most worrying to you?
I end up thinking, what if the restaurant goes under and I lose my job?
That’s what you’re thinking about the most, and it’s making you anxious.
Yes...
Mm-hmm, mm-hmm. You’ve been doing your best in that kind of situation.
I think there are people who are going through harder times than I am, so maybe it’s not really my place to complain...

That’s how you’re feeling. But it doesn’t change the fact that you’re carrying anxiety right now. Thank you for coming to talk about it. When you think about possibly losing your job, what kinds of thoughts come to mind?
I’ve heard that, unlike before COVID, there aren’t many job openings in any field, so that feels like it makes things even worse.
I see. If that’s the case, then thinking about losing your current job would feel worrying.
Yes.
Besides that, is there anything else you’re feeling anxious about or concerned about?
I’d be glad if those anxieties could lessen today.
I see. It’s about your work, then. Are you planning to continue with your current job?
Yes, I want to keep going.
I see. But you don’t know what will happen from here... You mentioned your salary has been cut by a quarter; how are things financially?
It’s not much, but I’m not dissatisfied—I think, “It can’t be helped.” I’m somehow managing day-to-day living expenses.
I see. You’re somehow managing things on your own, and you’re really doing your best.
Thank you.
So, for you, is your biggest hope to continue with your current job?
Yes... I’d be glad if I could continue and if my anxiety could lessen.
Mm-hmm, mm-hmm. Yes. What kind of feelings do you have about your current job?
I’ve been doing it for about 10 years, so I think I feel very attached to it.
Ten years! That’s amazing. It’s a job you have a lot of attachment to. Was there a reason you felt you wanted to keep doing this work for those 10 years?
As I kept doing it, I gradually started to find it rewarding. That’s exactly why I never thought about changing jobs.
Mm-hmm. Mm-hmm. I see. What parts of it did you find rewarding?
Well... I think it’s that I like customer service, seeing customers enjoying their meals, and the energy and good atmosphere among the staff.
I see. It’s a very good workplace for you, and you like this work.
Yes. That’s exactly why I want to keep doing it.

Mm-hmm. Mm-hmm. Yes. You want to keep going. Then, in order to keep going, what do you feel is realistically needed? I’d like us to think about that together, but I’m sorry. An hour has passed, and if you still have time, I’d like to continue—how is your schedule?
If it’s within another 15 minutes, that’s okay. Well... In order to keep going, I think the most important thing is to be able to accept whatever happens from here and not leave myself with regrets.

I’m sorry. Thank you for giving me your time... That’s the most important thing, then. What are the parts that feel like they could become regrets? What kind of outcome do you think would leave you with regrets?
Right now I’m feeling anxious, so if I stay in that emotional state, I think I’ll have regrets.
I see. What would need to happen for that anxiety to ease?
Well... I think maybe it’s to give my all to my daily work. By doing that, I think I’d feel a sense of fulfillment.
I see. I feel that a sense of fulfillment can become a source of strength. By having that sense of fulfillment,
Yes.
what do you feel might happen to your anxiety?
I think if I appreciate my work even more and give it my all, my anxiety will ease more than it does now.
That’s how you’re feeling right now. I feel that your current job and workplace are very important and precious to you, and that you are also an important presence for your coworkers and customers.
Yes.
The fact that you’ve continued for such a long time may be partly because of the workplace environment, but I also feel it reflects what you’ve built up, and your character and sincerity.
Thank you.
For you, as you’ve been talking today, how are you feeling about what a choice without regrets would be?
I feel like I want to work hard so I don’t have regrets!
That’s how you’re feeling. Yes, I hope you’ll be able to do things in a way that leaves you with no regrets,
Thank you!
I do. Even so, if something else comes up later, or if you find something you want to do, or if your situation or feelings change, I hope you’ll come back to talk with us again. How does that sound?
I understand. Thank you very much.
Yes, I’m rooting for you. I hope your workplace’s sales and your salary will improve from here. I’m sorry today took so much time. Is there anything else you feel you haven’t had a chance to say?
No, thank you. I’m glad I was able to talk with you!
Thank you as well. I’m glad to hear you say that. In that case, would it be okay if I send you the closing message?
Yes, thank you very much.
I learned a great deal. Thank you for the long time today. I’ll send the message now.

interaction.content: (We’ll begin when it’s time. Thank you.)
Thank you~
Hello, I’m the counselor. Thank you for coming today. To start, could you tell me your age and gender?
I’m 42, female.
Thank you. What would you like to talk about today?
It’s about work.
About work, I see. Would it be okay if you told me more about it?
I work as a care manager at a nursing home, and I do counseling then. But that counseling doesn’t go well.
I see. So you provide counseling to the residents. And that hasn’t been going well.
Yes, that’s right.
What part of it feels like it’s “not going well” for you?
I’m told things like, “Ask more about the emotional part.” By my supervisor. But I don’t know how to draw that out in conversation.

I see. Even when someone says, “Ask about the emotional part,” it’s difficult, isn’t it? I feel that way too, doing this work. In practice, when asking about the “emotional part” doesn’t go well, do the residents say anything to you about it?

It’s more my supervisor than the residents. I’m told I’m not listening properly. For example, when a woman is being bathed, wouldn’t it feel uncomfortable if it’s a man? I think that’s normal. But at our company, there are more men than women, so they want to assign male staff. Then complaints come from the family. So they tell me to ask the resident what exactly they dislike and how, the emotional part, and then they can explain it to the family. That’s the kind of thing.
I see. So it’s like they want you to ask what they dislike, identify the cause, and do something about that part.
Yes, though this is just one example.
It’s not that simple, is it. From your perspective, how would you like to be able to change the current situation?
For now, I want to become able to draw out the emotional part better.
I see, understood. Shall we think together a bit about how you might draw out the residents’ feelings?
Yes, please, I’d really appreciate that.
Thank you. I’d like to ask a few questions about the situation. Could you tell me the general flow of the counseling you usually do?
Once a month, there’s a meeting with the family and the facility. In that, we ask what kinds of things they want changed in the resident’s care, and we also explain how the care is going.
I see, so that’s the flow. At present, would you say the focus is more on concrete explanations from the care setting and exchanging opinions, rather than on the resident’s feelings?

No, I think it’s because they value the resident’s feelings that they’re telling me to go and ask. I know that if we can’t communicate their feelings, it’ll turn into even more complaints. We can’t just smooth things over.
I see, that’s what you mean. In the counseling, are there any moments when it’s especially easy to ask about feelings?
What I’m in charge of is the patients’ dissatisfaction with the facility. So it’s easiest to ask about how care is being provided. Like the bathing issue from earlier.
I see. In those situations, are there any things you try to do in order to actually “draw out feelings”?
I mean, they’re elderly, so even if I ask, “What don’t you like?” they just say, “I don’t like it because I don’t like it.”
I see. If you can’t draw out “what they don’t like,” you end up stuck, don’t you. And if your supervisor points that out, that leaves you at a loss.
Yes, exactly.

Even if you talk to the family, is it more like, since the resident themselves is saying they don’t like it, they just want it changed no matter what? And in the end, you still don’t know “why” the resident dislikes it...
Yes, that’s right.

Is there any chance that if you take time, the residents will talk about something more specific? (Though I imagine in reality the time you can spend with each person is limited...) For example, if you get closer to them or build trust, they might talk a little more.
They have some dementia, so they can’t really talk for very long. Even if we get close, the next day they’ll say, “Who are you?”
I see. In that case, building trust and drawing out feelings sounds difficult...
So I was wondering if there’s some simple way to ask about feelings.

It seems like drawing out complex feelings would be difficult. In each caregiving situation, it may be all they can do to judge whether it’s “okay” or “unpleasant,” but you need to draw out more complex feelings...
Yes, that’s right.

In that case, having family members who have been with them for many years speak on their behalf may be an effective approach. You could tell the family, “In this kind of situation, the resident had this kind of reaction,” and then make some inferences to a certain extent. What do you think?
But the ones making the complaints are the family. I think the complaints are already them speaking on the resident’s behalf.

I see, that was the situation. In those complaints, is there any content related to the resident’s feelings or thoughts?
(I made a mistake, I’ll retype that.)
(Not your feelings—the resident’s feelings.)

About the bathing issue from earlier: “She’s a woman, so I want a woman to do it.” Even if I say, “We can cover her with towels,” they say, “I don’t want a man!” “What would you like us to do?” “Change it to a woman.” “Women aren’t as strong, so baths are hard for them, I’m sorry.” Then they say, “You’re a woman, aren’t you? You wouldn’t like it either.”
Would your supervisor say that this doesn’t count as “drawing out feelings”?
Apparently so. I can’t draw out anything more than this, so I came to consult, but it’s difficult, isn’t it.

From what I’ve heard, it seems to me that the residents are expressing their feelings and thoughts fairly specifically. I’m very sorry that I’m not able to be more helpful, but one possible approach may be to tell your supervisor that, and clarify “what else they want you to draw out.”
I see, I understand. Thank you very much.
I’m truly sorry I couldn’t provide a clear answer. If there’s anything else you’d like to talk about, I may be able to help, so please feel free to come anytime.
No, no! Thank you for listening to me!
Thank you very much for coming today.
Thank you very much.
(Thank you for the role-play. I learned a great deal.)
(Thank you as well 😊)
(I’ll press the end button now (^^))
Okaaay!

interaction.content: Thank you for being here today. When it’s time, I’ll let you know.
Thank you.
Hello, I’m the counselor. What would you like to talk about today?
It’s about caring for my mother.
I see. Could you tell me a bit more about that?
My father passed away six months ago, and after that she developed depression. On top of that, it became difficult for her to walk.
I see. You must have felt very lonely. And then, on top of that, things became that way for her. Are you spending each day unable to really let your guard down?
Yes, even when I’m off work, it doesn’t feel like a day off.
I see. That sounds really hard. By the way, could you tell me what I should call you?
Eri.
Eri, then. Thank you. Eri, are you caring for your mother at home?
Yes.
I see. That must be very difficult. When you’re at work, who looks after her?
My younger sister looks after her.
I see. I imagine caregiving is difficult, but what kinds of things are you struggling with?
I’m worried about what’s going to happen from here on.
Yes. Yes. Of course you’re worried. Specifically, what kinds of things are you feeling anxious about?
Right now we’re caring for her at home, but I think there will come a time when we need to put her in a facility, and financially that’s difficult. But I don’t know what options there are.
I see. Not knowing can make you anxious, of course. Is your mother seeing a doctor or anything like that?
She was a healthy person, so no, not really.

I see. Earlier you mentioned “depression”; did she go to a hospital for that? I asked because if she were seeing a hospital or similar place, there might be opportunities to consult with someone there.
She went to a psychosomatic medicine clinic and was told that. I thought it was different from a regular hospital, so I left it out.
I see. So you and your younger sister have been watching over your mother yourselves, Eri. I imagine that has felt very worrying.
Yes.

There are places you can consult with, such as your local municipal office, consultation or coordination offices at medical institutions, and home care support offices. Do you feel like you might want to try consulting with them?
I do feel like I’d like to consult with someone, but is it okay even with a situation like ours?
I think they will listen to you no matter what the situation is.
I see. But I’d be in trouble if it just ended with them listening to me. What would the process actually look like?

They assess the difficulties in daily life, and based on that, the level of care needed is determined, which then determines what services can be used. A care manager at the Community General Support Center can consult with you about whether care at home is possible, what care facilities are available, and so on. First, if you consult with your nearby city office, I think you’ll be able to hear more specific information. How does that sound?
In our case, I think it would be difficult because she isn’t in a condition where she would be certified as needing long-term care.
(I meant “care is possible,” not “turning into care”—sorry.) So that’s how you see it. What makes you think that?
It’s far from what people generally call caregiving, but getting through right now is hard.

I’ve heard there are two signs that someone may need care. One is that illness or injury makes it difficult to live as they used to, and the other is that it starts to interfere with daily life. Are you saying your mother isn’t at that point yet?
Even if you say it’s interfering with daily life... the bigger issue is that ordinary conversation is difficult.

I see. I suggested it because I thought there might be someone nearby who could be of help to you, Eri. I’m sorry. Conversation is difficult, then. When it’s hard to communicate with each other, it can feel frustrating, and you may find yourself getting irritated. And in the midst of all that, you came to talk today. I’d like to take the time to really listen to how you’re feeling.
Yes. I’m sorry, but we’re out of time, so would it be okay to end here?
Yes. I’m sorry. We’ll end here even though we’re partway through. Thank you. Thank you for the role-play.
Thank you for your time. Thank you.

Kitchen at an izakaya.
I see. What are the conditions like?
Conditions? Pretty normal, I guess?
I see. You mentioned spending money on having fun—could you tell me what kind of things you mean?
Mainly gambling, and drinking.
I see... both of those cost money. What are you doing at university? If you’re okay sharing.
I haven’t really been going lately, so I don’t know.
I see. So right now it’s mostly just work and going out?
Something like that, I guess.
Thank you for coming here and talking with me today. Aside from money, is there anything else you’re having trouble with right now?
Not really.
I see... so not having money is the biggest problem right now? To increase your money, how would it feel to look for a part-time job with better hourly pay, or take on another part-time job as well?
Oh, also, since I don’t have money, I want to quit gambling, but I can’t quit—that’s a problem too. I looked for places with better hourly pay, but I couldn’t really find any, so I gave up.
I see. People do say gambling can be really hard to quit. Why do you think it is that you can’t stop? Is there anything that comes to mind for you?
Because I go whenever I have free time?
I see. On the other hand, if you didn’t have free time, do you think you could avoid going? What do you think?
I don’t know. I feel like I’d somehow make time and go anyway.
I see. What would you think about taking on one more part-time job so you don’t have that free time?
My current job goes until morning, so that’s impossible.
I see... that would be physically difficult too. What is it about gambling that appeals to you?
It’s just fun.
I see. What part of it is fun? The thrill of winning and losing?
That too, and it’s like killing time? Maybe because I don’t have to think about anything.
I see. Are there things you find yourself thinking about? Like your future?
Job hunting, I guess.
I see... has job hunting already started? Do you feel things like pressure or anxiety about it?
Apparently it’s started, but I haven’t done anything. I think I probably do feel that, but I don’t know.

I see. So right now it feels like you don’t really know. Would it be okay if I summarize what we’ve talked about so far? Right now, you’re struggling because you don’t have money. Gambling lets you not think about anything, and it’s fun, so it’s hard to stop. You can’t add another job, and you’ve given up because it’s hard to find a job with better hourly pay. You do think about job hunting sometimes, but right now you don’t really want to think about it? Is that about right?
Yeah, that’s about it.
Having talked through this so far, how are you feeling? Is there anything else you’d like to talk about?
I don’t know. Probably not.
I see. You said you have just enough money through this month, but will you be okay for next month?
If I don’t gamble, I think I can make it until payday.
I see. I’m relieved to hear that. For now, instead of quitting gambling, do you think you could try taking a little break from it?
Hmm, I think that’d be hard.
I see... yeah, that feels hard. Would you be able to come back and talk more about this another time?
If I have time.
Thank you for coming to talk today. If you have time, please come talk anytime. I’ll be here.
Thank you very much.
We still have a little time left, but is it okay if we end here?
That’s okay. Thank you very much!

interaction.content: Hello, thank you for being here today. When it’s time, we’ll go ahead and begin.
Hello. Thank you as well for today. Yes.
Hello, I’m the counselor. Thank you for coming to talk with me today. To start, could you tell me your age and gender?
Hello. I’m a 45-year-old woman.
Thank you. What would you like to talk about today?
I like watching live streams online—the kind where regular people chat and stuff—and I watch them often, but lately there are things that have been bothering me.
I see. What kinds of things have been bothering you?
The comments from viewers, mostly men.
I see. So comments from male viewers on live streams feel unpleasant to you. What kinds of comments were they?
What I find unpleasant are misogynistic comments that come from men. What kinds of comments...
Mm-hmm, words that show hatred or contempt toward women.
Yes. To female streamers, things like, “What cup size are you?” or “You’re ugly.” And to a divorced female streamer, things like “used goods.”
That’s... there are still people who use words like that, even nowadays. I can understand why you would find it unpleasant.
Right...? I think the male viewers say it unconsciously.
Doing it unconsciously, without meaning any harm, is the biggest problem. How do the streamers react?
It varies. Some talk back, and some laugh it off. There was also a female streamer who quit because the terrible comments kept coming and she said streaming felt scary.
I see. With streaming culture having developed this much, criticism, prejudice, discrimination, and things like that have become issues now, haven’t they.
Yes.
It sounds like it’s hard to watch streams in a fun and safe way. How does that feel to you?
That’s right. And so...
Yes.
Since I can see the comments when I’m looking at the screen and end up reading them, sometimes I put in earphones and listen only with my ears while I’m doing something else.
Mm-hmm, you’re finding ways not to take in harmful information. But with live streaming, that... seems like it would cut the satisfaction in half.
In half, yes, that’s true. But I think it’s better than getting irritated.
I see. There are probably people who make good comments too, and part of the enjoyment is seeing comments and relating to them. But I think not taking in harmful information is a really good thing.
Yes, that’s true.
If what you’re watching is on YouTube, you can hide just the comments.
Yes. I do that. Or...
Yes.
If I block a specific person who makes unpleasant comments, that person’s comments won’t show up.
I see, I didn’t know that. Thank you for telling me.
Yes.
It does seem like improvements to the system and monitoring by third parties are becoming necessary.
That’s true too, but I still think men’s awareness has to change.
Mm-hmm. If you were to say something to those people, what words would you use?

Don’t make comments about people’s appearance. Some things can’t be changed no matter how much effort someone puts in. Don’t ask about private parts when you’ve just met someone. Women are not objects. There’s a lot more I could say, but that’s the general idea.
Thank you. You have a lot of thoughts about this. I can feel your kindness in how much it hurts you when people use words that wound others.
Thank you.
I’d like to ask—when you feel that men’s views won’t change, what makes you think that?
Is it okay if I just say what I think?
Of course.
I think what’s at the root of it is male dominance and the patriarchal system.
Yes.
And also a society where gender bias is deeply ingrained, I guess.
I see. So attitudes and ideas that value men and look down on women, men holding enormous power within the family, and social expectations about masculinity and femininity.
Yes.
Were there many men like that around you?
I think life would be easier if both men and women were freed from ideas of what they’re ‘supposed’ to be like. No, I started thinking that from watching live streams online. Oh...
Mm-hmm, I see.
I’ve been studying sexual violence, and as I did, I started to see the situation women are placed in.
I’m interested. Could you tell me more?
As an extension of that, I started to see the misogyny in men, and I began to notice what they say online.
I see. Because you’ve been studying sexual violence, you’re feeling uncomfortable with men’s thoughtless words.
Yes. If I hadn’t studied sexual violence, I might have acted like a woman who brushes off sexual harassment from men is an admirable woman. Sorry, that was weird Japanese.
It’s okay. I understand what you mean.
I’m glad.
Have you yourself had painful experiences in the past?

Yes. I went through fertility treatment, but I wasn’t able to have children. During the treatment, the people who said things like, “No kids yet?” and “You’re just messing around and not even having a child—don’t your in-laws say anything?” were all men.
I see. So at that time, people said thoughtless things to you.
Yes.
Words said during such a painful time can be impossible to forget, even when you want to.
Yes, that’s true.
Even if they said it unconsciously and without bad intentions, I imagine it could make you feel unable to forgive them. How does that feel to you?
At the time, I couldn’t forgive them, but now only the scars remain in my heart.
I see. I would be glad if you came to talk again to help heal those wounds. We’re just about out of time. Thank you for sharing so many of your thoughts with me today.
Yes, thank you too.
Thank you for the role-play. If we have another opportunity, I look forward to working with you again.
Yes. Thank you, I look forward to it.
Well then, take care.

interaction.content: (Good morning. Thank you for meeting with me today.)
(Good morning. Thank you as well.)
(It’s before the scheduled time, but would you like to start at the set time?)
(Sorry, yes, at the set time, please!)
(Understood.) Good morning. I’m the counselor. To begin, if you don’t mind, please tell me your age, gender, and what you’d like to talk about.
Good morning. I’m in my 20s, female, and I don’t feel confident about raising a child.
I see. That must be something you’re struggling with. Specifically, what kinds of things make you feel that way?

I don’t like children, but my husband wants kids, so I’m planning to have one. But my husband is busy with work, so I already know I’ll end up having to raise the child by myself. But I don’t feel confident that I’ll be able to love a child...
I see. That would make you feel anxious.
Yes.
Have you ever talked with your husband about how you feel?
I have. I told him that I don’t like children.
I see. What did your husband say at that time?

Hmm, it was just something like, “Oh, I see,” and the conversation didn’t really go any further than that. But in the first place, when we got married, one of the conditions was that I’d be allowed to live how I wanted until I turned 28, and we’d have children after I turned 28, so having a child is already decided. So I have to come to like children by then.
I see. So that’s what happened. That must feel frustrating.
I feel rushed.
You feel that way. I think that’s a natural feeling. Have you talked to anyone about this? It sounds like quite a difficult situation...
I haven’t really talked to anyone. Everyone around me likes children, and I’m sure people like that would never understand how I feel.
I see. That must feel unbearable. What kind of image do you have of children?
They’re selfish, noisy, and they irritate me.
That’s how you feel. There certainly are situations like that in real life.
Yes.
You’ve been carrying something that’s hard to talk about with the people around you, and you came here to talk about it. Please feel safe here—whatever it is, I’ll listen.
Yes, thank you.
What else would you like to talk about regarding this issue?
I want to talk about what I can do to start liking children.
I see. When did you start feeling this way about children?
Hmm, I already felt this way when I was in middle school.
I see. Was there anything that might have triggered it?
That’s the thing, I can’t really think of anything... Up until around high school, I seriously thought that if I had a child, I would become an abusive parent.
I see. What made you start feeling that way?
Because children seemed so hateful to me, and I thought I wouldn’t be able to put up with it.
I see. Was there anything involving children that made you think that way?

I didn’t really have many chances to be around children, so I’ve wondered if maybe it’s because I hadn’t interacted with them. But when I think about it, I do have a younger sister, so maybe that’s not it... It’s just that I have a strong feeling that children are selfish and I can’t stand watching them. It’s not like a child did something to me or anything...
I see. Other than your younger sister, do you have any children in your family, like nieces or nephews?
No.
I see. What is your relationship with your younger sister like?
My sister and I don’t go out together just the two of us or anything, but we’re not on bad terms. We keep a comfortable distance, and it feels like we each live our own lives freely.
I see. So you have a comfortable relationship with your younger sister.
Yes.

You’ve shared a lot with me. With your younger sister, you have a comfortable relationship. And when it comes to children, too, I wonder if your feelings toward your own child might be different from your feelings toward children in general. What do you think?

That might be true, but I won’t know unless I actually have one. What am I supposed to do if I give birth and don’t feel any love at all? It’s not like I can just toss the child away... Even people who already think children are cute get irritated with their own kids, so I’m anxious about what would happen with me. And if my husband can’t take childcare leave, then if I stay the way I feel now, I feel like I’ll end up saying, “You’re the one who said you wanted a child!!” So I want to do something about this even a little, now... I’m sorry, I got emotional, but I thought that if I had a child in my current state, I’d end up blaming someone else, and I know that’s not okay...
I see. It’s okay—please talk about anything you need to.
Yes, thank you. I want to have a child properly, after feeling that I myself want to have one too.
I see. From what you’ve told me, I think you do have feelings about children themselves, but I also felt that your anxiety about parenting is quite strong. How does that sound to you?
Yes, I think if I could raise a child together with my husband, my anxiety would be somewhat less.
I see. Do you think you could talk with your husband about that in depth?

I think we can talk, but realistically, I think there are a lot of difficult parts. My husband is a teacher, so he can’t really take childcare leave like that. I’m thinking I’ll at least tell him, please don’t go to club activities.
So that’s the situation. That would make you anxious. Rather than talking about everything all at once, how would it be to gradually talk about the parts that feel easier to bring up?
I’ll try doing that.
Please do try that. I hope your anxiety can ease even a little.
Yes, thank you.
Thank you for coming here today. If you’d like to talk again, please feel free to come anytime.
Yes, thank you very much.
(Thank you very much. I learned a great deal.)
(Thank you for your time. Thank you very much.)

interaction.content: (Good evening. Thank you for being here today. Would it be all right if we begin?)
(Yes, that’s fine. Thank you.)
Good evening, I’m the counselor. To start, could you tell me your age and gender?
Yes, I’m a woman in my 50s.
Thank you. What would you like to talk about today?
Cherry blossoms are blooming around this time of year, right? Normally I’d think they’re beautiful, but now I don’t feel anything. I wonder why…
That’s how you’ve been feeling.
Yes.
When you look at the cherry blossoms, what feelings come up for you?
I don’t feel anything.
Yes, I see. How is it usually for you?
As I said earlier, until now I would think they were beautiful.
Yes, you did tell me that earlier. Thank you. Even though you usually find them beautiful, not feeling anything now must feel kind of sad.
Yes, I suppose so.
You mentioned “around this time.” Since when have you been feeling this way?
I don’t know… I just happened to notice that it felt different from usual. But it might be recently.
Yes, so recently you felt that something was different from usual.
Yes.
Has anything in your life changed recently compared with before?
Well, my environment is going to change a little from April.
I see. Could you tell me a bit more about that?
Yes. I’m a freelancer, and I work in a helping profession. Until now, I had been doing contract work for two companies, but starting this April, my contract with one of them is ending.
So that happened. When it was decided that your contract with one company would end, how did you feel about it?

Yes, to be honest, for about a year I had been unsure whether to continue doing business with them, so I do think this was probably for the best. But in terms of my own vision, I had been thinking I would first study how to attract clients myself, and then once I could bring in clients on my own, I would make that move. So I felt the timing came a little earlier than planned. Because the contract ended so suddenly, I do feel regret about whether I was able to fulfill my responsibility to my current clients through to the end.
I see, that’s how you feel. Having regrets about your current clients must feel painful.
Yes, I feel sorry, and I also feel frustrated.
Yes, that’s how you’re feeling.
Yes.
Was there any particular reason why the contract ended? For example, the contract period ending—how was that?
No, the contract renewed automatically. Basically, if either side was going to discontinue it, they were supposed to give notice in advance.
I see. So does that mean you hadn’t contacted them, but the contract suddenly ended?

The other day, because I didn’t check carefully enough, the date and time of an appointment with a client had to be changed on the day itself. I caused trouble for the client. Also, I didn’t follow the company’s policy and did what the client wanted.
Yes, I see that happened. When something like that happens, it can leave you feeling guilty. What kinds of things are meant by the company’s policy?
That is the reason the business partner gave for ending the contract.
I see. Thank you for sharing that with me.
I feel that the company’s policy is just a pretext.
So when you responded to what the client wanted, the fact that it differed from the company’s policy was also one of the reasons.
The client requested an extension of the session, so I explained the purpose afterward and also explained the fee. In fact, the client understood and accepted it.
Yes, so that kind of exchange took place. What did the company say to you?
Do you mean about the reason for ending it?
I’m sorry, that wasn’t clear. Did the company say anything to you about your responding to the client’s request for an extension?
At the time, not especially. I had actually reported that there was a possibility of that happening.
I see. You were doing your work by putting the client first.
Yes. So it was a one-sided notice of termination, but since there was also the matter of the client I caused trouble for by changing the appointment on the day, I just backed down.
I see. Even if there was the fact that you caused trouble, a one-sided contract termination would leave you feeling unsettled.
Yes. I thought that no matter what I said, it would be pointless.
Yes. What made you feel that way?

Even though they’re in a helping profession, they only think about their own profits, and they don’t try to improve their own skills. To be honest, I was fed up with that way of being. But I wanted to be as sincere as I possibly could with my clients.
I see, that’s what it was like. As someone in a helping profession, that would be hard to accept.
Yes, but I myself can’t attract clients.
Yes, listening to you, I can really sense your sincere way of facing your clients.
Thank you. That’s why I was just about to start studying how to attract clients on my own.
So this happened in the middle of that situation.
Yes. I’m so angry at myself for giving those people an opening to take advantage of. I feel pathetic. I think, after I worked so hard…

Yes, that’s how you feel. You may feel that way about yourself, but perhaps you feel this so strongly because you have such a strong sense of responsibility and have really faced your clients sincerely.
Yes, I have faced them sincerely.
Yes, I think your clients can feel that you have been taking them seriously and facing them with sincerity.
Yes, thank you. For the first time, tears are overflowing about this.

Yes, perhaps the feelings that had been building up inside you are coming out now. It’s proof of how hard you’ve worked up to this point. I’m sorry that our time is up today and we can’t talk all the way through to the end. How was it for you to talk today?

Thank you. Maybe that’s why my heart didn’t move even when I looked at the cherry blossoms. Yes, I realized the feelings I had been putting a lid on inside myself. Thank you. From here on, I think I’ll keep doing my best, just as I have until now.
Yes, I’m glad I was able to help you notice your feelings. I’ll be supporting you going forward as well, so if anything comes up, please come back here and talk again.
Yes, thank you.
Then I’ll send the closing message. Thank you for coming today.
Yes, thank you very much.
(Thank you for taking on the role of the client. I learned a great deal. It would be helpful if you could tell me about the client’s background and setup. Thank you.)

interaction.content: Counseling department: The theme is suicidal thoughts. Thank you for being here.
Thank you.
Hello, I’m a counselor. Thank you for reaching out. What would you like to talk about today?
I want to die.
That’s how you’re feeling right now.
Yes.
That sounds so painful.
Yes.
If you’re willing, could you tell me what happened?
I can’t go on living anymore.
You’re feeling that cornered. Where are you contacting us from right now? Is it warm there?
My income is low, and my pension is low too, and I’m just tired. I’m inside my house.
I see. You’re feeling anxious about finances. You’re inside your home. I hope you can keep your body warm while we talk.
And, ...
Mm-hmm.
It’s not financial anxiety. Spending time with my pet was my only joy. It was what made life worth living.
Mm-hmm.
My pet died, and one memory after another keeps coming up, and I can’t get them out of my head.
I see. That must be very painful.
Tears, tears. I want to die.
They were so important to you that the time you spent together felt like your reason for living.
Yes, that’s right. There’s no value in living.
I feel it’s understandable that you would feel that way. Are you able to tell anyone else how you’re feeling right now? Or are you carrying it all alone?
There’s no one I can talk to.
I see. You’ve been holding these painful feelings all by yourself, without talking to anyone.
That’s right.
That must have been very painful.
There’s no one.
I see. Does that mean you’re living alone right now?
That’s right. I have no contact with relatives. What happened? I want to die. What should I do? I want to die. Are you okay? I’m sorry.

I’m sorry to have kept you waiting. There was a system error, so my response was delayed. I’ll continue the consultation with you. Thank you for reaching out like this while carrying such painful feelings. What made you feel you wanted to talk with us today?
Thank you, let’s start again.
Thank you.
Anyway, I’m lonely, sad, I want to die. I can’t imagine life without my pet. I’m all alone. There’s no value in being alive.
That’s how you’re feeling. I can really feel how painful this is for you.
Thank you.
Thank you for reaching out like this while carrying such painful feelings. What made you feel you wanted to talk with us today?
I can’t get it out of my head. My pet. I’m sad.
I see, you keep thinking about it.
I can’t stop crying. Yes, that’s right.
I understand. It’s painful. I wonder if you’re in a situation where food won’t go down, or you can’t do the things you usually can.
Yes, I have no appetite, and I can’t sleep. I’m on edge. Tense.
I see. It makes sense that you’ve lost the energy to eat. And if you can’t sleep and you’re on edge, it’s no wonder you’re feeling more easily exhausted.
Yes,
That shows just how strong your feelings were.
Yes, there was a time when my pet ran with all their might at the dog run. And then,
Mm-hmm.
When I was eating, they would often come over to smell the food. Tears, tears. My pet was my only reason for living...
I see. You have so many memories. If it’s okay, I’d like to hear a little more about the time you spent together. When did you start living together?
From 14 years ago.
I see. You spent a very long time together. Were you raising your pet on your own from that time?
Yes, from when they were about four months old. But I think their life was on the shorter side.
I see. So you were together from when they were very small. When you say their life was short, did they have some kind of illness?
First they got injured, and after that they became ill.
I see. I imagine there were times when you felt very anxious and worried.
Yes. There were times when I went to the hospital every day. There were also times when they had surgery. Tears, tears.
I see. That must have been very worrying. You cared for them with such devotion.
Yes, I did my best. But only on the day they died, in the morning, I wasn’t able to take them to the hospital.
Even while carrying those anxious feelings, I think you really did so much for them up until now.
Yes,
I see. Was there anything different from usual that day?
I was worn out from all the hospital visits, and even though I wanted to take them, I just couldn’t get my body to move.
I see. You really had been caring for them so devotedly all this time. I can strongly sense that even while putting your own body second, you were truly caring for them with so much love.
Is that so...
From the time they were injured, and after they became ill too, you kept going and going, doing your best.
Yes.
Looking back, from around the time you were going to the hospital, were you not really able to eat or sleep much?
No, it started from the moment I thought, maybe it’s hopeless now. Thank you very much.
Thank you very much!

I see. When you’re not feeling well, being asked about tomorrow must put you in a difficult position.
I don’t know at that point, so I say I’ll try to get better so I can come in, but... Um, may I ask something?

Are you male or female?
I’m female. Please feel free to talk with me about anything.
Thank you. My period pain is really bad, and I end up taking one or two days off a month no matter what.
I see. That must be painful every month.
Yes, it’s painful.
Is your supervisor male, by any chance?
Yes, he is. My supervisor is male, so I can’t say it’s period pain.
Yes, that would be hard to tell him.
Yes.
In your workplace, what is the ratio of women to men like?
It’s about women to men = 3 to 1. The supervisors and management are all men.
I see. Since all the supervisors are men, is it also hard to tell other higher-ups?
Yes. My direct supervisor is male too, so it’s hard to say.
That must have been painful, having to take time off every month in an environment where it’s hard to explain. What do the other female staff members do when they have things like period pain?
It feels like there aren’t any people who have period pain. The other women are in their 30s to 60s. Maybe age doesn’t matter, though.
I see. If there aren’t other women taking time off for women-specific reasons, it may be harder for your supervisor to notice. So, what feels the hardest for you right now about taking time off?
Yes. I’ve never heard anyone talk about women-specific issues.
We got crossed there.
It’s okay.
Let me ask again. So, what feels the hardest for you right now about taking time off?
Every time I take a day off, I use paid leave, so I’m going to run out of paid leave soon.

I was told that once I run out of paid leave, it will be treated as an absence.

I thought that if I have a lot of absences, my evaluation will get worse, and my pay will go down too.
I see. It’s because you’re not feeling well—and period pain is a natural thing that happens to women and can’t be helped. If your evaluation goes down because of that, it feels unfair.
Yes. It’s unfair and I feel helpless...
Leave for menstruation is protected by law, but in your current workplace it’s difficult to bring it up, is that right?
Yes.
For this consultation, would it be accurate to say that you want to find some way to tell your supervisor about menstrual leave? If that’s not right, please feel free to tell me what you’re thinking.
Hmm, the company I work for doesn’t have menstrual leave, so I’d like to talk about what I can do so I can work with peace of mind.

interaction.content: (Thank you for being here today. We’ll begin at 3:00.)

Hello, I’m the counselor. Thank you for coming in to talk with me. To start, could you tell me your age, gender, and what you’d like to discuss?
25, female, wondering whether to get married
Thank you for telling me. You’re wondering whether to get married, then.
Yes.
What specifically are you struggling with?
The person I’m dating proposed to me, but I’m not sure whether to get married.
I see. The person you’re dating proposed to you, but you’re feeling unsure. What parts of it are making you feel anxious or conflicted?
I do love him, but I don’t really have much desire to get married. I’ve only just started working, and I’m enjoying living on my own. I don’t have any complaints about my life right now.
I see. You love him, but you don’t really have much desire to get married. That makes sense—you feel that you don’t have any complaints about your life as it is right now.
Yes.
But because he proposed, you’re now wondering whether or not to get married.
Yes.
I see. Your partner wants to get married, but for you, rather than taking the form of marriage, you’d prefer to continue the relationship as it has been—is that how you’re feeling?
That’s right. I like things the way they are.
I see, that makes sense. Have you talked with him about the things you mentioned earlier—like how you’ve only just started working, and how living alone is enjoyable for you?
I’ve talked about it before.
When you talked about it, what did he say?
He said he thinks I could keep working as I am, and that if we lived together, it would be even more fun.
I see. How did you feel when he said that?
I did think, maybe that’s true. But I still end up feeling that being alone is easier.
I see. You thought maybe that could be true, but you feel that being alone is easier. For example, what kinds of things make you feel that being alone is easier?
I can eat what I want when I want, and sleep when I want… I can also decorate my place however I like, things like that.

I see. It’s true that when you’re alone, there are many things you can do freely. Earlier you mentioned that you don’t have much desire to get married. Have you ever imagined yourself ten years from now?
Hmm, yeah. I haven’t really imagined ten years from now much.
I see. Then, more broadly, do you have an ideal kind of life you’d like to live?
I want to live freely and enjoyably.
I see. You want to live freely and enjoyably. Does marriage not fit into that for you?
It’s not that I absolutely don’t want to get married. It’s more like I just hadn’t thought about it yet, I guess.
I see, that makes sense. It’s not that you absolutely don’t want to, but you feel like you hadn’t thought about it yet. How did you feel when your partner proposed to you?

He’s someone I love, so I was happy. But not many people around me are married yet, and I don’t know if he’s the person I’ve loved the most up to now, so there’s a part of me that wonders if it’s okay to marry this person.

I see. You were happy to be proposed to by someone you love. But you’re also unsure, wondering whether he’s really the right person. Marriage is a big life decision, so of course it’s something you’d struggle with.
That’s about right. I’m struggling with it.
I see. Does your partner want to get married right away?
It sounds like his transfer is almost decided, and he’s saying right away.

I see. So because of the transfer too, he’s talking about wanting to do it right away. Up until now, in your relationship, have the two of you talked together about what kind of family or home you’d want to build if you got married?
We haven’t really talked about that much. His transfer was decided suddenly, so it seems like he rushed to tell me because of that too.
I see. What do you think is the biggest thing inside you that’s putting the brakes on this marriage?
Maybe that I wasn’t emotionally prepared. And also, I’m not sure I love him enough to marry him.
I see. So it’s that you weren’t emotionally prepared, and that you’re not sure whether you love him enough to marry him.
That’s right.
For you, what does being emotionally prepared for marriage mean, specifically?
What is it… I guess it means deciding in my heart, I’m going to live my life with this person.

I see. For you, being emotionally prepared means deciding in your heart, I’m going to live my life with this person. I imagine that connects with what you said about not being sure whether you love him—how does that sound to you?
I think that’s true. But I do love him. I didn’t have that sudden ‘this is the one’ kind of feeling, though.
I see. Then do you think you can decide in your heart that you’re going to live your life with him?
I don’t know… How do people decide when they get married, I wonder…

Yes, I wonder how people decide. But I think it may be about what you said earlier—whether you can feel that you want to live your life together. Marriage isn’t only fun things, and maybe people choose someone they feel they can still get through things with together.
I see, that’s helpful. It seems like I haven’t made that decision yet. I’ll think about it a little more.
I see. Maybe you need a little more time. How would it feel to try talking it over with your partner?
Yes, I’ll try talking to him.

Please do. Thank you for coming in to talk with me today. Whatever choice you make, I truly hope you’ll be happy, and I’ll be rooting for you. If anything else comes up, please come back anytime. Thank you for today. (Thank you.)
Yes, thank you very much. (Thank you.)
(Then we’ll end here.)
(Understood.)

interaction.content: Hello. Thank you for meeting with me today.
Hello. Thank you.
Is it okay if we start at 11:30?
Yes! Thank you.
<We’ll begin the role-play.> Hello. I’m the counselor. What brings you in for a consultation today?
(Thank you.) Hello.
Hello.

I’ve been struggling with Facebook and Instagram, and I was hoping you could listen. My friends all post things about themselves, but I’m not good at that kind of thing... I only look at posts. My friends say, “You should do it too!” but I don’t want to.
I see. It can definitely be fun to look, but when it comes to actually posting yourself, it can take a bit of courage.
That’s right.
I see. If it’s okay, may I ask your age, and what I should call you?
I’m 20, and my name is Ai.
Ai, then. Thank you. At 20… are you a student?
Yes. I go to university.
I see. Are your friends around you encouraging you to use Facebook and Instagram?
Yes.
Does not posting cause any kind of problem for you? You wrote that posting yourself is hard for you, and that you’re fine just looking, but...

It’s not exactly like I’m being left out, but it’s hard to join the conversation, I guess. Like, “Why don’t you post anything, Ai?” Maybe from my friends’ point of view, it seems strange that I’m refusing to.
I see… feeling like you can’t quite be part of the group can feel a little lonely.
That’s right. So sometimes I think maybe I should do it, but I still really don’t want to.
So it feels like, you feel lonely, but you don’t want to do something you’re not comfortable with… is that right?
That’s about it.
I see. …By the way, Ai, have you ever posted anything at all before?
Not at all...
Not even comments?
I have commented before, but I don’t like that everyone can see it. People I don’t know can see it too.
So it’s okay one-on-one, but you don’t like being seen by everyone...
Yes. With posts too, I think, people you don’t even know can see them, so I wonder how people can post so easily.

I see. Facebook does have settings for friends only, but that doesn’t necessarily mean everyone is someone you know… Have you ever told your friends that you’re not comfortable with Facebook or Instagram for those reasons?
Yes, I have. So when I really want to comment on something, I send a LINE message just to that person. I think they understand, but...
LINE is okay for you, then.
Yes. As long as there aren’t people I don’t know, it’s okay. I don’t like group LINE chats either if there are people I don’t know in them.
In group LINE chats, it’s true that friends of friends or people you don’t really know can sometimes be included. …When people you don’t know are involved, does that make it harder for you?
Yes.
I see. …When you think there are people you don’t know there, what feeling comes up most strongly for you?
I wonder, why do I have to share this with people I don’t know? Someone who doesn’t like me might see it too.
I see. …You don’t like being seen by someone who dislikes you...
Yes. I don’t think either of us would feel good seeing each other. And I don’t really understand telling everyone what I did today and things like that.
I see. Facebook and Instagram are often used with the purpose of having people see things about you… like wanting recognition, or wanting people to know.
Yes. I think people who want that should post, and it’s fun to look at.
People often talk about things being “Instagrammable,” too.
Yes. They’re pretty, aren’t they?
They are. I think it’s something like, if other people think something you thought was nice is nice too, then that’s enough.
I understand that!
Because it’s based on likes and things like that, I get the sense that people may not have that much personal attachment to it.
I see... Maybe they don’t really think about those kinds of things that much.

I don’t think everyone is good with Facebook or Instagram. Some people post simply because they want attention, and I’ve also heard of people who force themselves to post in order to ease their own loneliness or sense of isolation.
I see. There are all kinds of people, aren’t there?
So if you have the feeling that you don’t like being seen by people you don’t know, how about valuing your own feelings?
If everyone is different in their own way, then I guess it’s okay. I thought I was the only one who was strange.
…Even if you force yourself to suppress your own feelings and fit in with your friends, wouldn’t that become exhausting somewhere along the way?
That’s true. But I thought maybe I had to fit in.
Even if you fit in… if you yourself don’t like it, wouldn’t it become a burden?
It would be a burden, but I also want to get along with my friends.

I see. It’s true that when you have more things in common, conversations can get livelier, but Facebook and Instagram are only one way to connect. And from what you’ve told me, you can communicate through LINE, so it doesn’t seem like you’re completely disconnected from your friends...
Maybe I’m worrying too much...
As long as the feeling of, “I don’t like the thought of someone I’m uncomfortable with seeing it,” is strong, I think it’s okay not to do it.
Yes. I’ll try doing that. Thank you.
I think it’s more important to value your own feelings as you go through each day.
I’ll try to keep that in mind.
Even just telling your friends that you do properly look at Facebook and Instagram can show that you’re still connected. Please try interacting in different ways, within the range of what you can do.
Yes. I’ll try doing what I can!
I’m sorry, but our consultation time is almost up. If anything comes up again, please feel free to LINE me anytime.
Yes, thank you very much.
Thank you as well. I hope you enjoy your university life.
Yes!
<The role-play time has also come to an end. Would it be okay to finish soon?>
(Yes. That’s fine. Thank you very much.)
Thank you as well. Please put your thoughts and impressions in the report. Well then, we’ll end here.

Yes, every day goes by in a blur, and I get so tired that I end up taking it out on the kids sometimes.

I’m a consultant.

When he’s around sometimes, he’s affectionate with them, but he’s often looking at his phone too, and from my perspective I wish he would engage with them a little more.
Yes, I can understand that. You’d like him to show a bit more affection as their father, perhaps. Even so, your children are attached to him.
It seems like, for the kids, a kind father who shows up once in a while is nicer than a mother who gets angry.

That’s how you see it. You’re moving nonstop from morning until night, so I think it’s only natural that things turn out that way. It’s understandable that you feel like getting angry at your husband.
At first I kept putting up with it, but now I’ve gotten tired of asking him to do things, and we hardly talk anymore.
I see... So there’s much less conversation between you now...
Yes.

Yes, I think so.

Maybe since around last month.
I see. Have you talked to your parents about this situation?
Actually, I’m distant from both of my parents...
I see. That would make it hard to talk to them. Have you told your husband about these feelings of yours?
Not yet.
I see. With you carrying everything on your own, is your health holding up okay?
Yes, I’m careful about that at least.
I’m glad. So you’re making sure to get enough sleep and eat properly as well.
Yes. If I collapsed, it would affect the children.

Probably the financial side.

Not to that extent, but they wouldn’t be able to do extracurricular lessons anymore. I think I’d have to limit food expenses and toys too.
I see. So you’ve been realistically thinking through scenarios and things like that. For example, are there moments when you feel relieved when you see your husband playing with the children?
Yes. I do feel relieved.
That’s how you feel. Those moments when you feel relieved—maybe that’s one of the reasons you feel unsure.
That might be true.

That said, if things continue as they are, I’m really concerned about your physical and mental health. Perhaps you could set aside time to calmly and properly talk with your husband about what comes next.
Yes. I feel a sense of aversion too, so I don’t want to talk, but I guess I shouldn’t run away from it.
That’s how you feel. The fact that you noticed that shows what a wonderful mother you are. Please do try to do that. I’m rooting for you.
Thank you.
Thank you as well. I know your days are very difficult, but where you can cut corners, please do, and try to make time for yourself—to refresh your mood and relax slowly.
Thank you very much.
If anything comes up, please come again. It’s fine to continue from today’s conversation too. We’ve reached the end of our time, so would it be all right to end here?
Yes, thank you.
Thank you for coming today. I’ll play the closing announcement now. (Thank you very much.)
(Thank you very much.)
