interaction.content: Hello, I’m the counselor. Thank you for coming in for a consultation today. To start, could you tell me your age, gender, and what you’d like to talk about?
I’m 45, male, and I can’t quit smoking.
I see. So you’re thinking you want to quit smoking.
Yes.
It’s hard when you want to quit but can’t, isn’t it?
Yes, it’s painful.
Yes, I can imagine. What made you want to quit smoking?
It costs money, and it’s not good for my health.
I see. Money and health are things that would be on your mind.
Yes. I smoke a pack a day, and prices keep going up. I know that if I quit, I could save money, and it would be good for my health, but...
Since you understand that yourself, it must be painful not being able to stop.
Yes, it’s painful. Before I know it, I’m smoking.
So you find yourself smoking before you even realize it. Is there anything you’re doing to try to quit smoking?
A while ago, I had smoking cessation treatment at a hospital, but after a month I ended up smoking again, and now I’m in this situation.
I see. So you did treatment and have been making efforts.
Yes. It seemed like I might be able to quit, but right around then the medication ran out, and I smoked one cigarette.
I see. You really did try hard.
Yes, in my own way. But my willpower is weak, so it’s hard to quit. And it’ll be too late after I get sick. A lot of people I know only quit after they get sick.
I see. When people you know become ill, that makes you anxious, doesn’t it?
Yes. I heard that after they got sick, they were told, “If you smoke another cigarette, you’ll die.”
Hearing something like that would feel frightening, wouldn’t it?
Yes. So my friend quit completely. It’s too late once you get sick.
Seeing your friend quit, you’ve also been trying hard to quit yourself.
Yes, that’s part of it.
What do you think you could do, or what do you think would help, in order to quit smoking?

To avoid smoking, I think it would be good if there were something else instead. After meals and things like that, I always feel like I can’t calm down unless I smoke. If I quit smoking, I could go on trips and things. I’d save 30,000 yen a month.
Going on trips sounds wonderful. So you’re thinking you’d like to quit smoking and go traveling.
Yes, that’s right. If I quit smoking, I can save 30,000 yen every month.
Just thinking about that makes it feel exciting, doesn’t it? For that, what’s the first concrete thing you feel you could do?
Reduce the number of cigarettes, and change my mindset, I guess.
That’s what you’re thinking. How many cigarettes will you reduce it by? And how are you thinking of changing your mindset?
First, 10 cigarettes a day. For my mindset, I want to think about how there are lots of good things if I quit smoking.
You’re thinking about it in a positive way.
Thank you.
You’ve put your thoughts together in a concrete way, and I can feel your desire to make an effort.
Yes, thank you.
How was it for you to talk today?
Well, it was good to have you listen, but I was hoping you could give me some advice or tell me something new I could try.
I see. When trying to quit smoking, I think things like drinking water, brushing your teeth, or not going near cigarettes in the first place can be helpful.
I see, okay, I’ll try those.
I think it’s important to try it one step at a time, without rushing.
Yes, that’s true. Thank you.
I’ll ask again: how was it for you to talk today?
Right now, I just really want to do my best and quit.
I’d be glad if I was able to help even a little. I hope it won’t happen, but if there’s ever a time when it doesn’t go well, let’s think it through together again.
Yes, thank you. I appreciate your help.
I’m rooting for you to quit smoking and go traveling.
Yes, that’s right. Thank you.
Hearing your positive desire to make an effort really makes me want to support you. Please keep at it!
Yes, I’ll do my best!
We don’t have much time left, but is there anything you’d like to talk about before we finish?
I’m okay. I just want to keep doing my best. (Thank you for your time, and thank you.)
All right. Then we’ll end today’s consultation here. Thank you for today.
(Let’s both keep doing our best from here on, okay?)

extra.topic_sub: タバコによる健康への影響

interaction.content: (Good evening. I’ll be playing the counselor role. I’m sorry this was arranged on short notice. Thank you for meeting with me today. We’ll begin when it’s time.)
(Good evening. I’m the one who signed up on short notice. Thank you for meeting with me.)
Good evening. I’m the counselor. Thank you for coming in for a consultation. To start, could you tell me your age and gender, and what you’d like to talk about today?
Good evening. Thank you. I’m a 28-year-old man, and I’m so tired mentally and physically that I’m currently unable to go to work.
I see... So things have gotten to the point where you can’t go to work... You can start wherever you feel able, but could you tell me what’s been going on?
I’ve been overwhelmed by unpaid overtime and how busy work is, and the atmosphere at the company isn’t good either, so I just don’t feel any energy coming up.

I see. Even just one of those things would be exhausting... so it makes sense that you’d feel worn out both mentally and physically. When you say the atmosphere at the company isn’t good, what kind of atmosphere is it, specifically?
There are people sighing, and people make fun of others and laugh about it.
Things like that... In that kind of environment, it must be hard to keep up your motivation to work, wouldn’t it?
Even if they’re not directly making fun of me, it makes me feel awful.
Yes. That would be really discouraging. Unpaid overtime is illegal, and it’s something that shouldn’t be happening in the first place, but how often does it happen?
It’s illegal? I’m supposed to start work at 9 a.m., but there are things I have to come in and do at 8.
I see. Under the Labor Standards Act, it states that if an employer has a worker do overtime or work on holidays, they must pay the worker extra wages.
Who gets punished by whom?
The employer would be subject to punishment or investigation by the Labor Standards Inspection Office. By the way, are there other people besides you who are working from 8 in the morning?
Everyone works from 8 in the morning. So, as someone younger, it feels like I have no choice but to accept the situation.
I see. It’s hard both having to work from 8 in the morning, and not being able to be the only one who doesn’t go along with it.
Exactly.
Are there any other things you’re struggling with?
There isn’t a single senior coworker I can look up to, so the future feels completely bleak.
Yes. It’s sad that there’s no one like that. How long have you been working at your current company?
It’s been just under two years.
I see. Around when did you start feeling mentally and physically exhausted?
Maybe around September. I took about three days off from work once.
I see. When you took that time off, and when you went back afterward, how were you feeling?

I talked with my wife and decided I should just take some time off for now, so I did. I didn’t want to see anyone from the company, but someone at the management level came near my home because they were worried. Because of that, I lost even more trust in the company, but I felt like I had to work for the time being, and I’ve just kind of dragged myself along until now.
I see. So you’re still going through a lot of pain, both mentally and physically.
Yes. I’m working without any energy, so the negative cycle just keeps going.
Yes. I’m worried about you. How is your physical condition right now? Are you feeling fully well?
Right now, it’s basically that I’ve just continued to have no energy. Eating and sleeping are fine.
With you continuing in that state, I imagine your wife and your family must be worried about you. By the way, how much have you been thinking about changing jobs?
I want to change jobs right away, but I’ve been working without any motivation, so I’m not confident I could go to the next workplace either.

I see. Even if you’re in a situation where you want to change jobs right away, when you’re exhausted mentally and physically, it’s hard to find motivation, and it makes sense you’d feel anxious about the next workplace too.
Yes. I don’t know where to even start.
Yes. That leaves you feeling stuck, doesn’t it. I imagine even thinking about it must feel exhausting.
Thank you.
What have you and your wife been talking about regarding your current job or changing jobs?
We haven’t really talked about it, but I think she probably feels like she wants me to get myself together.
I see. It may be that your wife is respecting your decision.
Yes, maybe.
By the way, when you say, “I’m not confident even if I go to the next workplace,” what makes you feel that way?
Because I only recently changed jobs, and before that I was doing a completely different kind of work. Also, I’ve been struggling with communication for a long time.
I see. What kind of communication are you struggling with?
If I feel like someone is difficult for me to deal with, I don’t want to talk to them, so I can’t communicate well.

That’s how you feel. Regarding communication, I think you don’t have to force yourself to talk; as long as you can manage the bare minimum needed for work, that may be enough. What do you think? I meant, as long as you can do the bare minimum.
There are a lot of situations where the bare minimum isn’t enough, so I’m struggling.
That’s how it feels to you. Thank you for sharing such important things with me up to this point.
Thank you as well.

We talked a little about changing jobs, but whether you do or don’t change jobs is something you get to decide. At the same time, I am concerned that you’re exhausted both mentally and physically, and I worry that if this exhaustion continues as it is, someday you may not be able to keep going.
Yes. Thank you. I’ll take a little more time to think it through carefully.

You mentioned being worried about motivation, but motivation is easily affected by the atmosphere at work, so I think it’s natural that you don’t feel motivated in your current workplace. I also think changing jobs is becoming more common these days, so I don’t think you need to worry too much about the short time span.
Thank you.

For the sake of your mental and physical health, I’d like us to continue talking t— I think. At that time, let’s also talk about communication. I meant, if we can keep talking. I’m sorry. Lastly, do you have any questions or anything else?
Nothing in particular. I’d like to think carefully about what to do from here.
Understood. Then we’ll end here.
Yes. Thank you very much.
Thank you for coming to talk with me today. I’ll end here, then. I sincerely wish for your mental and physical health. (Thank you for the role-play. I’m sorry we went over time.)
(Thank you for your time. Not at all. Thank you very much.)
(I’d appreciate it if you could leave an evaluation when you have time. Thank you. Then we’ll end here. Thank you very much.)

extra.topic_sub: 職場の雰囲気によるストレス

interaction.content: (Good evening. We’ll begin when it’s time. Thank you.)
(Good evening. This is my first session today, and thank you as well.)
Good evening. I’m the counselor. First, please tell me your age, gender, and what you’d like to talk about today.
Good evening. I’m 13, male. What I want to talk about is that recently an older student called me out and hit me. I’m worried it’s going to keep happening.
I see. Thank you for telling me. What led to you being called out?
That older student is in a bad group, and he told me to join them.
I see. Did you give him an answer?
I kept saying no, but he said something like, “I’m gonna call you out again!”
I see. That must have been scary. What kind of relationship did you have with that older student?
I’d never really had anything to do with him before, but I think he noticed me because before, I was hiding with my friends and smoking cigarettes just for fun, and he found out.
I see. It would feel uncomfortable to suddenly be invited into a group by an older student you don’t have any relationship with. When he hit you, were you hurt?

Even if it was an older student I knew, I wouldn’t want to be in a bad group. I wasn’t hurt, I’m okay. Thanks for worrying about me. And I still have two more years with them, so if this keeps happening, I don’t want to go to school.
That’s true. I’m sorry. I’m relieved to hear you weren’t hurt. So that’s how you’re feeling. Have you talked to anyone about this?
If I tell a teacher, I don’t know what’ll happen afterward, and if I tell my parents, they’ll worry. I told a close friend.
I see. That’s how you’re thinking about it. What did your close friend say?
Not much. Just like, “Oh, that happened.”
That was their reaction, then. Maybe your friend was confused too. To summarize what you’ve told me so far,
I think that’s probably it. They looked surprised.

An older student you don’t really know noticed you and invited you into a bad group. When you refused, he hit you, and he said he would call you out again, so you’re feeling anxious. You feel like if this anxiety is going to continue for another two years, you don’t want to go to school. It’s hard to talk to adults about it. Is that about right?
Yeah, that’s right.
What do you feel you’d like to do from here? There might be different things, like wanting to persuade the older student, or wanting to get away from him...
There’s no way I can persuade him—if I could run away, I’d want to, but...
I see. So for now, it feels like you don’t want anything to do with that older student, is that right?
I don’t want to see the people in that group.
I see. Are all the people in that group older students?
It seems like some classmates are in it too. I’m not close with them, though.
I see. If there are classmates in it too, even if you’re not close, it seems like it would be hard to make sure you never run into them...
It’s the countryside, so there are only two classes in each grade. I don’t think I can get away.

I see. That would make it more likely that you’d see them. Listening to what you’ve told me, I don’t think this is something you can solve all by yourself. You said it’s hard to talk to school teachers or your parents, but I was wondering what you’d think about talking to the school counselor.
Hmm... I’m scared that they’ll find out I talked to someone... What should I do...
School counselors keep things confidential, so you don’t need to worry about them finding out.
I wonder how they’d solve it. It might depend on that. Oh, right, I guess it’s not about solving it, it’s about trying to talk to them.

That’s true. Since I haven’t seen the actual situation, I can’t say for sure, but adults should be able to respond appropriately depending on what’s going on. Yes, I think talking to them once is one option. We’re in the middle of the consultation, but we’re getting close to the end of our time.
Will they really make sure nobody finds out? Okay.

How about you try talking to them once, and if any other problems come up, you can come back here and we can talk about it. Next time, we can continue from what we talked about today, so please don’t worry. How was it to talk with me today?
I hadn’t really talked properly even with my friend, so after talking about it properly, I feel like I’m a little more relieved.
I’m glad to hear you feel that way. Thank you for talking with me today.
Thank you.
We’ll end the consultation here. Thank you.
I’ll come back to talk again.
(Thank you for your work. I learned a lot. When you have time, I’d appreciate your reflection comments. Thank you.)
Thank you for your work. I learned a lot too. Thank you!

extra.topic_sub: 先輩からのいじめ問題

interaction.content: Hello, thank you for being here today.
Hello, thank you for having me.
May we begin the role-play?
Yes, please!
Hello, I’m the counselor. What brings you in to talk with me today?
I’m struggling with my relationship with my husband.
I see. That’s a difficult issue in many ways. What is it about your husband that you’re struggling with?
Yes, I thought maybe it was strange to talk about something like this, but... I’ve been building up frustration about how my husband feels about our family...
I see. So a lot of frustration has been building up. That must be stressful. What kinds of things led you to feel that way?
Yes... Even when we have family plans on his days off, if someone from work invites him out, he prioritizes that instead, and I feel bad for the kids...
I see. He prioritizes going out with people from work... That really is hard on your children.
Yes, if it were work, that would be one thing...
Right. When you say going out, is it something like business entertaining, that kind of thing?

No, it’s a company my husband started, and he goes out with his employees. I’m a full-time homemaker, so without my husband’s income our household wouldn’t work, so I can’t really complain... He goes out drinking, goes to watch sports...

Your husband is the company president, then. Mm. Having to hold back in that situation must be painful. I see, so without much regard for the family, your husband spends his days off doing what he wants. You’d like him to help at least a little with raising your child, too. How old is your child?
He’s a boy in second grade of elementary school. Since he’s a boy, I think he probably wants to play outside with his father and things like that...
Yes, of course. Playing with his father and learning about the world that way is important too. How is your husband toward your child?

Yes, that’s part of it, and on his days off my son will just keep watching other kids playing ball with their fathers at the park, so it hurts to see. My husband always leaves early in the morning and comes home late at night, so I don’t really feel like he gives him much attention, but...
I see. So when you see the role other fathers are playing around you, you also feel like you wish he would do more of that.

When we sit around the dinner table, he does ask what school is like and things like that. Yes, with just a mother, there really are limits. Also, he’s never taken our family on a trip, but he goes on company trips about twice a year, so I can’t help thinking, what is that about?

It sounds like your husband is very busy with work as well. It seems like he does have interest in your child, but he also prioritizes his own outings. Mm. Ideally, child-rearing is something a couple can work together on.
Yes, he’s busy on weekdays and he’s not home on weekends either, so we haven’t been able to talk about what he thinks, but I do feel like he probably has some interest...
Yes. Listening to what you’re saying, I do think he has interest in your child.
I hope so...
You said your child is in second grade. Around when did your husband start prioritizing going out?
Well, it’s been that way ever since the company started getting on track, so...
Yes.
I think it started about five years ago.

About five years ago... So for quite a long time now, there have been many days when your husband hasn’t been around the home very much. That must feel quite lonely. What kind of work does your husband do?
Yes, not only my child, but I’ve been feeling lonely too. It’s in IT... a company that makes software.
Mm, you want him to think more about the family, and I’m sure there are so many things you want to talk about regarding your child’s growth. I see. It sounds like very demanding work.
Yes, there really are so many things I want to talk about, but when he says he’s tired and asks me to let him sleep, it’s hard to...
Mm. But then on his days off, he goes out...
Yes, but it’s a company he built himself, so I think he does feel it’s worthwhile. That’s right... So I really can’t talk to him about anything... Does he not want to come home?
I see, that may be part of it. He also has responsibilities as the president. So he’s really almost never home on his days off... Are there times when he doesn’t come home?
Yes, there are times when he only comes home in the morning to change clothes, or when he goes on overnight trips with employees. He does at least let me know by LINE, but...
I see, so there are times like that too. Mm. He does properly let you know, then.
Yes, he does let me know, but... I start wondering if maybe there’s someone he likes at the company... I end up wanting to suspect him, you know... haha

When things like that happen often, it’s natural to worry that maybe he doesn’t want to come home. I see, so those kinds of thoughts come up too. With your child still young, having to think about all of that as well must be really painful.
Yes... I’m worried, and it hurts, and I feel pathetic... If we didn’t have a child, I think I would have left him long ago.

You’re feeling that much pain, and yet your husband is just out enjoying himself all the time—it’s understandable that you’d feel sick of it. There are women working at your husband’s company too, then. About how many people work at the company overall?

Yes, working and going out to have fun—I end up thinking maybe he would have been better off staying single. Yes, when I glanced at photos from the company trip, there were women there too. The employees all seem young, maybe around 20 people. It’s not a big company, so it seems close-knit and like they all get along. A close-knit company... saying that myself just made me feel sad, haha.

I see. A company that has gotten on track, with 20 young employees—it does sound like it would be hard to manage. Mm, and because they’re such a close company, I suppose that’s why they have company trips and things. Mm, but his real home is with you. I can understand why that would make you feel sad. What was your husband like five years ago?

Yes, I think because it’s that kind of company, he works hard to create an environment where people can work comfortably. That’s something I can respect, but... if he could direct even one-thousandth of that effort toward the family, that’s how I honestly feel. Well, he used to want to be a comedian, so he likes making people laugh, and he used to help with housework too. He was like the embodiment of a service-minded person, so our home was always full of laughter.

One-thousandth... that really shows how little your husband has been involved with the family. That must be sad for your child too, not having much of an image of his father left in his memory. I see, so your husband’s personality is being put to use at the company. Even if you can’t talk at home, it sounds like you are able to stay in contact, so have you ever tried telling him these feelings through messages?

Yes, at home it’s just the two of us... I’m really worried about the effect on my child. But are all households like this? He does provide money, so was I just dreaming too much about marriage? You mean by LINE or email...? He’s told me not to call him during work, so I’ve never done that... I’m scared of putting this kind of thing into writing and having him read it when I’m not there. He’s a joker, and I wonder if he might show it off to his employees or something...

It’s difficult to say whether all households are like that. I was raised in a single-mother household, and I’ve only ever seen my father’s face in photos. I talk with many different people about their concerns, and I suppose what I can say is that every family is truly different. But what I can say is that the image of family you have is important.
I hate myself for imagining only bad things... I see. Maybe there’s no such thing as a family with no issues at all.
Mm, what you’re saying really makes sense. With LINE or email, those kinds of situations are imaginable. Let’s think about another way.

Thank you for telling me it’s okay to have this kind of image of a family. That really helped me. Counselor, did you not have painful experiences yourself? As a parent, the thing I worry about most is whether my child is holding things in...
Not at all. I also wish Japan were a place where that kind of family felt normal.
Thank you. And I’m grateful that you’re thinking about possible solutions with me.

In my case, my father wasn’t present from before I can remember, so I didn’t really have much pain toward him as a father. If there’s a chance to talk with your child, it might be good to talk with him about your husband. Your child’s feelings right now are important too.

I see. Thank you for sharing about yourself. Yes, I’ve never talked about his father with my child because I didn’t want to worry him. I think my son probably senses things in his own way and is holding back a lot, so I’d like to ask how he feels.

I see. Trying not to worry him... Thinking about this kind of issue all on your own is exhausting. If you can ask how your child feels about your husband, and what kinds of things he’s been holding back, it may give the client a hint about what you want to do from here. ↑ I mean you, the client. Sorry.
No, no 💦 I do think that’s true. If I can understand my son’s feelings, it will be easier to take steps going forward! When I think about my son, things like my own pride really don’t matter.

It’s only natural to not want your child to worry, and I think that feeling is okay to have. At the same time, when you do get a chance to talk with your husband, I thought it would be good to prepare so that your child’s feelings and your own feelings can really reach him.

Yes. I had only been thinking that I wanted to get out of this situation, that I wanted to leave him, but I can also prepare for a constructive conversation, can’t I? It’s kind of like the answer was right under my nose!

Mm. From what you’ve told me, it seems your husband relies on you when it comes to the household, so I think it would be okay to at least tell him that you want to have a home full of laughter again, like it was five years ago. Even after that, I don’t think it would be too late to choose to separate.
Yes, rather than saying five years’ worth of complaints, maybe I should try telling him how I feel!

Yes. Rather than complaining, tell him your feelings of loneliness, your child’s feelings, and the importance of your child having time with his father—not focusing on what your husband is or isn’t doing, but using “I messages,” like, “This is how I feel.” We’re at the end of our time, but is there anything else you’d like to discuss?
Yes, if that gets through to him, that’s good, and if it doesn’t, then it can’t be helped. Yes, I’m okay. Thank you very much.

Mm. Your husband also has a choice, after all. It’s difficult, though. Thank you as well. I hope that from here on, things can move even a little closer to what you want. This concludes the role-play. Thank you very much.
That’s true. Thank you very much!

extra.topic_sub: 夫とのコミュニケーション問題

interaction.content: (Hello. I look forward to speaking with you from 2:00 p.m. We’ll begin right at 2:00.)
Likewise, thank you.

(Thank you. I look forward to speaking with you.) Hello, I’m the counselor. Thank you for coming in for a consultation today. If you don’t mind, could you start by telling me your age, gender, and what you’d like to talk about?
I’m 60, male, and I’m anxious about my savings going down.
Thank you for sharing that with me. Could you tell me a bit more about it?
After retiring, I’ve been studying because I’d like to turn something I enjoy into work, but I’m not earning money from it yet.
I see, that’s how things are.
Yes.
Thank you. What kind of studying are you doing now?
I’m aiming to work in a sports-related field.
I see. When you say sports-related, would it be okay if I asked what kind of work specifically?
I’m thinking I’d like to do something to help children from here on.
You started studying because you want to do new work for the sake of children. I think that’s really wonderful.
Thank you. But I’m not earning money.
Yes, I truly think so.
What is it that you think?
I’m sorry, our messages crossed, and I made that unclear. I truly thought it was really wonderful. But you’re feeling anxious because you still aren’t earning money from it, is that right?
I understand now.
I’m very sorry for confusing you.
That’s right. Since my body is still able to move, I end up thinking that maybe I should do work that earns money after all.
I see. Do you feel that your current work doesn’t earn as much as you would like?
I don’t have much experience yet, so I think it will take years.
I see, so you’re concerned that it will take years before you start earning money.
Studying makes each day fulfilling, but living expenses are going out, and I’ve been in the red for about a year.
I see. I think it’s understandable that a conflict would gradually start to come up. You do feel a sense of fulfillment from studying, then.
That’s right, I’m torn. Yes, it’s something I’ve wanted to do, so the studying is fulfilling.
I see. I can tell that both studying and your savings are important to you.
When I think about the 100-year era, I sometimes feel anxious about both my savings and what I want to do. I mean the era of living to 100.
That’s how you feel. In an era of living to 100, I wonder if the road ahead can feel long at times.
I feel like I need to think about living expenses, and I also want to do what I want to do while I’m alive.
Yes.
Ideally, I’d like to turn what I want to do into a job, earn money from it, and live that way.
I see, you have a clear ideal for yourself.
I have an ideal, but what should I do in reality?
You’re concerned about the balance between your ideal and reality. That’s very understandable, and I think you’re thinking about it realistically. If it’s all right, may I ask you a few questions?
That’s fine. Please do.
Thank you. First, do you feel that you want to continue with your current studies going forward?
Yes, I think I’d like to continue even if it doesn’t make money.
I see. I can feel how strongly you feel about this. Could you also tell me why you feel that way?

Actually, after graduating from school, I wanted to work in a sports-related field, but my major was in the sciences, so I took the safer path and got a job in electronics. So I still have some lingering regret.
I see, so after retiring, you thought you would do what you truly wanted to do.
That’s right. I started studying about two or three years before retirement.
I think that shows wonderful initiative. So you don’t feel uncertain about continuing your studies as you are and keeping the goal of turning them into work, is that right?

It’s just that after retirement, I could have worked as a contracted employee for another two years with a decent salary, so when I look at my colleagues from the same year, I sometimes feel anxious about whether my decision was right.
I see. I think it’s natural to feel anxious when you see other people’s situations.
Yes.
At the same time, you have a strong feeling toward your ideal, so you’d like to connect that to a future you can feel satisfied with, wouldn’t you?
Yes, I’d like to be free of doubt about my decision and not feel anxious about my savings going down. What should I do to get to that point?

I see. I feel it’s wonderful that you have a clear goal. I think living expenses are what are weighing on your mind the most right now, but until you’re able to earn money through the work you’re aiming for, would it be possible to earn income in some other way? While continuing your studies, that is...
I registered with the local Silver Human Resources Center and am working, but I can’t earn as much as I expected. If I work full-time, it cuts into my study time.
I see. You’re making real efforts, and I think that’s wonderful. Can you estimate how long it will take until you’re actually able to earn money?
I think it depends on me, but I can’t make a prediction.
I see. I think it’s very understandable that you would feel anxious about that. Then I think an important point may be how to live with those anxious feelings until then. How does that sound to you?
Yes, I’d like you to teach me about that point.

It sounded to me like you want to continue your studies, but living expenses are also weighing heavily on your mind. Would you rather focus on moving forward with your studies even while carrying the anxiety, or would it feel easier to reduce your worries about living expenses by doing something like working full-time and then continue your studies little by little...? How do you feel about that?
I don’t want to do work I dislike just to earn money.
I see. Then for you, aiming to move forward with your studies and turn them into work sooner is more in line with how you feel, isn’t it?
I haven’t thought about whether to move faster or not, but I do think I want to go in that direction. It’s about time, isn’t it? I’ll think about it again on my own. Thank you.
I see, thank you. We’re just about out of time for today, but I felt it was significant that the direction of your feelings became clearer. How was it for you?
It still hasn’t become clear.

I see. I’m very sorry for that. Going forward, as you move toward your goal, if it seems helpful for us to think together about things related to living expenses or setting more detailed goals, please feel free to come for a consultation anytime.
Thank you.
Thank you for coming in today. We’ll end the consultation here.
(Thank you very much. I learned a lot.)
(Thank you very much. I’m sorry there were many areas where I fell short. I would be grateful if you could give me your honest evaluation.)

extra.topic_sub: 退職後の生活費に関する不安

interaction.content: Good evening. I have something I’d like to talk about. Is this reaching you?
(Good evening, thank you. I look forward to speaking with you.)
(Thank you.) Good evening, I have something I’d like to talk about.
Good evening, I’m the counselor. Thank you for coming to talk with me today. To start, could you tell me your age, gender, and what I should call you here?
I’m 22, male, and please call me “Yu.”
Thank you for telling me. What would you like to talk about today?
For the past week or two, I’ve been having trouble sleeping deeply.
I see... That sounds really hard. Did anything happen a week or two ago?
No, I can’t think of anything, but I’ve started waking up many times during the night.
I see... Not being able to sleep soundly until morning is hard on both your mind and body.
That’s right. I fall asleep easily, but my sleep is light and I don’t feel rested.
I see, so it feels like you can fall asleep smoothly when you go to bed. Yu, how do you feel about waking up so many times during the night?
I feel anxious when I think this might keep going on like this.
That makes sense... When you think about how long this situation of light sleep and not feeling rested might continue, it would make you feel very anxious.
Yes. I wake up every two or three hours, and I’ve started feeling scared to look at the clock.

Yes... Every time you look at the clock and think, “I woke up in the middle of the night again,” it brings up anxious feelings, doesn’t it? I imagine it must also be difficult in your daily life, with the fatigue still lingering. With life continuing like this right now, what kinds of difficulties are you having in your day-to-day life?
My job is physically demanding, so when I’m still tired, I can’t work the way I usually do. And emotionally, I get depressed thinking, “What if I can’t sleep again today?”
I see. So it’s affecting your work too. That sounds really hard.
It is hard.
For these past two weeks, you’ve been carrying those painful feelings on your own while still doing your best at work. You’ve really been trying so hard.
I appreciate you saying that.

I imagine that these days of not being able to sleep have been exhausting for you, both mentally and physically. It must have been very painful. Thank you for sharing this with me. Aside from not being able to sleep, is there anything else that feels depressing or weighs on you?
Because my sleep is light, I have a lot of dreams, and they’re usually dreams from my student days. That’s a period I personally don’t really like, so that’s unpleasant too.
I see... Only as much as you feel comfortable sharing, could you tell me what kind of dreams they are?

When I was a student, I lived by desperately trying to fit in so other people wouldn’t dislike me, and bowing down to people with loud voices. Even when something felt wrong according to my own values, I’d just grin and get through it. So I hate the person I was back then. But I have dreams where I’m living the same way again, being overly considerate and watching people’s reactions.
I see... You went through some very painful experiences. In your life now, do you ever find yourself prioritizing others over your own feelings in the same way you did back then?
It depends on the time and situation, but I almost never just go along with others while being overly considerate anymore. Now I live mainly according to my own values.

I see. I’m glad to hear that. So now you’re living in a way that values your own values. Then, because you wake up over and over during the night, having to go through painful experiences in your dreams is also making you feel depressed.
Yes. It’s something I’d rather not remember if I can help it.
That makes sense... Then even sleeping, which should be for recovering from fatigue, becomes a very painful time.
Yes. I end up worrying before I go to sleep.

That sounds hard. You do physically demanding work, so your body must be exhausted and wanting to rest, but when you have worries like that, going to sleep becomes painful... A week or two ago, when you were sleeping normally, did you not have those kinds of dreams?
When I did dream, I would sometimes have those kinds of dreams, but most of the time I slept deeply and didn’t even dream.
I see, I see. Until now, you were getting good sleep that allowed your brain to rest properly.
Yes. I think I was getting very good sleep.
I see. So compared with that time, your sleep quality has gone down now.
Yes.
What kinds of things do you think about before going to sleep now?
Things like, “I’m worried about work tomorrow if I can’t sleep,” or “What if I wake up in the middle of the night again?”

I see. Certainly, if I were in your position, I think I’d feel very anxious too, wondering what I’d do about work tomorrow if I couldn’t sleep. It seems the brain has a tendency to keep searching through what you were thinking about before sleep, even while you’re asleep, so apparently the brain keeps thinking all night about whatever you were thinking right before bed. I wondered if that might possibly be part of the cause. How does that sound to you?
That might be true. The longer the days of not sleeping go on, the more I’ve become conscious of it.
I see. That must have been a very painful situation.
Yes.
Then I was thinking it might be good if, right before bed, you could relax and think about something pleasant. Is there anything that feels enjoyable or relaxing for you, Yu?
I guess it’s better if the enjoyable thing isn’t the kind that gets me worked up or excited?

Yes, that’s right. Before bed, I think it may help your autonomic nervous system settle if you relax while thinking about something pleasant, and then after you wake up in the morning, think about exciting, enjoyable things.
I see. I think I’ll try that starting tonight.
That’s wonderful. I’m sure tonight will be a very calm time of sleep for you.
Yes, thank you.
Thank you as well. I’m thinking we’ll end today’s consultation here. Is that okay?
Yes, that’s okay. Thank you for listening and talking this through with me.
Thank you. I’ll be quietly hoping that you have lovely dreams and are able to rest well, Yu. If anything else worries you, please feel free to talk with us anytime.
Yes, I’ll reach out again.
(I learned a great deal today. Thank you very much.)
(Thank you as well.)
(Thank you. We’ll end the role-play here. Thank you for your work today.)

interaction.content: (Hello. Thank you for dealing with the error. Would it be all right if we get started right away?)
Yes, sorry. I can only make time until 11, but thank you in advance ^^

(Thank you! I understand about ending at the scheduled time as well. Then, I’ll go ahead and begin.) Hello. I’m the counselor. Please feel safe to talk about anything here. To start, could you tell me your age, gender, and what you’d like to discuss?
Thank you in advance.
(Thank you, and likewise.)
42 years old, male, I’m struggling with work-related things.
Thank you. So you’re struggling with work... Could you tell me specifically what the situation is?

I had been running a company, but I let go of everything for the time being, and although I had an annual income of tens of millions of yen, it became zero. I had lived my life working hard for status and honor.
I see... That sounds like a painful situation... I imagine you have worked very hard up to this point.
I didn’t say it was painful.
So it’s not “painful,” then. How are you taking in your current situation?
Rather than saying it’s painful, would it be okay if you listened until the end?
Yes. Of course. This is your time, so please go ahead and continue.
I have worked hard throughout my life, but I thought that unless I went after achievements and results, I was worthless. So
Yes. (I’m listening, so please continue.)

I produced a lot of results, but even so, I couldn’t obtain the things on the scale I had envisioned. So, I thought I would let go of everything for the time being, bring it to zero, and let go of my attachment to achievement. But, once I let it go, of course it’s not that I have no anxiety about what comes next, so I’m at the point of wondering what to do. I think the background is pretty hard to understand, sorry.

I see... No, not at all. Thank you for sharing that with me. Because you weren’t able to get the results you had hoped for, you chose to let go of things for the time being. In the current situation, it makes sense that you would feel anxious...
Yes, that’s right.
Even though it was something you chose yourself, there must be a lot that feels uncertain... By the way, I’m a little concerned—how are you managing day-to-day right now?
When you ask how I’m managing right now...
After letting go of the company for the time being, are you taking action toward what’s next, or on the other hand, there may be times when you don’t feel motivated—how is it for you?

I do have motivation. Right now I’m giving my all for the small number of clients I’m currently working with. I don’t have dreams anymore, but it feels like I’m doing my best in the present... It’s just that my income has become one-tenth of what it was, so I do feel like I have to do something about that. I have a family too.
You’re giving your all to what you can do right now. When you have a family, it’s natural to have worries about income... By the way, has your partner said anything about this?

She’s anxious, and we’ve been fighting more. I also have about 100 million yen in debt. I’m the type who tends to think things will work out somehow, so there’s an optimistic side to me too, but my wife is sensitive, so it seems she has a lot of thoughts about it.
I see, that’s how it is. So while you do feel anxious, you’re also able to think about it optimistically. What do you think you’d like to do from here?

I’m wondering what to do. If I just go earn small money again, it’ll end at the same kind of level, and even if I keep running a monthly deficit right now, do I see this through until new values or realizations come up...? That’s the difficult part. If I half-heartedly start a business again, then there was no point in letting go of everything...
You’re in the middle of thinking through many things in order to move on to the next step.

Every day is full of inner conflict. I’m going to do something about it, so I don’t really want my wife to keep saying various things to me, but of course she’s going to worry. If I look at the anxiety, it’s anxiety, but I want to look toward the possibilities.

You’re taking your partner’s feelings into account while also searching for a direction with possibility. Listening to you, I get the sense that you’ve faced forward and worked harder than anyone up to now. And that no matter what you choose, it may be time to move toward the next step from here. I’d like to help you organize the points you’re struggling with today, if that sounds okay to you.
Thank you very much. I’d appreciate that.

Thank you as well. I’ll support you as much as I can. Earlier, you mentioned that you’re struggling with whether to start earning pocket money again or to stay here and see this through—is that correct?

Well, to put it simply, I guess that’s it. It’s not pocket money, but small money. (By “small money,” I mean an amount that fits within the limits of what I’ve done up to now.) Sorry for the slightly crude wording. I mean both money and scale.
No, not at all. Thank you for correcting me. I’m sorry. Small money, and scale. What would you like your future to look like?
That’s the thing, there isn’t really anything I want to become, but if I had to say, I feel like I want to make the most of my potential.
I see. There isn’t something specific you want to become, but you want to make the most of your potential. You’re looking forward. What does your potential mean to you, specifically?
I wonder what it is... That’s what I don’t know.
So right now it feels like it isn’t clear yet. When you’ve been working, what kinds of moments have made you feel happy, or feel that it was meaningful?

My work is mainly interpersonal—I’m an instructor, consultant, and coach—but I think it’s when people are happy, or when they’re freed from suffering, or when they gain a major realization in a seminar and their faces become bright. That makes me really happy. On the other hand, I sometimes overdo it and end up getting hurt a lot too.

I see. You’ve valued your clients’ growth and changes in how they feel. If you feel that way, I’m sure your clients can place their trust in you. To return to the earlier topic a little, regarding whether to deepen things at the current scale or to stand in a new field and find possibilities there, one method when deciding something is to write out the pros and cons so it becomes easier to judge things objectively. Since we’re getting close to the end of our time today, next time I’d like to share and explore your thoughts around this together, and support you in organizing your thinking. How does that sound? I’d also like for us to think together about your current anxious feelings and what you want things to look like from here.
Thank you very much. Please go in that direction.

Given how you’ve faced forward and worked hard up to this point, I believe you can find possibilities even in your current situation. I’ll support you with everything I can, so please feel reassured. Well then, since our time is up for today, I’d like to send the closing message. Would that be all right?
Thank you very much for today. I learned a lot.
No, not at all. I’m glad we were able to talk. Thank you for today. I’ll send the closing message now. (Thank you very much. I learned a great deal! Take care.)

interaction.content: (Good evening. Thank you for being here today! Once it’s time, we’ll get started.)
Good evening! I was doing housework, so I’m sorry my reply came right at the last minute. Thank you as well, I’m looking forward to talking with you.
Not at all. It’s okay＾＾ Thank you. Thank you for coming in for a consultation today. If you don’t mind, could you tell me your age and gender?
I’m a 35-year-old woman.
Thank you for answering. What would you like to talk about today?

I have a daughter in junior high school, but she doesn’t help out. I’m a single mother, and I’m pretty overwhelmed doing housework and everything. When I get home from work I’m exhausted, but even when I talk to her, she just lets it go in one ear and out the other. I’m struggling with what I can do to get her to help.
I see… Is that right… You’re balancing work and housework, which is already so much, so that must be really difficult… What kinds of things would you like your daughter to help with?

Just bringing in the laundry and folding it would be enough. I think it would be nice if she washed the dishes once in a while too… but I’m not even asking that much, so at the very least I’d like her to wash her own water bottle. No matter how many times I tell her, she barely even does things for herself. Like leaving her raincoat from a rainy day just thrown down somewhere…

I see… You’d like her to at least do her own things to help lighten your load, so it’s exhausting when she doesn’t, isn’t it… You mentioned that when you ask her to help, she just lets it pass by. What is your daughter like in those moments?

She half-listens while playing with her phone, and when I say something inconvenient for her, she runs away, things like that. I’m not yelling at her or anything. Very, very rarely, if I’m really at the point of being like, “I seriously can’t do this anymore!” she’ll help… that’s about it. We get along well, and she’s not in a rebellious phase, but she’s just simply lazy… I keep wondering how I can get her to help without me having to say anything.

I see… So she does help once in a while. I think it’s very good that you’re telling her without getting angry. What would you like me to call you? A nickname is fine too, so I’d be glad if you could let me know.
Please call me “Karuta.”
Karuta, then. Thank you for answering. When did you start wanting your daughter to help with housework?

Since she started junior high school. I think it was about a year ago. Five days a week, after work, I drive her to and from her lessons, which takes two hours round trip, and the stress of waiting and all that increased, so I started feeling physically worn out.

I see… Work alone is tiring enough, and then driving two hours round trip afterward is truly a lot… I can really feel how hard you’re working, Karuta, with your daughter, the housework, and your job. Have you talked with your daughter about how you started feeling worn out about a year ago?

I have told her things like how driving at night takes a lot of focus and makes me tired, and that I’m getting older too so it’s hard… But it’s like it’s someone else’s problem to her. I feel like she’s the type who won’t understand unless I collapse.
I see… Is that right… That’s really difficult… When your daughter does help once in a while, what kinds of things do you say to her?

I say, “Thank youuuuuu!!” and praise her like crazy. When she brought in the laundry, I would definitely go all the way to her room and make sure to thank her. I mean, honestly, even just that much is really helpful, so I genuinely said thank you. But it doesn’t last. On top of that, she said, “I hate kids, and I don’t want to do housework, so I’m definitely never getting married…”

That’s wonderful! I think it’s very good that you make sure to praise her properly. I see… She’s still in junior high school now, so her thinking may change as she gets older. Why do you think it doesn’t continue, Karuta?

I hope it changes, but she’s been kind of cold about things like that since she was little…💧 I wonder why. I really don’t know at all. It feels like she thinks it’s normal to have things done for her. It looks like she has this sense of, “Why should I, the child, have to do something like that?”
I see… That is troubling… Looking back, do you think there were times when you handled the housework so efficiently that there wasn’t really room for your daughter to help?

Ah… that’s true. Even when she said she’d do something, if I thought it would end up creating extra work, I’d cut her off and say, “Oh, you don’t have to!” Or because I hated it if things weren’t done perfectly, I wouldn’t let her do it…
I see… It’s possible that after those things happened repeatedly, she may have thought, “It’s easier if Mom just does it by herself rather than me helping!”
That’s very, very possible…
I see… Then, if it’s all right, I’d like to briefly summarize what I’ve heard so far. Would that be okay?
Yes, please.
Because housework, work, and driving her around are so difficult, you want your daughter to cooperate, or at least do her own things herself. That’s how you feel, Karuta. How does that sound?
That’s exactly right.
Thank you. Then, how would it be if we think together about how to communicate this to your daughter?
Yes, please! I honestly don’t know anymore how to say it so it will get through to her.

Yes… it’s difficult, isn’t it. I think the key is to tell your daughter the point you noticed earlier yourself: that up until now there wasn’t much room for her to help, and that you had been carrying all the housework by yourself.
Yes, I see.

It might be good to honestly tell her something like, “Up until now, Mom has been trying hard to do all the housework perfectly by herself, but now that you’re in junior high school, I’d like you to help me with it from now on.”
Okay. I’ll start by telling her that. What should I do if her reaction is kind of lukewarm…

Right… I think your daughter simply hasn’t developed the habit of doing housework or helping yet, so after that, it may be good to have her help with small things first. For example… Since it would be hard for you too if laundry and other housework didn’t get done, how about leaving your daughter’s water bottle unwashed as it is? If she needs the water bottle, she may start washing it herself, filling it with a drink, and taking it with her. What do you think?

I tried that before… She didn’t wash it even by morning… In the end, I washed it in the morning. One time when I still didn’t wash it, she just didn’t take it. She said, “If I have to wash it, it’s too much trouble, so I just won’t take it.” It’s serious. There was one time she finally washed it after I kept saying it beside her. She won’t even prepare tea for herself when she goes to her own lessons… Maybe I’ve been doing too much for her…

So that happened… I think you were doing it out of care for your daughter, so I don’t think we can simply say you’ve done too much. It’s possible that if you leave it unwashed, she may wash the water bottle, or she may buy tea for herself. It may be helpful to keep in mind that you won’t do anything until she realizes that if she doesn’t do it herself, she will be the one who has a problem. What do you think?
Thinking about it now, maybe I was overprotective… Yes, I may need to steel myself a little and try it, since it’s gotten this bad. I’ll try doing it the way you suggested. Thank you!

I think it’s completely natural to feel like you want to say something. When it’s something where your daughter herself will be inconvenienced if she doesn’t do it, and she has to take responsibility, it may be good to watch over her. I’d like to talk a little more, but we’re just about out of time. I’m sorry.
Yes, that makes sense. I really understand what you’re saying. It’s okay, I can see a direction now!

I’m glad to hear that. Your daughter is kind and does help when things are really hard for you, so if she can develop the habit of doing housework and helping, she may start doing it on her own. Please give it a try. And please feel free to come back for a consultation anytime.
Yes, I’ll do my best to help her develop it as a habit. Thank you very much!
Thank you as well. Then, I’ll end the consultation here.
Yes, excuse me^^

(Thank you very much! Sorry we went over time! I learned a lot!)
(We’ll end here.)
Please don’t worry about the time at all! I also learned a lot, and I’m grateful that you gave me advice that was genuinely helpful.
(Thank you＾＾!)

interaction.content: (Good evening. Thank you for being here today. We’ll begin when it’s time.)
(Thank you as well.)
Good evening. I’m the counselor. Thank you for coming to talk with me. To start, could you tell me your age, gender, and what you’d like to talk about today?
Nice to meet you. I’m a 35-year-old woman. I’ve been feeling dissatisfied with my husband about how we split things like childcare, and lately I’ve been getting irritated.
I see. You mentioned dividing up childcare—for example, what kinds of things make you feel irritated? Could you tell me a bit more about that?

Well, both my husband and I work, but when our child gets a fever, I’m the one who leaves work early to pick them up, or takes the day off. When I really can’t go, it becomes like I have to ask my husband, and I think, why do I have to ask?

I see. You’re both working, and you’re raising your child together, so having it become something you have to ask your husband to do feels somehow strange. I think it’s very natural that you would feel that way.
Right? We make about the same salary, so lately I’ve started feeling that way.
Yes. Since you’re both working in similar ways. How are things with childcare and housework?
I think he takes the initiative with childcare at home, so maybe that’s about fifty-fifty. For housework, I think I do about 70 percent.
I see. It sounds like you feel your husband is doing his best with childcare and housework at home too. How does that sound?
Yes, I mean, I do think he does a lot.
Yes. So is it that you’re feeling burdened because your work is being affected more? It sounds like you take your work responsibilities very seriously.
Yes. I’m usually the one who does daycare drop-off and pick-up, and I’m also the one who takes paid leave more often. I do feel bad when I take time off or leave early.

Yes. That makes sense. Childcare isn’t just directly taking care of the child—it’s also drop-off and pick-up, taking time off when your child is sick, adjusting your work because of that, being considerate of your coworkers... those parts don’t get much attention, but they’re really hard.
Exactly!
Yes. It’s only natural to want him to notice that and understand it.
Yes. I want him to understand.
Yes. I think there are many people who feel the same way and want that to be understood. Is it hard for your husband to take time off because of his workplace environment?
His workplace is almost all men, so maybe it’s hard for him to take time off. Even when I was pregnant, he often went to work drinking parties, so we used to fight about that.
Is that right. So you feel it may be an environment where it’s hard to get understanding, being a male-dominated workplace. Is your workplace okay?
Yes, my workplace has a lot of people with children, and many people are understanding, so it’s okay.
I see. I had the sense that you’re someone who is very considerate of people at work too, so I’m relieved to hear there are many understanding people there.
Yes. That part really helps.

I imagine that may be because you yourself have been understanding toward coworkers around you who are raising children. Listening to what you’ve shared so far, I’m hearing that you want your husband to understand the hard parts of childcare that he hasn’t noticed. And because you’re trying to balance both work and parenting properly, you feel sorry about the impact on your workplace. How does that sound?

Yes, that’s it. Actually, I’m about to move up into a management position, so I feel like things won’t be able to continue the way they have. My workload has actually been increasing too. Until now it was okay, but I’m starting to think I really need to be working properly.
So there have been changes in your situation like that too. When you think about the future, it makes sense that you’d feel even more responsibility and start to feel anxious.
Yes, exactly.
Right now, with your workload increasing, have there been changes like work being left unfinished or your coworkers being affected?
I bring home the work I can’t finish and do it there, so I don’t think there’s been any impact.
I see. So you’re bringing work home and making sure it doesn’t affect your workplace.
That’s right. I want my husband to try a little harder with things at home, and I want him to do pick-up too.

Yes. It’s completely natural to feel that way. You’ve been doing your best somehow to balance work, childcare, and housework on your own. But I’m concerned about you trying to keep pushing yourself even more from here on. At the same time, you do have clear hopes that your husband will do more at home and help with pick-up. What do you think might help move things closer to that situation?
I did talk to my husband, but he says, “I’m already doing enough,” and we can’t come to an agreement. And there’s no one nearby we can rely on...
You had already had a proper conversation with him, then. When you can’t come to an agreement, it takes courage to bring it up again.
That’s right. It feels like we’re both irritated.
Yes. And if there’s no one you can rely on, that makes it even more anxiety-provoking. Is there anyone you can talk to about your frustration or consult with?
I talk to my friends and my mother. But it just ends up being them listening to me vent.
I’m glad there are people you can talk to, even just about your feelings. In that case, it does seem that having your husband understand is the most important thing.
Yes. I know he does plenty, though.

Yes. From the beginning, you recognized your husband’s efforts too. I felt that you’re a very kind person. But given how your work situation is going to change from here, I think there is a reality that things may not work well as they are. After acknowledging your husband’s efforts, what would it be like to tell him about your future work situation, and also one specific thing that would really help if he could do it?
Yes. I haven’t really told him about my work situation yet, so I think I’ll try telling him that.

Since you’re both working, having to “ask” him leaves me feeling unsettled too. But I think it may be one way to communicate that reflects your kindness and can reach your husband, so it may be worth trying to talk to him that way.
Okay.

I also think this is a situation that has come about because you work responsibly, and that has been recognized. I truly hope you’ll share this with your husband, and that things will improve even a little. Thank you for letting me listen to you today.
Thank you as well.
We’ll end the consultation here. (I’m sorry it ran long. I learned a great deal. Thank you very much.)
(Thank you so much for the full hour. I’ll give you feedback again.)
(Thank you. I’ll end it here, then.)

interaction.content: Good morning. We’ll begin when it’s time. Thank you for being here today.
Good morning. Thank you for seeing me!
Good morning. Thank you for coming to talk with me today. To start, could you tell me your age, gender, and what you’d like to discuss?
I’m 28, male, and my concern is about friendships.
Thank you for sharing that. So you’re struggling with friendships. Could you tell me a bit more about that?
I feel like I don’t have any friends I can call close friends...
That’s how it feels to you. Was there something that made you start worrying about this?
I’m close with a group of three, but I’m always the last one. I think the other two, excluding me, are the real close friends.
That’s how it feels to you. How long have you been friends with the two of them?
We’ve known each other since high school. We were teammates on the rugby team.
So you’ve known each other for about 10 years. Could you tell me a bit more about why you feel like you’re the last one, and that the two of them are actually the close friends?

What really made me feel sure was that one of the two got married. And the one appointed to give the speech as the friend representative was the other guy. Other than that, the two of them share the same lessons or hobby, they go on trips together, and even when we go out drinking, they invite me last, after the two of them have already settled their plans.
I see... Thank you for sharing that with me. Is your relationship with the two of them good?

I definitely think the two of them like me. They’re always looking out for me... But deep down, I’m not really sure. If we’re just talking about the surface-level relationship, I think it’s good, but... Also, I basically never invite them out for drinks myself. I’m always the one being invited.
Right, I think they invite you because they like you, and if they disliked you, they wouldn’t invite you. You said that deep down, you’re not really sure—what kinds of feelings are there?
Hmm, it’s hard to put into words, but somehow, when I’m with them, I’m not sure if I’m being my “real self.”
I see... When you’re with your friends, you wonder if you’re not able to show your true self—is that right?
Yes. I feel like I’m deliberately acting cheerful in front of them.
I see... Why do you feel like you’re acting cheerful?

Actually, they’ve both had excellent grades since we were students, and even now they work at bigger companies than I do. Somehow, in those areas too, I feel inferior to them. So I feel like I’m deliberately acting cheerful partly to hide that.
I see. Thank you for telling me all of that. Have you ever thought about how you’d like things to be with the two of them going forward?
It’s definitely not that I have complaints or dissatisfaction with them. So if anything is going to change, I think I should change the way I see them.
I think it’s really wonderful that you’re able to think about it that way. I’d like us to think together about how you might change things going forward—how does that sound?
Yes, please. I’d really appreciate that.

Thank you. Then let me summarize what you’ve shared so far. You’re close with your friends from high school, but you don’t have friends you can call true close friends. The two of them share the same lessons or hobbies, go on trips, go drinking, and then invite you last, so you feel that maybe the two of them are actually the close friends. You also feel inferior in front of them, and you wonder if you’re not able to show your real self. But the two of them like you, and you also don’t have any dissatisfaction with being with them. Is that right?

It’s not so much “I don’t have friends I can call close friends,” but more like, “Can I call these two my close friends? Are they my close friends?” That’s the nuance. I don’t know myself, and that’s why I came to talk about it this time...
Thank you for correcting me. As we just summarized that, did anything come up for you?
Looking back over it again, I started to wonder why I’ve been one-sidedly feeling hostility and suspicion toward these two kind people.
That’s what came up for you. Would it be okay if I shared a little of what I felt as well?
Please do.

Thank you. The relationship among the three of you has been maintained well for over 10 years, so I think it’s a really lovely relationship. I don’t think there’s just one fixed form of a close friendship. From my perspective, I think it’s a very good relationship to call a close friendship. How does that feel to you? I mean, I think it’s a relationship that you could call a close friendship.
The two of them are closer to each other than they are to me, but even so, are those two my close friends?

I don’t think a person can only have one close friend. I also think the two of them probably see you as a close friend. The reason is that, from everything you’ve told me, I can really see that they have trust in you. I think it’s a big realization that you wondered why you had hostility and suspicion toward them—how does that feel to you?
That’s definitely true. This is a really big realization.
I think it’s very good that you came to see it that way. Going forward, what kind of feelings do you think you’d like to have as you spend time in your relationship with the two of them?
I think I should enjoy it more purely. They’re very important to me.

That’s wonderful. I think people who are very important to you are exactly what close friends are. I’m sure you’ll be able to keep having a good relationship from here on, too. When the three of you meet, it would be good if you could gradually express your feelings honestly little by little. I’m sure the good relationship will continue, so I hope you can deepen it slowly.
Thank you. I think I’d like to do that.
We’re just about out of time, but if anything else comes up, please come talk again. Thank you for today.
Thank you very much.
Well then, I’ll be going. (Thank you for today. I learned a lot. If you have time, I’d appreciate it if you could leave a rating. Thank you.)
(Thank you as well. I learned a lot.)
(Thank you. Then I’ll end the session now. Take care.)

interaction.content: Thank you for doing this role-play with me today.
Thank you as well.
Hello. Thank you for coming in to talk with me today. To start, could you tell me your gender, age, and what you’d like to talk about?
Hello. Thank you for meeting with me today. I’m 35 years old, and I’m a woman. I contacted you because I’m struggling with relationships.
Thank you for answering. You’re struggling with relationships, then. Could you tell me a bit more about that?

I don’t have a very good relationship with one of the mothers whose child goes to the same kindergarten as my daughter. Even when I talk to her, she ignores me. I don’t know the reason, so I don’t know what to do. For my daughter’s sake, I want to have good relationships with all the mothers, but,
You have a daughter, then. Being ignored like that must feel very sad.
Yes.
When do you feel that kind of relationship started?
A year ago.
I see. Was there anything that seemed like a trigger at that time?
That’s the thing—I’ve thought about it over and over, but I can’t figure it out.
I see. That must be painful. How are your relationships with the other mothers?
My relationships with the other mothers are good. But there’s one mother who is closest to that mother, and I feel like the way she looks at me is a little different too.
I see. Do you mean that the mothers have formed groups among themselves?
No, that’s not what I mean. There are people who are individually close with each other, but people do normally talk with all sorts of different mothers.
I see. Do you ever talk with the other mothers about that mother—let’s call her Ms. A?

I have asked for advice. I asked one of my mom friends, “I feel like her attitude is different only toward me—what do you think?” My mom friend seemed to have noticed the difference in her attitude too.
I see. I imagine that took a lot of courage. Did your mom friend say anything else?
I didn’t say anything more than that, so… But she did say that being ignored for no reason must be really hard.
Yes. It’s comforting to have a friend who understands how you feel. How is the relationship between your daughter and Ms. A’s child?
My daughter has a quiet personality, and Ms. A’s child is active and very outspoken, so even if they’re in the same class, they’re not the kind of friends who play together.
So it doesn’t seem like a fight or trouble between the children is the cause. Being ignored for a whole year, without knowing the reason, must really wear on you.

I don’t think the children have anything to do with it. They hardly have any contact. When someone keeps ignoring you for so long, it feels like I’m going to lose my mind. If I knew the reason, I’m the type who would apologize right away. Being ignored means either she just doesn’t like me, or I unconsciously did something that hurt Ms. A. And if it’s the latter, I feel really sorry, so...

Yes, I can understand how you feel. Do you have any thoughts about what you’d like to do with Ms. A from here on? For example, “I want to know the reason,” or “For my daughter’s sake, I want to keep interacting with her normally.”
I don’t need to become close with her or anything. Right now, I just want to at least be able to talk normally.
Yes. Does Ms. A ignore you even when you talk to her normally? How about greetings?
Yes. Even when I say “Hello” to her first, she very clearly turns away and ignores me.
It’s so sad that you can’t even exchange greetings. Do you think it might be possible to ask her, just once, in that moment, why she’s ignoring you?

I’ve thought about that many times, but when she’s actually in front of me, she gives off such a cold impression, and I feel this kind of “don’t talk to me” aura from her, so it’s hard to say anything more than a greeting.
Yes, with that kind of attitude, it would be hard to speak to her.
Yes. It’s been going on for so long that I just don’t understand it.
Within you, how strong is the feeling that you want to know the reason?
Very strong. When someone ignores you for this long, I end up thinking, “Did I really do something that bad?”
Yes. One year is a long time. Do you think it would be possible to have someone mediate and help you have a conversation?
Have someone mediate… That would end up causing trouble for that person, so I’ve never thought about it.
I see. Has your daughter sensed anything?
My daughter doesn’t know anything about this. It has nothing to do with the children.
I see. I’m sure she watches her mother closely. You’re someone she loves very much, after all.
Do you mean my daughter has noticed something by watching me?

No, I don’t know that, but I thought there may be times when your painful feelings and your happy feelings come across to her. I’m sorry. The time has gone over, and I also couldn’t find the right words. I can really sense how much you want to improve your relationship with Ms. A.
Yes. What you said earlier—“I’m sure she watches her mother closely”—felt very off to me. It was kind of scary.
That’s how it felt to you. I’m very sorry for hurting you.
I wish you had understood a little more what it’s like to be ignored by another person for an entire year.

Because you’re a mother she loves very much, I was thinking I wanted to help you, the client, be able to smile again, including myself, but I think, looking at it myself, that I skipped over the painful situation you’re in now and moved too far ahead too quickly. I’m truly sorry. I will reflect deeply on what happened today and make use of it going forward. I’m very grateful that you pointed this out to me.
(Were those words just now directed toward the client?) (We are still in counseling time right now, so please keep that in mind.)
(I’m sorry, I got confused.)
(It’s okay on my end. Let’s take it calmly.)
I think this past year, this long period of time, has been truly painful for you. And it’s still continuing even now, isn’t it?
Yes.
I’d like for us to think together about what might help improve your relationship with Ms. A from here on, but we’ve run out of time. Would you come back and talk with me again?
Yes… I’ll think again about what I should do. Thank you for today.
Yes. I’m sure we can find a good way forward. Thank you for coming in to talk with me today.
Thank you. (Thank you for your hard work over such a long time. It’s fine to end the role-play now. Thank you for today.)
Well then, I’ll end the role-play here. I’d appreciate it if you could please do the evaluation.
