interaction.content: (Hello. Thank you for being here today. We’ll begin when it’s time.)
(Hello. Thank you for seeing me today.)
Hello. I’m the counselor. Thank you for coming in today. To start, could you tell me your age, gender, and what you’d like to talk about?
I’m 42, female. I’ve always been single, and I’ve never had a partner, and I feel unsettled, wondering if it’s okay to go on like this.
Thank you for answering. I see… That must feel like a lot to struggle with…

Yes. Around the time when everyone was rushing to get married in their early 30s, I didn’t really have much desire to marry. But now almost everyone is married and has children… I thought I could live on my own, but there are times when I feel lonely and unsure.
I see. That must feel unsettling…

Yes. People around me have called me things like “tough,” “cool,” or “a strong woman,” but deep down, I envy women who are married and settled. I moved to Tokyo from Kyushu when I was in university and have lived alone ever since, and after graduating I worked hard in a career-track position.
I see. You’ve been working hard and building your life on your own all this time…

Yes. I didn’t want people around me to see me worrying or feeling down, so I tried not to complain much and just kept going. I supported myself with the pride that I was far more independent than most women around me.
Yes, listening to what you’ve shared so far, I can really sense that you’ve lived your life with strong convictions…

Thank you. But in the end, there are times when women who get married, rely on men financially, and live being protected by them seem happier… And I sometimes feel empty, wondering what all my efforts up to now were for.
You feel that way too… You’ve worked so hard to live your life up to now, so I think it’s okay to give yourself credit for that.
Thank you. I do like and acknowledge the part of myself that has worked hard. But there’s also a part of me that feels miserable about having lived a life with no connection to men.
I see… Because you’ve prioritized your work and your life over men up to now, that may be why those connections didn’t happen, perhaps. What do you think?

Hmm, I do think there were ways I was able to satisfy myself through my own hobbies. But there were men I thought were nice, and I confessed my feelings to them, but they always only saw me as a friend.
I see… Even when you clearly expressed your feelings and confessed, it would feel discouraging if it didn’t really reach the other person…

Yes. I felt down, wondering if I had no appeal as a woman. But after I started working, taking classical ballet lessons and going to see musicals and stage plays became my greatest joys. I thought I was living proudly, believing I could make myself happy. But still, I’ve often been troubled by what you might call socially accepted happiness, or the common idea and trend of “a woman’s happiness.”
I see… So while you broadened your world even further and worked on yourself, you’ve also lived all this time feeling confused by society’s trends and ideas…
Yes. I think somewhere inside me, I do have a longing for marriage and having children.
You feel that way too… You’ve worked harder than most to build your life up to now… At this point, what do you feel would help you feel satisfied with yourself?

The biggest thing is, I feel like I could be satisfied if I found a partner who was right for me and could get married. Since I’ve never even dated someone of the opposite sex before, I don’t feel like it would be that easy to find someone, though…

Thank you for telling me… Yes, if you’ve never dated someone of the opposite sex, it’s natural to feel anxious… Listening to your thoughtful perspective, I feel that you’re really looking ahead and thinking seriously about this…
Thank you.
By the way… is there anyone of the opposite sex you’re interested in right now?

No. The people I think are nice are usually married. Friends have told me things like, “I’m sure you’ll find someone good who suits you,” but it just doesn’t happen. I keep going back and forth between thinking it’s boring to keep thinking about this, so I throw myself into my hobbies, and then still ending up bothered by it after all.
I see… That would make you feel at a loss…
Yes, I want to get out of this endless loop.

I think it’s completely understandable that you end up thinking about all kinds of things… These days there are various systems like dating apps, matchmaking events, and marriage-hunting services. How do you feel about those?

I registered with a marriage counseling agency and met with several people. But it was painful, because I could tell I wasn’t the type they were looking for, and even when I talked about my hobbies, the conversation didn’t really get going.
I see… You’ve taken concrete action in a very real way. But when things don’t go well, it can really wear you down…

Yes. Friends who really wanted to get married were much more dedicated to marriage hunting than I was, and they got married. As for me, I’m not having trouble getting by right now, so I can’t put everything I have into marriage hunting. But the unsettled feeling is always there. It’s half-hearted, isn’t it.
That’s how you’ve been thinking about it… No, not at all. From listening to you, I can fully tell that you’ve been taking concrete steps to make your own happiness happen.
Thank you.

I don’t think it’s half-hearted at all… You’ve done marriage hunting, and since becoming a working adult you’ve started doing many things to broaden your perspective, so please, do have more confidence in yourself. By the way, what kinds of things have you talked about with the person in charge of your marriage counseling agency?

Thank you. The person in charge recommends that I meet a wide range of different people, including people more than ten years older than me and people who have been divorced. It may be asking too much, but I just don’t feel up for it, so I’m taking a break from the service right now. I also don’t really like being confronted with something like my “market value”…

I see. It feels unpleasant to have labels put on you based on society’s arbitrary judgments… Listening to you, I can really tell that you’ve kept looking forward and have worked hard to live on your own up to now…

Yes, in the marriage market, in the end, for women it comes down to age and looks that appeal to men… I also don’t really want to wear clothes that feel like I’m trying to pander. I felt like the version of myself doing marriage hunting was becoming unlike me.
You feel that way too… Forcing yourself would be exhausting. In order to find a future partner, what method feels like something you could manage for now without too much strain?
Hmm, I don’t know. I haven’t tried it yet, but an acquaintance married someone they met on a matching site. I feel some resistance to it somehow, but I also feel like maybe I could try it.
You feel that way too. I’ve listened to many things you’ve shared up to this point, but I’m sorry, we’re getting close to the end of our time. How has it been for you, talking about this so far?
I feel like I was able to let out the vulnerable thoughts I usually can’t say to people around me, and you listened to them.

Thank you. I feel that you’ve worked hard and lived on your own up to now, engaged in marriage hunting, and continued searching for your own happiness… Whether it’s a matching site, restarting marriage hunting, or other approaches, I think there are many possible ways. Please don’t lose heart, and keep moving toward the happiness you’ve already found, and toward an even truer happiness for yourself. I’m rooting for you. I’d like to end our consultation here for today. Thank you very much.
Thank you for encouraging me.
(Thank you very much for today. I’ll give the signal to end shortly.)
(Thank you very much.)

interaction.content: (Hello, today I’ll be practicing the counselor role for the first time. Thank you in advance.)
(Hello. It’s your first time, then! Thank you as well.)
Hello, I’m the counselor. Please tell me your age, gender, and what you’d like to talk about.
Hello. I’m a 27-year-old woman. I’m struggling with something at work.
I see. What kind of work-related issue are you struggling with?
The other day, some important documents went missing, and I ended up being blamed for it. Since then, I haven’t been able to go to work.
That happened, then. That must be really painful.
Yes. Even though I think I have to go, I just can’t make myself go.
I see. I imagine it’s putting such a mental burden on you that you can’t go to work. How has your physical condition been lately?
At night, I can’t sleep much, and during the day, I’m extremely sleepy instead and just sleep the whole time.
I see. I’m relieved to hear that you are getting some sleep. When did you become unable to go to work?
About a week ago.

I see. I imagine you may be feeling anxious about not being able to go to work for a week. To the extent you’re comfortable sharing, could you tell me about the situation around the important documents going missing?

Yes. I work in administration at an insurance company, and I had put some important documents to give to a client in a drawer. But they disappeared, and everyone looked for them, but we couldn’t find them. Then the next morning, they were left on my desk. In the end, no one knew who had put them there, and my supervisor told me to write an incident report. I can’t trust anyone, and I don’t want to go to the company anymore.
That happened, then. I’m glad the important documents were found, but you were blamed for it, and it left you feeling frustrated and unable to trust the people around you.
Yes, I’m frustrated. Everyone thinks it’s my fault...
I think it’s only natural that you would feel that way. How long have you been working at your current company?
About five years.
You’ve been working hard there for five years. Before this happened, what kind of communication did you have with your coworkers around you?
I hardly talk to people at work. Since I transferred departments about a year ago, I haven’t been able to communicate with them at all. It feels like everyone just silently works away.
I see. So that’s the kind of environment you’ve been working in. I imagine that when communication isn’t possible, work may not always move forward the way you’d like. How do you feel about that?

Well, the work itself can be managed somehow if we communicate by email, so that part was relatively okay. But working in an office that’s completely quiet, with no small talk or anything, felt suffocating.
That makes sense. I imagine working in that kind of situation ever since your transfer must have felt tense as well. Is there anyone around you who you feel you might be able to talk with a little?
I got along well with people in my previous department, so when I occasionally passed them at the company, I would talk with them a little, but I haven’t talked with them in much depth.
I see. I wonder if not having anyone you can talk to might cause stress to build up. What do you think?
Yes. I’d already been feeling down about going to work before, but because of this incident, I just can’t go anymore.
I see. I imagine you may also feel pressured because you can’t go to the company. Have you talked with anyone at the company about this, or spoken to people around you?
I feel very pressured. I’ve told the company I’m not feeling well, but it’s already been a week, so I can’t take any more time off... What should I do?
I see. Have you thought about telling your supervisor about your current situation? I imagine you’ve been doing your work responsibly up until now. What do you think?
Right... but I don’t know how to talk about it.
I see. When you say you don’t know how to talk about it... could you tell me a little more?
Is it okay to honestly say that I don’t want to go to the company? I feel like they’ll just tell me to quit, then...
What kind of person is your supervisor? How do you usually communicate with them?
We don’t really communicate much. This time too, they left it unclear who put the documents there and, for the time being, told me to write the incident report. Maybe I have no choice but to quit.
That’s right, that’s what happened. It makes sense that you’d feel so pressured you’d want to quit. If a coworker came to you with the same concern, what would you say to them?
I don’t know...
I see. Thank you for answering. Going forward, do you want to keep working at your current company?

Well, if possible, I’d like to continue, but I just can’t bring myself to go. In the morning, when I try to go and start getting ready, I start feeling sick. It’s not okay, is it, becoming unable to go to work over something like this...

I think you’re going through a lot of emotional pain. I’m concerned about your well-being. I think you’ve been working hard up to now in a tense environment. I get the sense that you’re someone with a very strong sense of responsibility.
Do you think so...? But thank you.

Thank you for talking with me up to now. We’ve reached the end of our consultation time, so next time, I’d like us to think together about what might help you be able to go to the company. I hope you’ll come back to talk again.
I understand. Thank you very much.
Then we’ll end today’s consultation here. Thank you for sharing your story with me.
Yes, thank you very much,
(Thank you for your valuable time today. I was terrible. I learned a lot.) (I’ll send the closing message.)
(No, not at all. Thank you as well for listening to me so carefully.)

interaction.content: Good morning. Once it’s time, we’ll get started. Thank you.
Good morning. Yes, thank you.
Good morning. I’m the counselor. Thank you for coming for a consultation today. To start, could you tell me your age and gender?
Good morning. I’m 17, a second-year high school boy.
Thank you for telling me. What would you like to talk about today?
It’s not like I’m really, really struggling or anything, but I feel like my mom has been kind of cold toward me for a long time... and it’s just been on my mind.
I see. Thank you for telling me. What kinds of things make you feel that she’s being cold?
I feel like she doesn’t really look at me much when she talks to me. With my younger sister, she talks to her a lot, and I feel like she makes eye contact with her too.
So that’s how it feels to you. When did you start feeling that way?
I think things were okay when I started high school, but after I quit high school, I feel like she became colder.
So that happened. In that kind of situation, I think it’s natural that your mother’s responses would be on your mind. Could you tell me a little about what your mother is like?

My mom is, for better or worse, a normal person, I guess. She likes cooking and making sweets and stuff. She seems to enjoy talking with the neighbors too. She used to get mad at me a lot, but now she doesn’t get angry at me anymore... it feels like she’s busy taking care of my younger sister... and I don’t know, I might be feeling lonely.
I see. She sounds like a kind mother. Just to check, when you say feeling lonely, do you mean your mother is feeling that way?
Oh, sorry, I mean me.
Thank you for clarifying.
Because my mom doesn’t get mad at me anymore. It makes me wonder, does she not care anymore...?
I see. How long ago was it that you quit high school?
I quit high school in the first semester of my first year.
I see. So does that mean this kind of situation has been going on for about two years? Or about one year?
Oh, right. I’m in my second year now, so I guess a little over a year. When I first started high school, she made me lunches with lots of side dishes in them. She was kind.
I see. I can also feel your kindness toward your mother coming through.
Thank you.
How are you spending your time now?
After I quit public high school, I transferred to a private school. Since the second semester of my first year, I’ve been going to that private school.
I see. Do you also feel that things like what’s in your lunch have changed now?
She stopped making lunches for me. She gives me money. Maybe because I go to school sometimes and don’t go other times, she got tired of making them.
I see. That would make you feel lonely in a lot of ways, and it would be on your mind.
About the lunches, I think it’s my fault. There were times I stayed up playing games until the middle of the night or early morning and couldn’t wake up, so I didn’t go to school...
So that happened too. You mean the lunches she went to the trouble of making ended up not being needed because of you.
Yes, there were times like that. The lunch would be in the refrigerator, and when my mom was at her part-time job, I would eat it for lunch.
I see. Are there still times now when you can’t go to school because you play games too much?
There are. When it’s a lot, maybe about twice a week. When it’s not much, maybe about three times a month. There was also a day I had a certification exam, but I overslept and couldn’t take it...
I see. When that happens, how do you feel afterward?

Even then, my mom didn’t say anything to me... (Even though my teacher contacted her, so she should have known I was late and couldn’t take the exam.) I did feel like, I really messed up... but after I got home that day, I was playing games again, so maybe my mom is fed up with me. I know I have to do what I’m supposed to do... but games are too fun and I can’t stop. Lately I’ve kind of been giving up, thinking maybe it can’t be helped because I have a developmental disorder...
So you have those feelings. When you say developmental disorder, what do you mean by that, and how have you come to understand it that way?
I was diagnosed when I was in eighth grade. I have autism and ADHD.

I see. Including those things, you’ve been feeling like your mother has gradually become less interested in you. From what you’ve told me so far, even though you feel your mother’s responses are cold, you also recognize that there are problems with your own behavior, that you feel you haven’t been able to do what you should.

Yes. It was my mom who said we should go get a diagnosis. When I got diagnosed, she said she felt relieved (maybe because she was relieved to know the reason), but now somehow it feels like, I can’t do anything because I have a disability, so it can’t be helped. Yes. I do recognize it. I think I have to do something about it... I have to decide what to do after school too...
I see. That would feel lonely.
It does feel lonely. Not being scolded is lonely.
Yes. It feels like you can somehow sense that she isn’t interested in you... and even so, you’re thinking about trying to do something.

Yes. Not even being scolded feels lonely. My younger sister can kind of do anything, so my mom works hard every day taking her to and from lessons and things. I keep thinking, what should I do... but then I end up playing games...
I see. Do you feel that if you could stop playing games, something might change? I meant, “I see.” Sorry.

Yes. I end up playing for like seven hours a day... and I go to sleep at around 3 in the morning... so I think if she could see me studying at home, or if I could pass the math certification exam, maybe my mom might be able to smile a little.
I see. If you could see your mother smile, perhaps the way you feel now might start to change.
Yes. Right now she really doesn’t smile at me at all... so I think I have to change...
That’s how it feels to you. I think you’re a very kind person who cares deeply about your mother.
No, it’s because of me...

That’s how you feel. Still, for your mother’s sake and for your own sake too, I hope you’ll value that feeling of wanting to change. We’ve gone a little over time, but how do you feel after talking today?
Yes. For my own sake and for my mom’s sake, I want to value this feeling of “I want to change,” and then think about what I should do first... Could I come back here to talk about that another time?
As a counselor, I’m very glad that you’re feeling that way. I would really like you to come talk again. Let’s think concretely about what you can do.
Yes! Thank you very much. I’ll come again. I don’t know what to do on my own, so I’d like you to think it through with me. Thank you again. Thank you for today.

Yes! I’ll be rooting for you from here on too. Please take care of yourself as you move forward. Thank you for talking with me. (I’m sorry we went over time. I learned a great deal. Thank you very much.)
(Thank you very much ^^ I’ll send my reflections later ^^)
(Thank you very much. Take care.)
(Take care *ᴗ ᴗ)⁾⁾

interaction.content: Thank you for meeting with me today.
Hello. We’ll begin the role-play. Thank you.
Thank you.
Thank you for coming in for a consultation today. To start, could you tell me your age, gender, and what you’d like to talk about?
I’m a man in my twenties. My job search isn’t going well.
Thank you for answering. So you’re currently job hunting. It’s painful when things don’t go the way you’d hoped.
Yes. It’s not going well, and I’m feeling very anxious.
Are you currently a student?
I’m a fourth-year university student.
I see. When did you start your job search?
I’ve been job hunting since last year. Every place I wanted has rejected me, and it’s been really hard.
I see. That must be exhausting, both mentally and physically. Since you’re a fourth-year student, are you expected to graduate next spring?
Yes. I’m completely worn out. I really can’t stand the thought of continuing the job search anymore. I’ll graduate next spring.
I can understand that. How are things going for your classmates around you?
Everyone is getting job offers one after another. I feel rushed, but I just can’t find the motivation anymore.
When you see everyone around you getting things decided one after another, it’s natural to feel rushed. Have you been able to talk with any teachers or advisors about this?
I have talked to them, and they listen, but in the end, I’m the one who has to do it.
Yes, in the end, you’re the one who has to decide. What kind of jobs are you looking for?

I applied to financial institutions, but I was rejected by all of them. Since I’m in the humanities, I suppose it would be sales or a general career-track position, but there isn’t really anything in particular that I want to do.
It must have been very frustrating that the places you tried for didn’t lead to a job offer...
Yes. I worked hard, but it didn’t work out. I don’t even know what I want to do anymore.
Right now, it sounds like your motivation has gone down a bit, and I imagine you’re also very tired. Do you think it might be possible to spend some time away from job hunting for a while?
Yes, I’d like to take a little distance from it. But I feel like that won’t change the reality of anything.
That’s how it feels to you, then. When you have time off, if you were to do something you enjoy, what would you do?
I like reading books.
I see. Books can take us into all kinds of worlds, and they’re really wonderful, aren’t they?
Yes. It’s important time for me.
Yes, it sounds like very important time. Among the books you’ve read so far, have there been any that connect to future work or interests?
Let me think. I like self-help books, and I’ve also read a lot of books about starting a business. I’m interested in entrepreneurship too.
I see. I can really tell that you’re very studious and hardworking.
Thank you.
Perhaps there may be a new option for you—not only choosing from existing companies, but eventually starting your own business.
Yes. I’m job hunting, but I sometimes think it might be okay to consider becoming independent as an option too.
I meant starting a business. I’m sorry. Yes. I feel that you’re surely someone who has that kind of ability.
Thank you.
Have you decided specifically what kind of thing you’d like to try?
I have a vague image of it, but it’s not clear yet.
I see. It might be enjoyable to take your time thinking about that from here on.
Yes. Thank you.
Having talked this far, has there been any change in how you feel compared with the beginning?
I had been feeling rushed about finding a job, but somehow I’ve become able to feel that it isn’t everything.
I see. I’m glad to hear that. I think that by stepping away for a bit, going outside, or doing things you enjoy, new options can sometimes emerge.
Thank you. I feel a little more at ease. It really isn’t good to get too rushed, is it?
Even if, at the time, it feels like the situation isn’t changing at all, in reality you may be moving forward little by little.
That’s true. Thank you.
I’m really rooting for you and your future success. Were you able to talk about what you wanted to talk about today?
Thank you. Yes, I was able to. I feel a little lighter now.
Thank you. Our time is up now, so we’ll end here.
Thank you very much.
Thank you for the role-play today.

interaction.content: Can you see me this time? Sorry for the trouble.
I can see you. I’m sorry for the technical issue. Thank you for being here today.
Thank you too! Is it okay if I play the same role as the person seeking consultation from earlier?
Yes, thank you.
Got it!
Hello, I’m the counselor. Could you tell me your age, gender, and what you’d like to talk about?
I’m 18, female. I failed the entrance exam and I don’t know what to do.
(It seems the system is still acting a little strange. It may take me a bit longer to reply.)
(Understood.)
I see. You failed the entrance exam, and you’re going through a really painful time.
Yes.
What kind of day-to-day life are you living right now?
I don’t think I can recover from this. I’m at home.
That sounds very painful. Are you able to eat and sleep?
I don’t want to eat. At night I can hear my heartbeat and I feel anxious, so I can’t sleep.
I see. You don’t have an appetite. Has your family said anything?
They’re encouraging me.
Not being able to sleep at night must be really hard.
Yes. I want to disappear from this world.
Does it feel like you can’t bring yourself to do anything right now?
I’m anxious and scared. I’m the only one in my class who failed. The road ahead feels painful.
I see. You’re really going through something painful.
Yes.
Are you able to think about what comes next at all?
I wanted to go to a junior college for childcare and become a kindergarten teacher. But I can’t go to junior college, so there’s no meaning in being alive.
I see. You had a clear goal, and you’d been working hard toward it. You’re struggling so much that you feel there’s no meaning in being alive.
That’s the only dream I have.
It feels like your dream ended halfway through, and that’s really painful.
Yes.
Do you still feel the same way about wanting to become a kindergarten teacher?
I can’t become one, but I want to. It’s so frustrating.
It may not be possible right away, but do you think it would be difficult to try again?
Maybe I can’t right now. But I have to.
I see. It feels like you can’t think about the future yet right now.
I’m scared I’ll fail again.
Yes. You’re also seeing it in a forward-looking way, like you have to do it. And at the same time, even if you work hard again, you’re scared you might fail.
Yes. What should I do?
How would it feel to take a little time to rest?
I want to rest. But I also feel like I’ll be left behind.
How about taking a little rest and waiting until your mind feels more able to move forward?
Won’t it be too late?
I don’t think it would necessarily become too late once you’re feeling better.
How can I get better?
For now, how about waiting for recovery, and when your mind feels back to normal, trying again?
Will I recover just by staying alive?
To feel better, I think it’s important to get enough rest and to start feeling like you want to do something.
I understand.
Thank you for sharing with me. Would it be all right if we end here?
Yes, thank you very much.
Thank you. We’ll end here for today.

interaction.content: (Good evening. Thank you for meeting with me today.)
Thank you. If you have any preferences about the settings or anything, please let me know.
(Thank you for your consideration. I don’t have any in particular, so I’ll leave it up to you.)
Understood, thank you.
(We’ll begin when it’s time.) Good evening. I’m the counselor. To start, could you tell me your age, gender, and what you’d like to talk about today?
I’m 16, male. This spring, a friend from high school quit school, and school stopped being fun. I want to be able to go to school feeling cheerful again.
Thank you. Your friend quit school, then. That must feel lonely.
There is some loneliness.
School has stopped feeling enjoyable, then. You said you’re 16—what year are you in now?
I’m in my second year of high school.
I see. How long had you known the friend who quit?
They’re someone I met for the first time after starting high school.
You met after entering high school, and they became a very close friend.
Yes.
It’s been about half a year since your friend quit. Are you still in touch now?
We don’t really contact each other anymore. A lot of the time, I don’t get much of a reply.
I see. When that happens, it becomes hard to reach out.
Yes.
Could you tell me how you feel about your friend having quit?
It is disappointing, but I think it can’t be helped.
You feel that it can’t be helped. What reason did your friend give for quitting?
They said the reason was that it snowed and going to school became a hassle.
Do you and your friend live somewhere with a lot of snow?
Yamagata Prefecture.
Thank you for telling me. I’m sorry, I’m not very familiar with the climate in Yamagata, but in winter, does the snow pile up and make commuting to school difficult?
It’s difficult. I do my best to get to school by bicycle.
Ah, I see. Riding a bicycle on snowy roads is very dangerous and tiring, and really hard...
Once you get used to it, everyone’s fine with it and rides to school.
I see. I’m sure people get used to it quickly, and they have the stamina to keep at it.
Yes, everyone grew up in the snow.
So you know how to live with the snow. You said it can’t be helped that your friend quit school because of the snow—what made you feel that way?
They’ve already quit and aren’t at school anymore, so there’s nothing I can do about that, so I think it can’t be helped.
Thank you for telling me. Yes, at the beginning you said you wanted to go to school feeling cheerful. How are you spending your time at school now?

There isn’t anyone in my class I really click with, so during breaks I pretend to sleep. There are days when I don’t want to go to school, and on some days I deliberately take a long way around and go in late.
That sounds painful... Have you been spending your time in that kind of situation for about half a year? What do you do for lunch?
I think I started acting like that around June. It’s not really that painful. It just feels uncomfortable being at school. I eat alone in the classroom.

You’ve been doing your best to get through these three months since around June. It can be exhausting to spend time adjusting to people you don’t really click with, too... Can you think of anything that might help you go to school feeling brighter?
When that friend was there, I felt lively, so I think it would be good if I had something new, some purpose for going to school.
Thank you for telling me. A purpose for going to school, then. Do you have any dreams for the future?
I want to go to Tokyo and work in comedy.
That’s a wonderful dream—being able to make people happy. Did you maybe talk with that friend about your dream?

I don’t remember if I said it clearly. But I thought that thinking about how I could make that friend who quit laugh, and trying it out, might have been the reason I was able to enjoy going to school.

I see. You wanted your friend to laugh. I can sense your feelings toward your friend, and the kindness you have. We’ve talked up to this point, and our consultation time is almost over. How has it been for you to talk about this?
I think I was able to sort out, for now, what kind of presence that friend who quit was to me.

Thank you for sharing that. I think you were able to sort it out through your own strength. Today’s consultation will end here, but if you feel like talking again, please come anytime. I’m rooting for you, and I’d always like to hear what you have to say.
Thank you.
I think Yamagata will be getting colder from here on. Please take care of yourself. Thank you for sharing your story with me. (Thank you for your time. I learned a great deal. Thank you very much.)
(Thank you as well!)
(We’ll end here, then.)

interaction.content: (Hello. Thank you for being here today. We’ll begin when it’s time.)
(Thank you.)
Hello. I’m the counselor. To start, could you tell me your age, gender, and what you’d like to talk about?
I’m 40, female. I end up comparing myself to other people, and it’s painful.
Thank you for telling me. That sounds really painful... When do you find yourself comparing yourself to others?
I think, even though I’m working this hard, why am I not happy? Other people look happy to me.
I see. What kinds of times do you feel that you’re not happy? And when do other people look happy to you?

I work every day from morning until night, so I have a job, I have income, I have children, but when I see housewives around my age or people working part-time laughing, I feel like they seem happier than me.
Is that a little hard to answer? Sorry, our messages overlapped.
It’s okay.
I see. So at those times, you end up feeling, “I’m not happy.” Even so, you really are working so hard!
Every day is just going back and forth between home and work... When I think that life might stay like this until I retire, it feels painful.
I see. That’s how you’re feeling. Work and raising children—your days must be very demanding. How does that feel for you?

Yes. On top of that, there are difficult things both at home and at work... Housewives seem like they’re enjoying themselves without being tied down by work, and there are so few enjoyable things in my life.
Yes. (I’m listening.)
I feel like I can’t catch my breath anymore.
That’s... you really have been trying so hard... For now, please give yourself a lot of credit.
Thank you.
When you’ve been working that hard, it makes sense that other housewives would look that way to you.
Yes...
What kinds of feelings are there in that “...”?
I think housewives are working hard too. But I wonder why I can’t feel happiness well.
I see, so that’s the feeling you’ve been having. But there are actually quite a few people who come for counseling who feel that happiness is hard to feel, so please don’t worry.
Yes. Even small happiness would be enough.
Yes. You want to find small moments of happiness.
Lately, I don’t understand my own feelings.
I see. When you say you don’t understand your own feelings, what kinds of times do you mean?
Like looking at flowers and thinking they’re beautiful, or looking at the sky and feeling good.
Does it feel like you used to be able to feel those things, but now you can’t?
Yes, that’s right.
I see. I’d like for you to be able to feel that richness again.
Yes.
Listening to what you’ve shared so far, what I’ve felt is that you’re a kind person, and that you work really hard every day.
Thank you. But I can’t keep trying any harder than this.

Of course. You’ve already been trying more than enough. I don’t think you need to push yourself any harder. If anything, I was thinking it might be good to increase the time you have to soothe and care for yourself. How does that sound?
I want to increase it. But work is busy, so it’s hard to make time.

I see. Then, to understand your situation a little better, would it be okay if you told me what the flow of a typical day looks like? If you’re comfortable, please also tell me about your family structure.
I leave home at 7:30 and get back around 7:30 p.m., then dinner and cleaning up, I guess. My son is in his second year of junior high, my daughter is in her first year of high school, and my husband.
Thank you. I see... That really does sound like a situation where it’s hard to find time.
Yes.
In that situation, would you be willing to think together about how you might be able to make some time for yourself?
Yes.
Then, if you did have time, what would you want to do?
I’d like to slowly just zone out.
That sounds nice. Just zoning out.
I don’t want to think about anything.
Yes, of course. There are so many things you have to think about every day. Is there anything else you’d like to try doing?
I’d like to listen to music and drink coffee.
That sounds nice. What kind of music do you like?
I like K-pop.
I see, that’s nice. These days there are lots of tools where you can listen to all kinds of music.
Yes.
I was thinking a little—since you have three children and they’re getting older, how would it be to have them share some of the housework?
My junior high school child gets home late from club activities, and my high school daughter does help a little with cleaning up and things, but she doesn’t cook at all...
I see. How about washing dishes, laundry, or cleaning the bath? Maybe you could tell your family a little about how exhausted you are.
When they were in elementary school, they would do things like clean the bath or cook rice, but my daughter ended up not going to school, so she’s really just doing all she can to manage herself.
I see, that’s what happened. Then, would it be difficult to find someone in your family who seems like they could help a little?
We can’t divide things up any more than this. I’m only doing the bare minimum myself, though.
I see, that makes sense. Then how would it be to create just a very small bit of time to feel relieved, in the little gaps—like before bed?
Yes. I think I’ll try to get into bed earlier. I was able to let out things I’d been thinking but hadn’t been able to tell anyone, so I feel a little lighter.
I’m glad if I was able to help even a little. We’re still in the middle of talking, but we’re getting close to the end of our time. Still, if there’s anything on your mind, please let me know.
I’m okay.
I understand. Thank you for sharing today the things you hadn’t been able to let out to anyone. I hope you’ll come here again anytime to talk things through.
Thank you very much.
Please give yourself lots of credit for how hard you work every day. Thank you.
(Thank you very much.)
Thank you for today. We’ll end here.)

interaction.content: Thank you for meeting with me at 10:00.
Thank you as well. I look forward to it.
Do you have any preferences for the client?
I'll leave it up to you.
Understood. I'm ready to start anytime.
What would you like to talk about today? Could you tell me your age range and gender?
I want to die... I'm in my 30s, female.
You're feeling that overwhelmed. Please start wherever you feel able to talk. I'll listen to whatever you can share, even a little.
I don't have a job, and my boyfriend dumped me, and there's no point in living anymore.
You've lost hope in going on living. What is your life like right now?
I'm living off my savings, but I don't have much left anymore, and I'm just drinking all the time.
Your life is really difficult right now. And you're drinking because you want to forget.
Even though I don't have money, I'm drowning myself in alcohol. I'm the worst, right?
You feel like you want to rely on alcohol, don't you. It's so unbearably sad that you want to forget.
No one would worry about me anymore, and even if I died like this, no one would notice.
Thinking that far ahead must feel lonely. Is there anyone you can contact—a family member, friend, or coworker?
It's not like I feel lonely or anything anymore. I haven't contacted anyone. I don't want to. I don't want anyone to know I'm in this situation. I want to disappear like this without anyone knowing.
That's how deeply you're feeling this. Yes... you don't want to contact anyone.
There's no way anyone would understand if I talked to them.
You did well to come here and talk. It takes courage... thank you.
Thank you too, for listening to me when I don't even make sense.
Even if you talk to someone, they won't understand... Is it that you don't want to trust anyone?
Even if I trust them, in the end they'll betray me, won't they?

I'm sure there are people who will listen to you. Betrayal... you must have gone through something terribly painful. I hope that by talking here about what's happened, you can feel even a little lighter.
It was painful, but I guess it couldn't be helped. I think now it's only natural that someone wouldn't want to be with someone like me, but it hurt. Because I trusted him.
Yes, anyone wants to trust people.
If trusting only means getting hurt, then it's better to be alone. But I'm tired of being alive, too. And I'm going to run out of money soon, so I think maybe it's okay if I die.
You don't want to trust and get hurt anymore.
Right, I don't want to get hurt. Even if I keep living, I don't think anything good will happen anymore.
We need to do something about the money. There may be a way to get help with the procedures for benefits somehow... You are probably a gentle person who gets hurt easily. I'm sure of it.
Even if someone like me gets benefits and survives, I feel like it's a waste of money.
That's why you don't want to get hurt anymore, isn't it. I hope that talking at a support counter might make you feel even a little lighter.
That's right. I don't want to get hurt, so I'm going to die. Thank you for listening.
I am one person who hopes you will live with hope.
How can I have hope? What meaning is there in someone like me being alive?
What kinds of things can give you hope? What kinds of things do you like? I think the fact that you're here, alive, has meaning and value in itself.
I wanted to keep working, and I wanted to marry my boyfriend. But all of that is gone now. So there's no meaning in being alive, right?
Yes, I hear you. What led you to leave your job?
I was fired because of COVID.
What kind of person was he? I'll listen from wherever you can talk.
We had even talked about marriage, but he was cheating on me with my friend.
Because of COVID? That must feel so frustrating. It seems to me you did nothing wrong.
At work, I worked hard for 10 years and contributed so much, but they cut me off so easily. My boyfriend was the same. My friend too. I trusted them, and I was the only one who didn't know.
With your boyfriend too, you must be full of the feeling of being betrayed. After working hard for 10 years, that's awful.
Right? It's awful, isn't it?
It feels like your friend betrayed you too. You're at the very bottom of grief.
That's why I'm scared to try hard anymore or trust anymore, and I don't want to.
But let's climb up from that very bottom. Because you worked hard for ten whole years.
No, I don't want to try hard anymore.

And he cheated on you with your friend—that's awful. If you had married him, please try thinking about what kind of life that might have been. I see... you don't want to try hard anymore. You don't have to try that hard, because you've already worked so hard up until now. At any time, when you're exhausted, it's surely necessary to rest too.
How can I die painlessly?
You're so overwhelmed, and it's just too sad. I feel like I want to be someone who supports you. Please, I want you to value your life, at least...
If I value my life, will anything good happen?
It's enough just to be alive. Because you are wonderful.
What part of me is wonderful?
Because you've faced betrayal by your boyfriend and friend, and you worked hard at your job for 10 years.
Is that so...
I hope you find work from here on too. Because you're living so earnestly.
(It's time, isn't it. Thank you very much.)
It would be such a waste. Please live, precisely because you are you. This concludes the role-play. Thank you very much.

interaction.content: (Thank you for being here today. We’ll begin when it’s time.)
Thank you.
Hello, I’m the counselor. Thank you for coming in for a consultation today. To start, could you tell me your age and gender?
I’m 16, female.
Thank you. What brings you here today?
Every day is hard.
I see... It’s okay to take your time, but would you be willing to talk about how you’re feeling?
A year ago, because of my father’s job transfer, I started going to a local school in America. I still can’t speak English very well. I can’t make friends.
I see... That must be really painful...
I want to go back to Japan.
That’s how you’re feeling...
Because I think if I were in Japan, I’d be having fun with my friends like normal.
Yes...
Sometimes I end up being alone at lunch too.
I see... That’s lonely... You said you still can’t speak English very well; does it feel hard to talk to people?
Even if I want to have a conversation, if I don’t understand the English the other person is speaking, I feel inferior, and I think they must be bored too. So the conversation doesn’t work.
I see... That sounds exhausting... What are the local students like? Do they ever come and talk to you?

They almost never talk to me. Until just recently, a Japanese friend at the same local school had been eating lunch with me, but she lived overseas when she was little and can speak English, so she went off to an American group. I got left behind...
Hmm, I see. That must have been sad... What was it like when you were in Japan?
I had a close group of friends, and we were always together on the way to school and during lunch break.
I see. In that case, your situation now must feel even lonelier... When you spend lunch break alone, how do you usually spend it?

After I eat my sandwich alone, I study English vocabulary. The reality is that English isn’t something you can improve at easily, and also, Americans aren’t really interested in kids who can’t talk much, and they’re enjoying their own world. I’m not even in their sight. That’s what it feels like.
I see. Even while things are painful, you’re trying hard to be able to speak English, but it isn’t easy, and you feel that the other students aren’t friendly...
Yes. School isn’t fun, and on Mondays especially, my stomach hurts too.
I see... When you feel depressed, changes can start showing up in your body too... Have you ever talked to anyone about your current situation?

When I told my parents it was hard and that I wanted to go back to Japan, they yelled at me, saying, “Then go back by yourself!” Since then, I can’t tell my family. At the local school there isn’t a homeroom teacher either, so I don’t really know who I should talk to.
I see... So since then, you’ve been enduring it all on your own...
Yes.
Thank you for talking with me when things are so painful. I’m asking because I’m worried about you: are you able to eat? How is your sleep?
I can eat. I can sleep. But sometimes my stomach hurts in the middle of the night.
I see... That’s concerning... What do you do at those times?

I told my mother once, and when we went to the hospital, they did an X-ray of my stomach. The result was that there was no problem, but a Black nurse spoke at me really fast in English I couldn’t understand, and it was scary.
Hmm... You went through something that frightening too... That’s awful...
It was my first time being made to drink barium, and it was painful, and I didn’t understand when they said things like more, or don’t burp, over and over and over. I thought I was going to die.
That was really hard... I think it must have been very painful not to have your feelings understood. What was your mother like at that time?

She was worried. But I don’t think she knows what happened during the exam and stuff. My mother seems to be dealing with all kinds of things too, like my younger sister and brother, so I can’t really talk to her in detail either.
You have younger siblings too... So you’ve been holding it in all by yourself... You really have been carrying so many worries until now, and it’s been painful...
Yes. My parents say that saying you don’t like something you don’t like is selfish, so maybe I’ve been holding it in.
That’s how you’ve been thinking... Holding it in...
So having someone listen to me here, somehow it’s making me cry.

I think you’ve done so well enduring it all this time. You’re still only 16. You’re at an age where it’s okay to get help from other people. I imagine it took courage to come here too. It’s okay to talk about anything here, so please let out the things that are painful.

Thank you. It’s comforting to think that someone understands. I think I’ll try talking a little with the English teacher for the class for students whose second language is English. In that class, everyone is someone who can’t speak English well, so it might be easier to talk to them.
There’s a class like that, then. I think it would be good to try talking with those people.
The students in that class all end up gathering together, like Koreans with Koreans, Chinese with Chinese, and that makes it kind of hard to join in too, but I’ll try little by little.
I see. But they may be struggling in similar ways too... After listening to what you’ve shared so far... would it be okay if I tell you what I’m thinking?
Yes, please.
Your life in America started a year ago, and because of the language barrier, you haven’t been able to make friends at school and you’ve been feeling lonely...
Yes.
You want to go back to Japan, but that can’t happen, and since your parents yelled at you that one time, you haven’t been able to tell them how you really feel...
Yes.
You had a frightening experience at the hospital too, but because of your younger siblings and other things, you couldn’t tell your parents, and you’ve been enduring it all this time...
Yes.
But in the class for second-language students, you thought maybe you could try talking to someone... How does that sound?
Yes, that’s exactly right. I guess I do still think there isn’t an option to run away from this environment...

Mm-hmm, yes... I think your perseverance is truly admirable. But... saying you don’t like something is not necessarily selfish. I think it’s important to communicate your feelings. So talking to someone about what you’re struggling with and getting help is not selfish; I think it’s necessary.

Hearing you say that makes me feel relieved. My friends in Japan only envy me, saying things like, an American high school, getting a foreign boyfriend, improving my English, but there’s no one who understands the reality. I want to find someone I can say “this is painful” to.
I see... Even if it may look enviable on the surface, the reality can be really hard in many ways...
That’s right.

Please find someone you can say “this is painful” to. And here, I’ll always listen to how you’re feeling, so you don’t have to push yourself too hard. Please come and let it out before it gets too hard.
Finding this place has saved me.
I’m glad! How was it for you to talk today?

Even if the reality doesn’t change, being able to talk made the painful feelings a little lighter. When it seems like I can talk to other people, I thought I’ll try to be a little more honest about my real feelings from now on. Thank you very much.
Thank you as well for sharing your feelings with me. Since you had the courage to come here and talk, I think you’ll surely be able to talk about your true feelings little by little from here on.
Yes, I’ll try.
Yes, please do. We’ll be ending here for today; is that okay?
Yes, I’ll leave it here. Thank you very much.
Thank you as well. Then we’ll end here. (Thank you very much.)
(Yes, I’ll submit an evaluation later. Thank you very much.)
(Thank you.)

interaction.content: Hello. I’m a counselor. Thank you for coming in today. To start, could you tell me your age, gender, and what you’d like to talk about?
Hello. I’m 40, male. I’m struggling with my relationship with my sibling.
I see. That must be troubling. Could you tell me a bit more about what kind of things you’ve been struggling with?
Yes. For about three years now, whenever we see each other, we just fight, and I can’t forgive him. He doesn’t help out at home, he’s always out having fun, and he barely works.
I see. That sounds really painful, and it would make you angry too. Do you and your sibling live together? What is your family situation like?
We don’t live together, but he lives nearby. It’s my parents and the two of us brothers, and my younger brother is the problem.
Thank you for telling me. So it was about your younger brother. Are you living near your family home, and your younger brother lives with your parents?
No. I live with my parents, and my younger brother lives alone nearby.
I see, that’s how it is. Thank you for explaining it carefully.
No, it’s fine.
You mentioned it started about three years ago. Was there something that triggered it around then?

Yes, until three years ago, our relationship was normal, but then debt collectors suddenly showed up at our house. It turned out to be debt my younger brother had created. After the whole family got dragged into that, our relationship went wrong.
I see. That must have been frightening. Yes. I can understand how something that big could disrupt the family relationship like that.
Yes, I’d seen things like that on TV, but when it actually happens...
Yes. What did you feel at the time?
I was scared, and at the same time I felt like I couldn’t forgive my younger brother.
Of course. It’s natural to feel that way. Your parents are there too, and it’s about your younger brother, so I imagine you may have struggled with feeling, “I have to do something!”
That’s right. But at the time, there was nothing I could do. I felt pathetic.

Yes. When you’re thrown into such an extraordinary situation, it’s only natural to feel like you can’t do anything. And the fact that you felt pathetic—I feel that may be because you have such a strong sense of responsibility.
Yes. He’s a pathetic younger brother, but I want to somehow help him. My parents are worried too.
Yes. You’re worried about your younger brother.
Yes, very much.
I can really feel your kindness as his older brother. When you do meet, what kinds of things lead to fights? How do you talk to your younger brother?
I think he pushes back because I end up nagging him. I think what I’m saying is reasonable, but he won’t listen.

So you point out the things you mentioned earlier—that he doesn’t help out at home, goes out having fun, and isn’t really working properly. And that’s advice coming from concern for his future, isn’t it?
Yes. That’s right.
Because you’re worried, you feel like you have to tell him. In reality, is your younger brother’s living situation and work situation difficult?
Yes. He doesn’t work, and he gambles with borrowed money and drinks.
I see. It’s completely understandable that you would be worried.
Yes.
It sounds like there is still borrowed money now. Are things okay in terms of the impact your younger brother’s debts and so on are having on your household?
I think it’s quite a critical situation. We’re not wealthy, and my parents are living on their pension.
I see. Your own household is already in a difficult situation, and on top of that you’re worried about your younger brother. That must feel really unbearable. What kind of work do you do?
I’m just an ordinary office worker.
I see. You have stable employment, then. So if it weren’t for your younger brother’s debts and related issues, would you be able to live with your parents with peace of mind?
Yes. If it weren’t for the debt problem, we should be able to live normally.
I see. From what you’ve shared so far, I’ve sensed that you are a very kind and responsible older brother.
Yes.
It’s really admirable that you’re concerned about your younger brother, but I also felt that you may be the one carrying most of the burden. What do you think?
Is that so? I don’t really know myself. In a case like this, what should I do?
From here, I’ll share what I’m thinking.
Yes.
You are working properly and living together with your parents. I feel it may be okay to put that life first.
That’s true.
I didn’t ask his age, but I imagine your younger brother is already an adult.
Yes.

First, if your own life is in a critical situation, I think one option would be to consider getting legal consultation about the debts so far. I feel it may be okay to think about your younger brother after that. Because you are so kind, I think you may have been putting your younger brother first. I think it’s okay to value your life with your parents more, and not try to carry everything all at once. What worries me most is that by taking all of this on, your own life will become difficult. What do you think?
Thank you. I see! I realized I’ve only been thinking about other people until now. You gave me a concrete suggestion, so I’ll definitely consider it.
I’m glad to hear you say that. Listening to you all this time, your kindness really came through. But please take care of yourself too.
Yes, thank you. I’ll do my best.
It’s okay to start with what you can do. You’ve already been thinking this through very carefully. If other worries come up, please feel free to talk with me again.
Yes. I’ll ask for your help again.
Thank you. Then we’ll end here.

interaction.content: (Good evening. Thank you for being here today. We’ll begin when it’s time.) Good evening. I’m the counselor. To start, please tell me your age, gender, and what you’d like to talk about.
I’m sorry, I’m late.
That’s okay. Thank you for letting me know.
I’m 46, female. Thank you for your help.
Thank you as well. I look forward to speaking with you today.
I’m worried about my children.
Thank you for telling me. You’re worried about your children. Could I ask a little more specifically, including how old they are?
Yes, I have one child in elementary school and one in junior high school.
I see. You have two children, then.
One is in sixth grade, and the other is in ninth grade. Yes. They’ve been tending not to go to school, and I’m struggling with what to do.
I see. You’re worried because they’ve been tending not to go to school. Is that true for both of them?
Yes, the elementary school child is mostly going to the nurse’s office, that kind of situation.
I see. That must leave you feeling really worried too. Your elementary school child is at least able to make it to school for now, then. How about your junior high school child?
Yes, the ninth grader goes once or twice a week, when he feels like it...
I see. When you think about everything with your children, I imagine you may feel anxious. Specifically, when did this start, and was there any trigger?

It started about a year ago. With the elementary school child, she just laughs it off or says she doesn’t get along with her friends, and she won’t really talk to me. With the ninth grader, it’s been since he started junior high. The elementary school child is my daughter, and the junior high school child is my son.
I see. I think you’ve been doing your best as a parent in that kind of situation.
Yes, thank you. My junior high school son has always seemed to have trouble building relationships. It seems to tire him out.

I see. Your daughter says she doesn’t get along with her friends, and your son has trouble building relationships. I see. Certainly, with changes in environment and all different kinds of classmates, there can be people they click with and don’t click with, and that may be exhausting.
Yes.
Are both of them eating and sleeping at home?
Tha—thank you. I try to act cheerful, but... Yes. At home they talk normally, and they’re energetic.
I see. While feeling anxious about the two of them, you’ve been watching over them all this time, trying not to show how worried you are.
They have appetites too. Yes...
I’m glad that even though they may have all kinds of feelings and find it difficult to go to school, they’re doing okay. Is there anyone else in your family?
But sometimes I feel down, wondering if I’m immature as a mother. My husband is away on a work assignment and lives far away.
I see. Your husband is away on a work assignment and isn’t there with you. Given the current situation, you end up feeling down and wondering if you’re immature as a mother.
Yes. But we do talk, so he seems to understand.
Listening to you, I really think you’ve been raising your children on your own in this situation as well as you can.
Yes, it’s hard.

It is hard. I think it’s natural that the current situation would make you feel down. So even though your husband is far away, you are able to talk with him about it. What does your husband say about your children’s current situation?
Yes. Before, I used to keep telling them to go to school, but...
I see. As you look at how your children are doing now, is there anything you hope will happen, or any way you hope they’ll be?
My husband seems worried, but he doesn’t really have any particular suggestions.
Yes. As a parent, it’s natural to feel worried.
Yes, I want them to go to school normally. Yes.
That’s how you feel. Have you talked with their schoolteachers or the school counselor at all?
Both of them ask me, “Why do we have to go to school?” and it’s like they don’t have any sense of urgency...
That’s what both of them say, then.
Yes, I forced them to meet with the school counselor, but... it seems they didn’t really talk much. Lately I’ve been trying not to say anything, but is it okay to keep going like this?
I see. I can really sense that you’ve been thinking of all kinds of ways to help your children, out of your concern for them. It may take a lot of courage for them to talk about their own feelings.
Yes, I suppose so...

From what you’ve told me so far, what do you think about talking with your children about two possibilities: what might happen if they continue not going to school, and what might happen if they do start going? Earlier, you mentioned that they don’t seem to have a sense of urgency, but you’ve been doing your best to be involved with them, and maybe they feel protected and reassured because of that.
Yes. My son seems to have a high school he wants to aim for, but I’m worried about his grades... That may be true.
I see. Your son has a school he wants to go to, but from your perspective, you’re worried about his grades.
Yes, I tell him, “You won’t be able to get into high school like this,” but... he just gives me empty replies...

I can really feel how sincerely you care about the two of them, and I’m sure your children understand that too. So how would it be to have a conversation with them once about the future, and about those two paths?
Yes, that makes sense. My son seems to like computers, and he wants to go to a high school that specializes in that... I’ll try it once.

It’s a good thing that he has something he wants to do. Yes, rather than making them decide, it may be more about giving each of them the information and continuing to watch over them as they come to their own answers...
I’m anxious about whether I can talk about it well... Yes, that’s true. I was only thinking about getting them to go.

It’s understandable to feel anxious. But rather than trying to say it perfectly, I think if you speak from the caring feelings you have for them, it will come across. When your child isn’t going to school, I think it’s natural to want to somehow get them to go.
Yes, I’ll try it. I feel a little lighter.
You really are doing your best, and perhaps letting go a little could be one option too. I’m glad to hear that. You’re welcome to come talk again anytime, but how was it for you to talk today?
Thank you. You’re right. I feel very relieved, and I think I’ll be able to sleep tonight.
Please keep warm and rest well. I hope your feelings reach your children, and that your heart feels even a little more at ease.
Thank you very much for today.
Thank you as well. (Thank you. Would it be all right to end here?)
Yes, I’m sorry I was late.
Not at all. I was worried that something might have happened. Thank you for taking the time when you’re busy. We’ll end here, then.
Thank you as well. This was helpful.

interaction.content: (Thank you for being here today.) (We’ll begin when it’s time.)
(Yes. Thank you as well.)
Hello, I’m the counselor. What would you like to talk about today? If you don’t mind, could you also tell me your age and gender?
Hello. I’m 35, male, and I’m wondering whether I should change jobs.
Thank you for sharing that. Could you tell me a bit more about your concern about changing jobs?
I’ve stopped feeling fulfilled by my current job. It feels like every day is just exhausting now.
If every day feels exhausting, it seems like it could start affecting your daily life, too... Do you have a sense of why you’ve stopped feeling fulfilled?
The work is complicated and hectic, and I feel like I’m not really able to face customers properly. I’ve started thinking I’m not helping people.
When do you feel that you’re not able to really face your customers? Feeling like you’re not helping people must be painful...
It’s when I’m pressed for time and can’t respond to them carefully.
I see... Is your workplace quite busy?
Yes.
When did you start feeling this way?
I’d sort of felt it for the past few years, but over the last few months I’ve been feeling it clearly.

You’d sort of been feeling it for a few years... so it sounds like you’ve been thinking about this for a long time. Since it’s become clear over the past few months, does that mean your own wishes have become clearer to you as well?
Yes, I think so. Right now I’m thinking about it pretty realistically.
Yes. By realistically, do you mean the job change you mentioned earlier?
Yes.
Thank you for telling me. With the job change, is your concern about what kind of work you would do? Or is it more that you’re still considering whether to stay at your current workplace?
I’m still considering it. I’m wondering whether changing jobs is really the best option.
I see... So even within yourself, you haven’t clearly found an answer yet about what you should do.
Yes.
Are there any reasons you feel it might be better to keep working at your current workplace?
Yes. I’ve been working at my current workplace for a long time, so when I think about various things, it is stable.
Yes, do you mean things like income and being used to the work?
The atmosphere isn’t that bad either, and yes, the income too.
So the atmosphere isn’t bad either. Would you say things are going well with your coworkers and others?
Something like that.
Yes. So what concerns you is that you’ve stopped feeling fulfilled.
That’s right. It’s becoming clear in my mind that if I keep going like this, I’ll regret it in the future.
It’s that clear for you... In that case, it makes sense that you’d really be struggling with this...
Thank you.
You mentioned regretting it in the future... Could you tell me specifically what you feel you might regret?
I’d regret myself for not being able to take action back then. And for choosing stability and things like that.
Yes. Would it be regret over not changing jobs even though you feel there’s no fulfillment? Yes... I see...
I’m sure that’s how I’d feel.
Yes. Even though you haven’t changed jobs yet, you already feel that clearly.
I think it’s something I’ve realized clearly while talking about it now. When I put it into words, my feelings start to get organized.
Even so, do you still have a feeling that you want to stay in a stable workplace?
I’m torn...
Yes. You’re still unsure... I felt that those are very honest feelings.
I’m also scared that I’ll change jobs and fail.
Yes. What do you mean specifically by failure?
It might end up being the same again, or it might be an even worse environment.
Yes. So you mean you can’t predict whether the result will be good or bad.
It’s obvious, but that’s what makes me anxious.
No, I think everyone feels that way. The future is something no one can predict... Could I ask what fulfillment means to you? I’d like to hear, if that’s okay.

It means really facing each person and responding in a way I can feel satisfied with. At my current workplace, that’s absolutely impossible, and we’re in a situation where complaints come in almost every day.
Yes... So it’s clear that it’s not the kind of workplace you have in mind. If complaints are coming in every day... that must be emotionally hard too.
Yes. I want to live more like myself.

Yes. It sounds like you have a sense of what living like yourself looks like. I think it’s wonderful that you can clearly feel that you want to live like yourself. What does living like yourself mean to you? I’m sorry for asking one question after another.
Like myself... I might not really know, but the one thing that’s clear is that the way I’m living now is not like me.
Yes. The one thing that’s clear is that the way you’re living now is not like you. And you feel that you want to live like yourself.
Yes. Because I don’t think I’m supposed to be feeling this unenjoyable.
That feeling of not enjoying things... that’s clear to you too... How has it been talking this through up to this point? Has anything changed regarding today’s concern? Even any realizations.
Yes. I’m feeling much more positive. By putting my feelings into words, I think I was able to understand them clearly.

I’m relieved to hear that you’re feeling more positive and that you were able to understand your feelings. I think you may still be in a place where you haven’t reached a clear conclusion, but the fact that you have a desire to live like yourself, and that you’re clearly recognizing your own feelings, may be because you have a desire to live while valuing yourself. You’re clear about things like how you would regret it if you let yourself be carried along by stability, and you seem to recognize yourself well. I felt that this will be important as you think about what comes next.
Thank you. Yes. Until now it had just been kind of vague, but now I feel like I was able to organize it clearly in words.

I see... I’m glad it seems you were able to organize it clearly in words. We’re getting close to the end of our time, but is there anything you’d like to talk about before we finish? It’s also fine if there’s something you’d like to tell me.
I’m really glad I reached out. I want to think positively about changing jobs and live a life without regrets. Thank you for responding so carefully.

Thank you as well for sharing such an important concern with me. I learned from it too. Yes. I truly hope you can live a life without regrets, in a way that feels right for you. Thank you for your valuable time. I think we’ll end here. (Thank you for spending just under an hour with me! Is it okay to end now?) (If there’s anything else, I’d be grateful if you could let me know in the evaluation comments.)
(Thank you very much. Yes, it’s okay to end. Everything was really helpful and gave me a lot to learn from. At some point I even started wondering, are you a teacher? lol)
(Thank you for such kind words, I’m humbled sweat sweat sweat. Thank you as well for responding so thoughtfully; it was a pleasure to talk with you. I’m grateful. Well then, I’ll take my leave.)
Yes.

interaction.content: (Hello. Thank you for meeting with me today.)
(Thank you.
(Would it be all right if we get started?)
(Please go ahead.
(Thank you.) Hello, I’m the counselor. To start, could you tell me your age, gender, and what you’d like to talk about?
I’m 35, female. I’m concerned that I don’t really have much attachment to having a partner or getting married. It’s not that I’m feeling down or anything, but...
I see. What makes you feel that you don’t have much attachment to it?
I feel that way when people around me are working hard at dating, or when friends say things like, “Marriage is a good thing!”
Yes, so you feel that way from the situations around you and what people say. It can feel unsettling to think that.
I don’t feel like I have to get married, so when people ask me why I’m not getting married, I just kind of feel like, why would they say something like that?
Yes, that makes sense. It would make you wonder why they would say something like that.
Yes.
Yes. Recently, Shironeko, how have you been spending your private time? Only what you feel comfortable sharing is fine.
Do you mean like whether I have hobbies or something...?
Yes, that was unclear, wasn’t it. I asked because I was wondering what kinds of time feel enjoyable for you, Shironeko.
Basically, I enjoy a lot of things, and I like my work too. In that sense, when people talk as if getting married will somehow make life work out, I don’t really understand it.
I see, so you’re enjoying things, including your work. The idea of “if you get married...” is hard to understand.
Yes.
Yes. You said you’re concerned that you don’t have much attachment to having a partner or getting married. Is it that you’re concerned your way of thinking is different from those around you?

There are a lot of people who understand, but sometimes when someone strongly says something like, “Marriage is the greatest happiness in life!!! You should do it,” I just feel kind of... I don’t know.
Yes, I see. It feels unpleasant when that’s said to you. I’m sorry. Let me rephrase that. When that’s said to you, it feels unpleasant.
Yes, it does feel like it’s being pushed on me...
Yes, when it feels like someone’s pushing their views on you, it doesn’t feel good.
Yes.
When people say things like that about romance or marriage, how do you talk to them about it, Shironeko?

I tell them that I have my own views, but sometimes they still say marriage is a good thing, so I feel kind of, I don’t know... From their perspective, maybe there isn’t any particularly deep meaning behind it.
Yes, I see. You do share your own thoughts, but when they say that, it feels like they’re not understanding you. Even if there isn’t any deep meaning behind it.
Yes... Maybe they just want me to hear that marriage was a good thing for them... For me, it doesn’t feel very good though...
Yes. That may be true. You’re being considerate of the other person’s feelings in that way. Still, it doesn’t feel good for the person on the receiving end, does it.
Some of them are people I’m close with. They’ve had their own ups and downs in life too, so they may have all kinds of feelings about it.
I see. I feel that you’re a very kind person, Shironeko, to be able to take in the other person’s feelings.
Do you think so...? Well, I do think everyone has their own things going on. But when it comes to marriage, the conversation turns into “you should do it,” so... well, maybe they’re worried about me.
Yes, I see. You think they may be saying it out of concern. For you, Shironeko, I get the sense that if things stay like this, your feelings may not settle. How does that sound?
I do feel like I don’t really want to bring up marriage anymore. I just wonder why they say so strongly that I should do it... If we keep being close, that topic might come up again...

Yes, when someone strongly recommends it, it can feel uncomfortable. Since you said you’re close with that person, I wonder if they may feel like they can talk to you about anything. How does that sound?
Yes, we talk about all kinds of things.
I see. Because you’re someone they trust, there may be things they end up saying without meaning to.
Yes. Rather than criticism of me, it might just be my friend’s own self-talk about themselves coming out toward me.
I see. Shironeko, I really feel that you’re a kind person who thinks from the other person’s perspective.
No, no, I just don’t want to hold on to anger as much as possible... Well, I can tell they’re not trying to fight with me... I think they’re just saying it naturally.
I see. I think it’s wonderful that you can think from the other person’s perspective like that. At the same time, it’s hard if anger gradually builds up.
Rather than anger, maybe it’s more of a question? I wonder why they have such strong feelings about marriage.
Yes, that’s how you feel. Let me summarize what we’ve talked about so far.
Okay.

Shironeko, while you’re spending your days happily and feeling fulfilled with work and other things, you see things about romance and marriage around you and sometimes feel like other people’s views are being pushed onto you. On one hand, you think the other person is worried about you, but on the other hand, you don’t want to talk about marriage, and it’s hard to understand why they have such strong feelings about it.
It’s not that I don’t want to talk about marriage, but...
Yes.
Even if I’m told to agree that getting married will make you happy, I’m not sure about that... I guess that’s what it is... My view is that getting married might make you happy, or it might not.
Yes, that’s right. Everyone has their own way of thinking about marriage. I also thought that you don’t have to take on that person’s individual view, Shironeko. How does that sound?
I can’t exactly ignore what they’re saying, so... I guess I try to listen for the time being and answer like, “Yeah, I see, but I’m different, so I’m okay.”

I see. I think you have a clear sense of your own views. If you talk to that friend about things you’re interested in and so on, they may be able to feel that the current you is happy, Shironeko. How does that sound? (I’m sorry. It looks like we’re out of time.) (Were you able to talk about even a little of what you wanted to?)
I often talk about things I’m interested in, but maybe I need to respond clearly about marriage. (Yes.)
Yes. I think if you say it clearly once, it will get across, so please try saying it when it feels easy to talk.
Thank you.
I’m rooting for you, that it comes across.
Yes, thank you.
Thank you for today. (I’m sorry we went over time.) (I’ll send the closing message.)
(Thank you. Good work today!
(Thank you.)
