interaction.content: Hello. I'm a counselor.
Hello. Thank you for seeing me.
Thank you. To start, please tell me your age, gender, and what you'd like to talk about today.
I'm 25, male, and I'd like to talk about relationships at my workplace.
Thank you for sharing that. You mentioned workplace relationships—could you tell me a bit more about that?
It's my boss. No matter what I do, the way he talks to me is harsh, and it's painful.
I see. When your boss speaks harshly to you no matter what you do, that can really feel painful, can't it.
Yes.
What kind of things does he say, or how does he say them?
It feels like he's looking down on me.

Since he's your boss, I imagine you have to communicate with him every day, and feeling like you're being looked down on every time you talk must be really hard... Have you had a long relationship with your boss?
Well... it's only been about a year.
So it's been about a year since you became his subordinate. Does your boss have other subordinates as well?
Yes, he does. He's the same way with other people too.
I see, so it sounds like that may be the kind of personality your boss has. (If you're comfortable, what would you like me to call you? A nickname is fine too.)
I think that's about right. Please call me Toshi.
Toshi, then. Thank you for telling me. Toshi, have you talked about this with coworkers who have the same boss?
Yes, I have. My coworkers agree too.
So your coworkers feel the same way. Regarding how harsh your boss's way of speaking is, what would you like to see happen?
It would be good if he fixed it, but I think it's part of his personality, so I think it's impossible.
That's true, when it's someone's personality, it can feel like it's not something that will change easily... What is his reputation like with the people above him?
He sucks up to the higher-ups, so I think they like him.
So he's harsh toward his subordinates, but tries to be liked by the people above him and manages that well. Seeing that must make it even more painful...
It irritates me.

You have to see him every day, and you have to follow his instructions, so it's understandable that it would make you feel that way. Do you think there is anything you and your coworkers might be able to do together toward resolving this? Thank you for telling me about the situation in detail. Could you tell me what you'd like to consult about today? For example, how to recover mentally, how to deal with your boss, or what you might do to change the situation—could you tell me?
I guess it's how to deal with my boss. I've talked with my coworkers about consulting the higher-ups, but since they like him, I feel like they won't take us seriously.
So you'd like to talk about how to deal with a boss whose attitude probably won't change because it's part of his personality.
Yes.
You've also talked with your coworkers about consulting the people above him. If you were to do that, when do you think it might be?
We haven't decided anything clearly yet.
I see. When you're thinking about consulting higher-ups about someone they like, it makes sense to feel like you shouldn't expect too much from them in terms of taking action... Thank you.
Thank you.

interaction.content: I'm Hitsuji, and I'll be your mental trainer today. Oomisoka, it's a pleasure to work with you. Today's mental training, first match theme, is romance. Is it okay to get started?
Yes, thank you.
Hello. I'm the counselor. Thank you for reaching out. What would you like to talk about today?
I want a girlfriend. I've never had one before.
I see! Yes, falling in love can make everyday life feel kind of sparkly, can't it? It's something you long for, isn't it?
I do long for it! I'm always all alone at Christmas.
I see. Then you'd really like to spend it with a girlfriend. Is it okay if I call you Oomisoka?
Yes!
Oomisoka, how old are you now?

I want someone like that in my life.

I watch YouTube at home, or watch movies on Netflix.

Yes!

Within six months. And before that, I'd like to have someone I can get close to within three months.
I'm sorry, my computer froze just now!

Within six months.

I used to use dating apps, but...

I'm not good at finding people, and...

No. I don't have any close friends who met someone through social media.

Hmm...

I feel like I could maybe say, 'Can you introduce me to someone you know?' lol

I see!

Is that right!

Like you were saying earlier, you can put it out there in different ways, like, 'I wonder if there's someone I could go to baseball or soccer with—if you know anyone, introduce me,' that kind of thing!

Yes! Thank you!

interaction.content: Nice to meet you. I’m the counselor. To start, could you please tell me your age and gender? Thank you.
I’m a woman in my 40s.
Thank you. What would you like to talk about today?
I’m going to be changing jobs, and the type of work will change too, so I’m anxious.
I see... That would make you feel anxious. When are you planning to change jobs?
I’m planning for February.
I see. What kind of work have you been doing up until now?
Food-related work.
Food-related work, I see. What kind of things did you do in that field?
Sales.
I see, you were doing sales. How was that work for you?
It was fun.
That’s good. Feeling that something is fun is really important, isn’t it.
Yes.
What parts of it were fun?
I guess interacting with customers.
I see. When you’re interacting with customers, time can really fly by, can’t it.
Yes.
What led you to change jobs?
Income.
Yes, income is important. Would it be okay if you told me what led you to change jobs because of income?
It’s to increase my income.
So there was a need to increase it.
Yes.
That’s important. Where do you feel that desire to increase it came from?
Family circumstances.
Thank you. Let me organize things for a moment. You’re going to leave the sales job you liked and change jobs. The reason is that, because of family circumstances, you need to increase your income.
Yes.
That makes you anxious... Did something happen in your family?
Yes. But there’s nothing I can do about that anymore, so I have no choice but to move forward.
I think it’s really admirable that you’ve made that decision within yourself.
Yes.
What kind of work will you be doing from February?
It’s similar, food sales, but it will be more niche and specialized, aimed at a limited group of people.
I see. So even though the type of work is the same, the content feels different. When it becomes specialized, it does seem difficult.
Yes. Since it will be for a limited group of people, I think it won’t feel as easygoing as before. I’ll also have to study, so I’m anxious about whether I’ll be able to keep up.
Yes, when it comes to studying and gaining new knowledge, it can feel very anxiety-provoking.
Yes. More than enjoyment, I’m worried I might feel stuck... or that I won’t be able to feel the same sense of freedom I do now.
Mm-hmm. So the fact that the people you interact with will be more limited is also a difference from your previous job.
Yes.
That’s a difficult point. Even if it’s in exchange for higher income, that would make you anxious.
I think the basics are the same, but... I’m anxious about whether my feelings will keep up. It will probably be harder. And I don’t have the knowledge either.
Mm-hmm. It makes you anxious, and if anything, it’s scary...
Yes.
But everyone starts from zero at first, and I think that, for you, even if your past experience doesn’t apply 100 percent, there will be parts of it that can help. What do you think?
I think there are. That’s why I decided to change jobs.
Mm-hmm. It’s very reassuring to have confidence and courage within the anxiety. By the way, how did you interview for the job starting in February?
It’s not confidence and courage, but I do think my past experience will be useful. I had an in-person interview. It’s a job change I requested myself.
Thank you. Experience is important. But the fact that you interviewed and were accepted means they likely judged that you were a good fit for the company, so I think it’s okay to have confidence.
Thank you.
It’s difficult to deal with anxiety about something that’s a month away, but there’s also the fact that you won’t know until you try.
I realized that what I’m most anxious about is whether or not I’ll be able to find that job enjoyable.
Yes, that makes sense. That’s important. If, hypothetically, you weren’t able to enjoy it, what would you do?
People around me are saying I can just come back to my current workplace. I think maybe that’s the only option, but then I’d be back to square one.
Yes, because you have a clear reason: income.

Yes. There’s also the issue of physical stamina. I haven’t done it yet, so I can’t really say, but I feel like I don’t have the stamina to continue my current job either. I think this is a necessary choice for me.

I see. I think that’s good. I honestly want to support you. “Enjoyment” is something you don’t know until you try it. When you think about it before starting, negative things may naturally come up, but it would be good if you could find some “enjoyment” somewhere in the work.

Yes. In my own way, this job change is the result of thinking it through very seriously. Not only income and physical stamina, but I also want to increase my own sense of satisfaction. So it’s a challenge.
Self-satisfaction is very important. It would be wonderful if you could encounter a new kind of enjoyment in February. I’m rooting for you.
Thank you. So that I can move forward, I’d like to create a password.
Thank you as well. With that, we’ll end today’s consultation.
Thank you very much. Goodbye.
(We will now end the role-play.)

interaction.content: (Good evening. We’ll begin when it’s time. Thank you.)
(Good evening. Thank you for meeting with me today.)
Good evening. I’m the counselor. To start, could you tell me your age, gender, and what you’d like to talk about today?
I’m 48, female, and my hourly wage for my part-time job is low.
Thank you for telling me. I see.
Yes.
How long have you been working part-time there?
This is my fourth year at my current company.
I see. In what ways is the low hourly wage at your part-time job causing difficulty for you?
I’m dissatisfied because the pay doesn’t match the work I’m doing. It’s not so much that I’m having trouble—it feels unpleasant.
I see. So rather than it being a practical difficulty, you’re feeling dissatisfied. What kind of work are you doing now?

I was hired for general office work, but I’m doing everything—general affairs, accounting, HR, secretary work, sales administration, and other things like processing CSV data, scouting tasks, and so on. There are no full-time employees doing office work at the company, so I’m in a situation where I, as a part-timer, do everything.
I see. Are you handling all of that work by yourself?
Yes. The other part-time workers are doing different work.
That must put quite a lot of burden on you.
Yes.
You mentioned there are no full-time employees in general office work. Do you have a supervisor?
It’s a small company, so the president is my supervisor.
I see. When your direct supervisor is the president, it can be hard to casually talk or consult with them. Do the other part-time workers have a similar workload?
I think it’s different, but it’s work I’m not actually doing myself, and their work is mainly remote, so I can’t really see the situation and can’t say for sure.
You’re working remotely, then. It’s true that it’s hard to compare workloads with other people. I’m sorry about that. Have you talked with people around you about what you’ve been telling me?
I work about half remote and half in the office. The other part-time workers are mainly remote. I’ve complained a little to people around me, people at related companies, and my husband.
So that’s the kind of work arrangement you have. What did the people connected to the company and your husband say?

The people at the related company said, “You should negotiate your hourly wage.” My husband said, “It might make things uncomfortable, so if you’re going to bring up the hourly wage, maybe you should wait until you have a prospect for your next job.”
I see. Hearing those opinions, how did you feel?

I thought my husband’s opinion was probably realistic. When we were going through the process of renewing the employment contract every six months, I checked with the president about the hourly wage. At that time, he said, “We’ll leave it as it is this time and think about it at the time of closing the accounts,” and I felt that negotiating would be a high hurdle.
I see. When you’re told they’ll think about it at the time of the financial closing, it sounds like something quite far off, and it can feel like the issue itself is being put off.
Yes, it felt like he skillfully dodged it.
I think it’s understandable that you felt that way. Have you ever talked with the president about the workload you mentioned earlier?

Yes, I have told him I don’t want my work to increase any more. But maybe the president recognizes my abilities, because he’s now saying he wants me to take on writing work too. I do think it’s a positive thing to be able to take on new work and gain new skills, but I can’t accept that my hourly wage doesn’t change.
I see. So taking on new work and gaining new skills is a plus for you, so that part is okay, but it’s the hourly wage aspect that you can’t accept.
Yes.
About what your husband said when you consulted him—waiting until you have a prospect for your next job—at this point, is changing jobs an option for you?
It’s not that it isn’t an option.
So you do have changing jobs in mind as one possibility.
Not actively, though.
I see. Do you feel it would be hard to leave your current job?

If I quit, I think the president would be in a lot of trouble. Not only that, but for me too, the flexibility with my schedule, being allowed to work from home, and the short commute are all benefits. But I also end up thinking there are probably jobs out there with higher hourly pay that are easier than what I’m doing now, simpler jobs.

I see. So your current job has benefits for you, and you think the president would be in a lot of trouble if you left, while at the same time you feel there are probably places with less work and better hourly pay than what you have now.
Yes.
With all those different circumstances, it makes sense that you’d feel torn.
Yes.
Listening to you today, what I felt is that you seem like a very serious and capable person.
Thank you.
And because of that, I imagine the president may be giving you all kinds of work.

Do you think so? I do think he trusts me. Up until now, I’ve tried to come to terms with the low hourly wage by telling myself, “My schedule is flexible,” and “I can work from home,” but lately, that hasn’t been enough for me to keep it down inside anymore.
You’ve been working in that kind of environment for four years, after all. I think it’s understandable that it’s becoming hard to hold down your dissatisfaction.
Thank you.
How would it be to summarize what you’ve shared today in your own way and talk with the president once more?
Hmm, talking about the hourly wage is really difficult.
If it feels difficult to organize what you want to say, I’d like us to think it through together here.
It’s not so much that organizing it is difficult; it’s difficult to talk directly with the president about the hourly wage.
I see. I’d like to hear a little more about that, but it’s just about time to end our consultation.
Thank you for today.
Next time, we can continue from what you shared today, so please feel free to come back anytime.
Yes, thank you. I’d appreciate your help again.
Thank you as well for sharing your story with me. We’ll end the consultation here.
Thank you very much.
(Thank you for your time. Thank you.)
(Thank you for your time. Thank you as well.)

interaction.content: Good evening, thank you for accepting. I appreciate your time today.
Good evening. Thank you as well for accepting my consultation request. I appreciate it.
Thank you as well. Then, once it’s time, we’ll begin. If there’s any topic you’d like to talk about, please feel free to say so.
Thank you for your consideration.
(Not at all. Then, I’ll go ahead and begin.) Good evening, I’m the counselor. Thank you for coming to talk with me this late in the evening. To start, could you tell me your gender and age?
Good evening. Thank you for meeting with me so late. I’m male, 35 years old.
Thank you. What would you like to talk about today? It’s late, so you may be tired, and it’s perfectly fine to share only what you feel comfortable with. Please take your time.
Yes, I don’t know if I’d call it a concern exactly, but I’ve been thinking I’d like to find something like “a new enjoyment that’s just for me,” and I don’t know what I should start with.
Yes, yes, a new enjoyment that’s just for you. Do you mean a hobby? Or something more like a sense of purpose in life?
If anything, I’d say it’s closer to a hobby.
Yes, I see. So it’s more like a hobby. Was there something that made you want to find that?
Lately, I tend to just laze around on my days off, so I thought I’d like to do something that clears my mood a bit.
I see. You want to find something on your days off that lifts your mood. I think that’s a very positive and wonderful thing to want. Have you tried various things so far?
I used to ride my motorcycle and go out to different places, but lately, with the cold and COVID, I haven’t really felt like riding much.
Ah, with COVID, that does naturally happen, doesn’t it. So you like motorcycles. Do you tend to like active things, or outdoor kinds of things?
Deep down I’m more of an indoor person, but around this time last year I had some extra income, so I bought one for the first time in about 10 years.

I see, I see. You finally bought one again after so long, and then not being able to go out... When you end up lazing around, it can make your mood feel kind of deflated too. I think it’s very natural that you’d want to find a new hobby. When you say you don’t know what to start with, do you mean you can’t think of anything you want to do?
Originally, even though going out was fun, I thought spending my days off relaxing at home was the best after all, but lately I’ve been feeling pretty pent-up. I can’t really think of anything...

Pent-up, is it. If that’s how it feels, it makes sense you’d want to find something. Can you think of anything that might be causing that pent-up feeling? If you’ve always liked spending time at home, I wonder why being at home has started to feel so stifling...

When the day off ends, I think, “Ah, today was another day where nothing happened, I didn’t do anything,” and then the next day off comes around like that again, so I feel like days off are becoming heavier and heavier.

I see. So rather than spending time at home itself, it’s that the day off ends without doing anything, and that feels somehow like you lost out on something, maybe. I can understand that... yes, certainly...
Ah, yes, that may be what it feels like.

Yes, yes. If that’s the case, if you could find something you want to do, it might help you spend time at home without feeling so pent-up. As for that thing you want to do, is there anything you’ve been really into since long ago?
Hmm. Not really. I have no idea what I want to do...
I see. You’re feeling pent-up, but you want to find something new, so I wonder if there are times when you feel a little rushed and confused.
Ah, yes. I think about whether there’s anything, while slowly doing cleaning and laundry, and then the day off ends, and it’s like, sigh, that’s it.

Yes, yes. So that’s what it’s been like. Even in the midst of that, the fact that you’re thinking about whether there’s something out there gives me the sense that you have a strong wish to change the current situation.
I do want to change it, even little by little...

I’ve been thinking about various possibilities too, and for now, what about making the search itself a kind of hobby—in other words, trying to enjoy the act of trying different things? If you’re okay with changing little by little, then perhaps you could try various things little by little. I thought the most important thing is that it’s something you can enjoy.
Do you mean, like enjoying the process of looking for it itself?
Yes, I think that’s the idea. And if, in that process, you find something you can enjoy, then you can keep doing that.
I see. Then, when taking the first step, what would you say is important?
Among the things you currently do in your daily life, is there anything that feels enjoyable when you do it? It’s also fine if it’s something that looks fun to you when you see it.
I don’t do it at all, but maybe cooking. Also, I think bouldering looks fun.
Cooking and bouldering! That’s wonderful. You already have two things that seem fun to you. I think that feeling of “this looks fun” may be the most important thing.
Since I live alone, with cooking, maybe I could start by making something simple. And for bouldering, there’s a gym nearby, so maybe I’ll go take a look...
That sounds good. It feels like it’s becoming more and more concrete. When you say something simple, would that be something like miso soup, for example?
A small hot pot for one in a little pot might be good too.
Oh, that sounds delicious! This season really is the time for hot pot, isn’t it. With hot pot, it seems like you could arrange the ingredients in lots of different ways too.
I’ll try it on my day off this week.
Yes, it would be nice if you try it and it goes well. Even if it starts as just a small interest, I think sometimes when you try it, that interest can grow.
Yes, I’ll try taking that first step.
Yes, that feeling of trying to take one step forward is wonderful. We’re almost out of time, but is there anything else you feel you haven’t said enough about?
I’m okay. I’m glad I talked with you.
I’m glad to hear you say that as well. In that case, would it be all right to end the consultation here?
Yes, thank you very much.
Thank you. Then, I’ll excuse myself. [The consultation has ended.] (Thank you. Thank you for your time this late in the evening.)
(Thank you for your time. Let’s both do our best putting it into practice.)
(Thank you. I’m sorry, but regarding the evaluation, I have a small favor to ask. Would that be all right?)
Yes, what is it?)

(Thank you. About the evaluation, I do this too, but it would be very helpful and easy to understand if you could write it by category, with ● good points and ● points for improvement. Also, if possible, I’d be grateful if you could write in detail especially about the acceptance and empathy parts. I often receive advice on those, and they seem to be weak areas for me.) (I’m sorry to trouble you.)
(I understand. I think it may take me a little time, but I’ll write as much detail as I can.)
(Thank you. Please don’t worry about the time. I truly appreciate it. Well then, if we have another opportunity, I look forward to working with you again. Let’s both do our best.)
(Yes, thank you so much.)
(Thank you. Then, I’ll end the role-play here.)
(Understood.)
(Then, I’ll excuse myself.)

interaction.content: (Thank you for being here today. We'll begin when it's time.)
Thank you as well.
Hello, I'm the counselor. To start, could you tell me your age and gender?
I'm 14, female.
Hello. What would you like to talk about today?
I'm worried about my body.
You're worried about your body. What kinds of things are you worried about, for example?
Lately my chest has started getting bigger... I hate it, and I keep thinking, why?
I see. Lately your chest has started getting bigger, and you find yourself feeling like you hate it.
Yeah. I never really thought about being a boy or a girl, but I thought I was a boy...
I see. Up until now, you've had the sense that you're a boy. That would feel confusing.
I feel unsettled, and it makes me feel awful...
I see, you hate it, and it feels really unsettled. If you've thought of yourself as a boy until now, it makes sense that it would feel wrong.
I guess that's how it feels...
It really can be startling when changes in your body suddenly become visible. It can make you feel awful too.
So I don't want to wear my uniform either.
Mm, yeah. The uniform feels wrong too. I think it's only natural that it's hard to accept.
Is that so...?
Yes, I think so.
Then I'm glad.
Mm. I think it's very important to value your own sense of yourself.
Thank you.
Mm, I think it's okay to value it. In your life right now, is anything causing problems for you?
When I wear the uniform and stuff, I feel nauseous and exhausted. So I don't want to go to school either.
I see... You feel nauseous, and your body feels exhausted too... That sounds really hard. Really exhausting.
I don't have anyone I can talk to either.
Yeah, it can be really hard to talk about. That's painful. Do you always feel that way when you're wearing a girls' uniform or underwear, or when you're around things that feel feminine?
Maybe. Girls' underwear and clothes in general, all that kind of stuff... probably all of it...
I see. In Japan, there are still a lot of things divided into men's and women's, so there are a lot of situations like that. That must be really exhausting.
It's really exhausting...
When did you start feeling this way? It must have been really hard to keep putting up with it until now.
Maybe since starting middle school. Before that, there weren't uniforms, so I didn't really think anything of it.
That makes sense. In elementary school, what you wear is more free.
I didn't wear skirts or anything.
So now you're in an environment where you have to wear a uniform every day, and that's just too hard.
That's why I don't want to go to school either.
It makes sense you'd feel that way.
Yeah...
Have you ever thought about what you wish could happen, deep down?
I think it would be better if there were no boys or girls...
Mm, I can understand feeling that way. It would be nice if those distinctions disappeared.
Is there even any point in dividing people like that?
I think it's only a physical distinction, really. Biologically, men may tend to be stronger or have larger bodies, and the shape of the reproductive organs is different, that's all.
But everyone wants to categorize people as boys or girls, and schools especially are like that, aren't they?
That's really true. It feels like teachers have just kept doing things the same way since the Meiji era.
People online often say it doesn't matter and stuff, but it's not like that at all.

That's true. In reality, even if that's the ideal, there are still so many times when it feels like things haven't changed yet. But things are gradually changing now. You might already know this, but some schools let girls choose pants for their uniforms, and more local governments are recognizing marriage between people of the same sex.
But at my school, we can't choose our uniforms, and even if we could, I'm scared people would look at me weird.
It makes sense you'd feel that way.
My parents don't understand either, and it hurts...
Yeah, it feels like you want your parents to understand.
They say it'll change eventually so it'll be okay, and they don't really listen...
I see, so you have told them before. And even when you told them, things didn't change then.
Yeah. Even if I say it again, they won't understand, so I don't want to, and I don't know what to do...
Yeah. It gets hard to know how to explain it. It really leaves you struggling. But, you know, you're not alone. The counselor will always listen whenever you need to talk.
Thank you... I was thinking about it by myself, but I still just didn't know what to do...
There are probably actually a lot of people in the world who are struggling with worries like yours. They just don't say it.
Really? I didn't know...
And I understand that this isn't something you can easily talk about, so you can come talk to us anytime. Nothing you share here will ever be shared outside, so please feel safe.
Thank you... When I thought that I'm not alone, I felt a little better.
Yes, you are not alone. Unfortunately, we're out of time for today, but how was it for you? Please come back again if you want to talk about anything or when things feel hard.
Thank you. If it gets hard again, please listen to me.
Please come anytime. (Thank you for today. We'll end here.)

interaction.content: Hello, thank you for being here today. We’ll begin when it’s time.
Hello. Thank you as well.
Hello, I’m the counselor. To start, could you tell me your age and gender?
Hello. I’m a 41-year-old woman.
Thank you. Please tell me what you’d like to discuss.
It’s about my own relationships and my child’s relationships.
I understand. Then could you tell me a bit more about that?
I’m not very good at getting along with neighbors, or making mom friends. Lately I’ve been wondering if that’s affecting my child.
Yes. Was there something specific that made you feel that way?

My child started elementary school, and after school, they say they want to play with friends. But there aren’t really any children to play with. My child is feeling down, saying they’re always the one inviting others and no one invites them. Actually, I do have a few people who are sort of mom friends, but we don’t have that kind of relationship, like getting together to play.
I see. Hearing that your child is feeling down made you start to feel concerned?

Yes. I’d been worried about it myself for quite a while, just about me. But if it was only me, I could kind of make myself accept it. But when it comes to my child, I started thinking I want to do something for them, and wondering if it’s my fault.
Yes, I see. You find yourself thinking it’s your fault, and you feel like you want to do something for your child.
Yes, that’s right. I wonder if I need to change something about how I act, or change the way I think. But I don’t know what I should do...
I see. I think it’s very positive and really admirable. I feel I’d like to help in some way—would you like to think through it together a little?
Yes, please, I’d really appreciate that.
All right. Then, what kind of change do you imagine would be good for you?

I’d like to become a little more sociable, and whether my child is involved in that or not, I’d like to have relationships where we can communicate not just on the surface, but emotionally too. I think seeing me like that, my child might learn how to interact with friends. I mean, learn from it. Sorry.

Yes, you’re analyzing this very specifically, and you have a clear sense of the kind of person you’d like to become. It sounds like you feel that first, you need to become that version of yourself, that “kind of person.” Would that be right?
Yes. That’s right.
I feel like there may be a clue in that “kind of person.” What do you think?

I just can’t seem to get closer to being that person. I end up feeling like the other person doesn’t really need to be involved with me. And if they don’t need it, then it would be strange for me to force it.
I see. You end up feeling anxious about engaging with the other person.
Not anxiety, exactly. It’s more like I worry because I don’t know how the other person sees their relationship with me, or how much they want from it.
I see. Would you say it’s about a sense of distance?

Maybe it’s a sense of distance. Right now, with most people, it feels like the relationship doesn’t go beyond a certain point—or can’t. Like saying, let’s have tea sometime... well, with COVID too, it’s hard to be proactive.
Yes, I do think COVID has had a major impact. So, do you yourself feel there’s something you want in your relationships with others?
Even among mom friends, I do wish we could talk a little more deeply, but right now that doesn’t happen, and I can’t take that step. It feels like I can’t really hope for much.
I see. You said “right now”—do you feel that COVID is the reason you’ve come to feel that distance?

That’s a big part of it. We moved to our current home right around the time COVID started. So my new relationships began from there. So it’s almost like I’ve never seen the real faces of the people in the neighborhood. And it’s hard to build relationships. The people around me already had relationships before COVID, so I wonder if they’re able to maintain contact based on what they had before. If so, I think they can keep relationships going while being flexible. I feel a bit of loneliness as a family, in our household.
I see. You moved right around the time COVID began... so it was like, just as you were starting a new life, the world changed drastically too.
Yes. Somehow I don’t even know what’s normal anymore. I suppose there isn’t really a normal.
I see. It’s been two years since life with COVID began, and even though you want to start building relationships, it feels like there just aren’t many opportunities.

Yes. In my own way, I try to make sure I greet people properly, act cheerful, and show that I care, but I wonder if that comes across as awkward. I can be a bit oblivious myself too... so I wonder if I might be giving people the wrong impression.
You’re really doing what you can right now. I think that’s wonderful.
Am I really doing it...?

Now that we’re living with masks, it’s harder to read other people’s reactions, and misunderstandings can happen more easily on both sides, making communication more difficult. I also sometimes feel anxious about whether I’m getting my feelings across properly.
Really. Is there anything more I can do?
Yes. We only have a little time left, so would it be all right if we organize what we talked about today?
Yes.

Today, as we thought together about moving toward solving the issue, I feel we were able to find a key point and a goal. The key point was moving during COVID. The goal is to get closer to being that “kind of person.” How does that sound?
Yes. The goal is there, I think.

Yes. Listening to you today, I felt that you are someone who is able to think carefully about what you can do right now, and who has the ability to take action on what you can do. How was it for you, talking about this today?

Yes. Starting from my child’s problem, I realized that it really is my own issue. I felt that maybe it would be good if I can keep thinking about what I can do now, and try taking action. Thank you very much.

You’ve analyzed this carefully, and I can feel the energy you have to move forward. I’ll be rooting for you as you move even a little closer to the version of yourself you’re aiming for. We’ll end here for today, but is there anything else you’d like to add?
No, I’m okay. Thank you very much for today.
Then, if anything else comes up, please feel free to come back for counseling. Thank you for today.

interaction.content: (Thank you for meeting with me.)
I’m the counselor. Thank you for being here. I’d like to work with the theme of “suicidal thoughts.”
(Understood. I’ll play the client role for suicidal thoughts.)
What brings you in to talk today?
I’m just tired of so many things. It’s not exactly that I want to die... I just want to disappear and be gone.
I see. So that’s how deeply you’re feeling this... Where are you contacting us from right now?
I’m at home.
I see. Are you keeping warm right now? I’m concerned because you said you’re very exhausted.
I’m okay.
I see. You mentioned feeling like you want to die. Have you thought about any specific method or anything like that?
I haven’t thought that far yet, but... maybe I should think about it.
That’s not what I mean. If it hasn’t gone that far, I feel a little relieved. What has been going on that has left you this exhausted? Could you tell me a bit more about it?

Caring for my parent, and my son lost his job because of COVID and has been shut in at home, and my husband is always irritated. No one needs me, and no one listens to what I have to say. If life is just going to keep going on like this every day, I want to stop here.
I see. So many things have really piled up on you. I think it’s completely understandable that you would end up thinking that way.
Yes...
On top of everything already being so hard, having your husband be irritated too must be unbearable...
It’s his mother I’m caring for, and he doesn’t do anything.
I see. That’s awful. It must feel very irresponsible, leaving it all to you alone. That would make you angry.
Yes. I’m angry, and I also feel sad. Like no one is thinking about me at all.

That’s how it feels to you... So right now, while you’re worried about your son being shut in, you’re caring for your husband’s mother, and on top of that your husband isn’t helping, so you’re completely exhausted.
Yes. I’ve started to not understand what I’m even living for.
When you’re this exhausted, I think it’s natural that you would feel that way. If you’ve been carrying all of this by yourself, of course you would be worn out.
Do you think so? Thank you.
Of all of this, what are you struggling with the most?
Maybe that I don’t know what I’m living for anymore.
I see. Not being able to see the meaning of living must be very painful.
Yes... I don’t know the meaning of living, and there’s no one who will listen to me, so it’s hard.
Are you able to get rest, like sleep?
Because of the caregiving, I get woken up often... but when I can take a nap during the day, I do.
I see.
Yes. With naps, it feels like even when I’m not trying to sleep, I end up falling asleep.
It feels like you fall asleep before you know it...
Yes.
If you’re able to sleep for a decent stretch even during the day, does it feel like your body can rest a little?
I think it’s better than not sleeping.
I see. Have you talked to anyone about the caregiving?
Yes. I’ve talked to a social worker. But she’s not severe enough to be placed in a facility, and she herself says she wants to stay at home, so I feel like there’s nothing I can do.
I see. You’re being considerate of your mother-in-law and putting her wishes first. Still, I think you also need a change of pace sometimes. Are you able to get that kind of time?
I don’t have that kind of time. I have to make three meals a day for my son and three meals a day for my mother-in-law.
I really think you’re doing so much. It’s because you’re there that your son and your mother-in-law are able to live day to day.
Hearing you say that makes me feel saved. Thank you.

If you’re always taking care of other people, of course you’re going to get exhausted. I’d like you to take care of yourself sometimes too. What would it be like to make even a little time to do something you enjoy?
Yes. I want my husband to help too. Time I can use for myself... Even if I had the time, I don’t know what I would do.
It doesn’t have to be a long time.
Yes. It’s been such a long time since I did anything for myself...
I see.
Yes. I’ve completely forgotten. I guess I’ve only been living for other people. (Thank you very much.)
Thank you very much.

interaction.content: Hello. Thank you for meeting with me today.
Hello. Thank you as well.
When it’s time, we’ll go ahead and begin. Thank you. Hello. Thank you for coming in to talk today. To start, could you tell me your gender, age, and what you’d like to discuss?
Hello. I’m a 45-year-old woman. I’m struggling with work.
Thank you for telling me. You mentioned it’s about work—could you tell me a bit more about that?

I changed jobs at 30 to my current small workplace so I could balance work with raising my children, but there’s been no change at all in my promotion or career. I’m wondering whether it’s okay to just keep going like this.
You’ve been working hard at both raising your children and your job all this time. You’re wondering whether it’s okay to stay like this—what parts of that are you feeling troubled about?
I’ve worked there for many years, but I’m still just a regular staff member.
I see. Earlier, you mentioned that your promotion and career haven’t changed in 15 years. How do you feel about your current job?
I like the work, but I’ve been on the front lines the whole time, so physically I’m at my limit.
I see. Even though it’s work you like, the physical side has been difficult. I can hear that you’ve been giving your all on the front lines for a long time. By the way, what kind of work do you do?
I work in nursing.
Thank you for telling me. It’s wonderful work, but it’s also very physically demanding, isn’t it. In that situation, how are you hoping things will be for you going forward?
I’d like to do management work, like being in a managerial position, but even though I’ve worked there for a very long time, I haven’t even been made a chief. It’s pathetic.
So that’s the situation. I imagine there may be some feelings of frustration too. How are you feeling?
It’s not so much frustration as anxiety. The thought that things might stay the same all the way until retirement...
I see. Is the biggest source of anxiety the idea that your current situation—being physically at your limit—will continue from here on?
That’s part of it, and I’m also anxious that I might be turned down for promotion because of my age. The evaluation system isn’t clear.

I see. So you had been thinking about bringing up promotion. When the evaluation system isn’t clear, I think it’s only natural to feel unsure about how you should act. Have you ever talked with anyone before about promotion or the evaluation system?

Yes. Because I don’t really understand how I’m being evaluated. Until now, I’ve used my own time to obtain various qualifications. I think my relationships at work aren’t that bad either. Under my current supervisor’s policy, they don’t have the position of chief. Even though other workplaces do have that position.
I see. I can hear how much effort you’ve put in, and how much care you’ve taken with your workplace relationships too.

Without a position title, there are trainings I can’t attend, and I also found out that trainings that come to the workplace in the first place—management and career development trainings—were being stopped by my supervisor, and the information wasn’t even reaching me.
I see.
I’m not aware of it myself, but maybe I don’t have people’s trust or support. But I feel like I’m being conveniently used as a regular staff member.
Listening to you, I get the sense that what you’re aiming for and your supervisor’s thinking are different. How do you feel about your supervisor?
I wonder if they’re just pretending to recognize me. Even though it’s hard to get time off, I’ve obtained several qualifications.
I see. You really have made a tremendous effort, even while raising your children.
About those qualifications, they said things like there’s no point in getting them, and...
I’m listening, so please go on.
They include national qualifications other than nursing too, and I don’t think they’re meaningless. I got them on my own time, so I don’t think they have any right to say anything about it.

So your supervisor says things like that. I can hear your motivation to improve and your strong, positive feelings. You’ve really made so much effort while wanting to advance your career. And in that situation, your supervisor seems to recognize you, yet you also feel there’s a part of them that wants you to stay as you are.
Somehow, I’m starting to get angrier and angrier.
That’s how you’re feeling right now.
As I’ve been putting it into words, feelings of shame and anger have been welling up, and I’m sorry if this is unpleasant.

No, not at all. It’s okay. I think the true feelings you had been holding back are coming out. These are feelings from a deep place, so please do value them. If you were being treated in a way that didn’t match the important effort you’ve made, I think it’s natural for feelings like that to come up.
It’s late to say this now, but I should have realized it much earlier.
I think you’ve been putting yourself last and devoting yourself to your patients and your workplace. I can also sense your sincere character.
I feel like that feeling was used to their advantage.
That’s how you feel.
Yes. (Our time is up. Thank you.)

I think you may be feeling, for the first time now, the feelings that were deep inside your heart. (Yes, we’ll move toward ending.) Please keep valuing those feelings as you think about what comes next.
Thank you for listening to me.
Thank you for coming in to talk today. If you’d like, please come back to talk again. (We’ve gone over time. Thank you for today.)
I will do that. Thank you very much.
Then we’ll end here. Thank you very much.
(Thank you as well. I learned a lot. If there’s another opportunity, I’d appreciate it.)
(Thank you very much. I’d like to make use of this going forward, so I’d appreciate your evaluation.)

interaction.content: Hello, we’ll begin when it’s time. Thank you for being here today. Hello, I’m the counselor. Thank you for coming to talk with me today. To start, could you tell me your age, gender, and what you’d like to discuss?
I’m 38, male. I’m currently on leave from work and receiving benefits, but I’m struggling because the person in charge is slow to respond.
That sounds troubling. Could you tell me a bit more about it?

I pay my rent every month with the benefits I receive, but for some reason they said it’s only going to be late this month, and I’m not really satisfied with that. I’m thinking I might not be able to pay.
That makes sense. You have plans on your end too, so it’s difficult when it gets delayed. Did you ask the person in charge why it would be late?
I did ask, but they wouldn’t tell me the reason. Apparently there was some kind of problem with the paperwork, but they contacted me five days after receiving it.
I see... That’s hard to accept. Even if they have their own circumstances, it throws off your plans... By the way, did you ask around when it would be deposited?
They said it would probably be next month. I’m in a hurry here, but they seem so laid-back.
Really... Did you also tell the person in charge about things like your rent?
I did, but they just say, “This is our job, so...” Must be nice for people who can work.
That would make you feel even more angry. Earlier, you said you might not be able to pay—do you mean you might not be able to pay by the due date?
I’m really irritated. There isn’t really a due date; it’s more like it’s usually deposited around a certain day, and this time it’s going to be later than usual.
I see... Thank you for telling me. You mentioned that you’re on leave from work. If you don’t mind, could you tell me the reason you’re on leave?
I’ve been told it’s an adjustment disorder. Basically, depression.
I see. Then if things like promised dates get delayed, that would make your feelings even more unstable...
Yes, sometimes I get so anxious thinking I might be kicked out of my apartment that I can’t sleep.
I think it’s completely understandable that you’d feel anxious. It’s not as though you’ve done anything wrong...
I’m not taking time off because I want to, so I don’t know what I should do.
That makes sense... If it’s okay, could you tell me what’s weighing on your mind the most right now?
It’s really about what I’m going to do to live. I’m at the point where I can barely buy groceries, and I’ve started using the canned food I had stocked up.
Thank you. I’d like to confirm again: if your leave benefits are deposited, you’ll be able to pay the rent, correct? And aside from that, buying food is also becoming difficult?
Yes, that’s right. Basically, I just don’t have the money...
I see... You said the payment will come next month, but in the meantime, is there anyone you can talk to, like family?
I’d rather not tell my family if I can avoid it.
That’s how you feel. If it’s okay, could I ask why?
I guess I don’t want to worry them too much, and I know my parents’ home doesn’t have much money either...
You’re worried about your family. Thank you for telling me all of this.
Yes.
If you’re willing, would you like to think together with me about what you can do?
I’d like that.
First, about the rent—do you think you could explain the situation to the owner and ask if they could wait a little for the rent?
I see. Do you think they’d wait?

We won’t know unless you ask, but I don’t think you would be kicked out just for being one month behind. Also, given the circumstances, if you talk to them in advance, I think they may be willing to wait a little.
I see, okay. What should I do about food and things like that?
For the rent, let’s start by talking to the owner. Next, about food—you said you don’t want to worry your family.
Yes.
Do they know that you’re on leave from work?
No, I haven’t told them...
I see. So is that why you feel you can’t explain the situation to them?
Because I don’t want them to worry.
I see... You really care about your family. If you did talk to your family, what do you imagine might happen?
What would happen, right. I haven’t been in touch with them much lately, so it’s hard to imagine. I haven’t seen them in over five years.
I see... You haven’t been in contact for that long... Then, is there anyone else you could talk to?
It’s not that there’s no one, but... kind of.
I see. Thank you for telling me so much. Would it be okay if I shared a little of what I’m sensing?
Yes.

Thank you. First, let me organize what we’ve talked about. Right now, you have an adjustment disorder and your emotions are unstable, and on top of that, your benefits deposit has been delayed, so you’re worried you might be kicked out of your apartment. And you don’t want to worry your family, so you can’t talk to them about your current situation. But in reality, you’re also struggling right now with money to buy food. Is that correct?
Yes, that’s correct.

Thank you. First, you’ll try consulting the owner about the rent. And about money going forward—because I’m most concerned about your health, I think it may be good to talk to your family first. Of course, I understand that you don’t want to worry them, but I’d like you to think about how your family, not knowing your current situation, would feel if something happened to you. What do you think?
Yes, I do think maybe I should talk to my family. But if there are any other options, I’d like to hear them too...

I’m relieved to hear that. It may be painful, but I do hope you’ll use this as an opportunity to tell them. If you still can’t tell them, you mentioned earlier that there is someone else you might be able to talk to, so perhaps you could ask that person? Since it’s only for the few days until the money is deposited, they may be able to help you.
Even if there is someone, it would be a friend, so it’s kind of hard to say...
I see... Why does it feel hard to talk to them?
I feel like it’s hard to say when they know my face. With the rent, I can say it because I don’t know the owner’s face.
That’s how you feel. What if you were in the opposite position? If your friend were in trouble, what would you do?
Do you mean if I had money?
Yes.
Hmm... Yeah, I do think I might lend them a little. I wonder if my family would feel that way too.

Just as you worry about your family, I think your family would worry about you too. So maybe you could take this opportunity to tell them about different things and talk with them. I think they would surely support you, but what do you think?
Yes, I’ll try to push myself a little.
We’re almost out of time, but if anything else comes up that you’re struggling with, please feel free to reach out anytime. Let’s think it through together again.
Yes, thank you very much.
I’m rooting for you to be able to move forward, even a little. Thank you for today.
Thank you.
(Thank you. If you have time, I’d appreciate it if you could leave a rating.) (I’ll end the system now. Take care.)

interaction.content: Hello, I’m the counselor. I’d like to begin when it’s time, so thank you for being here today.
Thank you as well!
Hello. I’m the counselor. Thank you for coming in for counseling today. To start, could you tell me your age and gender?
I’m 19, female.
Thank you for telling me. I’ll listen to what you’d like to talk about today.
Right now I’m struggling with making friends... I came because I want to know how to build good friendships.
I see. I imagine that leaves you feeling unsettled and thinking about all kinds of things. About when did you start having this concern?
I feel like it’s been since I was little, as far back as I can remember.
Do you have a rough idea of what age?
Since elementary school, I already felt like making friends was tiring.
I see... In what kinds of situations do you feel tired when you’re with friends?
I think I have a strong feeling of not wanting people to dislike me, but I get tired because I can’t say what I really feel...
I see. Did you have that tendency even when you were in elementary school?
I did. Back then, I thought everyone was like that.
I see. So you felt that everyone, like you, was actually finding it painful not being able to say what they really felt?
Yes.

Have you had any experiences where you talked with friends and felt hurt or disliked something, or anything like that? If you don’t mind, please tell me. You can share only what you feel comfortable talking about.
In the end, because I can’t say what I really feel, I feel like I often get used... People cancel on me at the last minute and things like that...
I see. No one likes being used. Is it that you get nervous around friends and have a hard time saying what you really feel?
Rather than nervous, I think it may be more that I have a strong fear that if I say what I really feel, they might dislike me.
Have you ever thought about why you so quickly think, “If I say what I really feel, they might dislike me”?
I think about it a lot. When I was little, my parents were strict, and if I didn’t do what they said, I’d get scolded, so I couldn’t express my feelings... I feel like it might come from that.
I see, so that’s how it was. Are you able to tell your parents how you feel now?
I feel like I’ve become able to say my opinions more than when I was little.
That’s good. For example, have you ever talked to anyone else about not being able to say what you really feel when you meet people?
No. I’m scared of people finding out that I’m carrying those feelings...
I see. But I think it’s natural to feel scared about other people finding out something like that.
Is that so... Do people generally carry feelings like that?

Yes, there are many people who feel this way. At the same time, I wondered if you may be very kind and sensitive to everyone’s feelings, and because you’re kind, you end up thinking about all sorts of things too much. How does that sound to you?
In the end, I think it might be because I’m scared of getting hurt and scared of being disliked. And I wonder if people around me sense that.
That’s how it feels to you. What do you think would help so that people around you don’t sense that?
I don’t know...
I understand. Would it be okay if we organize the situation once?
Yes.

Since you were little, you’ve had a strong feeling that if you say what you really feel, people will dislike you. When you think about it, your parents were strict when you were little, and that tendency may have come from there. Now, compared to before, you’ve become more able to say things to your parents. And now you want to build good friendships where you can talk honestly. Is that right?
Yes.
Then, what is a good friend like, in your mind?
Ideally, it would be someone I don’t get tired being with, and we could say what we want to say to each other.
I see! That sounds really nice. What kind of person is someone you don’t get tired being with, for you?
Maybe someone who doesn’t seem to be thinking about anything, haha.
I see! Is it the image of someone who seems like they’d let anything slide?
Yes, that’s right.
Is there anyone around you who, for example, is easygoing, mentally steady, and seems like they’d let anything slide?
That’s kind of hard... I guess there is someone, but they seem like they don’t listen to what people say at all...
I see. For example, is that person the type you yourself would want to become friends with?
Hmm... maybe not.
I see. Then in your current environment, there may not really be the kind of friend you’d like to have... Do you go out for any hobbies or clubs or anything like that?
I do. I joined a club that a friend told me to join.
How has that been? Did it seem like an environment where you could make friends without having to be too careful or considerate?
My friend seems to be enjoying it. The club I’m in now is an outdoor club, and I’m basically more of an indoor person.
I see, that makes sense. In that case, how would it be to try joining an indoor club?
Yeah... But I can’t say no to my friend.
I see. For example, do you think you could say something like, “Next term, I’m going to try joining an indoor club”?
I want to say it. But wouldn’t they end up disliking me...?

I think it would be okay. Everyone has things they want to do, so for example, you could say, “I’m really interested in indoor activities right now, so do you want to go to that club too, OO?” and invite your friend. That might be one way. If you do that, I don’t think your friend would feel rejected, because you’re inviting them.
That’s true... For me, since I can’t say what I really feel, the hurdle is a little high, but I think I’ll try my best.
Yes, please do try it if you’d like.
Yes. Thank you.

It’s about time for our session to end. Would it be all right to stop here for today’s consultation? Also, if anything is on your mind or you feel anxious about anything, please do come to counseling again. I’ll be here anytime.
That’s okay. Thank you very much.
(Thank you! Good work today!)
Good work today! (Thank you very much!)
Then we’ll end the role-play here! Thank you very much. I look forward to working with you again.
Thank you as well, and I look forward to continuing to work with you!

interaction.content: (Good evening. Thank you for speaking with me.)
Good evening, thank you for speaking with me.
Good evening. I’m the counselor. Thank you for coming. To start, could you tell me your age, gender, and what you’d like to discuss?
Good evening. I’m 50, male, and I’d like to talk about my child not attending school.
Thank you for telling me. I see. You’re worried about your child. That must be concerning. May I ask how old your child is, and their gender?
Yes, she’s my daughter, in her second year of high school, but since starting second year she hasn’t been able to go to school at all.
I see… That must be painful. Is there something that seems to be the reason?

She couldn’t go during the third term of her first year either, and somehow she made it to second year. It seems like she’s struggling with friendships. I don’t think it’s bullying, but she just doesn’t seem to fit in.
I see. As a parent, that must be so unsettling. Before the third term of her first year, was she going to school every day?
There were signs from around the end of the second term. Until then she was okay.
I see… There were signs… When you say she “doesn’t fit in,” what is that like?
It seems like they treat my daughter in a harsh way.
I see. Her friends do. You’d want them to treat her kindly. Is it just one friend?
No, it seems like she feels that way from a lot of students. And she commutes by train, but on the way she started getting stomachaches or feeling sick, and it seems like she became unable to go.
I see. That many people. I can imagine how you must feel. From your perspective as her father, what kind of child is your daughter? Her personality and so on…
She’s probably too kind. Or maybe timid.
I see. She’s very kind. When you say harsh… what kind of situations specifically?
I think maybe she can’t talk back. So I wonder if she kept it all bottled up.
I see. That’s certainly possible. Has she been like that since she was little?
She wasn’t really like that before.
Is that so? When did she start being in the state she’s in now?
I think part of it is that the high school is a bit rough. It’s been since she started high school. I told her to go to a different high school, though.
So that happened. Was there some reason your daughter chose her current high school?
It was my daughter’s first choice, at least. She seemed to think it matched her academic level. I wanted her to choose a quieter school with a slightly lower ranking.
I see. You recommended a different high school because you were thinking about your daughter.
Yes, that’s right.
From your perspective as well, you feel her current high school doesn’t suit her?
Now especially, I really think so.
That’s how you feel. After graduating from this high school, does your daughter have anything she’s hoping to do?
It seems like she hasn’t decided on a path yet. That said, at this rate she’ll have to repeat the year. There’s not much time left anymore.
That’s true. It feels like there isn’t much time. Have you talked with your daughter about what to do from here?
Yes, it seems like she’ll soon reach the limit for the number of days she can be absent. My daughter says she still wants to try, but in reality she hasn’t been able to go.
I see. Your daughter is someone who tries hard. For example, I wondered if one option might be for her to take high school entrance exams again next year.
I don’t want to take that route, since she’d end up two years behind. If anything, maybe transferring into a correspondence school.
That’s what you’re thinking. She’s a kind daughter who thinks about the other person’s feelings and doesn’t talk back. But she says she wants to keep trying a little longer…
I’ve actually started looking. I haven’t told my daughter, though. I don’t want her to repeat the year…
I see. You really care deeply about your daughter.
Thank you. Do you think transferring schools would be good?

If it’s possible, I think taking a transfer exam and changing schools could be an option. It might also be good to set a deadline, and say that if she can’t go by that date…, then talk with her about correspondence school.
Yes, maybe I should talk to my daughter about transferring schools…
Your daughter has been going through the painful feeling of “I want to go, but I can’t” for a long time. I imagine it’s painful for you as her father as well. What does your wife say?
My wife is also starting to give up on her continuing at the current high school. We’ve started looking for places she could transfer to together.
I see. You’re feeling the same way. But your daughter feels she wants to keep trying a little longer…
Yes. But if we tell her about repeating the year, her feelings might change.
I see. Your daughter may be blaming herself for things not going well in her relationships. I think it may be good to tell her that she is okay as she is.
Yes, at first I was harsh with my daughter too, but I need to treat her that way, don’t I…
You’ve been struggling with this for a long time too. I hope your daughter can somehow move in a good direction.
Thank you.
How is your own health? Are you able to sleep at night?
Sometimes I still get angry and can’t sleep.
I see. There are feelings of anger too. What is the anger directed toward?
Anger, or maybe regret—I feel like choosing that high school was a mistake.
That’s how you feel. I don’t think this mistake will be a wasted experience for your daughter’s future.
I hope it turns out that way… Right now it’s hard for me to think that.
It’s very understandable that you feel that way. I hope this experience becomes something valuable for your daughter’s life going forward.
Thank you.
Thank you as well for sharing this with me. If anything comes up again, please feel free to come anytime. I’ll be here.
I feel a little better, at least. I’ll think about moving in the direction of transferring schools.
I’m glad you’ve come to feel that way. Tonight, please try to rest slowly, maybe by having a warm drink.
Thank you.
Thank you as well. Would it be all right to end here?
Yes, thank you.
(Thank you for speaking with me at this late hour.)
Thank you for your time.

interaction.content: Good evening. Thank you for being here today.
Good evening. Thank you for speaking with me.
Good evening, I’m the counselor. To start, could you please tell me your age, gender, and what you’d like to talk about?
I’m 30, female. What I want to talk about is my boyfriend.
Thank you for answering. It’s about your boyfriend, then. What kind of concern are you having?
We’ve been living together for about five years, but he still won’t really face the idea of marriage.
I see. When your feelings about wanting to get married don’t line up, that can feel really painful... Sakura, when did you start thinking that you wanted to get married?
About four years ago. We’ve been together for eight years now.
You’ve been together a long time. If you’ve wanted to get married for four years, you must have been holding a lot in...

I didn’t want to put pressure on him about marriage, so I couldn’t say anything all this time. I wanted to get married while I was still in my twenties, but just recently I turned 30 without any proposal or anything from him, and now I don’t know if he even intends to get married...
Mm-hmm. So you’re in a situation where you haven’t been able to tell him how you feel. As time passes, it can get harder to understand what the other person is thinking.
That’s right...
That sounds like a really painful situation. What makes you think it would put pressure on your boyfriend?
When women reach the age where they want to get married, they start bringing up marriage more often, and I read in a magazine that this becomes a burden for men, and I thought, I see.
I see. So it was influenced by the magazine. There are a lot of different opinions out there, so it can be a difficult thing to sort through.

It seems like for some people, even just talking about going to a friend’s wedding, or saying that a friend looked beautiful, can feel like a burden. Once I saw that, I just really couldn’t bring up marriage...

I see. If someone is cautious about marriage, there may be people who feel that way. If you were to talk about marriage while not knowing whether it would be a burden or not, what do you feel might happen?
When we started living together, we did talk about it being with marriage in mind, at least.
Mm-hmm.
But there was just so completely nothing after that, so last year I talked to him a little. I said, we’re both going to be 29 soon, so shouldn’t we start thinking about marriage?
Yes. I’m listening.
Then he kind of brushed it off lightly, like, “Yeah... I guess so...” Since that happened, it’s really hard to bring it up now...
You worked up the courage to say it, so it must have hurt to have it brushed off lightly. When that happens, it makes sense that you’d feel hesitant to bring it up again...
That’s right. It’s just too painful for me to say any more about it...
Yes, I can understand that... I think it’s wonderful that you found the courage to take action. I’d like to ask a little about your boyfriend too. What kind of person is he?
He’s a very gentle person, and he’s very kind to me.
Having a kind boyfriend is a really wonderful thing. What kind of work does he do?
He works at a real estate company, in sales.
I see. Real estate sales sounds like it could be a busy job. Does he seem busy with work?
Yes, he works a lot of overtime, but it’s a company where he gets two days off a week properly.
It must feel reassuring that he works with a good sense of balance! What is he usually like at home?

Usually, well... he shares the housework properly too. Whoever gets home first makes dinner, and whoever gets home later does the laundry, things like that. When our days off match up, we go out together or enjoy our hobbies.
It sounds like you’re living a very fulfilling life together. I think that’s wonderful.
Yes, it’s really easy and comfortable being with him. That’s exactly why I want to marry him, but it’s not going well... I’ve already turned 30, and I feel like I’m the only one being left behind.
Feeling that way can make you feel lonely, can’t it.
Yes, exactly...
As I’m listening to you, I wonder if maybe your boyfriend is avoiding the change of getting married while things are currently fulfilling for both of you. How do you feel about that?
I don’t know... I have absolutely no idea what he’s thinking, or why he won’t marry me.
Yes... Trying to figure out what someone else is thinking can be really exhausting.
He’s not really the type to express his own opinions much, and he always puts me first, so it’s really hard to figure out what he’s thinking.
Yes. When the situation is difficult, it may actually help if you can think about it in a more positive way.
Positive...?

Yes. Since you’ve realized that trying to guess is exhausting and doesn’t give you an answer, I thought it might be important to say, I’m not going to try to guess anymore! or to try letting go of that way of thinking.
Do you mean not thinking about marriage either?
Marriage is an important value for you, Sakura, so I don’t think you should let go of that! Let’s think together, in a positive way, about marriage with your boyfriend from here.
I’m sorry, please help me.

Then let’s organize things for a moment. Sakura, you want to marry the boyfriend you’ve been with for many years. You brought up marriage once, but you had the experience of being brushed off, and since then you haven’t brought it up. Your boyfriend is very gentle, and there are no problems in your daily life together. But you don’t know how he feels about marriage. And it feels painful that you weren’t able to get married in your twenties.
Yes, that’s right.
Thank you. It’s okay, there is still plenty of time. Also, I think one thing that’s causing you pain right now is the influence of that magazine. How do you feel about that?

Do you think something can be done...? From a man’s perspective, I do understand that the twenties to early thirties are probably the time when they most want to work. His work is really going well for him right now too, so I think what the magazine said probably isn’t entirely wrong.

Yes, I can see that. It’s written in a way that makes it feel reasonable, isn’t it. But with things like this, if you compare yourself with people around you and look at it in terms of numbers, like age, I think there’s no end to it. More than anything, I think what matters is being happy now. There are plenty of people who get married at 40 and are happy, and people who get married at 20 and feel it was a mistake.
That’s true. If I think about my happiness now, maybe age doesn’t matter.
Yes. You are you, Sakura. But at the same time, I also think it’s important that you’re feeling now that you want to get married.
That’s right. I want children too. So I want to get married as soon as possible if I can...
Mm-hmm, so you’ve been thinking about children too. To help you face your boyfriend seriously, would it be all right if I offered a few pieces of advice?
Yes, please...!

In conclusion, as I’ve been listening, I strongly feel that there is trust between you and your boyfriend, so I think it would be good to try talking with him once more. And I have two pieces of advice.
Talking it through really is the best thing, isn’t it...

First, based on your past experience of being brushed off, “talk in a situation where it’s harder for him to brush it off.” For example, when there’s a third person present, when he doesn’t seem tired, on a day that’s important to both of you, or while you’re traveling somewhere...
I see, a situation where it’s harder to brush off... That might be really important.

Second, when you talk, instead of focusing on expressing your own feelings, be very thorough and be a good interviewer for your boyfriend. If you do that, I think you’ll understand his thoughts, and it will definitely lead to the next step. → toward your boyfriend (correction)
An interviewer... So I should be the one listening. Somehow I feel like I might be able to talk to him now.
I’m glad to hear that. I’m rooting for you!
Thank you. I’ll try my best!
I think that’s because there is a trusting relationship between you and your boyfriend, Sakura. It’s about time to end our session, and thank you for sharing so much with me today.
Thank you too, for listening to me!
Then we’ll end the consultation here. Thank you for today.
Yes, thank you very much!

interaction.content: Good evening. Thank you for being here today. We’ll begin when it’s time.
Good evening, thank you as well for today. If you have any requests, please let me know.
I don’t have any particular requests, so it’s all right.
Understood. Thank you.
Good evening. I’m the counselor. Thank you for coming to talk with me today. To start, could you tell me your age and gender?
Good evening. I’m a 32-year-old man.
Thank you. What would you like to talk about today?
I came to talk about marriage and the future.
I see. What specifically would you like to discuss about marriage and the future?
Well, I’m not really sure myself, and I came today because I’ve been wondering if it’s okay to just stay like this.
I see. It sounds like you’re feeling some anxiety... Would it be okay if I ask you a few questions and we go from there?
Yes, that’s fine. Please do.
Yes, thank you.
Thank you as well.
How do you feel about marriage?
Well, I’m not that conscious of it myself, but when people around me say things, I do feel a little rushed.
I see. By the way, are you currently married? If you don’t want to talk about it, that’s completely okay.
Thank you. I’m not married yet, so I came to talk, hoping I might feel even a little bit better.
I see. So when people around you say things about marriage, you feel pressured... I hope I can help you feel even a little lighter.
Thank you. Yes, that’s right. When people around me start getting married and things, I start feeling like I should too, and I get anxious.
Mm-hmm. I’m listening.
But I also feel like, for now, I’m okay as I am.
I see. So right now you feel like you don’t necessarily need to get married, but because people around you bring it up, you’re wondering what to do...
Yes. But I also think I don’t want to be alone forever, so I came to talk about it.
I see. You said you’re okay not getting married right now, but do you feel like you’d like to someday in the future?
Yes, I do think I’d like to.
I see. Is there any particular reason you feel like you don’t need to get married right now? You can share only what you’re comfortable with.
There isn’t any particular reason, but personally I just feel like not yet.
I see. You mentioned that people around you say things about marriage. Who says these things to you?
It’s mainly my parents, as expected.
I see... How did you feel when your parents said that to you?
I felt rushed, and at the same time I also wanted them to leave me alone.
It makes sense that you’d feel like you don’t want them to interfere that much...
Yes.
Do you live with your parents?
I live alone. I hate being told that when I go home sometimes, and recently, with COVID too, I’ve started avoiding it.
I see. It’s understandable that you’d want to avoid that.
Yes. It’s also hard to go out.
That’s true. It really is hard to go out these days...
Yes.
Would it be okay if I take a moment to organize what we’ve talked about so far?
Please do.

People around you, especially your parents, say things about marriage, and you feel rushed and also feel like you want them to leave you alone. There are also other people who are starting to get married. You feel that as pressure. You’d like to get married someday, but right now you feel you don’t need to get married yet. Is that about right?
Yes. The “leave me alone” part made me laugh a little lol. Thank you.
Was that a little too blunt...? (laughs) Was it okay?
It’s okay. It was just a bit funny, and I ended up laughing myself. Thank you.
Not at all. I’m glad if it made you laugh.
Yes.
Listening to you, I wondered if the pressure from people around you about marriage is making it hard for you to feel at ease. How does that sound?
Yes, it does feel like pressure.
Then today, how would it be if we think together about how that pressure might be eased a little more than it is now?
Yes. I’d like to think about it together. Thank you.
Yes, let’s think through it together. Thank you as well. What do you think might help reduce the pressure from people around you?
I’m not really sure myself, and I’m feeling lost. Sorry.
No, no, there’s no need to apologize.
Thank you. When we’re talking, the time goes by so quickly. Thank you for listening today.
Yes, it does. It’s about time to end... How was it for you to talk today?
I was able to talk about a small worry of mine, and I feel a little lighter. Thank you. If something comes up again, I’ll feel free to come talk.
I’m glad to hear that. Let’s keep thinking about ways to reduce the pressure. I’ll be here.
Thank you. I’m looking forward to it again. Well then, I’ll be going now.
Thank you. Then I’ll end the consultation here.
Please take care of your health too, counselor. Yes, see you again.
Please take care of your health as well. Thank you. (Thank you very much. I learned a lot.)
“Thank you as well.” “I look forward to speaking with you again.”
(Thank you as well. I look forward to it. Then I’ll end here.)
