interaction.content: Good evening. Thank you for being here. I’ll work with the goal of building rapport through messages of acceptance and empathy.
Good evening. Thank you.
We’ll begin at 7:00 p.m. Good evening. I’m the counselor. To start, please tell me your gender, age, and what you’d like to talk about today.
Good evening. I’m 15, female. I don’t want to go to school.
Thank you for telling me. So you’re struggling with school. You can start wherever feels easiest to talk about. When did you start not wanting to go to school?
Yes, since about a month ago..
I see. So you’ve been struggling with this for about a month... Could you tell me why you don’t want to go to school?
Yes. I’m being bullied, and it’s exhausting.
I see. That must make you feel really hurt... If you’re okay with it, could you tell me what kinds of things happen to you when you go to school?
Yes.. It’s really hard. They throw my gym clothes in the trash, and they say mean things about me in loud voices.
I see... So they’re doing such awful things to you. That must be really exhausting, and I can understand why you wouldn’t want to go to school.
Yes. That’s right.. I can’t go anymore.
Thank you for telling me what’s going on right now. When those awful things happen, what do you do?
I stay quiet.. because I don’t know what to do...
I see. If something like that happened, it would make sense that you wouldn’t know what to do, and that you’d feel sad. When it happens, what feelings come up for you?
Yes. That’s right. I feel sad and hurt.
I see. Even while feeling that sadness and pain, you kept doing your best to go to school for a month.
Yes. At first I thought I’d be okay even if they did things like that to me, but... little by little I couldn’t go anymore... and I didn’t know what to do..

I see. I was struck by the fact that, at first, you had the feeling that you’d be “okay.” Could you tell me why, even though such awful things were happening, you were able to think you’d be “okay” at first?

I thought it would stop soon. I thought maybe it was just temporary.. I’d always been teased a lot anyway.. so I thought maybe it was that. At first it felt like they were just teasing me... so I thought maybe it would be okay. But it gradually escalated, and then I felt like I just couldn’t take it anymore.

I see. So because what was being done to you at first was different from what’s happening now, you were able to feel like you’d be “okay.” You said you’d always been teased a lot—what kinds of things happened back then?
Yes, at first they’d say things like “shorty,” or “do an animal impression,” and then I’d do it and everyone would laugh..
I see. So back then, it felt like everyone was laughing together. I think some people like doing those kinds of things, and some people don’t. How did you feel spending time with everyone back then?
Yeah... back then I thought, well, as long as everyone laughs, that’s fine. I really didn’t want to be left out... But I did feel a little bad about it too.

I see. You had mixed feelings... At the same time, I feel that your thought of “as long as everyone laughs, that’s fine” is very positive, generous, and really wonderful. What do you think about that part of yourself?
Yes. Is that right.. I thought, so I have a big heart, huh. I was just going along with everyone around me..
I feel that having a big heart is one of your wonderful qualities. Being able to go along with the people around you is also a really lovely kindness of yours.
I see.. I never knew that before. So it’s kindness..
Yes, I feel you can be confident in the fact that you have the generosity to forgive people and the kindness to think about everyone.
Yes. Thank you. I kind of thought that going along with other people was a bad thing..
I see. I think it may be because there are people like you, who can go along with others, that everyone is able to get along.
I see.. I feel a little better somehow.
I’m really glad that you were able to feel even a little better. Right now, I think there are painful feelings because of the unpleasant things happening at school.
Yes. It’s really hard..

That makes sense. When such awful things are done to you, I don’t think those painful feelings go away easily. And I’m sorry, but we’re in the middle of talking and our time is getting close to the end. How was it for you to talk today?
Yes. Talking today made me think that I have a big heart. I think I was able to feel a little more confident in myself. Thank you very much.
Thank you as well. I’m very glad that you were able to notice such a wonderful part of yourself. You can continue talking about this here another time, so please feel free to reach out.
Yes. Thank you very much.
The cold season is coming, so please take care not to catch a cold. Thank you for today.
Thank you very much.
Well then, we’ll end today’s consultation here. Thank you very much.
(Thank you for the hour. I learned a lot. If there’s another opportunity, I’d appreciate it.) Thank you very much.
(Thank you as well for your valuable time.)

interaction.content: Hello. I’m the counselor. It’s nice to meet you. To start, could you tell me your age, gender, and what you’d like to talk about?
Nice to meet you. Thank you. I’m 35, male, and I’m wondering whether I should continue with my hobby.
Thank you for reaching out. It sounds like there’s something difficult going on. What is making you unsure about whether to continue??

It’s not exactly that it’s painful, but I feel kind of unsettled, like, what should I do. My hobby is clay shooting. But recently, the shooting range is far away, and I’ve started feeling like it’s a hassle to go. If it were another hobby, like fishing, it probably wouldn’t be a problem, but because it’s a sport that uses guns, if I don’t use them often, the police kind of indirectly say, do you really need this? and suggest that I quit, or give them up. So that’s why I’ve been wondering what to do.

Clay shooting sounds really cool. I see. It’s not exactly something you can do just anywhere, is it? Long travel times can get exhausting. And on top of that, you get that kind of contact from the police. In that case, it becomes hard to go at your own pace. By the way, if you don’t use them for a long time, can the police forcibly confiscate them?
I don’t think it would go as far as confiscation, but I think I’d be put on their radar. The police want to eliminate guns that aren’t being used, to reduce the risk of them leading to crime.
I see. So that’s how it works. Have you been doing clay shooting for a long time?
It’s been more than five years since I started shooting. Recently, not at all, but... I mean, not at all. That was a mistake.
Thank you for correcting that. But doing it for five years is impressive. In that case, it makes sense that giving it up would feel difficult. How long has it been since you last went recently?
I haven’t done it for years.
I see. What are the reasons you don’t want to quit?

First, it took money and effort with the procedures to be able to possess them. It’s not like you can get permission right away; it took a little over half a year with all kinds of procedures and exams. One reason is that I feel like letting that go would be a waste. Also, because it’s an unusual hobby, maybe there’s a part of me that feels proud of it. It’s not like I brag about it, though.

It really does take time and effort, doesn’t it. Certainly, after putting in that much effort, it would feel wasteful to give it up. An unusual hobby can definitely be something to feel proud of. I thought it was impressive too, and honestly, I’d like to ask you more about it. Are there any reasons you think it might be okay to quit?
Well, first, money. It would reduce the burden of paying several thousand yen or so in fees for renewing the permits.
I see. Is that an annual renewal?
It’s not yearly; it’s renewed every three years. But I have two guns, so the fees are doubled.
I see. Has the renewal fee once every three years been a financial burden for you up to now?

The fee itself isn’t a burden. It was more the effort involved in the procedures—preparing various documents, and since there are interviews with family and friends, asking them to do that. That part was more of a hassle.
It goes that far. That sounds quite troublesome. If you gave them up and then tried to get them again, would it involve the same procedures and about the same amount of effort?
Yes. I’d have to redo the written and practical exams too. There would also be interviews and so on. It would be about the same, or even more.

So you’d have to start over from the exams. That sounds exhausting. I’ve briefly summarized the pros and cons of giving them up, and the pros and cons of not giving them up. Does this feel more or less right? Please take a look, and if there’s anything that needs correcting, could you let me know?
Yes.

Benefits of giving them up: ・No more renewal costs. ・Reduced risk of them being connected to crime. Drawbacks of giving them up: ・It feels wasteful considering all the effort up to now. ・If you try to get them again, the procedures would take a lot of effort. ・You’d have fewer things to talk about. Benefits of not giving them up: ・You can talk about it with people around you. ・You can do it again when you feel like it. Drawbacks of not giving them up: ・Renewal fees are needed once every three years. If there’s any additional information you’d like to add, please let me know.
Benefit of giving them up: the psychological burden of feeling like I have to use them would go away.

I see. That’s true. I’ll add that. Benefits of giving them up: ・No more renewal costs. ・Reduced risk of them being connected to crime. ・The psychological burden of feeling like you have to use them goes away. Drawbacks of giving them up: ・It feels wasteful considering all the effort up to now. ・If you try to get them again, the procedures would take a lot of effort. ・You’d have fewer things to talk about. Benefits of not giving them up: ・You can talk about it with people around you. ・You can do it again when you feel like it. Drawbacks of not giving them up: ・Renewal fees are needed once every three years.

If I summarize what I’m thinking now, I think that’s probably it. Also, as an addition, or maybe not exactly an addition, I realized that whether I have them or not probably doesn’t affect topics of conversation that much.

I see. Then it may be better to remove “having fewer things to talk about” and “being able to talk about it with people around you.” Benefits of giving them up: ・No more renewal costs. ・Reduced risk of them being connected to crime. ・The psychological burden of feeling like you have to use them goes away. Drawbacks of giving them up: ・It feels wasteful considering all the effort up to now. ・If you try to get them again, the procedures would take a lot of effort. Benefits of not giving them up: ・You can do it again when you feel like it. Drawbacks of not giving them up: ・Renewal fees are needed once every three years. Looking at this, what do you think?
It kind of feels like giving them up would be better.

There are more benefits to giving them up now. I’m sorry that we’re coming up on time, but I thought that if you compare this with the main values or priorities you have right now, or the things you consider important, it may become clearer what you need.
I’m still okay for time. I’ve started to think that maybe it’s not good to just keep holding onto them indefinitely.
Understood. I see. If you’re not that attached to the drawbacks of giving them up, then it may be okay.
Compared to when I first started, I feel like it’s changed into “I have to do it because I want to shoot.”
Would you say it feels like a sense of obligation, or like you’re putting pressure on yourself?
It kind of feels that way.
Does that make it hard to enjoy it?
I do like shooting itself, and it’s fun.
But getting to the point where it’s fun feels hard—is that it?
Yes. Actually getting to the shooting range and doing it is hard, and on weekend days off it’s crowded, so I don’t like that I can’t shoot at my own pace.

It gets that crowded. That makes sense; other people probably go on weekends too. If you could create an environment where you could do it at your own pace, how would that be? For example, moving closer to the shooting range.
The shooting range is up in the mountains, so I don’t really want to move there. To go on a weekday, I’d have to take a day off work.
I see. If it’s far away, you’d need to take paid leave and things like that.
Yes.
So it feels like you don’t quite feel strongly enough to go that far?
Yeah, I don’t think I feel that strongly. I can’t be the kind of person who, when winter comes, takes days off and goes skiing all the time.
I understand that feeling. I’m the same way. Looking at the pros and cons from earlier, what do you think would be good for you right now?
Quit gradually? For now, give up one of the two guns I have, and reduce the financial burden too.

I see. Certainly, if you try quitting gradually, your feelings may change. I’d encourage you to try that. As you quit gradually, if you think about it using the pros and cons as a guide, you may find what feels right.
Yes. I still have ammunition left, and I want to use it up. I’d like to think about each of these things.
You’d want to use that up, yes. Please do take some time to think about it. I’m rooting for you.
Thank you.
Thank you as well. We’ll end the consultation here, then. Thank you very much.
Thank you very much. This was very helpful.
I’m glad. Thank you. I’m sorry it took a while. I hope to speak with you again.

I see. What was it that made you start feeling like school was boring?
Hmm, I had a close friend, but somehow she started hanging out with other people and stuff, and it feels like she stopped staying with me.
I see. When something like that happens, it feels lonely, and even being at school can start to feel boring.
Yeah. I go when I can, like from the afternoon. I do like school, so...
I see. So when you’re able to go, you do go to school. You’re doing your best to get through each day. By the way, what do your family members say about you sometimes staying home from school?
My mom says, “Why aren’t you going?” but...
Yes, I see.
I go from the afternoon and do club activities. It’s fun because I can talk with everyone.
I see, so you’re able to enjoy your time at club activities.
Yes, it’s fun.
Yes, I think having time where you’re able to enjoy yourself is very important. What do your teachers say?
They ask me, “Why don’t you come?” but...
Mm-hmm.
Even if I tell the teacher, it’ll get passed on to my mom, so I can’t say it.

I see. When you think it will get told to your mother, you end up not being able to tell your teacher. That sounds painful... By the way, if it did get told to your mother, what do you think might happen?
I think she’d get mad and say, “You promised, but you’re not doing it.”
Yes, that’s what you think. If you think she’ll get angry, it would feel scary, and you wouldn’t be able to say it. If you’re okay telling me, what kind of promise did you make with your mother?
Yeah, when I became a junior high school student, I promised I’d make my own lunch, but since summer vacation ended, I just haven’t felt like doing it...
I see. Thank you for telling me.
There are times I can’t make it. Sometimes my mom hasn’t bought the ingredients, and it’s a hassle.
Yes, I see. If there aren’t ingredients, you can’t make it, and even if there are ingredients, I think it’s very natural for making lunch to feel like a hassle.
But if I don’t bring lunch, I kind of can’t go. If I don’t go, I won’t be able to keep up with my friends’ conversations either...

I see. Since everyone brings lunch, it becomes hard to go. And when you stop going, little by little you can’t keep up with what your friends are talking about, and it can feel like there’s distance between you. I think that’s very natural too.
If I don’t bring lunch, the teacher buys something for me, so then I have to pay money, and my mom won’t give me money.

I see. The teachers buy food for students who don’t bring lunch, for everyone’s health. But because of that, it can actually put you in a difficult position. So that’s why sometimes you end up going to school from the afternoon. How do you feel about the promise to make your own lunch?
I think I should do it because my mom has a hard time. But when I can’t make it, it costs money, so I try to go from the afternoon.
I see. Because you love your mother, you’re trying to be considerate of her. And you’re also being careful not to burden her financially. I can really feel your kindness.
I don’t want to worry my mom, and it’s a promise, so it can’t be helped.
Yes, I see. It’s a promise, and you feel like you have to do your best.
Yeah...
Do you think you could tell me how you’re feeling right now?
I want to go to school every day. But I might not be able to make lunch every day.
Yes, that’s how you feel. Thank you for telling me. By the way, besides you and your mother, who else is in your family?
It’s just me and my mom.
I see. So that’s why you feel like you have to help your important mother.
Yeah. Maybe that’s it. It’s scary when my mom gets angry, and she’s the only one I have.

Yes, that’s how you feel. I thought that you have a strong sense of responsibility, and that you’re a hardworking person who really cares about your mother. I think you’re doing your best every day to help her.
I wonder if that’s true... No one has ever told me I’m doing my best before.

Because I think it’s hard for a 13-year-old to wake up early every morning and make lunch. I also imagine there may be other things around the house that you’re doing your best with to help your mother.
I think I’m the only one in my class who makes my own lunch. Everyone else’s moms make it for them. But I don’t think my mom will make mine.
I see. When you feel like you’re the only one, it can make you feel sad. Why do you think your mother won’t make it?
She said since it’s just the two of us, she wants me to become independent quickly. My mom is the kind of person who doesn’t change once she’s decided something...
I see. In her own way, your mother is thinking about your happiness, wanting you to be able to live firmly on your own. How do you feel about that?
I don’t really know, but I don’t want my mom to go away.

Yes, you want to keep living the way you are now with your mother. Because she’s important family to you, I think it’s natural to feel that way. You came to talk today because not being able to make lunch has made it hard for you to go to school every day, and you’re having trouble with that. From here, what do you think you yourself might be able to do?

I don’t think I can do anything. I guess it’ll stay like this, going sometimes and not going sometimes. But being told today that I’m doing my best made me feel a little better. I’d never talked about it before.

I see. Making lunch can be hard if you try to make it from scratch, but for example, there are things you can do ahead of time, like leaving a little dinner aside or freezing something. If you have a strong wish to keep your promise with your mother, I’d like to talk next time about those kinds of ideas to make things less hard for you. How does that sound?
Yes. I’d like that, please.
Yes, you feel that way. Thank you. I want to support your wish to go to school every day. Please let me think through it together with you again next time.
I’d like to talk with you again.
Yes, please let me hear more from you again. Our consultation time for today is ending, so we’ll finish here. Thank you for coming to talk with me.
Thank you very much.
(Thank you for your time. Thank you.)
Thank you too. I appreciate it. I learned a lot.
(I’ll send the closing message.)

interaction.content: Hello, I’m the counselor. Thank you for coming in to talk today.
Hello. Thank you for meeting with me today.
Thank you as well. What would you like to talk about today?
It’s about time. I’m struggling with always ending up just barely on time for meeting people, and I was hoping I could talk with you about whether there’s some way to improve that.
I see. Does it feel like that happens almost every time?
Yes, it does...
I see...
Is there any good way to deal with it?
Let’s think through together what kinds of things might help.
Thank you.
Even when you’re just barely on time, do you usually not end up being late?
Most of the time I’m not, but sometimes I am a little late.
I see... When you end up cutting it close or being late, what is it that causes trouble for you, or that bothers you?
I do feel bad toward the other person. They’ve gotten ready and prepared by the agreed time, and then I’m rushing around, and I think I’m so sloppy.
That’s how you feel... You’re even imagining the other person’s preparation... I get the sense that you’re a very considerate person.
Do you think so? I think to myself, if I know that, then I should just go earlier.
Even when we know something, actually doing it can be difficult, can’t it.
Yes...
About what causes you to always end up cutting it close—are there any things you’ve noticed yourself?
I think maybe I misjudge the time it takes to get ready, and, and the time it takes to get there. Sorry. I used too many “ands.”
That’s okay.
Thank you.
How long does it usually take you to get ready?
About an hour, I think.
I see.
Yes.

You mentioned that the cause may be your estimate of the time it takes to get ready or the time it takes to get there. If you were to build in some extra time for one of those right now, which one feels easier to think about?
Probably the time it takes to get there.
I see.
Yes.
For example, in cases where it takes 30 minutes by public transportation, how far in advance would you usually leave home?
I think about 50 minutes before.
I see. In that case, if you were to give yourself more leeway for the travel time, for something where you used to allow 50 minutes, how much extra time do you think you could realistically plan for?
Maybe 60 minutes... But then, that’s not really much different...
Even just making it 10 minutes earlier seems like it could give you a little more room emotionally, but for you, does that still feel a bit worrying?
I’m a little worried. It’s okay for it to be just 10 minutes?
I think it depends on the transportation you use, but for example, if it’s a train or bus, there’s a chance you could take one that’s a little earlier, right?
That’s true!
And if you move according to that kind of schedule, it also means you’ll finish getting ready 10 minutes earlier.
Yes.
And if some kind of problem comes up and you’re delayed in leaving, it seems like those 10 minutes could be useful. What do you think?
That sounds good.
How does that feel? Do you think you could do that?
I think I can. I’ll try it right away.
I’m glad. Please do give it a try.
Thank you.
Thank you as well for coming to talk with me. Try it out, and if it doesn’t go quite as well as you’d hoped, let’s think about another way together.
Thank you. I’ll start by trying it.
Yes, I’ll be rooting for it to go well.
Thank you.
Well then, we’ll end today’s consultation here.
Yes. Thank you very much.
Thank you for playing the role of the client today. Is it okay to end the role-play now?
Yes. That’s okay. Thank you very much.
Thank you. We’ll end here.

interaction.content: (Good evening, thank you for being here today.)
(Good evening. Thank you.)
(Would it be all right to start now?)
(Yes, that’s fine.)
(Well then, thank you.)
(Understood.)
Good evening, I’m the counselor. To start, could you tell me your age, gender, and what you’d like to talk about?
Good evening. I’m 28, male, and I’m struggling with something about my hobby.
Yes, thank you for sharing that. Could you tell me more about it?
It’s about my hobby, fishing. I’m thinking about whether I should quit or not.
I see... so you’re feeling unsure about it. What are the reasons you’re thinking about quitting?
Well...
Yes.
I haven’t been doing it at all lately. So I sometimes think maybe that’s enough.
I see, so you haven’t been fishing recently. Is there a reason you haven’t been going?
After actually trying it, I realized I don’t think it suits my personality. It is fun, though.
That’s how you felt, then. How long had you been fishing?
I went with a friend for about a year. But since then, not at all.

I see. You were going your friend, then. When you say fishing doesn’t suit your personality, in what way did you feel it doesn’t suit you? Sorry for the typo. I meant, you were going with your friend.
It’s okay. I can’t really come to like doing things early in the morning. Even at other times of day, I kind of think it’s a hassle.
Thank you. Yes, that’s how it feels for you. It makes sense that you’d feel unsure about whether to quit fishing. For you, what would it mean to quit fishing?
How should I answer that?
I’m sorry, the question was unclear. It could mean deciding emotionally that you’re going to quit fishing, or letting go of your gear, or...
Is it okay if I talk?
Yes, that’s okay.
Letting go of the gear, selling it, maybe?
I was thinking letting go of it could mean things like selling it or giving it to someone.
I see.
Were your fishing tools something you cared about a lot? If so, I’m sorry.
No, I wasn’t offended or anything. I just didn’t understand what you meant by “ways of letting go could be selling...”

I see. I’m relieved. I asked because I wanted to understand what quitting would mean for you. I’m sorry that was hard to understand. I’ll change the question. When you weren’t fishing, did you have any other hobbies?
I watched movies, or watched foreign dramas at home. I still watch them now, the same as before.
So you had time for hobbies through watching movies and things like that. Time is flexible, after all. Do you not really feel like fishing much right now?
Honestly, no.
I see. Would there be anything that would trouble you if you quit fishing?
Probably not. I’m not doing it now, actually, and there’s no inconvenience.
Are you enjoying watching movies and dramas as a hobby?
Yes. I’m enjoying it.

That’s good. Watching movies and things like that can be enjoyable too. It feels to me like fishing, which had been your hobby, is now shifting toward hobbies like watching movies, but how does that sound to you? I also thought that with the freedom of time, it might suit your personality too.
It’s not so much that I changed hobbies; I’d been doing that from before, separately from fishing.
I see. I’m sorry about that. So right now, you’re not fishing, and you’re enjoying the hobby time you’ve had since before.
That’s right.
I’m sorry this has taken time.
No, no. But I have plans after this, so would it be okay to stop here?
Yes, thank you for coming to talk with me today.
Thank you as well.
I’ll end the session here. (I’m very sorry we went over time. Thank you.)

interaction.content: Hello, I’m a counselor. Could you tell me your age, gender, and what you’d like to talk about?
Hello. I’m 50 years old, female. I’d like to talk about my poor physical condition.
You’d like to talk about your health issues. Could you tell me more about that?
Yes. For many years, I’ve been suffering from frequent coughing.
I see. That sounds very painful.
Yes. It’s hard because it’s painful both physically and mentally.
Are you currently seeing a doctor?
Yes. Right now I go regularly and use medication.
I see. Are you working at the moment?
I used to work, but because of the coughing and raising my child, right now I’m doing housework and studying to get a qualification.
You’re studying to get a qualification. What kind of studying are you doing?
Psychological counseling. Is that the same as what you do, maybe?
I see. That’s wonderful.
Thank you.
At the moment, with the medication, is your physical condition okay?
I’m still coughing now, and I’m suffering. I’m tired from the coughing.
I see. That sounds really hard.
Yes.
You said the coughing makes you tired. Is it affecting your studies?
Yes. I can only do the bare minimum of studying... I’m falling behind.
I see. How do you usually spend your days?
Well... housework, things related to my child, studying, and so on... When I get tired, I lie down in between.
Is your child still young?
No, they’re in high school.
I see. Does your child not need as much hands-on care anymore?
No. My child has been the type who needs a lot of attention ever since infancy, and still does now.
That sounds really difficult.
Yes. It’s often exhausting.
Do you do all of the housework yourself?
Yes, I do all of it.
I see. What part of the housework is the hardest for you?
The hardest is probably cooking and cleaning up... Making lunch early in the morning is especially burdensome.
Making lunch early in the morning is hard.
Yes. The anti-allergy medicine I take before bed starts to take effect around then, so I’m sleepy and sluggish.
I see. The medication can make you tired too, then.
It’s a side effect.
Even with the medication, do you still cough quite a lot?
It’s seasonal too, and especially from spring through July, even medication can’t suppress it.
I see. That must be really troubling.
Yes, it really is troubling.
Coughing takes a lot out of your body too, doesn’t it?
Yes. It’s tiring, and my throat feels painful...
At the doctor’s, is the medication you’re currently getting about the only treatment option?
It seems that way. I’ve been to various hospitals, but it seems like current medicine can’t do anything about it.
I see. That sounds very painful.
Yes. It’s really been so many years, just being alive is painful.
Does your partner worry about you?

No... It feels like they just see me as someone who normally coughs... They don’t do anything for me either. They do provide living expenses, though... And on top of that, they’re the type who wants me to take care of them too.
I see. That sounds like a very painful situation.
Yes. It’s stressful. And both my husband and my child are sloppy, so that’s hard too.
Is there anything, like a hobby, that helps you relieve stress?
I used to go to yoga classes... But because of the coughing, in the end I couldn’t go much anymore. When I’m at home, I end up doing housework without meaning to...
I see. That must be exhausting.
Thank you. (It’s about time, isn’t it!)
Thank you for sharing your story with me. We’ll end here for today.

interaction.content: (Good evening. We’ll begin when it’s time, so thank you in advance.)
(Good evening. Thank you.)
Good evening. I’m the counselor. To start, please tell me your age and gender, and what you’d like to talk about.
Good evening. 16, male. I don’t want to go to school.
I see. What grade are you in, by the way?
I’m in my second year of high school.
Thank you. You don’t want to go to school.
Yes.
Did something painful happen at school?
Yes, everyone in my class is ignoring me.
That must be really hard.
Yes. It’s hard.
About being ignored—when did it start, and have you been enduring it even though it’s been painful?
It started in the second term of my second year of high school and it’s still going on. I’m on winter break now, though.
I see. Are you doing okay physically? I imagine you’re feeling a lot of stress from being ignored by everyone.
It’s really stressful. I can’t really eat much.
I see. It’s really painful when everyone ignores you, isn’t it. Since you’re on break now, how are you feeling?
It was exhausting. I feel a lot better now.
Yes. So when you’re at home, it feels easier. Do you feel like you really don’t want the break to end?
Yes, I hate that school is starting. I don’t want to go, but if I don’t go, my mom will worry. But I don’t want to go.
That makes sense. I think it’s really something that you go even though you don’t want to. You don’t want to trouble your mother, do you.
Thank you. Yes, I don’t want to make her worry.
You’re kind. Is there a reason you don’t want to trouble your mother?
My dad isn’t around, and my mom works by herself, so I don’t want to give her extra worries.
I see. Your mother is a single mother. It must be painful for a child who has been given love to be ignored like this.
Is that so? I don’t know, but I haven’t told my mom that I’m being bullied.
Right. I can understand that it’s hard to say. But I think your mother is worried. Is there anyone other than your mother you can talk to? A teacher, for example.
At home I act normal, and she doesn’t ask about school, so I don’t think she’s noticed. No, there isn’t. When I told my homeroom teacher before, it got worse. The bullying.
That’s not good. Is there a counselor at your school?
By not good, do you mean me?
No. I mean the homeroom teacher.
Oh, okay.
Yes.
There is a counselor, but I don’t want the same thing to happen again, so I can’t say anything.
I don’t think the same thing will happen. I think they studied properly and became a counselor. I think it will be okay.
Do you think so? Is it okay to feel reassured?
Yes. Please try trusting them and talking to them.
I don’t know how to talk about it. I’m not good at talking, and I don’t want my mom to know either.
I see. You can make an agreement with the counselor so your mother doesn’t find out. If you’re not good at talking, would you like to practice together?
If it can be done without her finding out. But if I tell the counselor, and it gets passed on to my homeroom teacher, and then it becomes a class issue, I’m scared I’ll get bullied even more.
It’s okay. A counselor’s job exists to protect you. Counselors also don’t share your personal information.
I see... Then maybe I’ll try talking to them. How should I talk about it?
Yes. That’s right. Please do try trusting them and talking to them. I think it’s okay to talk as if you’re talking to a friend.
Okay. I’ll try.

Yes. Thank you. Please think together with the counselor about what to do from here about being ignored. I’ll be hoping that the ignoring stops. And if, just in case, things don’t go well, please come talk again.
Yes, when the new term starts, I’ll go to school for now and try meeting with the counselor.
That sounds good. I think that’s a very good thing. Please do your best.
Yes, thank you very much.
If anything else comes up, please come talk anytime. I’ll be here.
Okay.
Thank you for today. I believe you’ll find happiness going forward. I’ll be going now.
Thank you for listening. (Thank you very much.)
Thank you as well. (Thank you very much. Take care. Goodbye.)

You'd like him to listen to his children as he gets older, wouldn't you.

Yes. My family says it's better to just leave him alone. Because he's stubborn. But I'm his daughter, so I can't just leave it alone after all. And then I end up irritated all by myself.

I persuaded him many times, and recently a care manager? was assigned to them. I met that person once too.

Yes.
For the parts you can leave to others, leave them to others, and let your parents hear your voice over the phone. It will reassure them, and they get energy from you.
Yes. Is it okay to keep things this way?

Am I wrong for getting irritated? Oh, I'm sorry. It's time, isn't it.

interaction.content: (Good evening. Thank you for being here today. We’ll begin when it’s time.)
Thank you.
Good evening. I’m the counselor. Thank you for coming to talk with us today. To start, if you’re comfortable, could you tell me your age, gender, and what you’d like to talk about today?

I’m 32, female. I got married the other day. But we’re not having a wedding. My husband started saying he doesn’t understand the point of having one. When there’s something he doesn’t like, he gets his way by verbally attacking me or ignoring me. I don’t have anything to look forward to anymore. I’ve been thinking I want to go to where my late grandfather is.
I see. I imagine you’re feeling very distressed. If you’re comfortable, could you tell me more about it?

Yes. We dated for four years. Before we got married, he had said it would be okay to have a wedding, but then he started saying we wouldn’t. My father-in-law and my father both say we don’t need to have one, and the only ones who say, “Why don’t you have one?” are my mother and sister.
What I hate is that when he doesn’t want to do something, he forces his way through with verbal abuse.
If I have to keep putting up with this forever, I want to die.
Listening to you, I’m really concerned about you being in such a painful situation. Where are you sending these messages from right now?

I’m at home.
I’m in bed.
He’s in the next room making a lot of noise.
When he gets irritated, he takes it out on things.
So your husband sometimes takes things out on objects. After we finish talking, it’s okay to delete this exchange, so let’s keep your safety in mind as we talk.
Yes. Thank you.
Does it feel okay to keep talking like this right now?

It’s okay.
I’m grateful you’re listening.
There’s no rush, so please tell me how you’re feeling.
Yes. I don’t have anything to look forward to anymore, and it’s painful to think I have no choice but to keep putting up with this.

It’s painful to think about continuing on with days that feel hopeless and days of just enduring things, isn’t it.
I get the sense that, for you, having a wedding was something you really wanted. Is that right?
Yes. If we weren’t going to have a wedding, I wouldn’t have gotten married. I got married because before the marriage he said it was okay to have one. It’s a scam.
It makes sense that you would feel deceived. You said that before you got married, there had been a promise about having a wedding. How did things end up moving toward not having one?

All of a sudden, he started saying he didn’t understand the point of doing it. Even when I try to talk to him, he ignores me or says abusive things, so we can’t have a conversation. It’s always like that. In the end, if I don’t give in, things just stay tense between us.
I see. That must feel really frustrating.
Yes. I have no choice but to put up with it.
It must have been so painful to carry those feelings by yourself. Have your mother or sister said anything about the promise about the wedding being broken?
About that, they’ve said, “That’s really disappointing.”
I’m really glad there are people close to you who understand your feelings, even a little. Was your husband like this even when you were dating?

Yes. I hated the verbal abuse and tried to break up with him before, but he said he didn’t want that. When I tried to go back to my parents’ house, he apologized, and he would be kind for a while, but then the verbal abuse would happen again. It kept repeating.
He says things like, “I’ll fucking kill you.”
Yesterday, when I did the laundry, it seems there was a tissue in a pocket, and it got on his jacket, and he threw it away right in front of me, saying he couldn’t wear something like that.
Listening to you, I feel that your husband sounds very frightening. How do you feel about him?
Yes. I’m scared…
You feel scared. Has he ever actually used violence against you? I’m worried.
There hasn’t been any violence.
I see. I’m relieved to hear that. Still, I imagine living in fear must feel very suffocating. How do you feel about your life right now?
It feels very suffocating. I’m always worrying about his mood. I’m just tired.

That makes sense. It must be emotionally exhausting. In the midst of all that, you’ve been doing your best every day, and I’d like us to think together about how you might be able to live each day with some hope going forward. How does that sound?

I don’t feel like I can have hope anymore…
I want to die and be at peace.

You’re so exhausted that you can’t even feel hope. Having had the chance to talk with you like this, and as someone who has been allowed to be even a small part of your life, I don’t want you to die.
But that’s how deeply painful it feels, isn’t it.
Yes. I came here and wrote this like it was a suicide note.
So that’s the feeling you had when you shared this with me.
Thank you for listening to me for so long.
Not at all. But as I wrote earlier, I don’t want you to die.
Thank you.

I can’t just stand by and watch you, who has been trying so hard every day, choose death.
Could you tell me more about yourself?
I’m just so tired. Every day feels like hell.
Your days have been so painful that every day feels like hell, haven’t they.
Yes.

Even now, while you’re feeling so exhausted, you came here to talk with me. Thank you. I’ll always be waiting here, so anytime is okay. Before you take a step toward death, could you come talk with me one more time?

Thank you. Please let me come back to talk again.
I’ll try to hang in there a little longer.
I’m truly glad you feel that way. I hope I can be of even a little help. Please come and tell me more again.
Yes. Thank you for listening to me today.

Thank you as well.
(Thank you. This was very educational for me.)
(Thank you. Thank you for your hard work.)
(I’ll end the session now.)

interaction.content: Hello(?) It's time. What seems to be going on(?) Thank you for speaking with me.
Hello. I'm the counselor. Mental trainer: relationships. Thank you for being here.
Okay. Thank you.
To start, could you tell me your age, gender, and what I should call you?
I'm 29, female, Gel.
Thank you. Gel, then.
Yes.
Could you tell me what you'd like to talk about?
There's someone I'm thinking of marrying.
I see.
He's the eldest son, and the heir.
I see.
I'd be living with his parents. I feel anxious about getting married.
I see. That certainly would make you feel anxious, wouldn't it. What part feels the most worrying?
I feel like I don't really get along with his mother.
That's how you're feeling...
He also says living together is the assumption.
I see. When you're worried about compatibility, it really is hard to have a positive image of it...
Yes. It's not officially decided or anything, but I don't know what to do.
I see. So it sounds like things are leaning toward living together.
I'm already 29, too.
Mm-hmm.
Yes.
You end up thinking about the future, don't you.
Yes.
For you, Gel, is there a way you wish things could turn out?
Living together is a bit...
Mm-hmm.
It's in the countryside, I mean, it's rural.
That's something that's been on your mind too, then.
Yes. There's nothing but fields around.
I see.
His mother-in-law is the kind of person who says things very directly.
I see. (I'm listening, so please go on.)
He says that's just her personality. But there are times when it really cuts into me. It becomes stressful. When I asked if it had to be living together,
Yes... Even if she doesn't mean any harm, when someone says things so bluntly, it can hurt. I understand that feeling...
He said it's because he's the heir.
I see... Does it feel like he can't take over the work unless you live together?
Yes. It's a family business.
I see.
The house is big, too.
I see. So it sounds like he would watch how his parents work up close, and gradually take over from them.
I think so.
I see. Do you feel, Gel, that you understand that part—that it's necessary?
Yes. I think the work part can't be helped.
Right. You would want your future husband to properly take over the work, wouldn't you.
His father is the president of a small company,
Mm-hmm.
And right now he's working at a related company, kind of like training,
I see. He's working hard toward the future, then.
It seems like they told him to go work outside the company once.
I see. It may be a parent's wish for their son to grow into someone capable.
Yes.
From here on, would it be that, when you get married, he'll start learning the work at his father's company?
Yes.
I see. So the work side of things is steadily moving forward. In that case,
Yes.
Then for you, Gel, is it that ideally you'd like to be able to separate work and daily life?
His mother is the issue. I guess that's what it comes down to.
Right. You were saying that talking with her itself is stressful...
If I have to see her every day, the irritation will...
Yes... It sounds like an unimaginable amount of stress could build up, and I'm worried about your health, Gel...
Even now, there are things I'm putting up with.
Mm-hmm.
Even if I tell him, he just insists there's nothing that can be done.
I see...
It feels like he's more on their side.
When the person you most want to support you says that, it makes you feel sad, doesn't it...
Yes.
You've been keeping it inside and putting up with it all this time, haven't you... (We've reached the end of our time, so we'll finish here.)
